# PraisonAIUI

> A web UI for AI agents in Python: streaming chat, an artifacts canvas, selectable layouts, a dashboard and docs sites.

---

# PraisonAIUI

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/

> A web UI for AI agents in Python. Streaming chat, an artifacts canvas, selectable layouts, a dashboard and docs sites, from one pip package.

## Run it in 30 seconds

1. **Install**

   Python 3.10 or higher.

   ```bash
   pip install aiui
   ```

2. **Scaffold or write app.py**

   Scaffold a starter for any agent framework (`agent`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `langgraph`, `crewai`, `pydantic-ai`, `praisonai`, or `dashboard`), or write `app.py` directly:

   ```bash
   aiui init --template agent
   ```

   ```python title="app.py"
   import praisonaiui as aiui


   @aiui.reply
   async def on_message(message: str):
       await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")
       await aiui.send_block(aiui.metric("Status", value="Online", delta="Live"))
   ```

3. **Run it**

   ```bash
   aiui run app.py
   ```

   Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. `aiui run app.py` opens cleanly in **focused mode**
   (Chat + your own pages) in the React app shell. Pass `--preset agent` for
   Sessions, Approvals, Usage and Memory, `--preset ops` for the full control plane,
   or `AIUI_LAYOUT=chat-canvas aiui run app.py` to open the side canvas.

## Pick a starting point

- [Agent UI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/overview.md)
  Build streaming AI agent interfaces with starters, profiles, reasoning steps, tool calls, HITL approvals and an artifacts canvas.
- [App & Dashboard](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/app-ui/overview.md)
  Combine chat with 5 selectable layouts, Python or YAML data pages, notifications, themes and built-in ops views.
- [A2UI (Generative UI)](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/quickstart.md)
  Let agents push live interactive surfaces, forms and controls over JSONL and WebSocket into a split Chat + Canvas workspace.

- [UI Components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/components/overview.md)
  Explore all 81 Python and YAML UI builders — inline chat blocks, split-pane chat panels, file uploads, spreadsheets, whiteboards, DataFrames, Plotly charts and forms.
- [Docs UI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/docs-ui/overview.md)
  Turn a folder of Markdown and one `aiui.yaml` into a fast, searchable documentation site with SEO, OpenAPI and `llms.txt`.
- [Plugins & Security](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md)
  Extend the app with pip-installable `@aiui/sdk` React pages and themes, behind deny-by-default auth and reverse proxies.

Looking something up? The [CLI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/cli.md), the [Python API](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python.md)
and the [YAML configuration](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md) cover every command,
function and key.

PraisonAIUI is MIT licensed. Install it from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/aiui/)
as `aiui`; the import name is `praisonaiui` and the command is `aiui`.

---

# Installation

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/installation

> PraisonAIUI is one Python package. The PyPI name is aiui, you import it as

PraisonAIUI is one Python package. The PyPI name is `aiui`, you import it as
`praisonaiui`, and the command is `aiui`. The browser UI ships inside the
wheel, so you do not need Node.js or npm to run an app or build a docs site.

## Requirements

Python 3.10 or higher.

> **Note: No Node.js needed**
>
> The browser UI ships inside the wheel. You need Node.js only to change the
> React frontend in a clone of the repository (version in `src/frontend/.nvmrc`).

## Install

=== "pip"

    ```bash
    pip install aiui
    ```

=== "uv"

    ```bash
    uv pip install aiui
    ```

=== "pipx"

    ```bash
    pipx install aiui
    ```

Check the install:

```bash
aiui --version
# praisonaiui version 0.3.x
```

> **Check:**
> A version number means the `aiui` command is on your path. Next: the
> [quick start](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md).

The wheel installs two commands that do the same thing: `aiui` and `praisonaiui`.

## Optional extras

The base install runs the server, the chat UI and `aiui build`. Extras add
integrations. Install one with `pip install "aiui[<extra>]"`.

| Extra | Adds |
|-------|------|
| `praisonai` | PraisonAI Agents, the PraisonAI wrapper, gateway and bot dependencies, for `--backend praisonai`. A YAML chat app (`aiui run chat.yaml`) needs only `pip install praisonaiagents` |
| `memory` | ChromaDB and LiteLLM for agent memory |
| `knowledge` | mem0, ChromaDB, MarkItDown and Chonkie for the knowledge base |
| `graph` | mem0 graph memory |
| `sql` | SQLAlchemy (async) and aiosqlite for `SQLAlchemyDataStore` |
| `postgres` | `sql` plus asyncpg |
| `bot` | Telegram, Discord and Slack bot libraries |
| `slack`, `discord`, `teams` | One channel's SDK only |
| `mcp` | The MCP client SDK |
| `a2ui` | PraisonAI Agents with A2UI support (agent canvas) |
| `langchain`, `llama-index`, `semantic-kernel` | Framework integrations |
| `all` | Every extra above |
| `dev` | pytest, ruff, mypy and the test dependencies (for contributors) |

The list is `[project.optional-dependencies]` in
[`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

## No npm package is needed

Nothing in this repository is published to npm for the current UI:
`src/frontend/package.json` is private and its build is committed into the
Python package. Plugins for the React app shell import `@aiui/sdk`, which the
shell provides at runtime; see [UI plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md).
The older `praisonaiui` package on npm (0.1.0) is a separate docs-site runtime,
described under [TypeScript SDK](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/typescript.md); `aiui run` and
`aiui build` do not use it.

## Development install

To work on PraisonAIUI itself:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI.git
cd PraisonAIUI
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Only when you change src/frontend/src/**
cd src/frontend
npm ci
npm run build && npm run sync   # rebuild and copy the bundle into the package
```

See [Testing](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/testing.md) for the test commands.

## Next steps

- [Quick Start](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): run your first app
- [CLI Usage](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/cli.md): the commands you will use most

# Quick Start

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart

> Run a chat app, connect it to a model, then try the other UI styles and layouts.

Run a chat app, connect it to a model, then try the other UI styles and layouts.

## Install

Python 3.10 or higher:

```bash
pip install aiui
```

## 1. A chat app

Scaffold a starter app for any framework (`agent`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `langgraph`, `crewai`, `pydantic-ai`, `praisonai`, or `dashboard`):

```bash
aiui init --template agent
aiui run app.py
```

Or create `app.py` directly:

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")
    # Render any of the 81 UI blocks (or DataFrames / Plotly figures) inline in chat:
    await aiui.send_block(aiui.metric("Status", value="Ready", delta="Live"))
```

Run it:

```bash
aiui run app.py
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 and send a message.

> **Tip:**
> If port 8000 is taken, `aiui run` picks the next free port and prints the URL
> it used.

`aiui run app.py` opens in the React app shell (`style: app`) in **focused mode**
(Chat + your own pages). Pass `--preset agent` to add Sessions, Approvals, Usage
and Memory, or `--preset ops` for the full control plane. The minimal example is
[`examples/python/01-chat`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/examples/python/01-chat/app.py).

## 2. Reply with a model

Stream tokens from any client library with `aiui.stream_token()`. With OpenAI
(`pip install openai`), set your key first:

### macOS and Linux

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

### Windows

```powershell
setx OPENAI_API_KEY sk-...
```

Then open a new terminal.

```python title="app.py" {9,14-16}
import praisonaiui as aiui
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

client = AsyncOpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    stream = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": message}],
        stream=True,
    )
    async for chunk in stream:
        if chunk.choices and chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
            await aiui.stream_token(chunk.choices[0].delta.content)
```

`aiui run` also reads a `.env` file in the current folder (and
`~/.praisonai/.env`) without overriding variables already set.
[`examples/python/03-chat-with-ai`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/examples/python/03-chat-with-ai/app.py)
adds conversation history, a welcome message and starters.

## 3. Other layouts and the classic chat

The app shell has selectable layouts. Pick one per run with `AIUI_LAYOUT`, or
in the app with `aiui.set_layout()`:

```bash
AIUI_LAYOUT=chat-canvas aiui run app.py   # the chat beside a canvas of artifacts
AIUI_LAYOUT=workbench aiui run app.py     # a quiet sidebar of chats
aiui run app.py --style chat              # the classic chat style instead of the app shell
```

See [React app shell](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/react-shell.md) and
[Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) for every layout.

## 4. Add a custom page or 5-line function interface

Register a custom page with `@aiui.page` — or wrap any Python function (including
`yield` generators) with `aiui.interface()`. An app with pages opens in the
React app shell (`style: app`) in focused mode (Chat + your own pages); pass
`--preset ops` for all built-in ops views, or `--style dashboard` for the legacy
vanilla dashboard:

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")


@aiui.page("metrics", title="Metrics", icon="bar-chart-2", group="App")
async def metrics():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.columns([
            aiui.container([
                aiui.card("Users", value=1234),
                aiui.table([{"Name": "Alpha", "Value": 100}, {"Name": "Beta", "Value": 200}], searchable=True),
            ]),
            aiui.chat_panel(title="Ask about metrics", height=460),
        ]),
    ])
```

How the style is chosen: `--style` on the command line wins, then
`aiui.set_style()` in the app. Without either, `aiui run` opens the React app
shell (`app`), or `agents` when `@aiui.profiles` is paired with registered
agents. See [UI Styles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/styles.md) and
[Build a focused app](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app.md).

## 5. A chat agent from YAML

A YAML file can define the agent without Python. It runs on PraisonAI Agents,
so install that first: `pip install praisonaiagents` (or the full
`pip install "aiui[praisonai]"`), and set `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

```yaml title="chat.yaml"
name: My Assistant
instructions: You are a helpful assistant. Be concise.
model: gpt-4o-mini
welcome: "Hi! How can I help you today?"
starters:
  - label: "What can you do?"
    message: "Tell me about your capabilities"
```

```bash
aiui run chat.yaml
```

## 6. A documentation site

`aiui build` turns a folder of Markdown into a static site:

```bash
aiui init --template docs        # writes aiui.yaml
mkdir docs && echo "# Hello" > docs/index.md
aiui serve                       # builds into ./aiui, then serves it
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs/. To publish it, see
[Deploy to GitHub Pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/github-pages.md).

## If something is wrong

> **Warning:**
> Never paste an API key into `app.py` or `aiui.yaml`: read it from the
> environment, as above.

With the server running, in another terminal:

```bash
aiui doctor                    # structured diagnostics
aiui health --detailed         # per-feature health
```

  Build a full AI app one feature at a time, from first message to production deploy.

  Push live agent-driven surfaces and interactive canvases over WebSocket and JSONL.

  Publish a searchable Markdown documentation site with SEO, OpenAPI and `llms.txt`.

# UI Styles

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/styles

> The style decides which frontend serves your app. aiui run picks one from your

The style decides which frontend serves your app. `aiui run` picks one from your
code when you do not name it.

## Available Styles

| Style | What it renders |
|-------|-----------------|
| `chat` | React chat interface: sessions, streaming, starters, profiles |
| `agents` | React multi-agent view with a tabbed agent/session sidebar |
| `playground` | React side-by-side input and output panels for prompt testing |
| `dashboard` | The legacy vanilla-JS admin dashboard with built-in and custom pages (only when asked for) |
| `docs` | React documentation site (sidebar, table of contents, search) |
| `custom` | React site built from your YAML templates and components, with an optional floating chat widget |
| `app` | The React app shell with selectable layouts (the default) |

`app` is what `create_app()` and `aiui run` open when nothing else picks a
style (owner decision, 2026-11-22); `aiui run` starts it in
the `chat` layout (no canvas) unless the app, its YAML or `AIUI_LAYOUT` picks
another. See [React app shell](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/react-shell.md) for what it contains and
[Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) for its layouts.

## Auto-Detection

```bash
aiui run app.py    # style is inferred from app.py
```

After loading `app.py`, the CLI looks at the callbacks and agents it registered
(`server.detect_style`):

| Your code registers | Detected style |
|---------------------|----------------|
| `@aiui.profiles` and at least one `aiui.register_agent()` | `agents` |
| one or more `@aiui.page(...)` callbacks | `app` (it lists the pages; `dashboard` before 2026-11-22) |
| anything else, such as `@aiui.reply` only | `app` (the React app shell, `chat` layout) |

### Example: detected as `agents`

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.register_agent("Coder", {"name": "Coder", "instructions": "..."})

@aiui.profiles
async def get_profiles():
    return [
        {"name": "Coder", "icon": "💻", "default": True},
        {"name": "Writer", "icon": "✍️"},
    ]

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    await aiui.say(f"Echo: {message}")
```

```bash
aiui run app.py
# ℹ️ Auto-detected style: agents
```

## Setting the Style

### From the CLI

```bash
aiui run app.py --style chat         # the classic chat style
aiui run app.py --style agents
aiui run app.py --style playground
```

`--style` has no default value, so any style you name, `chat` included, wins over
`aiui.set_style()` and detection.

### From Python

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("playground")  # wins over auto-detection

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    await aiui.say(f"Echo: {message}")
```

### From YAML

A YAML chat app (`aiui run chat.yaml`) reads `style:` and applies it through
`aiui.set_style()`:

```yaml
name: My App
instructions: You are a helpful assistant.
style: agents

profiles:
  - name: "General"
    icon: "🤖"
    default: true
  - name: "Coder"
    icon: "💻"
```

```bash
aiui run chat.yaml
```

### Environment

`AIUI_SHELL=app` turns the `dashboard` style into `app`; `AIUI_SHELL=legacy`
turns `app` back into `dashboard` (the kill switch). It has no effect on the
other styles.

## Priority Order

1. `style:` in a YAML chat app
2. CLI `--style`
3. `aiui.set_style()` in Python
4. Auto-detection (`agents`)
5. Default: `app`

## Chat Positioning

`layout.mode` in a YAML site config places the React chat on the page instead of
filling it:

| `layout.mode` | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| `fullscreen` | Full-page chat (default) |
| `sidebar` | Fixed right-side panel |
| `bottom-right` | Floating widget, bottom-right corner |
| `bottom-left` | Floating widget, bottom-left corner |
| `top-right` | Floating widget, top-right corner |
| `top-left` | Floating widget, top-left corner |

In the `docs` and `custom` styles, `chat.enabled: true` with one of the four
corner modes adds the floating chat widget on top of the site. In the
`dashboard` style the equivalent is
`aiui.set_chat_mode("fullpage" | "floating" | "sidebar")`.

# CLI Usage

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/cli

> The commands you will use most. Every command and option is in the

The commands you will use most. Every command and option is in the
[CLI Reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/cli.md); `aiui <command> --help` prints the same from
the installed version.

## Scaffold and run an app

```bash
aiui init --template agent           # starter app.py (also: openai, anthropic, langgraph, crewai, pydantic-ai, praisonai, dashboard)
aiui run app.py                      # opens in focused mode (Chat + your own pages)
aiui run app.py --preset agent       # adds Sessions, Approvals, Usage, and Memory
aiui run app.py --preset ops         # enables the full built-in control plane
aiui run chat.yaml                   # a YAML-defined agent (needs praisonaiagents)
aiui run app.py --style chat         # the classic chat instead of the app shell
aiui run app.py --port 3000 --reload # another port, restart on file changes
aiui run app.py --datastore json     # keep sessions as JSON under ~/.praisonaiui
```

Without `--style`, the style comes from `aiui.set_style()` or is detected from
the callbacks; Python apps with `@aiui.reply` or `@aiui.page` open the React app
shell (`style: app`) in focused mode. See [UI Styles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/styles.md) and
[Build a focused app](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app.md).

## Build a docs site

```bash
aiui init --template docs            # writes aiui.yaml
aiui dev                             # preview on :8000; saves reload the browser
aiui validate --strict               # check the configuration
aiui docs check-links                # broken links, anchors and images
aiui build --output site --minify    # static site in ./site
aiui serve                           # build and serve the production site
```

See [Deploy to GitHub Pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/github-pages.md) to publish the build.

## Check a running server

```bash
aiui doctor                          # diagnostics; the imported aiui version and folder, PyPI's latest, stale installs
aiui health --detailed               # per-feature health (alias of health-check)
aiui test all --server http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

`aiui test` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8082`, so pass `--server` for a
server on another port. See [API Testing](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/testing.md).

## Manage a running server

Management commands call the server's HTTP API. They default to
`http://127.0.0.1:8000`; pass `--server URL` for another one.

```bash
aiui sessions list
aiui sessions messages SESSION_ID
aiui memory search "dark mode"
aiui pages ids                       # page ids for aiui.set_pages()
aiui config set model gpt-4o-mini
aiui approval list --status pending
```

The full list (`sessions`, `session-ext`, `memory`, `provider`, `features`,
`pages`, `config`, `approval`, `schedule`, `skills`, `hooks`, `workflows`,
`eval`, `traces`, `surface`, `plugins`) is in the
[CLI Reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/cli.md#management-commands).

# Server pages

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/server-pages

> Pages built in Python with @aiui.page and aiui blocks - filters in the URL, forms and page actions, lazy tabs, auto refresh and job status.

A server page is a Python function that returns blocks. The app shell
(`style: app`, the default) fetches them from `GET /api/pages/{id}/data` and
renders them; forms and buttons talk back through `POST /api/pages/{id}/action`.
Both endpoints sit behind the same auth as every other `/api/*` route.

This guide builds a filter page step by step. Each part works on its own.

## 1. A page

`@aiui.page("channels", title="Channels")` on a function that returns
`aiui.layout([...])` (`{"_components": [...]}`) makes a page; every helper in
`aiui` (`metric`, `table`, `tabs`, `form`, ...) is a block, see
[Components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/components.md). `aiui.register_page(id, title=..., handler=fn)`
does the same without the decorator. Run the app with `aiui run app.py`.

## 2. Page parameters: filters in the URL

A handler that takes `params` receives the page URL's query string as a dict.
A key given once is a string; a key given more than once is a list:

```
/channels?format=shorts&tag=ai&tag=dev   ->   {"format": "shorts", "tag": ["ai", "dev"]}
```

The handler is matched by its signature: a parameter named `params` (or
`**kwargs`) gets it by keyword, a single required positional parameter gets it
positionally, and a handler with no parameters is called as before.

The app shell sends the URL's query string with every data request, so a
filtered view survives a refresh, a bookmark and a shared link. The page's
Refresh button re-fetches with the current params.

## 3. Forms

`aiui.form(action_id, children=[...], submit_label=...)` collects every input
inside it by `name` (or by its label when it has no `name`). Give inputs a
`name` so the keys are stable. The first argument is the action id, normally
the page id.

There are two ways to submit.

### `method="get"`: filters

The values are written into the page URL (`history.replaceState`) and the page
data is fetched again, so the page handler sees them in `params`. No action
handler is needed. This is the right choice for a filter form:

```python
FORMATS = ["all", "long", "shorts"]


@aiui.page("channels", title="Channels", icon="📺", group="Research")
async def channels(params):
    fmt = params.get("format", "all")
    query = params.get("q", "")
    rows = [r for r in load_channels() if matches(r, fmt, query)]
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.form("channels", method="get", submit_label="Apply", children=[
            aiui.columns([
                aiui.text_input("Search", name="q", value=query),
                aiui.select_input("Format", name="format", options=FORMATS, value=fmt),
            ]),
        ]),
        aiui.table(headers=["Name", "Format"], rows=[[r.name, r.format] for r in rows]),
    ])
```

Render each input with `value=` taken from `params`, so the form shows the
active filters after a refresh. An empty value removes its key from the URL;
other keys in the URL stay. Keys starting with `_` are never written.

### `method="post"` (default): page actions

The values are POSTed as JSON to `/api/pages/{page_id}/action`. Handle them
with `aiui.register_page_action(page_id)`:

```python
@aiui.register_page_action("channels")
async def channels_action(data):
    if data.get("action") == "sync":            # a button: aiui.button_group([{"label": "Sync", "action": "sync"}])
        start_sync()
        return {"message": "Sync started"}       # a toast
    save_note(data["note"])                     # a form: the inputs by name
    return aiui.layout([...])                   # re-renders the page
```

What the reply can hold:

| Key | Effect in the app shell |
|-----|-------------------------|
| `_components` | Replaces the page with these blocks (return `aiui.layout([...])`). |
| `message` (or `status`) | A success toast. With `_components`, both happen. |
| `error` | An error toast; the page is left as it was. |
| `_params` | Written into the page URL's query string (`aiui.layout([...], params={...})`); `None` or `""` removes a key. |
| `_refresh_every` | Starts or changes auto refresh (section 5). |

`aiui.form(..., update_url=True)` writes the submitted values into the URL
after a successful POST, as `method="get"` does. Use it when the action both
does something and changes the view; a reply's `_params` wins over it.

A button posts `{**payload, "action": action, "_params": {...}}`. A form posts
its values alongside `"_params"` (the page URL's current query string, same
dict shape as `params` in the page handler).

### Streaming replies (`yield`)

To stream LLM tokens or step-by-step progress live without polling, make your
`@aiui.register_page_action` handler an `async def` (or sync) generator that
`yield`s `aiui.layout([...])` frames:

```python
@aiui.register_page_action("writer")
async def writer_action(data):
    text = ""
    async for token in run_llm(data["prompt"]):
        text += token
        yield aiui.layout([aiui.markdown_text(text)])
    yield {"message": "Done"}
```

The server streams each yielded frame as `application/x-ndjson`; the app shell
updates the page live and displays a **Stop** button to cancel the stream.

## 4. Lazy tabs and expanders

Heavy sections can load when they are first opened instead of with the page:

```python
@aiui.page("youtube", title="YouTube", icon="▶️", group="Research")
async def youtube(params):
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.tabs([
            {"label": "Overview", "children": [aiui.metric("Views", value="1.2M")]},  # eager
            {"label": "Retention", "load": "retention"},                              # lazy
            {"label": "Traffic", "load": "traffic"},
        ], lazy=True),
        aiui.expander("Every video", lazy=True, load="videos"),
    ])


@aiui.register_page_action("youtube")
async def youtube_action(data):
    key = data.get("_lazy")
    params = data.get("_params", {})       # the page URL's query string
    if key == "retention":
        return aiui.layout([retention_chart(params)])
    if key == "traffic":
        return aiui.layout([traffic_table(params)])
    if key == "videos":
        return aiui.layout([videos_table(params)])
    return {"error": f"Unknown section {key!r}"}
```

- With `lazy=True`, a tab item without `children` is lazy; its key is its
  `load` value, or its `label`. An item with `children` renders at once.
- `aiui.expander(title, lazy=True, load=key)`: the key defaults to the title.
- The body is fetched with `POST /api/pages/{id}/action` and the JSON body
  `{"_lazy": key, "_params": {...}}`. Reply with `_components`, as for any
  action. A reply with `error` (or an HTTP error) shows the message and a
  "Try again" button; a skeleton shows while it loads.
- Once loaded, a section stays loaded. When the page data reloads (Refresh,
  auto refresh, an action that re-renders), open sections fetch again; a
  closed one fetches again the next time it opens.

## 5. Auto refresh and job status

`refresh_every` (seconds, at least 1) re-fetches the page while its browser
tab is visible. It pauses while the tab is hidden and resumes when it is shown
again. After a failure it keeps the last good content, shows one error toast
and doubles the wait on each failure in a row (up to 5 minutes).

Set it when you register the page, or per reply (a reply's value wins, so a
page can refresh only while something runs):

```python
@aiui.page("sync", title="Sync", icon="🔄", group="Research")
async def sync():
    jobs = list_jobs()  # your job store
    rows = [
        # state: "queued" | "running" | "done" | "failed"; progress 0-100 or None
        aiui.status(j.name, state=j.state, detail=j.detail, progress=j.percent, log=j.lines[-20:])
        for j in jobs
    ]
    running = any(j.state in ("queued", "running") for j in jobs)
    return aiui.layout(
        [aiui.button_group([{"label": "Sync now", "action": "sync"}]), *rows],
        refresh_every=3 if running else None,
    )


@aiui.register_page_action("sync")
async def sync_action(data):
    start_sync()
    # Re-render, so the reply's _refresh_every starts the polling.
    return {**await sync(), "message": "Sync started"}
```

`@aiui.page(..., refresh_every=10)` and
`aiui.register_page(..., refresh_every=10)` set a fixed period; the data
reply carries it as `_refresh_every` unless the handler set that key.

`@aiui.page(..., badge=...)` and `aiui.register_page(..., badge=...)` show a
short pill beside the page title in the app shell sidebar (across Classic and
all selectable layouts). Pass a string, an integer, or a zero-argument callable
(evaluated when the manifest is served) for live counts such as unread items or
queued jobs. To update badges dynamically after an action without reloading the
page, return `aiui.layout([...], badges={"inbox": 2})` (or `refresh_manifest=True`).

## 6. Declarative YAML pages

`aiui run app.yaml` can declare server-driven block pages directly in YAML
(alongside built-in page ids such as `chat`):

```yaml
style: app
branding:
  title: "Operations"
pages:
  - chat
  - id: overview
    title: "Overview"
    icon: "bar-chart-2"
    group: "Workspace"
    badge: "Live"
    refresh_every: 30
    components:
      - type: columns
        children:
          - type: metric
            label: "Active users"
            value: "1,420"
            delta: "+12%"
          - type: card
            title: "Status"
            value: "Healthy"
      - type: table
        columns:
          - { key: "name", label: "Service", type: "text" }
          - { key: "lift", label: "Lift", type: "number", format: "multiplier", tone_above: 1.0 }
        rows:
          - { name: "API", lift: 1.8 }
  - id: runbook
    title: "Runbook"
    icon: "book-open"
    group: "Docs"
    markdown_file: "./runbook.md"
    toc: true
```

Every component block (`card`, `metric`, `table`, `chart`, `gallery`,
`card_grid`, `filter_bar`, `select_input`, `list_detail`, `markdown_text`,
`doc_viewer`, `pagination`, `color_picker_input`, …) uses the same JSON/YAML
dict format as Python's `aiui.*` helpers. Large apps can split page definitions
into separate files with `$ref:` (e.g. `- $ref: ./pages/overview.yaml`). Edits
to the YAML file, any `$ref`-included file, or a referenced `markdown_file`
reload dynamically on the next fetch without restarting the server. Set
`api_endpoint:` instead of `components:` to back a YAML-declared page with a
custom API or plugin endpoint.

## Shell support

The app shell supports everything in this guide. The legacy `dashboard`
style renders the page and its forms. It ignores `params`, `method="get"`,
lazy loading and `refresh_every`, and shows a status as plain text.

# Build a focused app

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app

> A dashboard with only your pages, in the new app shell, with its own chat history.

Your own pages, Chat when you have a `@reply`, and nothing else: no built-in
tabs, no pages from other apps on the machine, no other apps' chats.

## The whole app

```python
# app.py  ->  aiui run app.py
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("app")        # the new shell (already the default; says so)
aiui.only_my_pages("chat")   # my pages + Chat; same as aiui.set_pages(["chat"])


@aiui.page("posts", title="My posts", icon="📈", group="My posts", order=1)
async def posts():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.columns([aiui.metric("Posts", value=42), aiui.metric("Best", value="12.4k")]),
        aiui.table(headers=["Hook", "Views"], rows=[["I replaced my IDE", "12,400"]]),
    ])


@aiui.page("links", title="Links", icon="🔗", group="My posts", order=2)
async def links():
    return aiui.layout([aiui.markdown_text("- [YouTube Studio](https://studio.youtube.com)")])


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")
```

```bash
uv pip install -U aiui        # always start from the latest release
aiui run app.py               # opens http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

The sidebar shows Chat and a **My posts** group with your two pages. Every
layout of the app shell lists your pages in their group, and the layout
picker still works.

## What each line does

| You want | Use |
|---|---|
| The new app shell | Nothing: `style: app` is the default. `aiui.set_style("app")` makes it explicit |
| Only your pages | `aiui.only_my_pages()` or `aiui.set_pages([])` |
| Your pages and Chat (minimal preset) | `aiui.set_pages("minimal")` or `aiui.only_my_pages("chat")` (automatic default when running `aiui run app.py` with `@aiui.page`/`@aiui.reply`) |
| Core Agent preset (Chat, Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory) | `aiui.set_pages("agent")` or `aiui run app.py --preset agent` |
| A few specific built-in pages | `aiui.set_pages(["chat", "sessions", "usage"])` (ids: `aiui pages ids`) |
| Every page (full Ops console) | `aiui.set_pages("ops")` / `aiui.set_pages("all")` or `aiui run app.py --preset ops` |

## 5-line function apps (`aiui.interface`)

Wrap any Python function (sync, `async def`, or streaming `yield` generator) into an interactive page without writing separate `@aiui.page` and `@aiui.register_page_action` handlers:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

async def summarize(text: str, tone: str = "Brief"):
    yield f"**{tone} summary:** {text[:120]}"

aiui.interface(
    summarize,
    inputs=[
        aiui.textarea_input("Text", name="text", placeholder="Paste text..."),
        aiui.select_input("Tone", name="tone", options=["Brief", "Detailed"], value="Brief"),
    ],
    title="Summarizer",
)
```

`set_pages` is the one switch for what shows. It covers built-in pages, the
app shell's layout pages (`start`, `artifacts`, `templates`, `connect`,
`api-reference`) and dashboard-plugin folders, including the ones in
`~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins` that every app on the machine would
otherwise share. Pages you register yourself (`@aiui.page`,
`aiui.register_page`, `aiui.register_plugin`) always show. A wrong id is
reported at startup: `set_pages() names 'chta', but no page has that id`.

## Add pages and links

- A server-driven page: `@aiui.page(id, title=..., icon=..., group=..., order=...)`
  returning `aiui.layout([...])` of blocks (`aiui.metric`, `aiui.table`,
  `aiui.columns`, `aiui.markdown_text`, `aiui.card`, ...). Pages with the same
  `group` sit together in the sidebar; `order` sorts them.
- Links: a page of markdown links, as `links` above.
- A React page or a whole plugin: see [UI Plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md).

## Your own data

`aiui run app.py` keeps the app's chats in its own folder,
`~/.praisonaiui/apps/<file name>-<hash>/sessions/`, so the sidebar never
lists the chats of other apps or agents. Point it elsewhere with
`--datastore sdk:/path` (or `json:/path`), or share the old machine-wide
history with `--datastore sdk`. Set `AIUI_DATA_DIR` to move everything aiui
keeps (config, sessions) for one app. See [Sessions](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/sessions.md).

## Show everything

`aiui.set_pages("all")` (or `aiui run app.py --pages all`) is the opposite
of a focused app: every page of the product, each in its React version where
there is one and otherwise the legacy view inside the new shell, with every
group (Agent, Work, Control, ...) listed in the sidebar of whatever layout is
on. Your own pages still show in their group.

## Mount only the shell (no agent endpoints)

When you embed PraisonAIUI as a dedicated dashboard host and do not want
agent/chat endpoints (`/sessions`, `/run`, `/agents`, `/teams`, `/api/chat/*`)
mounted on the port, use `aiui.create_shell_app()` instead of `create_app()`.
Pass `csp="strict"` (or a directive mapping / callable) to attach a strict
`Content-Security-Policy` with the exact `'sha256-…'` hashes of the shell's
inline scripts — no HTML buffering middleware or manual route allowlists needed:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.routing import Route

async def api_operations(request):
    return JSONResponse({"status": "ok"})

app = aiui.create_shell_app(
    plugins=[MyDashboardPlugin()],
    routes=[Route("/api/operations", api_operations, methods=["GET"])],
    csp="strict",
)
```

`GET /focus` serves the plugin page under a strict `script-src 'self' 'sha256-…'`
header; `GET /sessions` and other unmounted routes return `404`. For custom
hosts that render the HTML themselves, `aiui.render_shell_html(request)`
returns `(html, script_hashes)` and `aiui.shell_csp_header(html)` formats the
full header (`connect-src 'self'` covers same-origin WebSockets; pass `extra=`
for any external host).

## Check it before you call it done

```bash
aiui doctor                   # warns when aiui is older than PyPI's latest
AIUI_NO_BROWSER=1 aiui run app.py --port 8765 &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/shell/manifest | python -c \
  "import json,sys; print(sorted(p['id'] for p in json.load(sys.stdin)['pages']))"
```

The list must hold only your page ids (and `chat`). Then open the page in a
headless browser and look at the sidebar.

## The legacy dashboard

`style: dashboard` is the old vanilla UI. It still works
(`aiui run app.py --style dashboard`, `aiui.set_style("dashboard")`, YAML
`style: dashboard` or `AIUI_SHELL=legacy`, which prints a one-line notice),
and `set_pages` applies there too, but new apps should not use it. Docs and
examples that pass `--style dashboard` describe the legacy UI.

# Step-by-Step Quickstart

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/quickstart

> Build and run your first interactive A2UI surface in PraisonAIUI step by step.

Follow these five steps to go from zero to a live, interactive A2UI workspace.

## Step 1 — Install PraisonAIUI

```bash
pip install aiui
```

If you want PraisonAI agents to generate A2UI surfaces via tool calls, also install the optional agent SDK:

```bash
pip install "praisonaiagents[a2ui]"
```

## Step 2 — Create your first A2UI app

Save this as `app.py`. It enables the split **Chat + Canvas** view, a full-page **Canvas**, and a custom **Agent Canvas** page backed by surface `"main"`:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_branding(title="My A2UI App")
aiui.set_chat_preview(enabled=True, surface_id="main", width="40%")
aiui.set_pages(["chat-canvas", "chat", "canvas", "agent-canvas"])

def build_card(clicks: int = 0) -> list[dict]:
    return aiui.a2ui_surface(
        surface_id="main",
        theme={"primaryColor": "#2563eb"},
        components=[
            {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["title", "count", "btn"]},
            {"id": "title", "component": "Text", "text": "Hello from A2UI!", "variant": "h2"},
            {"id": "count", "component": "Text", "text": {"path": "/label"}},
            {"id": "btn-text", "component": "Text", "text": "Increment"},
            {
                "id": "btn",
                "component": "Button",
                "child": "btn-text",
                "variant": "primary",
                "action": {"event": {"name": "inc", "context": {}}},
            },
        ],
        data={"clicks": clicks, "label": f"Button clicked {clicks} time(s)."},
    )

state = {"clicks": 0}

@aiui.page("agent-canvas", title="Agent Canvas", group="A2UI")
async def agent_canvas():
    return {"_surface": {"id": "main", "messages": build_card(state["clicks"])}}

@aiui.surface_action("main")
async def on_action(action: dict):
    if action.get("action") == "inc":
        state["clicks"] += 1
        await aiui.push_surface("main", build_card(state["clicks"]), replace=True)
    return {"clicks": state["clicks"]}
```

## Step 3 — Run the server

```bash
aiui run app.py
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000` and switch between **Chat + Canvas**, **Canvas**, and **Agent Canvas**. Click **Increment** to watch the surface update live over WebSocket.

## Step 4 — Push updates from the CLI (JSON or JSONL)

Save a JSONL file `hello.jsonl`:

```json
{"version":"v0.9","createSurface":{"surfaceId":"main","catalogId":"basic"}}
{"version":"v0.9","updateComponents":{"surfaceId":"main","components":[{"id":"root","component":"Text","text":{"path":"/msg"},"variant":"h1"}]}}
{"version":"v0.9","updateDataModel":{"surfaceId":"main","path":"/","value":{"msg":"Pushed live from CLI!"}}}
```

Push it to your running server:

```bash
aiui surface push main --file hello.jsonl --replace
aiui surface capabilities
```

## Step 5 — Let an AI agent drive the canvas

Wrap `send_a2ui_messages` with `coerce_a2ui_tool_messages` so any LLM output shape (JSON, JSONL, v0.8, or v0.9) is normalized automatically:

```python
from praisonaiagents import Agent
from praisonaiagents.tools.a2ui_tools import send_a2ui_messages as sdk_send
from praisonaiagents.tools.decorator import tool
from praisonaiui.a2ui_utils import coerce_a2ui_tool_messages

@tool
def send_a2ui_messages(messages):
    """Push A2UI v0.9 messages to the live canvas."""
    return sdk_send(messages=coerce_a2ui_tool_messages(messages, surface_id="main"))

aiui.register_agent(
    "ui-builder",
    Agent(name="ui-builder", instructions="Always call send_a2ui_messages to render UI.", tools=[send_a2ui_messages]),
)
```

Next: explore all **[18 Basic Catalog Components & 14 Functions](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/components.md)**.
