
```bash uv
uv pip install aiui
```

## Cards

`<Card>` is a tile with a title, an optional `icon` and an optional `href`
(a page like `quickstart.md`, or any URL); with a link the whole card is
clickable. `<CardGroup cols={2}>` lays cards out in 1 to 4 columns (one on
phones).

```markdown
<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Quick start" icon="rocket" href="../getting-started/quickstart.md">
A chat app in five minutes.
</Card>
<Card title="Layouts" icon="panels-top-left" href="layouts.md">
Five frames for the same app.
</Card>
</CardGroup>
```

- [Quick start](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md)
  A chat app in five minutes.
- [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md)
  Five frames for the same app.

`icon` takes any [icon](#icons). A list whose items start with bold text
also becomes a grid of plain cards.

Card options:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `horizontal` | Icon beside the title, one compact row. |
| `img="images/x.png"` | A header image across the top (relative paths resolve like Markdown images). |
| `cta="Read the guide"` | A call-to-action line with an arrow at the bottom. |
| `arrow` / `arrow={false}` | A link arrow in the corner (on by default for links that leave the site). |
| `color="#0f766e"` | The icon's colour (a hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` or colour name). |

```markdown
<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Quick start" icon="rocket" horizontal color="#0f766e" href="../getting-started/quickstart.md" />
<Card title="Themes" img="../images/theme-comparison.png" cta="Pick a theme" href="theming.md">
Light, dark and the presets side by side.
</Card>
</CardGroup>
```

- [Quick start](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md)
- [Themes](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md)
  Light, dark and the presets side by side.

## Columns

`<Columns cols={2}>` lays any content side by side, one `<Column>` per cell,
in 1 to 4 columns; on phones the columns stack.

```markdown
<Columns cols={2}>
<Column>
**Python**: `pip install aiui`
</Column>
<Column>
**From source**: `pip install -e ".[dev]"`
</Column>
</Columns>
```

**Python**: `pip install aiui`
**From source**: `pip install -e ".[dev]"`

## Icons

Every `icon` (frontmatter, a navigation group, `<Card>`, `<Callout>`,
`<Step>`, `<Tab>`, `<Accordion>`, `<Badge>`, `<Prompt>`) and the `<Icon>` tag
take the same values:

- any [lucide icon](https://lucide.dev/icons) name, case-insensitive (`flag`,
  `git-branch`, or an old name such as `home`);
- an emoji (`icon="🚀"`);
- an image URL: `https://…` or a site path such as `/icons/logo.svg`.

`<Icon>` puts one inside a sentence: `size` in pixels (default: the text's
size) and `color` (a hex, `rgb()`, a colour name or a theme token).

```markdown
Ship it <Icon icon="flag" size={20} color="#0f766e" />, go <Icon icon="house" /> or <Icon icon="🚀" />.
```

Ship it , go  or 🚀.

The most used icons are drawn at once. Any other lucide icon loads on demand
from one of 32 small files (about 4 kB each), so a page downloads only the
icons it shows and no page gets heavier for the 1,900 icons on offer.
`aiui validate` warns (7009) about an icon name that is not lucide's, with the
nearest name.

## More components

```markdown
<Callout icon="rocket" color="#0f766e">Any colour: a hex, rgb()/hsl()/oklch() or a theme token (`success`).</Callout>

Status <Badge color="green" shape="pill">New</Badge>, see the <Tooltip tip="Software Development Kit" cta="Set up" href="sdk.md">SDK</Tooltip>.

<Tree>
- app/
  - layout.tsx
  - **page.tsx**
- package.json
</Tree>

<Prompt description="Write **clear** docs." actions={["copy", "claude", "cursor"]}>
You are a technical writer. Use the second person.
</Prompt>

<Columns cols={2}>
<Tile href="quickstart.md" title="Quick **start**" description="Five minutes">![Preview](../images/x.png)</Tile>
</Columns>

<Color variant="table">
<Color.Row title="Brand">
<Color.Item name="accent" value={{ light: "#0f766e", dark: "#5eead4" }} />
</Color.Row>
</Color>
```

- `<Callout>`: `icon` (any [icon](#icons)), `color`, `title`.
- `<Badge>` (inside a sentence): `color` (`gray`, `blue`, `green`, `yellow`, `orange`, `red`, `purple`, or a token), `size` (`xs` to `lg`), `shape="pill"`, `icon`, `stroke`, `disabled`.
- `<Tooltip>`: `tip`, `headline`, `cta` + `href`. It opens on hover or keyboard focus; Escape closes it.
- `<Tree>` (or `<FileTree>`) around a Markdown list, which reads on GitHub too: an item ending in `/` or with items under it is a folder (open), `**name**` is highlighted. The MDX form `<Tree.Folder name defaultOpen openable={false} highlight>` / `<Tree.File name highlight />` works as well; arrow keys move between rows, Right / Left open and close.
- `<Prompt>`: `description` (Markdown), `icon`, `actions` from `copy`, `chatgpt`, `claude`, `cursor` (default: the first three). The prompt folds under "Show prompt"; Copy and the links carry it exactly as written.
- `<Tile>`: `href`, `title` (Markdown), `description`; the body is the preview.
- `<Color variant="compact|table">`: `<Color.Item name value>` (one colour or `{{ light, dark }}`; a click copies it), grouped by `<Color.Row title>` in a table.
- Table column widths: `<colgroup><col width="30%"><col width="70%"></colgroup>` in an HTML `<table>`.

## API fields

Document an endpoint's parameters and response with field rows. Each row
shows the name, its type, where it goes, `required` and `deprecated`, and
its default, then the description (any Markdown). For Python code, a
`::: mypkg.module` line writes these rows from the docstrings
([Python API reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/api-reference-python.md)).

`<ParamField>` names the parameter by where it goes: `path`, `query`,
`body` or `header`. `<ResponseField name>` is a field of the response.
Both take `type` (any text: `string`, `string[]`, `object`, `User | null`),
`required`, `deprecated`, `default`, and `pre` / `post`: labels shown before
or after the name (`pre={["beta"]}`, or `pre="beta, internal"`).
`placeholder` is accepted for API playgrounds and not shown.

Every row has its own link: `#param-user_id`, `#response-next_cursor`, and
for a nested field the path from its parent (`#response-user-address`). The
name is that link, and opening it opens the `<Expandable>` around the field.
`id="…"` sets the link yourself.

```markdown
<ParamField path="user_id" type="string" required>
The user to fetch.
</ParamField>

<ParamField query="tags" type="string[]" default="all" pre={["beta"]}>
Only users with these tags.
</ParamField>

<ResponseField name="user" type="object" required>
  The user.
  <Expandable title="user properties">
    <ResponseField name="name" type="string">Display name.</ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="email" type="string" deprecated>Use `emails`.</ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ResponseField>
```

- `user_id` (path, string, required): The user to fetch.

- `tags` (query, string[], default: all): Only users with these tags.

- `user` (object, required): The user.
  - `name` (string): Display name.
  - `email` (string, deprecated): Use `emails`.

`<Expandable title="…">` folds nested properties behind "Show …" (default
"Show properties"); `defaultOpen` starts it open. Nest them as deep as the
object goes.

### Request and response examples

`<RequestExample>` and `<ResponseExample>` hold code fences, labelled like a
[code group](#code-groups) (several fences become tabs; `dropdown` picks one
from a menu instead). They leave the article: on wide screens they stay in
view in a column on the right, in place of "On this page"; on phones they
follow the article. `<Panel>` puts anything else in that column.

`````markdown
<RequestExample>

```bash cURL
curl https://api.example.com/v1/users/42
```

```python Python
client.users.get("42")
```

</RequestExample>

<ResponseExample dropdown>

```json 200
{ "user": { "name": "Ada" } }
```

```json 404
{ "error": "not_found" }
```

</ResponseExample>

<Panel>
Rate limit: 10 requests a second per key.
</Panel>
`````

Put each on lines of its own, outside list items (a `<Panel>` inside a list
item stays where it is). This page has none, so it keeps its "On this page".

## Reusable snippets and variables

Write a block once and use it on many pages. Put it in `docs/snippets/` (that
folder is never published as pages) and include it where it should appear:

````markdown
<Snippet file="install.md" pkg="aiui" />
````

`docs/snippets/install.md`, where `{pkg}` takes the value passed in:

````markdown
```bash
pip install {pkg}
```
````

Site-wide values go in one key of `aiui.yaml`, and `{{name}}` in any page or
snippet becomes the value, in text, code and front matter (`title`,
`description`):

```yaml
variables:
  productName: Acme
  version: 2.1.0
```

```markdown
---
title: "{{productName}} quickstart"
---
Install {{productName}} {{version}} with `pip install acme=={{version}}`.
```

- Snippets nest, and take any number of props. A path is looked up next to
  the page, then in `docs/snippets/`, then the docs folder; `/x.md` starts at
  the docs folder. Indent the tag inside a list item and the snippet follows
  the indent.
- Existing MDX snippet syntax works too: `import Install from '/snippets/install.mdx'`
  then `<Install pkg="aiui" />`. From MkDocs: `--8<-- "install.md"` on
  a line of its own.
- Write `\{{name}}` for a literal `{{name}}`. A snippet tag in a code block
  stays as written.
- It all happens in `aiui build`, so the page, its `.md` copy, `llms-full.txt`
  and search all hold the expanded text. A missing snippet, a path outside the
  project folder, or a snippet that includes itself fails the build (7008), and
  `aiui validate` names each `{{name}}` that has no value (7007).
- To publish a docs folder that is really called `snippets`, add
  `"!snippets"` to `content.docs.exclude`.

## Changelog

A changelog page is a list of `<Update>` entries, newest first. Add
`rss: true` and readers can subscribe:

```markdown
---
title: Changelog
rss: true
---

<Update label="2026-11-18" description="v1.2" tags={["API", "Fix"]}>
Builds are twice as fast. See [the guide](guide.md).
</Update>

<Update label="2026-11-02" description="v1.1" tags={["Docs"]}>
New quickstart.
</Update>
```

- `label` (a date or version) is the entry's section heading: it gets an
  anchor (`#2026-11-18`, or `id="…"`), a copy-link icon, a line in "On this
  page" and its own result in site search. From 768px wide it sits in a left
  column that stays in view while the entry scrolls.
- `description` shows under the label, `tags` (`{["A", "B"]}` or `"A, B"`) as
  chips.
- A page with tagged entries gets a tag filter above the first entry. Choosing
  tags shows the entries with any of them and keeps the choice in the address
  (`?tags=API,Fix`), so a filtered view is a link you can share.
- `rss: true`: `aiui build` writes `<page>/rss.xml` (RSS 2.0, one item per
  entry: the label and description as its title, the entry's anchor as its
  link, its tags as categories and its body as HTML; a label that is a date,
  such as `2026-11-18` or `November 18, 2026`, becomes its date). The page's
  head gets `<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">`, so browsers
  and feed readers find it, and the filter row shows an "RSS feed" link. Links
  are absolute when the site URL is known (`seo.siteUrl` or a `CNAME` file),
  base path included.
- The entries are `## label` sections in the page's `.md` and `llms-full.txt`.

## Component tags

Tags work the way MDX reads them: on lines of their own, on one line with
their text, inside a list item (indent the tag with the item's text), or
self-closing (`<Card title="Docs" href="index.md" />`). Attributes take quotes
or braces (`cols={3}`) and may run over several lines. A body indented under
its tag is text, not code, as in MDX.

```markdown
1. Install the package.
   <Warning>Use Python 3.10 or newer.</Warning>
2. Run `aiui build`.
```

A tag the site does not know (say `<Gadget>`) keeps its
text as plain Markdown, and `aiui build` and `aiui validate` name it:
`Warning: docs/guide.md:12: <Gadget> is not a docs component; its content shows as plain Markdown`.

`<Visibility for="humans">` / `for="agents"` shows its content only on the page /
only to agents ([AI-ready docs](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#content-for-people-or-for-agents-only)).

## Your own components

Write a React component once and use it on any page as a tag. Point the site
at one ES module beside `aiui.yaml`:

```yaml
site:
  components: ./components/index.js
```

The module registers each component with `registerBlock` from `@aiui/sdk`, or
exports it under the tag's name. It imports React and the SDK as bare names:
the build maps them to the page's own copies, so no bundler is needed for
plain JS, and hooks work.

```js
// components/index.js
import { useState } from 'react'
import { jsx, jsxs } from 'react/jsx-runtime'
import { registerBlock } from '@aiui/sdk'

registerBlock('Counter', ({ start = 0, label, children }) => {
  const [n, setN] = useState(start)
  return jsxs('div', { children: [
    jsx('button', { onClick: () => setN(n + 1), children: `${label} ${n}` }),
    jsx('div', { children }),
  ] })
})

export function Price({ amount, plans }) {
  return jsx('strong', { children: `$${amount} (${plans.join(', ')})` })
}
```

```markdown
<Counter start={2} label="Clicks">
Try it: **click** the button.
</Counter>

Plans from <Price amount={9} plans={["pro", "team"]} /> a month.
```

- **Props.** A quoted attribute is a string; `{…}` is a value: a number, `true`
  or `false`, an array or an object (`{{ calls: 10 }}`, JSON or JS-style); a
  bare attribute (`<Counter compact />`) is `true`. The component gets them as
  props, and as `node.props` like any block.
- **Children.** The tag's body is Markdown, rendered and passed as `children`.
  A self-closing tag that shares its line with text sits inside the sentence.
- **Loading.** The module loads only on a page that uses one of its tags,
  after the page has painted; until then, and if the module fails or the
  component throws, the page shows the tag's body. A built-in tag name
  (`<Note>`, `<Card>`) keeps its built-in meaning.
- **Tags.** The build finds them in the module (`registerBlock('Name'` and
  `export function Name`). A minified bundle hides them: list them with
  `site.components: {src: ./components/index.js, tags: [Counter, Price]}`.
  Declared tags are not reported as unknown; a missing module, or one with no
  tag the build can find, is a 7021 warning.
- **Security.** The module is your site's own code, served from the site
  (`script-src 'self'`); the build adds the import map's hash to the
  [Content-Security-Policy](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-security-policy.md). Only same-site
  modules load. In the `.md` copy for agents the tag's body stays and the tag goes.
- **Styles.** Use the theme's CSS variables (`var(--primary)`), or add a
  stylesheet with `site.customCss`.

An installed [UI plugin](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md) whose `blocks()` include a type named
like a component (`HelloCard`) provides that tag too, with no config: when a
page uses a tag nothing else knows, the build asks the plugins and publishes
the plugin's static folder with the site.

## Comments

`` and `` never show on the page, in search or in
`llms-full.txt`; inside a code block they stay as written.

## Tables

| Key | What it sets | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` | colours (and for `paper`, the type) | `zinc` |
| `mode` | `light`, `dark` or `system` | `darkMode` |
| `radius` | corner radius, `none` to `xl` | `md` |

```markdown
| Key | What it sets | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` | colours | `zinc` |
```

A wide table scrolls inside its frame, never the page.

## Images

```markdown
![What the image shows, for readers who cannot see it](../images/tool-streaming.png)
```

Paths are relative to the page. Write the alt text as a sentence about what
the image shows; it is also what search engines and assistants read. Click
any image (or focus it and press Enter) to see it at full size, with **Copy
image** and **Download** buttons; Escape or a click elsewhere closes it. An
image inside a link opens the link instead, and `noZoom` turns zoom off for
one image:

```markdown
[![Status badge](../images/badge.png)](status.md)

<img src="../images/diagram.png" alt="The request flow" width="480" height="270" noZoom />
```

`width` and `height` on `<img>` set its size and reserve the space before it
loads, so the page does not jump.

### Light and dark images

Show one image in light mode and another in dark mode. They follow the site's
theme toggle, not only the system setting. Any of these forms works, so the
same Markdown also reads well on GitHub:

```markdown
![Dashboard](../images/dash-light.png#gh-light-mode-only)
![Dashboard](../images/dash-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

<img className="block dark:hidden" src="../images/dash-light.png" alt="Dashboard" />
<img className="hidden dark:block" src="../images/dash-dark.png" alt="Dashboard" />

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="../images/dash-dark.png" />
  <img src="../images/dash-light.png" alt="Dashboard" />
</picture>
```

## Videos

Paste a YouTube, Vimeo or Loom URL (watch, share or embed form) in an
`<iframe>`, or a video file in `<video>`:

```markdown
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" title="Product tour" width="560" height="315"></iframe>

<video autoPlay muted loop playsInline src="../videos/loop.mp4"></video>

<video controls poster="../images/clip.png">
  <source src="../videos/clip.webm" type="video/webm" />
</video>
```

- An embedded video shows a play button (with `poster`, if set) until the
  reader presses it: nothing loads from the provider before that, so a page
  of videos stays fast and sets no third-party cookies. YouTube plays from
  `youtube-nocookie.com`, Vimeo with Do Not Track; the player runs in a
  sandboxed frame. `width` and `height` set the shape (16:9 by default).
- An `<iframe>` from any other site shows as a link to it, never as a frame.
- `<video autoPlay>` always plays muted and inline, and readers who ask for
  reduced motion get the controls instead. Without `autoPlay` it shows
  controls.
- In the page's `.md` copy for assistants, each video is a link.

### Raw HTML

Pages may use plain HTML for layout and text (`<div>`, `<details>`,
`<kbd>`, `<sup>`, tables, `<img>`, `<picture>`), plus the `<iframe>` and
`<video>` above, styled with [utility classes](#styling-with-classes). Anything that could run code or send the reader's data
elsewhere is not rendered, so a page can never become a way to attack its
readers:

| You write | The reader sees | Instead |
|-----------|-----------------|---------|
| `<iframe>` from a site other than YouTube, Vimeo or Loom | a link to it | a link, or a screenshot with a link |
| `<script>` | nothing | `site.customJs` |
| `<style>`, `<link rel="stylesheet">` | nothing | `site.customCss` |
| `<form>`, `<audio>`, `<object>`, `<embed>` | nothing | a link |

`aiui validate` and `aiui build` name each one with its file and line
(finding 7019). HTML inside code fences and inline code is shown as code and
never flagged.

`<Frame>` sets an image on a mat, with an optional `caption` under it and a `hint` above
it (both Markdown, links included):

```markdown
<Frame caption="A tool call, then an approval the agent waits on.">
![A tool call row above the answer, then an approval card for pip install numpy](../images/tool-streaming.png)
</Frame>
```

![A tool call row (execute_command, Done in 0.3 s) above the answer, then an approval card for pip install numpy with Approve and Deny](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/images/tool-streaming.png)
*A tool call, then an approval the agent waits on.*

## Styling with classes

Add `className` (or `class`) to a component tag or to raw HTML to adjust one
block: its spacing, width, text, colour or layout. The classes use the site's
theme tokens, so they follow light and dark mode and any theme preset:

```markdown
<div className="grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<Card title="Install" href="install.md" className="bg-muted">Set up the CLI.</Card>
<Card title="Deploy" href="deploy.md">Ship your site.</Card>
</div>

<Note className="mt-8">Read this before you deploy.</Note>

<p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground text-center">Updated every release.</p>

<span className="dark:hidden">Shown in light mode.</span>
```

Only these classes work (`{a,b}` means either). Any other class is dropped,
and `aiui validate` and `aiui build` name it with its file and line, with the
nearest allowed class (finding 7022). Nothing on a page can move the site's
header, sidebar or search, or cover them, so there is no `fixed`, `absolute`,
`z-*` or arbitrary `[...]` value.

| Group | Classes |
|-------|---------|
| Display | `block`, `inline-block`, `inline`, `flex`, `inline-flex`, `grid`, `hidden` |
| Flex and grid | `flex-row`, `flex-col`, `flex-wrap`, `flex-1`, `flex-none`, `shrink-0`, `grid-cols-{1,2,3,4}`, `col-span-{2,3,full}`, `items-{start,center,end,baseline}`, `justify-{start,center,end,between}`, `self-{start,center,end}`, `gap{,-x,-y}-{0,1,2,3,4,6,8}` |
| Spacing | `m`, `mx`, `my`, `mt`, `mb`, `p`, `px`, `py`, `pt`, `pb` with `-{0,1,2,3,4,6,8,12}`; `mx-auto` |
| Size | `w-{full,auto,fit,1/2,1/3,2/3,1/4,3/4}`, `max-w-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl,2xl,full,prose}`, `h-auto`, `min-w-0`, `aspect-{video,square}`, `object-{cover,contain}` |
| Text | `text-{xs,sm,base,lg,xl,2xl,3xl}`, `font-{normal,medium,semibold,bold,mono}`, `text-{left,center,right}`, `italic`, `underline`, `no-underline`, `uppercase`, `truncate`, `whitespace-nowrap`, `break-words`, `leading-{tight,normal,relaxed}`, `tracking-{tight,wide}` |
| Colour (theme tokens) | `text-{foreground,muted-foreground,primary,primary-foreground,destructive,success,warning,info}`, `bg-{background,card,muted,accent,primary,secondary}`, `border-{border,primary}` |
| Borders | `border`, `border-0`, `border-2`, `border-t`, `border-b`, `border-dashed`, `rounded{,-none,-sm,-md,-lg,-xl,-full}` |
| Other | `overflow-hidden`, `overflow-x-auto`, `opacity-{50,75}` |
| Screen size | `sm:`, `md:` and `lg:` before a display class, `flex-row`, `flex-col`, `grid-cols-{1,2,3,4}`, `text-{left,center,right}` or `w-{full,1/2,1/3,2/3}` (from 640, 768 and 1024 px wide) |
| Dark mode | `dark:` before a display class: `dark:hidden`, `dark:block`, `dark:inline-block`, `dark:inline`, `dark:flex`, `dark:grid` |

- A class wins over the component's own look, so `<Note className="mt-8">`
  really moves the note.
- `style="…"` is always removed (finding 7022 names it). For anything the
  classes do not cover, write CSS in `site.customCss`.
- Your own components (`site.components`) receive `className` as a prop and
  decide what to do with it. `<Tab>` and `<Visibility>` take no classes.

## Search

Readers press <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd>) or the
search field. Search covers page titles, every `##` and `###` heading and all
the text under it, and a result opens the page at its section with the words
marked. It forgives typing: plurals and verb forms match ("themes",
"theming"), a word matches as you type it ("inst"), one typo in a longer word
still matches, and question words drop out ("how do I deploy"). Titles rank
first, then headings, then text, each BM25 style.

While the dialog is open the address bar carries the query, so a link such as
`/docs?q=api+keys` opens search filled in. On a site with header tabs
([Navigation](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md)), chips filter results by tab: search starts in
the reader's tab, and one row offers the other tabs' results when it has none.

```markdown
---
keywords: [login, sign in]   # found by these words, never shown (or "login, sign in")
boost: 2                     # rank higher within its tier (0.1 to 10)
searchable: false            # out of site search; sidebar and search engines keep it
---
```

A navigation group's `boost:` applies to its pages (a page's own wins).
Site settings (`search.provider` is ignored and `aiui validate` says so):

```yaml
search:
  prompt: "Search the handbook"   # placeholder (default "Search docs")
  maxResults: 10                  # 1 to 100 (default 24)
  enabled: false                  # turn search off
```

`aiui build` writes the index (`search-index.json`, up to 6,000 characters
per section) and the same index in parts under `search-index/`, so the dialog
downloads only what a query needs:

| Part | Holds | Fetched |
|---|---|---|
| `search-index/meta.json` | each page's path, keywords, boost and section headings with their word counts, and the sorted list of every word | the first time a reader opens search |
| `search-index/<key>/w<n>.json` | for a run of those words, the sections each appears in and how often | when a query has a word in that run (by stem, prefix or one typo) |
| `search-index/<key>/p<i>.json` | page `i`'s section text | when the page is in the results, for its snippets |

Ranking is the same as over the whole file: BM25, stems, prefixes, typos,
keywords, `boost` and the tab chips. On this repository's 99 searchable pages
the first open downloads 35 KB gzipped instead of 181 KB, and a first query
about 13 KB more. `<key>` is a hash of the index, so a page cached from an
older deploy never mixes parts; a missing part, or a site built before the
parts existed, makes the dialog read `search-index.json` whole, which every
other reader (the [MCP server](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#mcp-server), Ask AI, older
pages) still uses. A site with [sign-in](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/docs-auth.md) gets no parts: its
`search-index.json` is cut per reader.

## Links between pages

Link to another page by its file: `[Theming](theming.md)`. The build turns it
into the page's URL, so links work on GitHub and on the site.

A folder's `README.md` or `index.md` is served at the folder's URL
(`protocols/adp/README.md` at `/docs/protocols/adp`), and a number prefix is
dropped (`adr/0003-selectable-layouts.md` at `/docs/adr/selectable-layouts`).
List such a page in the nav by its file path (`protocols/adp/README`); the
header still opens the tab that lists it.

## Check links

`aiui docs check-links` finds every link that leads nowhere, before readers do:

```bash
aiui docs check-links
```

```text
docs/guide/setup.md:11: instal.md: page not found (did you mean install.md?)
docs/guide/setup.md:12: ../index.md#nowhere: anchor #nowhere not found on /docs/index
✗ 2 broken of 40 links checked in 12 pages
```

It checks Markdown links and images, reference links, `href` and `src` on
components and HTML (`<Card href>`, `<a>`, `<img>`), the docs home `hero` and
`features` links, the nav page entries and the navbar and footer links in the
YAML. A `#section` link is checked against the ids the site gives its headings
(`## The aiui CLI` is `#the-aiui-cli`). Links in code are skipped. Paths outside
the docs (app routes such as `/chat`) are not judged.

`--external` also requests every `http(s)` URL, and `--json` prints the result
for scripts. The exit code is `1` when a link is broken, so a CI step needs one
line. `aiui validate --strict` and `aiui build --strict` fail on broken links
too; without `--strict` they print them as warnings.

## Page actions

Above every page's title, **Copy page** copies the page's Markdown, ready to
paste into an assistant. `Ctrl+C` (`⌘C` on a Mac) does the same when nothing
is selected and the cursor is not in a text field. Its menu also has:

| Action | Id | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Copy page | `copy` | The page's agent-ready Markdown on the clipboard |
| View as Markdown | `view` | Opens `/docs/<page>.md`, the page as plain Markdown for assistants |
| Download as PDF | `pdf` | The browser's Print dialog; pick **Save as PDF** |
| Listen to page | `listen` | The browser reads the article aloud, with pause and stop; hidden where the browser has no speech |
| Open in ChatGPT | `chatgpt` | A new ChatGPT chat that reads the page and takes questions |
| Open in Claude | `claude` | The same, in Claude |
| Copy MCP server URL, Connect to Cursor / VS Code | `mcp` | On a site `aiui serve` runs ([MCP server](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#mcp-server)) |

Nothing to configure: they use the Markdown `aiui build` already publishes.
Try it on this page.

To pick and order the actions, list them. Besides the ids above there are
`perplexity`, `grok`, `google` (Google AI Mode), `copilot`, `mistral` (Le Chat)
and `cursor`, and links of your own:

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    pageActions:
      - copy
      - chatgpt
      - perplexity
      - label: Ask our support bot
        href: https://support.acme.dev/new?q={prompt}
        icon: life-buoy                   # optional: a lucide name, an emoji or an image URL
        description: Opens a support chat # optional: the line under the label
```

In `href`, `{url}` is the page's address, `{md}` its Markdown, `{title}` its
title and `{prompt}` the "read this page" prompt the assistants get, each
URL-encoded. `pageActions: false` turns the menu off. One page can have its own
list, or none, in its front matter:

```yaml
---
title: Release notes
pageActions: [copy, view]   # or: pageActions: false
---
```

### Printing and PDF

A printed page (Download as PDF, or the browser's own Print, `Ctrl+P` / `⌘P`)
is the article alone, on light paper even when the reader uses dark mode:

- The header, sidebar, "On this page", page actions, previous / next, footer
  and feedback are left out. Breadcrumbs and "Last updated" stay.
- Everything a click would reveal is shown: accordions, `<Expandable>` field
  lists and file trees open, every tab of `<Tabs>` and `<CodeGroup>` prints
  under its own title, and `expandable` code blocks print every line.
- Code wraps instead of running off the page; code blocks, callouts, cards,
  steps, table rows and images are not split across pages.
- External links print their address after the link text:
  `link (https://example.com/docs)`.

Site chrome added by custom JS (`site.customJs`) or a plugin can opt out of
print with `data-print="hide"`. The PDF comes from the reader's browser: no
build step, no server-side renderer.

## Page footer

Under each page: "Was this page helpful?" (on by default, see
[Page feedback](#page-feedback)) and two optional parts, turned on in `aiui.yaml`:

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    editLink:
      pattern: "https://github.com/acme/site/edit/main/docs/:path"
    lastUpdated: true
    feedback:
      issues: "https://github.com/acme/site/issues/new"
```

- **Edit this page** links to `pattern` with `:path` replaced by the page's
  file under the docs folder (`getting-started/quickstart.md`).
- **Last updated** is the date of the last commit that changed the page.
  `aiui build` reads it from git. In a shallow clone, pages changed inside the
  cloned history keep their date; older ones get none rather than the clone's
  date. In GitHub Actions, check out with `fetch-depth: 0` to date every page.
  A page's `lastUpdatedDate: 2026-05-01` sets the date by hand, and
  `timestamp: false` (or `true`) turns it off (or on) for that page alone.
- **Was this page helpful?** keeps the vote (next section). With `issues`, a
  "No" also offers a new issue there with the page's title and address filled in.

The footer of this page shows all three.

### Related pages

Under each page, "Related pages" lists the three pages closest to it. Nothing to
configure: `aiui build` compares the words of every page (title, `keywords`,
description and headings count most, then the text) and favours pages in the
same sidebar group. Hidden, `noindex` and `searchable: false` pages and the home
page are never suggested. The list is part of `docs-nav.json`, so it works on any
static host and offline, and each page's [agent-ready `.md`](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md)
ends with it too.

Pick the list for a page in its front matter, or turn it off:

```yaml
---
related:
  - guides/setup                  # a page, by its path under the docs folder
  - ./deploy#docker               # relative to this page, with an anchor
  - Upgrade notes: guides/upgrade # a label of your own
  - https://example.com/blog/v2   # an external link (opens in a new tab)
---
```

`related: false` shows none on that page. Site-wide, `content.docs.related: 5`
shows five (at most 10) and `content.docs.related: false` only the lists pages
set themselves. `aiui validate` reports a target that is no page (7013). The
block is left out when the page prints.

### Page feedback

Nothing to configure: under `aiui serve` and `aiui dev` every docs page asks
"Was this page helpful?". A vote is stored at once; the reader can then add a
comment (up to 1,000 characters), which joins that vote. Read them with:

```bash
aiui docs feedback                            # votes per page, least helpful first
aiui docs feedback --format csv -o votes.csv  # every vote with its comment (or json; --site <title>)
```

Votes are lines of `docs-feedback/feedback.jsonl` in the data directory
(`$AIUI_DATA_DIR`, default `~/.praisonaiui`). `POST /api/docs/feedback` takes
same-origin requests only (plus `--cors-origins`, `AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`),
checks the Host header, takes 4 KiB and 20 posts a minute per client, and
stops at 20 MB. Nothing is readable over HTTP; the export is the CLI.
Agents report through the docs MCP server's `submit_feedback` tool into the
same store and limits ([MCP server](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#mcp-server)).

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    feedback:                       # false: no question at all
      issues: "https://github.com/acme/site/issues/new"  # a "No" also offers a new issue
      code: true                    # default false: a flag in each code block's corner
      endpoint: "https://hooks.example.com/docs-votes"  # default: the aiui server; false: none
```

A code flag is a `-1` vote with `kind: "code"` and `block`, the block's index
on the page, plus an optional comment. `aiui serve` and `aiui dev` say in the
`ui-config.json` they serve where they keep votes (`docsFeedback.url`); a
static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) serves the built file, which has no such
entry, so with no `endpoint` the page sends no request at all and the
question is shown only if `issues` is set.

`endpoint` receives the vote as JSON, sent as `text/plain` when it is on
another origin so the browser makes no preflight request: `{"id", "path",
"value", "kind", "block", "comment"}`. A comment arrives as a second post with
the same `id`. Every vote, wherever it goes, also fires a browser event your
own script can send to analytics:

```js
window.addEventListener('aiui:docs-feedback', (e) => console.log(e.detail.path, e.detail.value))
```

### Load telemetry

Off by default. Every docs page records how each of its requests went
(`aiui:docs-load` records: retries, time-outs, failures, timings). Turn on
telemetry and the page also sends the ones that went wrong, plus a sample of
the good timings, home, so a reader's stalled page shows up without anyone
watching that tab:

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    telemetry: true                 # aiui serve / aiui dev store the records
    # or, for a static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN), your own collector:
    # telemetry:
    #   endpoint: "https://collect.example.com/docs-load"
    #   sampleRate: 0.1             # share of good loads sent for timings (0-1); problems always
```

Read what `aiui serve` stored with:

```bash
aiui docs telemetry                              # per file: records, problems, reasons, p50 / p95 ms
aiui docs telemetry --outcome problems --since 24h
aiui docs telemetry --format json                # or csv; --site <title>
```

What is sent: the requested file, its kind (`doc` or `manifest`), the
attempt, the time it took, the outcome and reason, the HTTP status and the
page path. Query strings and fragments are dropped. No user or session id and
no user agent is sent, and the server stores no IP address or header. The
page collects records while it is open and sends them in batches of up to 50
with `navigator.sendBeacon` when it is hidden or left, so nothing is sent
while it loads. A post is JSON sent as `text/plain` (no preflight on another
origin): `{"v": 1, "records": [{"url", "kind", "attempt", "of", "ms",
"outcome", "reason", "status", "page", "sampled"}]}`.

With `telemetry: true` only `aiui serve` and `aiui dev` receive records: they
name `/api/docs/telemetry` in the `ui-config.json` they serve
(`docsTelemetry.url`). A static host serves the built file, which has no such
entry, so the page sends nothing and asks nothing. The endpoint takes
same-origin requests (plus `--cors-origins`, `AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`), checks
the Host header, takes 16 KiB and 30 posts a minute per client, and stops at
20 MB; on a site with [sign-in](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/docs-auth.md) it needs a signed-in reader.
Records are lines of `docs-telemetry/telemetry.jsonl` in the data directory
(`$AIUI_DATA_DIR`, default `~/.praisonaiui`). The pre-QA dashboard
(`tools/preqa`) shows them when that file exists.

## What the build publishes for assistants

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `/llms.txt` | every page with its description, by nav group ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org)) |
| `/llms-full.txt` | every page's agent-ready Markdown in one file |
| `/docs/<page>.md` | one page's agent-ready Markdown ([AI-ready docs](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md)) |
| `/docs/<page>.source.md` | the page source the site renders |
| `/search-index.json` | headings and text per page, for the site's own search |
| `/search-index/` | the same index in parts, fetched as a query needs them ([Search](#search)) |
| `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt` | for search engines |

Each page's HTML also carries that page's source (a JSON script,
`id="aiui-initial-doc"`), so the first visit renders without a second request
for it. Pages over 200 KB of Markdown are fetched as before. It also carries
`docs-nav.json` and `route-manifest.json` (`id="aiui-boot-data"`, each up to
100 KB; not the navigation of a site with sign-in) and preloads
`ui-config.json`; see
[Deploy to GitHub Pages → How pages load](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/github-pages.md#how-pages-load).

# Deploy to GitHub Pages

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/github-pages

> Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.

Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.

## Quick Start

### 1. Project Structure

```
my-project/
├── aiui.yaml    # Site configuration
├── docs/                 # Your markdown content
│   ├── index.md
│   └── guide.md
├── CNAME                 # Custom domain (optional)
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
        └── deploy.yml    # GitHub Actions workflow
```

### 2. Configuration

Create `aiui.yaml`:

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1

site:
  title: "My Docs"
  description: "Documentation for my project"
  ui: "shadcn"
  theme:
    preset: "zinc"
    darkMode: true

content:
  docs:
    dir: "./docs"
    include:
      - "**/*.md"

templates:
  docs:
    layout: "ThreeColumnLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "header_main" }
      left: { ref: "sidebar_docs" }
      main: { type: "DocContent" }
      footer: { ref: "footer_main" }

components:
  header_main:
    type: "Header"
    props:
      logoText: "My Docs"
  footer_main:
    type: "Footer"
    props:
      text: "© 2026"
  sidebar_docs:
    type: "DocsSidebar"
    props:
      source: "docs-nav"

routes:
  - match: "/docs/**"
    template: "docs"
```

### 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`:

```yaml
name: Deploy Docs

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: write
      pages: write
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install AIUI
        run: pip install aiui

      - name: Build
        run: |
          # auto: user.github.io/<repo> gets the /<repo> prefix; a CNAME or a
          # <user>.github.io repo is served at the root
          aiui build --output site --minify --base-path auto
          # Keep the custom domain, if there is one
          if [ -f CNAME ]; then cp CNAME site/CNAME; fi

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./site
```

### 4. Enable GitHub Pages

1. Go to **Settings → Pages** in your GitHub repo
2. Set **Source** to `Deploy from a branch`
3. Set **Branch** to `gh-pages` / `/ (root)`
4. Push to `main` — your site deploys automatically

## Project sites (no custom domain)

A repository other than `<user>.github.io` is published at
`https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/`, under a path prefix. `--base-path auto` in
the workflow above handles it: in GitHub Actions it reads the repository name,
so every asset, page, link, search and Markdown URL starts with `/<repo>`, and
the sitemap, `llms.txt` and canonical links use
`https://<user>.github.io/<repo>` as the site URL. Nothing else to configure,
and no custom domain needed.

`auto` builds for the root when the repository has a `CNAME` file, when the
repository is `<user>.github.io`, when `seo.siteUrl` is set (its path is the
prefix), and outside GitHub Actions. To set the prefix yourself:

```yaml
site:
  basePath: /my-repo        # or: aiui build --base-path /my-repo
```

The same works for any host that serves the site under a path, such as
`example.com/docs` behind a reverse proxy (`--base-path /docs`). Write links in
your Markdown as usual (`/docs/guide`, `../img/x.png`): the build and the app
add the prefix. Order of precedence: `--base-path`, then `site.basePath`, then
the path of `seo.siteUrl`. `--base-path /` builds for the root.

If you deploy with `actions/configure-pages` (Pages source "GitHub Actions"),
you can pass its output instead, which also knows a custom domain set in the
repository settings: `--base-path "${{ steps.pages.outputs.base_path }}"`.

Preview a prefixed build locally: `aiui serve --base-path /my-repo` serves it at
`http://127.0.0.1:8000/my-repo/` (and `aiui serve --no-build` serves an
existing build under the prefix it was built for).

Under a prefix, the legacy plugins that read the URL themselves
(`content-loader`, `homepage`, `topnav`) are not supported; the default
`nav-intercept` and `fetch-retry` are.

## Custom Domain

To use a custom domain (e.g., `docs.example.com`):

1. Create a `CNAME` file in your repo root:
   ```
   docs.example.com
   ```
2. Configure DNS — add a CNAME record pointing to `<username>.github.io`
3. The workflow above copies `CNAME` into the build output. The build also
   uses it as the site URL for the sitemap and canonical links.

## Migrating from MkDocs

| MkDocs | AIUI |
|--------|------|
| `mkdocs.yml` | `aiui.yaml` |
| `mkdocs build` → `./site/` | `aiui build --output site` → `./site/` |
| `mkdocs serve` | `aiui dev` |
| `pip install mkdocs-material` | `pip install aiui` |

What carries over from Material for MkDocs pages:

- Admonitions (`!!! note "Title"`, collapsible `???`), content tabs
  (`=== "Tab"` with 4-space indented content) and fenced code blocks render.
- `attr_list` (`{ .class }`) is not supported and shows as literal text;
  `:material-*:` icon shortcodes do not render as icons; raw HTML blocks are not
  styled. Remove them.
- The `nav:` list in `mkdocs.yml` is not read. Pages are ordered by the
  frontmatter `order` value, then a number prefix in the file name
  (`01-intro.md`), then the file name. See [Navigation](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md).

### Migration steps

1. Create `aiui.yaml` (see the example above) and run
   `aiui validate --strict`.
2. Replace `mkdocs build` with `aiui build --output site --minify` in your CI workflow.
3. Check the pages for the unsupported syntax listed above.
4. Push to `main`.

## Local preview

```bash
aiui dev     # build, serve on http://127.0.0.1:8000, reload the browser on save
```

See [Hot Reload](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/hot-reload.md).

## Build output

`aiui build --output site` produces:

```
site/
├── index.html           # single-page app entry
├── 404.html             # copy of index.html, so GitHub Pages serves deep links
├── .nojekyll            # tells GitHub Pages not to run Jekyll
├── assets/              # JS and CSS bundles
├── aiui-manifest.json   # list of hashed bundle chunks
├── ui-config.json       # site configuration manifest
├── docs-nav.json        # navigation tree
├── route-manifest.json  # route definitions
├── robots.txt
├── plugins/             # plugin-loader.js, plugins.json and the enabled legacy plugins
└── docs/
    ├── index.html       # one pre-rendered page per document (title, description)
    ├── index.md         # the Markdown source, loaded by the app
    └── ...
```

With a site URL (`seo.siteUrl`, or the `CNAME` file) the build also writes
`sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`; see [SEO](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/seo.md).

Everything is static, so GitHub Pages serves it directly.

## How pages load

Opening a page from the sidebar fetches its `.md` file. A reader on a lossy
network (Wi-Fi, VPN, a mobile link) sometimes gets one new connection that
hangs for 15 to 30 seconds while every other request is fast. The docs app
keeps one such request from freezing the page:

- **Time limit and retry.** Each request for a page has 3 seconds to get an
  answer from the server. Past that it is cancelled and a fresh request goes
  out, which opens a new connection. There are three attempts (3 s, 5 s, then
  8 s for a link that is only slow), with a short random pause between them.
  A network error or a 5xx answer is retried the same way; a 404 is not. From
  the second attempt the loading skeleton says "Taking longer than usual.
  Trying again (2 of 3)", so a slow page is never a silent skeleton.
- **Stalled downloads.** Once the answer starts, a page whose download sends
  nothing for 4 seconds has stalled and is requested again; one that keeps
  arriving, however slowly, gets up to 15 seconds.
- **No queueing behind another tab.** A browser lets one request per URL at a
  time fill its HTTP cache entry; a second request for the same file (from
  another tab, say) waits inside the browser until the first one is answered.
  Page Markdown, and every retry, is requested with `cache: 'no-store'`, so a
  stuck request elsewhere can never hold this page. The CDN still caches, and
  the app keeps pages it has loaded in memory.
- **`aiui:docs-load` records.** Every attempt's outcome is pushed to
  `window.__aiuiDocsLoad` (newest 200), sent as a `window` event
  `aiui:docs-load` and logged to the console (`console.warn` for retries and
  failures). A record is `{v: 1, type: 'aiui:docs-load', url, kind: 'doc' |
  'manifest', attempt, of, ms, outcome, reason?, status?, detail?, at}`, where
  `outcome` is `ok`, `retry`, `failed`, `inline`, `inline-mismatch` or
  `duplicate`, and `reason` is `headers-timeout`, `body-idle`, `body-timeout`,
  `network-error`, `http-5xx` or `network-change`.
- **A dead connection.** Every tab of a browser profile shares one HTTP/2
  connection per site. When it dies silently (the laptop slept, the Wi-Fi
  changed), requests on it wait until the browser notices, and only the
  browser decides when (its own ping and idle timeouts); a page cannot close
  it or pick another. What a page can do, it does: each attempt is cancelled
  at its time limit and a fresh request goes out, and when the browser comes
  back online or the tab becomes visible again while a request has waited
  half a second or more, that attempt ends at once (`network-change`) and a
  new request goes out on the browser's fresh connection, since browsers drop
  their pooled connections when the network changes. The last attempt is
  never cut short.
- **Prefetch.** Resting the pointer on a sidebar, previous / next or
  in-article docs link for 80 ms, focusing it with the keyboard, or pressing
  it starts loading that page. Once a page has shown, its previous and next
  pages load while the browser is idle.
- **Other spellings of a page URL.** A page's file URL (`/docs/x.html`,
  `/docs/x/index.html`) and a URL in the wrong letter case
  (`/docs/API/sessions`, which a static host answers with `404.html`) show
  the page and then move the address bar to the page's own URL
  (`history.replaceState`, so Back does not return to the old spelling). The
  docs home page's own URL is the site root: its sidebar link goes to `/`,
  never `/docs/index`. A wrong-case URL has no redirect file, because the
  spellings of a path are unbounded; when two pages differ only by case, such
  a URL shows "not found" rather than a guess.
- **Nothing optional delays `load`.** The page's `load` event waits for
  every request in flight. The previous / next prefetch, hover and focus
  prefetch, the GitHub star count and the opt-in telemetry chunk start only
  after `load`, when the browser is idle (`src/frontend/src/docs/afterLoad.ts`);
  a press on a link still loads its page at once.
- **In-memory cache.** A page loaded or prefetched once shows at once when you
  come back to it, without a request, until the tab is reloaded.
- **The last click wins.** Clicking another link cancels the request for the
  page you left, so fast clicking never builds a queue.
- **No long wait for the renderer.** A fetched page waits at most one second
  for the code highlighter and math renderer; after that the text shows and
  upgrades when they arrive.
- **Retry state.** When every attempt fails, the page says "Couldn't load this
  page" with a **Retry** button instead of a loading skeleton.
- **First load.** Every page `aiui build` writes carries the navigation
  (`docs-nav.json`), the route manifest and the page's own Markdown, so a first
  visit or a reload asks for none of them (`aiui build --strict` fails if a
  page's inlined Markdown is keyed by another URL than the app requests); `ui-config.json` is preloaded with the page (a
  live `aiui serve` adds Ask AI, MCP and feedback to it, so it is not baked in).
  The loader's tag names the plugins, so `plugins/plugins.json` is not
  requested either: on this site a first docs page went from five JSON requests
  and three plugin scripts to one and two. A file the page does not carry (a
  navigation over 100 KB, the navigation of a site with
  [sign-in](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/docs-auth.md), a page served without its content)
  loads with the same time limit and retries as a page. If it cannot load, the
  page says "Couldn't load the docs" with a **Retry** button instead of
  staying blank.

This site, https://ui.praison.ai, is built the same way: see
[`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml).
It deploys only when the built site changed: every deploy replaces the
branch and empties the CDN cache, so a merge that does not change the site
(tests, CI, Python code the docs do not show) publishes nothing.
`src/frontend/scripts/site-hash.mjs` hashes the fresh build (every path and
its bytes; a sitemap's `<lastmod>` dates are left out because they are file
times, the checkout time in CI) and writes `aiui-site-hash.txt` into it. The
workflow compares that with the file the last deploy published and skips the
deploy when they match. Run the workflow by hand with **force** to deploy
anyway.

```bash
node src/frontend/scripts/site-hash.mjs site --previous previous-hash.txt
# hash=<sha256>
# changed=true|false
```

## Legacy plugins

The docs app renders code (Shiki), mermaid diagrams, MkDocs tabs and
admonitions, "On this page" and the header tabs itself. By default a build
loads only one of the vanilla plugins in `plugins/`:

| Plugin | Why it loads |
|---|---|
| `nav-intercept` | Keeps in-article `/docs` links on in-app navigation (no full page load) |

`fetch-retry` (retry a failed request for the site manifests) is no longer in
the default list: the app reads the navigation and route manifest from the
page and fetches `ui-config.json` with its own time limit and retries, which
`fetch-retry` leaves alone. List it under `site.plugins` to keep it.

`mermaid`, `syntax-highlight`, `code-copy`, `toc`, `mkdocs-compat`,
`content-loader`, `homepage` and `topnav` no longer load by default: they skip
React docs pages, and `mermaid` and `syntax-highlight` fetched about 40 files
from cdn.jsdelivr.net and cdnjs.cloudflare.com on every page (each new origin
is another connection that can stall). A site can still list any of them under
`site.plugins` in `aiui.yaml`.

`index.html` loads `plugins/plugin-loader.js?v=<version>`, where the version
is a hash of the plugin files in the build (also in `plugins/plugins.json`),
and names the plugins on the same tag (`data-plugins`), so the loader does not
fetch `plugins.json` (a server's pages, which lack it, still do).
The loader imports every plugin with the same `?v=`, so browsers and the CDN
cache them until a build changes a plugin.

# Agent UI Overview

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/overview

> Build streaming AI agent interfaces in minutes with Python decorators or zero-code YAML.

PraisonAIUI gives any AI model or agent a polished, responsive agent interface without writing frontend code. Every app ships with streaming Markdown, tool calls, reasoning steps, approvals, code blocks, conversation history, light and dark themes, and mobile support out of the box.

## Two ways to build an agent app

Pick whichever matches how you work — you can switch or combine them at any time.

### Python (5 lines)

Use simple decorators in `app.py` to hook into any model, SDK, or custom logic:

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")
```

Run it with `aiui run app.py`.

### Zero-code YAML

Define an AI assistant without writing Python (`pip install "aiui[praisonai]"` and set `OPENAI_API_KEY`):

```yaml title="chat.yaml"
name: Support Assistant
instructions: You are a friendly product specialist. Keep answers short and clear.
model: gpt-4o-mini
welcome: "Hi! Ask me anything about getting started."
starters:
  - label: "Explain features"
    message: "What are the top 3 features?"
  - label: "Help me set up"
    message: "Walk me through the first setup step."
```

Run it with `aiui run chat.yaml`.

## What Agent UI includes out of the box

| Capability | What your users see | Learn more |
|------------|---------------------|------------|
| **Lifecycle hooks** | Greeting on open, per-chat setup, live Stop button, clean-up on exit | [Chat lifecycle](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/lifecycle.md) |
| **Streaming & prompts** | Token-by-token replies, interactive questions, action buttons and toasts | [Messages & streaming](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/messages-and-streaming.md) |
| **Starters & profiles** | One-click starter cards on empty chats and selectable assistant personas | [Starters & profiles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/starters-and-profiles.md) |
| **Reasoning & tool steps** | Collapsible, timed tree of tool calls, searches and sub-runs | [Steps](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/steps.md) |
| **Artifacts canvas** | Side-by-side preview for generated code, tables, diagrams and files | [A2UI canvas](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/a2ui-canvas.md) |
| **Attachments & media** | Drag-and-drop uploads, inline images, audio, video and downloadable files | [Attachments](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/attachments.md) |
| **Voice & MCP tools** | Spoken replies, real-time voice input and external MCP tool servers | [MCP servers](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/mcp.md) |

## Learn the core concepts in order

- [1. Chat lifecycle](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/lifecycle.md)
  Understand when welcome, start, reply, stop and end handlers run.
- [2. Messages & streaming](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/messages-and-streaming.md)
  Send replies, stream tokens, ask follow-up questions and show action buttons.
- [3. Starters & profiles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/starters-and-profiles.md)
  Guide new users with clickable prompt cards and switchable assistant modes.
- [4. Steps & reasoning](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/steps.md)
  Show live, collapsible tool calls and thinking steps inside every reply.

# Chat Lifecycle

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/lifecycle

> Understand every moment in a chat session — from the opening greeting to streaming replies, stopping and clean-up.

Every conversation follows a predictable sequence of events. You only need to write `@aiui.reply` to start; add the other decorators whenever you want custom greetings, per-chat setup, or clean-up.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Open["User opens chat"] --> Welcome["@aiui.welcome"]
    Welcome --> FirstMsg["First message sent"]
    FirstMsg --> Start["@aiui.on_chat_start"]
    Start --> Reply["@aiui.reply"]
    Reply -->|"User sends another"| Reply
    Reply -->|"User clicks Stop"| Cancel["@aiui.cancel"]
    Reply -->|"Browser closes"| End["@aiui.goodbye"]
```

## Lifecycle decorators at a glance

Every decorator works with both `async def` and plain `def`.

| Decorator | Alias | When it runs | Typical use |
|-----------|-------|--------------|-------------|
| `@aiui.welcome` | — | Once when an empty chat loads | Show a friendly greeting above starter cards |
| `@aiui.on_chat_start` | — | Once per chat, right before its first reply | Initialize per-chat memory, DB client, or agent |
| `@aiui.reply` | `@aiui.on_message` | Every time the user sends a message | Call your model, stream tokens, run tools |
| `@aiui.cancel` | `@aiui.on_stop` | When the user clicks **Stop** mid-reply | Log cancellation or clean up an external job |
| `@aiui.goodbye` | `@aiui.on_chat_end` | When the chat's last browser tab closes | Close database connections or temporary files |

> **Tip:**
> Annotate your `@aiui.reply` parameter as `str` (`async def on_message(text: str)`) to receive plain text. Omit the annotation (or type it as `MessageContext`) when you also need `message.session_id`, `message.agent_name`, or `message.attachments`.

## Complete lifecycle example

Save this as `app.py` and run `aiui run app.py`:

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.welcome
async def greet():
    await aiui.say("Welcome! Ask a question or pick a starter below.")


@aiui.on_chat_start
async def setup():
    # Stored separately for each conversation
    aiui.user_session["history"] = []


@aiui.reply
async def handle(message):
    history = aiui.user_session.get("history", [])
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": message.text})

    reply_text = f"Message #{len(history)}: {message.text}"
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply_text})
    aiui.user_session["history"] = history

    await aiui.say(reply_text)


@aiui.cancel
async def on_stop():
    await aiui.notify("Generation stopped", type="info")


@aiui.goodbye
async def cleanup():
    aiui.user_session.pop("history", None)
```

## How errors and stops behave

- **Stopping a reply:** Pressing **Stop** cancels the running `@aiui.reply` task (`asyncio.CancelledError` at the next `await`), immediately halting slow model calls or tool loops.
- **Exceptions:** If `@aiui.reply` raises an error, the UI displays the error cleanly beneath anything already streamed and preserves it on reload.
- **Per-chat isolation:** `aiui.user_session` is scoped to the current chat session, so two users talking at the same time never overwrite each other's state. See [Handler context](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/handler-context.md).

## Next steps

- [Messages & streaming](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/messages-and-streaming.md)
  Stream tokens, ask interactive follow-up questions and add clickable buttons.
- [Sessions & persistence](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/sessions.md)
  Save conversations to disk or SQL so users can resume later.

# Messages, Streaming & Interactions

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/messages-and-streaming

> Send complete replies, stream tokens live, ask the user follow-up questions, attach media and trigger clickable buttons.

Inside `@aiui.reply` (or `@aiui.on_chat_start`), PraisonAIUI gives you simple async functions to communicate with the user.

## Send or stream text

Use `aiui.say()` when you already have the full reply, or `aiui.stream_token()` to display tokens live as your AI model generates them.

```python title="app.py"
import asyncio
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    # Stream word by word (works with any LLM streaming iterator)
    for word in f"Here is a live streamed reply to: {message}".split():
        await aiui.stream_token(word + " ")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
```

Markdown — headings, tables, links, math, and syntax-highlighted code blocks — renders automatically as tokens arrive.

## Ask a question mid-reply

Pause the agent to ask the user for clarification or confirmation using `aiui.prompt()`. It waits for the user's answer and returns a result object (`answer.text` or `answer.choice`).

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    tone = await aiui.prompt(
        "Which tone would you like?",
        options=["Friendly", "Formal", "Concise"],
    )
    if tone:
        await aiui.say(f"Drafting a **{tone.choice}** response to: {message}")
```

## Add clickable action buttons

Show buttons below a message with `aiui.action_buttons()` and handle clicks with `@aiui.button("<name>")`:

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"Draft ready for: {message}")
    await aiui.action_buttons([
        {"name": "shorter", "label": "Make it shorter"},
        {"name": "polish", "label": "Polish tone"},
    ])


@aiui.button("shorter")
async def handle_shorter():
    await aiui.say("Here is a tighter one-sentence version.")
```

## Send interactive UI blocks inline

Render any of PraisonAIUI's **81 UI blocks** — metrics, searchable tables, pandas/Polars DataFrames, Plotly figures, charts, spreadsheets, whiteboards, cards, or `aiui.layout([...])` — directly inside a chat reply with `await aiui.send_block(...)`:

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"Live breakdown for **{message}**:")
    await aiui.send_block(
        aiui.columns([
            aiui.metric("Latency", value="42 ms", delta="-8%"),
            aiui.metric("Success Rate", value="99.4%", delta="+0.3%"),
        ])
    )
    await aiui.send_block(aiui.table([{"Region": "US", "Runs": 412}, {"Region": "EU", "Runs": 289}], searchable=True))
```

## Send media and notifications

| Helper | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `await aiui.send_block(block)` | Render any UI block, DataFrame, or Plotly figure inline | `await aiui.send_block(aiui.table(df, searchable=True))` |
| `await aiui.image(url, alt="")` | Display an inline image | `await aiui.image("/static/chart.png", "Sales chart")` |
| `await aiui.audio(url)` | Embed an audio player | `await aiui.audio("/static/briefing.mp3")` |
| `await aiui.video(url)` | Embed a video player | `await aiui.video("/static/demo.mp4")` |
| `await aiui.file(url, name="")` | Attach a downloadable file | `await aiui.file("/static/report.pdf", "report.pdf")` |
| `await aiui.notify(msg, type="info")` | Show a toast (pass `persist=True` to also save in the header bell) | `await aiui.notify("Saved!", type="success", persist=True)` |
| `await aiui.error(msg, details=...)` | Show a formatted error card | `await aiui.error("Request failed", details=str(exc))` |

> **Tip:**
> Want rich cards, tables, or side-by-side previews inside chat? See [Message elements](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/message-elements.md) and [A2UI canvas](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/a2ui-canvas.md).

# Starters, Profiles & Author Names

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/chat-ui/starters-and-profiles

> Help users start fast with clickable prompt suggestions, switchable assistant personas and friendly display names.

A blank chat box can feel intimidating. Starters show users what your assistant can do on the very first click, while profiles let them pick a specialized mode (such as **General**, **Code**, or **Writer**).

## Clickable conversation starters

Return a list of `{label, message}` items from `@aiui.starters`. They appear as cards on every empty conversation.

### Python

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.starters
def get_starters():
    return [
        {"label": "Summarize notes", "message": "Summarize my meeting notes into 3 bullet points."},
        {"label": "Draft an email", "message": "Help me write a short project update email."},
        {"label": "Explain a concept", "message": "Explain APIs in plain English."},
    ]


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"Working on: {message}")
```

### YAML

```yaml title="chat.yaml"
name: Team Assistant
model: gpt-4o-mini
welcome: "How can I help today?"
starters:
  - label: "Summarize notes"
    message: "Summarize my meeting notes into 3 bullet points."
  - label: "Draft an email"
    message: "Help me write a short project update email."
```

## Switchable chat profiles

Use `@aiui.profiles` to offer multiple personas or models in the UI. Inside `@aiui.reply`, inspect `message.agent_name` to route to the chosen profile.

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.profiles
def get_profiles():
    return [
        {"name": "General", "description": "Everyday answers and brainstorming"},
        {"name": "Writer", "description": "Polished emails, posts and docs"},
        {"name": "Analyst", "description": "Structured tables and comparisons"},
    ]


@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    mode = message.agent_name or "General"
    await aiui.say(f"[{mode}] Received: {message.text}")
```

## Customize author display names

When internal agent IDs look technical (like `support_triage_v2`), map them to friendly display names with `@aiui.author_rename`:

```python
@aiui.author_rename
def rename(name: str) -> str:
    return {
        "support_triage_v2": "Support Specialist",
        "billing_agent": "Billing Assistant",
    }.get(name, name)
```

## Collect user feedback

Turn on thumbs-up / thumbs-down buttons and log ratings with `@aiui.on("feedback")`:

```python
aiui.set_chat_features(feedback=True)


@aiui.on("feedback")
async def on_feedback(event):
    print(event["session_id"], event["message_id"], event["value"], event.get("comment"))
```

# Steps

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/steps

> A step is a named piece of work inside a reply: a tool call, an LLM call, a

A step is a named piece of work inside a reply: a tool call, an LLM call, a
retrieval, a sub-run. The chat shows the reply's steps as a collapsible tree
with each step's name, status (running, done, failed, stopped) and duration;
opening a step shows its input, output and child steps. Steps are saved with
the reply, so a reload shows the same tree with the same durations.

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

@aiui.step(type="tool")
def web_search(query: str):
    return f"3 results for {query}"

@aiui.reply
async def answer(message):
    async with aiui.Step("Plan", type="run") as plan:
        await plan.stream_token("Looking it up")   # streamed into the step's output
        results = web_search(message.text)          # the step "web_search", nested under "Plan"
    await aiui.say(f"Found: {results}")
```

**`@aiui.step`** works bare, with `()` or with arguments
(`@aiui.step("Search the web", type="tool")`), on sync and async functions. The
step is named after the function unless named; its input is the call's
arguments (`self`/`cls` left out), its output the return value, and an
exception marks it failed (and is raised as usual).

**`aiui.Step`** is used as `async with` or `with` (sync code and worker threads
too); in sync code `step.stream_token(t)` sends without `await`.

**Nesting** is automatic: a step opened while another runs becomes its child,
across `await`s, in tasks started from it (`asyncio.gather`, `create_task`) and
in `aiui.make_async` threads. `parent=` sets the parent explicitly.

## Reference

`aiui.Step(name, type="reasoning", parent=None, metadata={}, input=None, output=None)`

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | `run`, `tool`, `llm`, `embedding`, `retrieval`, `rerank`, `undefined`, `tool_call`, `reasoning`, `sub_agent`, `custom` |
| `input`, `output` | Shown when the step is opened; data as JSON, text as is, each at most 1 MB |
| `metadata` | Extra data sent with the step's start and end |
| `id`, `start`, `end`, `duration`, `status`, `error` | Read-only: epoch ms, seconds, `running`/`done`/`error`/`stopped`, the exception text |

`@aiui.step(name=None, type="reasoning", **metadata)` wraps each call in a `Step`.

**Events** (WebSocket and `/run` SSE, protocol 1.2), each with `step_id`:
`step_start` (`name`, `step_type`, `parent_id`, `start` in epoch ms, `input`),
`step_update` (`token` to append) and `step_end` (`end`, `status`, `duration`
in seconds, `error`, and `input`/`output` when changed). The saved reply keeps
`steps: [{step_id, parent_id, name, step_type, status, start, end, input,
output, error}]`. A step outside a reply sends nothing but still times itself.
`await aiui.think("...")` still shows unnamed reasoning text.

# Session Management

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/sessions

> PraisonAIUI provides full session management for chat conversations — create, switch, view history, and delete sessions.

PraisonAIUI provides full session management for chat conversations — create, switch, view history, and delete sessions.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Sessions persist by default (the praisonaiagents session store)
aiui run app.py

# Plain JSON files in ~/.praisonaiui/sessions/
aiui run app.py --datastore json
```

## Data Persistence Options

| Mode | Flag | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| SDK (default) | `--datastore sdk` | The praisonaiagents session store, shared with PraisonAI agents; falls back to `json` when `praisonaiagents` is not installed |
| SDK (custom path) | `--datastore sdk:/path/to/dir` | That directory |
| JSON files | `--datastore json` | `$AIUI_DATA_DIR/sessions/` (default `~/.praisonaiui/sessions/`) |
| JSON (custom path) | `--datastore json:/path/to/dir` | That directory |
| Memory | `--datastore memory` | Lost on restart; for tests |
| SQL | `aiui.set_datastore(aiui.SQLAlchemyDataStore(url))` | SQLite (`~/.praisonaiui/aiui.db` by default) or PostgreSQL; install `aiui[sql]` or `aiui[postgres]`. SQLAlchemy is imported only when this store first opens its database |
| Your own | Implement `BaseDataStore` | Your database |

## REST API

### List Sessions
```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions
```

### Create Session
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions
```

### Get Session Details
```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions/<session_id>
```

### Get Message History
```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions/<session_id>/runs
```

### Delete Session
```bash
curl -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions/<session_id>
```

### Send Message
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/run \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Hello", "session_id":"<session_id>"}'
```

## Where `aiui run` keeps chats

Each app has its own chat history. `aiui run app.py` stores the sessions of
that app file in
`~/.praisonaiui/apps/<file name>-<hash of its path>/sessions/` (under
`$AIUI_DATA_DIR` when it is set), so one app never lists the chats of
another app or agent on the machine, and nothing is written into the app's
own folder.

| You want | Run |
|---|---|
| This app's own history (default) | `aiui run app.py` |
| The history shared with every praisonai agent (`~/.praisonai/sessions/`, the old default) | `aiui run app.py --datastore sdk` |
| A folder you choose | `aiui run app.py --datastore sdk:/path` or `--datastore json:/path` |
| Nothing kept | `aiui run app.py --datastore memory` |

A YAML chat config (`aiui run chat.yaml`) keeps its `datastore:` key, and
without one uses the shared SDK store as before.

## CLI Commands

Every API endpoint has a CLI equivalent:

```bash
aiui sessions list                    # List all sessions
aiui sessions create                  # Create a new session
aiui sessions get <session_id>        # Get session details
aiui sessions messages <session_id>   # View message history
aiui sessions delete <session_id>     # Delete a session
aiui health-check                     # Server health check
```

Use `--server` to target a different server:
```bash
aiui sessions list --server http://localhost:3000
```

## Feedback

Chat thumbs up/down (`POST /api/feedback`, listed with totals by
`GET /api/feedback`) is kept by every store:

| Store | Where votes go |
|-------|----------------|
| SDK (default) | `feedback/feedback.jsonl` in the session folder (the app's own folder under `aiui run app.py`, else `~/.praisonai/sessions/`) |
| JSON files | `feedback/feedback.jsonl` in the session folder; an older `feedback.json` is moved into it on start |
| SQL | The `feedback` table |
| Memory | Memory (lost on restart) |
| Your own `BaseDataStore` | `$AIUI_DATA_DIR/feedback/feedback.jsonl` unless you override `record_feedback` and `list_feedback`, or `feedback_file()` to move the file |

The file stores append one JSON line per vote, so a vote never rewrites the
earlier ones. Turn the buttons off with `aiui.set_feedback_enabled(False)`.

## Thread Sharing

Create read-only share links for any conversation session with opaque 32-byte tokens. Access is **denied by default** until you register an access-control callback with `@aiui.on_shared_view` (alias `@aiui.on_shared_thread_view`):

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

@aiui.on_shared_view
async def allow_shared(thread_id: str, viewer) -> bool:
    # Return True to allow read-only viewing; viewer is a User or None (anonymous)
    return viewer is not None
```

| Endpoint | Method | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/threads/{thread_id}/share` | `POST` | Bearer token | Generate a share token and return `{"url": "...", "token": "..."}` |
| `/api/threads/{thread_id}/unshare` | `POST` | Bearer token | Revoke share tokens created by the caller for `thread_id` |
| `/shared/{token}` | `GET` | Optional | View a shared thread (read-only HTML, or JSON when `Accept: application/json` is sent); gated by `@aiui.on_shared_view` |

Python helpers exported on `praisonaiui`: `create_share_token(thread_id, created_by)`, `get_thread_by_share_token(token)`, `revoke_share_token(thread_id, user_id)`, `list_share_tokens(user_id)`, and `get_share_url(token, base_url="")`.

## Custom Data Store

Implement `BaseDataStore` for any database (SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB, etc.):

```python
from praisonaiui.datastore import BaseDataStore

class PostgresDataStore(BaseDataStore):
    # The six session/message methods are abstract; update_session, close,
    # count_sessions (len(list_sessions()) by default; override it when the
    # database can count) and the feedback methods have defaults (votes go
    # to a JSON-lines file; see Feedback above).
    def __init__(self, dsn: str):
        self.dsn = dsn
        # ... set up connection pool

    async def list_sessions(self) -> list[dict]:
        # SELECT id, created_at, updated_at, message_count FROM sessions
        ...

    async def get_session(self, session_id: str) -> dict | None:
        # SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE id = ?
        ...

    async def create_session(self, session_id: str = None) -> dict:
        # INSERT INTO sessions ...
        ...

    async def delete_session(self, session_id: str) -> bool:
        # DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ?
        ...

    async def add_message(self, session_id: str, message: dict) -> None:
        # INSERT INTO messages ...
        ...

    async def get_messages(self, session_id: str) -> list[dict]:
        # SELECT * FROM messages WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY timestamp
        ...

    async def close(self) -> None:
        # Close connection pool
        ...
```

Register before the server starts:

```python
# In your app.py:
import praisonaiui as aiui

store = PostgresDataStore("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/db")
aiui.set_datastore(store)
```

## Backend Modes

| Mode | Command | Session source |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Standalone (default) | `aiui run app.py` | The datastore above |
| PraisonAI | `aiui run app.py --backend praisonai` | The `WebSocketGateway` of the praisonai package |
