# Handler context

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/handler-context

> Inside an @aiui.reply (or @aiui.on_message) handler you can ask who is calling, keep state for

Inside an `@aiui.reply` (or `@aiui.on_message`) handler you can ask who is calling, keep state for
this chat, read the chat's history in the shape an LLM wants, pop a notice,
and call the UI from blocking worker code. Nothing to configure.

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

client = AsyncOpenAI()

@aiui.reply
async def answer(msg):
    session = aiui.context.session              # who, from where, which language
    aiui.user_session["turns"] = aiui.user_session.get("turns", 0) + 1

    reply = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=aiui.chat_context.to_openai(system=f"Answer in {session.language or 'en'}."),
    )
    await aiui.say(reply.choices[0].message.content)
    await aiui.notify("Answer ready", type="success")
```

Each API resolves to the chat being answered (two people chatting at once never
see each other's data), also in tasks the handler starts and `aiui.make_async` threads.

## `aiui.context.session`

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | The chat (session) id. |
| `user` | The signed-in user as a dict (`id`, `username`, extra fields; never the password hash), or `None`. `aiui.current_user()` returns the same dict. |
| `client_type` | `"webapp"` (a browser), `"api"` (a script or HTTP client), `"copilot"`, or the bot platform (`"slack"`, `"discord"`, `"teams"`, …). |
| `chat_profile` | The profile chosen for this chat, or the server-wide selection. |
| `chat_settings` | Settings sent with the chat (dict). |
| `env` | Per-chat values sent by the client (dict of strings). |
| `language` | The best tag of the caller's `Accept-Language` (`"fr-CA"`), or `None`. |
| `headers` | Request headers, lower-cased, with credentials removed (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, and any header whose name mentions a token, key, secret, password, auth or session). |

It is `None` outside a handler. A client names itself with `?client=<name>` on the chat WebSocket or an
`X-Aiui-Client: <name>` header (letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 32
characters). A chat turn (`{type: "chat", ...}` on `/api/chat/ws`, or the body
of `POST /api/chat/send`) may carry `chat_profile`, `chat_settings` and `env`;
they stay with the chat for its later turns.

## `aiui.user_session`

A key/value store private to the current chat, kept across its turns.

```python
aiui.user_session.set("plan", "pro")       # or aiui.user_session["plan"] = "pro"
plan = aiui.user_session.get("plan", "free")
```

Preset keys: `id`, `user`, `chat_profile`, `chat_settings`, `env`. Values live
in memory (the last 5,000 chats), so keep what must survive a restart in your
own database. Outside a handler `get` returns the default and `set` raises.

## `aiui.chat_context`

The chat's messages, oldest first, including the one being answered; each
finished reply is added. After a restart the saved history is reloaded from
the datastore. At most 200 messages are kept.

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `get()` | A copy of the messages: `[{"role", "content"}, ...]`. |
| `add(content, role="assistant")` | Append a message (a string with a role, or a `{"role", "content"}` dict). Roles: `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`. |
| `remove(message)` | Remove the latest message equal to `message`; returns `True` if one was removed. |
| `clear()` | Forget the history (for example on a "new topic" command). |
| `to_openai(system=None, max_messages=None)` | OpenAI chat messages, with an optional system prompt first and only the last `max_messages`. Works with any OpenAI-compatible client. |

## Blocking code: `aiui.make_async` and `aiui.run_sync`

Run blocking work in a thread so the chat stays responsive, and call the UI
from inside it:

```python
def slow_tool(query: str) -> str:
    aiui.run_sync(aiui.say(f"Searching for {query}..."))   # reaches this chat
    return search_index(query)

@aiui.reply
async def answer(msg):
    result = await aiui.make_async(slow_tool)(msg.text)
    await aiui.say(result)
```

`make_async(fn, executor=None)` runs `fn` on a thread pool (yours, if given)
with the handler's context. From that thread, `run_sync(coro, timeout=None)`
runs the coroutine on the server's loop and waits; in a plain script it starts
its own loop; in async code it raises `RuntimeError` (use `await`).

## Per-chat setup and clean-up

`@aiui.on_chat_start` runs once per chat before its first reply, as that chat,
so it is the place to fill `aiui.user_session`; `@aiui.on_chat_end` runs as the
chat when its last connection closes. See
[Chat lifecycle](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python.md#chat-lifecycle).

## `aiui.cache`

Load a model, an index or a client once and share it across every chat
(`@aiui.cache(ttl=3600, maxsize=8)` takes options; `async def` works too):

```python
@aiui.cache
def load_index(path: str):
    return build_index(path)          # runs once per path

@aiui.on_chat_start
async def start():
    aiui.user_session["index"] = load_index("docs/")
```

| Option | Does |
|---|---|
| `ttl=None` | Seconds an entry is kept; `None` keeps it until cleared. |
| `maxsize=None` | Keep only the most recently used entries; `None` for no limit. |
| `fn.cache_clear()` | Forget every entry. |

Entries are keyed by the arguments (unhashable ones, like a list, by their
`repr`) and live in the server's memory. It is thread-safe; concurrent first
calls share one computation (a caller cancelled by Stop does not cancel it).
Exceptions are never cached, so the next call tries again.

## `aiui.notify`

```python
await aiui.notify("Saved to your notes", type="success", duration=2000)
```

`type` is `info`, `success`, `warning` or `error`; `duration` is in
milliseconds. The notice is never saved with the reply or added to
`aiui.chat_context`. Clients receive `{type: "toast", session_id, run_id,
message, variant, duration?}` on the chat WebSocket; both built-in chats show
it as a toast. Returns `False` outside a handler. (`aiui.toast(...)`
builds a toast component for a page.)

# A2UI canvas — agent-driven UI

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/a2ui-canvas

> PraisonAIUI hosts A2UI (v0.8, v0.9, and v0.10) surfaces: agents push structured UI messages to a live canvas while users chat in the same window or on a full-pa

PraisonAIUI hosts **A2UI (v0.8, v0.9, and v0.10)** surfaces: agents push structured UI messages to a live canvas while users chat in the same window or on a full-page workspace.

> Looking for the full step-by-step guide? Start in the **[A2UI Overview](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/overview.md)**, **[Quickstart](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/quickstart.md)**, **[All 18 Components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/components.md)**, and **[All-in-One Playground](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/all-in-one-playground.md)**.

For dashboard extension patterns (views, plugins, layout JSON), see [Agent UI host](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agent-ui-host.md).

## Quick start

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("dashboard")
aiui.set_chat_preview(enabled=True, surface_id="main", width="38%")
aiui.set_pages(["chat-canvas", "chat", "canvas"])

@aiui.page("agent-canvas", title="Agent Canvas", icon="🖼️")
async def agent_canvas():
    return {"_surface": {"id": "main", "messages": []}}

@aiui.surface_action("main")
async def on_surface_action(action: dict):
    return {"received": action}
```

Run the full example: [`examples/python/30-a2ui-canvas/app.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/examples/python/30-a2ui-canvas/app.py).

## Dashboard pages

| Page id | Route | Purpose |
|---------|-------|---------|
| `chat-canvas` | `/chat-canvas` | Split view — chat left, live A2UI preview right |
| `chat` | `/chat` | Vanilla chat (unchanged) |
| `canvas` | `/canvas` | Full-page surface workspace |

Enable the split preview with [`set_chat_preview`](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python.md). Settings appear in `/ui-config.json` as `chat.preview: { enabled, surfaceId, width }`.

## Agent integration

Agents should call **`send_a2ui_messages`** (from `praisonaiagents.tools.a2ui_tools`) with A2UI message dicts:

```python
send_a2ui_messages(messages=[
    {"createSurface": {"surfaceId": "main", "catalogId": "basic"}},
    {"updateComponents": {"components": [
        {"component": "Text", "text": {"literal": "Hello"}},
        {"component": "Button", "text": {"literal": "Submit"},
         "action": {"name": "handleSubmit"}},
    ]}},
])
```

Wrap the tool with **`coerce_a2ui_tool_messages`** so common LLM argument shapes still work:

```python
from praisonaiui.a2ui_utils import coerce_a2ui_tool_messages

@tool
def send_a2ui_messages(messages):
    coerced = coerce_a2ui_tool_messages(messages, surface_id="main")
    return sdk_send_a2ui(messages=coerced)
```

`coerce_a2ui_tool_messages` accepts:

- A JSON string or list of message dicts
- A dict with a `messages` key
- A bare `components` list (wrapped in `updateComponents`)
- A single component dict (wrapped in `updateComponents`)
- Missing `createSurface` (inserted automatically for the given `surface_id`)

Tool results are detected by [`a2ui_utils`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/a2ui_utils.py) and ingested into the surface store; connected clients receive WebSocket `a2ui_surface` events.

## HTTP API

| Method | Path | Behaviour |
|--------|------|-----------|
| `GET` | `/api/surfaces` | List surfaces and message counts |
| `GET` | `/api/surfaces/capabilities` | Return A2UI supported versions, catalog IDs, 18 components, and 14 functions |
| `GET` | `/api/surfaces/{id}` | Surface state; **200 with `{ messages: [] }`** if not created yet (empty canvas is normal) |
| `POST` | `/api/surfaces/{id}/messages` | Append or replace messages (`replace: true` in body; accepts v0.8/v0.9/v0.10) |
| `POST` | `/api/surfaces/{id}/action` | User action from a button/component (`/actions` alias also supported) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/surfaces/{id}` | Clear surface |

Realtime updates use the existing dashboard WebSocket (`a2ui_surface` payload).

## CLI

Manage surfaces against a running server (`--server` / `AIUI_SERVER`, default `http://127.0.0.1:8000`):

```bash
aiui surface list
aiui surface get main
aiui surface get main --json
aiui surface push main --file messages.json
aiui surface push main --file messages.json --replace
aiui surface clear main
aiui surface status
```

`messages.json` must contain `{ "messages": [ ... ] }`.

## Frontend modules

Shared dashboard JS (lazy-loaded with `chat-canvas`):

| Module | Role |
|--------|------|
| `surface-utils.js` | Load surface, WebSocket sync, post actions |
| `canvas-preview.js` | Right-hand preview panel |
| `a2ui-mapper.js` | Default DOM mapper (Text, Button, Column, Row, Card, …) |
| `plugins/views/chat-canvas.js` | Composes chat + preview without modifying `chat.js` |

Override rendering: `window.aiui.registerSurfaceRenderer("main", fn)`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Chat works but canvas stays empty | Agent did not call `send_a2ui_messages` | Strengthen instructions; wrap tool with `coerce_a2ui_tool_messages` |
| Tool error / invalid JSON | LLM passed wrong shape | Use coercion wrapper; include schema prompt from `praisonaiagents.ui.a2ui.adapter` |
| Preview shows raw JSON | Component type not in `a2ui-mapper` | Extend mapper or use supported components |
| `GET /api/surfaces/main` empty | Normal before first push | Push via agent or `aiui surface push` |
| Button click does nothing | No `@aiui.surface_action` handler | Register handler for that `surface_id` |

## Related

- [Agent UI host](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agent-ui-host.md) — `registerSurfaceRenderer`, layout tiers
- [Python API — `set_chat_preview`](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python.md)
- [Python API — `@aiui.surface_action`](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python.md#aiuisurface_actionsurface_id)

# Message Elements

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/message-elements

> A message can carry elements: images, PDFs, videos, audio, files and code

A message can carry elements: images, PDFs, videos, audio, files and code
blocks shown with the message text. Each element is a dict with a `type`, the
fields below, and an optional `name` and `display`.

## Sending elements

These reach the chat as `message_element` events:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiui import Message

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    # One media item per call
    await aiui.image("https://example.com/chart.png", alt="Monthly sales")
    await aiui.file("https://example.com/data.csv", name="Data Export")

    # Or elements as dicts on a Message
    msg = Message("Check out this chart:")
    msg.elements = [
        {"type": "image", "url": "https://example.com/chart.png", "name": "Sales Chart"},
    ]
    await msg.send()
```

`aiui.audio(url)` and `aiui.video(url)` work the same way.

`msg.add_image()`, `add_pdf()`, `add_video()`, `add_audio()`, `add_file()`
and `add_code()` validate their arguments and append typed elements
(`ImageElement` and the others in `praisonaiui.schema.models`); they reach the
chat like dicts. So does any object with `model_dump()` or `to_dict()`.

## Several messages in one reply

Each `aiui.Message(...).send()` and each `aiui.say(...)` is its own message:
the chat shows it at once, as its own block under the same answer, with its
author when it is not the agent, and its elements and actions under it. A
reload shows the same blocks.

```python
@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    await aiui.Message(content="Looking that up...").send()
    chart = aiui.Message(content="Here is the chart:", author="Analyst")
    chart.add_image(url="https://example.com/chart.png", alt="Sales")
    await chart.send()

    answer = aiui.Message(content="")
    for token in ["The ", "total ", "is 42."]:
        await answer.stream_token(token)
    await answer.send()  # finalizes: the text is not repeated
```

Copy, feedback and Regenerate act on the whole answer. The saved reply keeps
`content` (the messages joined by a blank line) and `segments`
(`[{id, text, author?}]`); elements carry the `message_id` of their message.
`msg.update()` and `msg.remove()` change only that message while the reply
runs.

On the wire every piece of reply text names its message: `run_content`
carries `message_id` with a `token` (appended) or a whole `content` (sets that
message's text), plus `author` when set. `message_element` and
`message_actions` carry the same `message_id`; `message_update`,
`message_remove` and `action_remove` edit a message already shown.

The sections below list each element's fields.

## Element Types

### 1. Image Elements

Display images with thumbnail and click-to-zoom functionality.

```python
from praisonaiui import Message

msg = Message("Check out this chart:")
msg.add_image(
    url="https://example.com/chart.png",
    name="Sales Chart",
    alt="Monthly sales chart showing growth",
    display="inline"  # or "side", "page"
)
await msg.send()
```

**Properties:**
- `url` (required): Image URL
- `name` (optional): Display name
- `alt` (optional): Alt text for accessibility
- `display` (optional): Display mode - "inline" (default), "side", "page"
- `width` (optional): Fixed width in pixels
- `height` (optional): Fixed height in pixels

### 2. PDF Elements

Display PDF documents with inline viewer or link to open in new tab.

```python
msg.add_pdf(
    url="https://example.com/report.pdf",
    name="Quarterly Report",
    display="inline"  # Shows PDF viewer inline
)
```

**Properties:**
- `url` (required): PDF URL
- `name` (optional): Display name
- `display` (optional):
  - `"inline"`: Embedded PDF viewer (600px height)
  - `"side"`: Smaller embedded viewer (400px height)
  - `"page"`: Link to open in new tab

### 3. Video Elements

Display videos with native HTML5 video player.

```python
msg.add_video(
    url="https://example.com/demo.mp4",
    name="Product Demo",
    controls=True,  # Show video controls
    autoplay=False  # Don't autoplay
)
```

**Properties:**
- `url` (required): Video URL
- `name` (optional): Display name
- `controls` (optional): Show video controls (default: True)
- `autoplay` (optional): Auto-play video (default: False)
- `loop` (optional): Loop video (default: False)

### 4. Audio Elements

Display audio with native HTML5 audio player.

```python
msg.add_audio(
    url="https://example.com/clip.mp3",
    name="Audio Clip",
    controls=True
)
```

**Properties:**
- `url` (required): Audio URL
- `name` (optional): Display name
- `controls` (optional): Show audio controls (default: True)
- `autoplay` (optional): Auto-play audio (default: False)
- `loop` (optional): Loop audio (default: False)

### 5. File Elements

Display downloadable files with file type icons and size information.

```python
msg.add_file(
    url="https://example.com/data.csv",
    name="Data Export",
    size=1024000,  # Size in bytes
    mime_type="text/csv"
)
```

**Properties:**
- `url` (required): File download URL
- `name` (optional): Display name
- `size` (optional): File size in bytes
- `mime_type` (optional): MIME type for file type detection

### 6. Code Elements

Display syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy functionality.

```python
msg.add_code(
    content='print("Hello, World!")',
    language="python",
    name="Hello World Example"
)
```

**Properties:**
- `content` (required): Code content
- `language` (optional): Programming language for syntax highlighting
- `name` (optional): Display name

### 7. Interactive UI Blocks, DataFrames & Plotly Figures

Render any of the 81 built-in `aiui.*` UI blocks inline inside a chat message with `await aiui.send_block(...)`. It also accepts pandas/Polars DataFrames (converted to searchable `table` blocks), Plotly figures (converted to native Recharts `chart` blocks without bundling `plotly.js`), and `aiui.layout([...])`:

```python
@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    await aiui.send_block(aiui.metric("Active Runs", value=12, delta="+3"))
    await aiui.send_block(df)                   # pandas or Polars DataFrame -> searchable table
    await aiui.send_block(aiui.plotly_chart(fig))  # Plotly figure -> native Recharts chart
```

Legacy `DataframeElement` (`{"type": "dataframe", ...}`) and `PlotlyElement` (`{"type": "plotly", ...}`) elements sent on `Message.elements` render through the same lazy `BlockElement` renderer automatically.

## Display Modes

All elements support three display modes:

- **`inline`** (default): Full width, normal display
- **`side`**: Smaller size, suitable for sidebars
- **`page`**: Full page width, maximum size

## Size Limits

`add_file()` raises `ValueError` when `size` is over 100 MB and `add_code()`
when `content` is over 1 MB. Dict elements are not checked.

## Typed models

`praisonaiui.schema.models` has a model per type (`ImageElement`, `PdfElement`,
`VideoElement`, `AudioElement`, `FileElement`, `CodeElement`) that validates the
fields above:

```python
from praisonaiui.schema.models import ImageElement

element = ImageElement(url="https://example.com/image.png", alt="Description")
msg.elements.append(element.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
```

## Agent-generated images (streaming)

When an agent or tool **creates** an image during a chat run, the UI receives `message_element` events over WebSocket/SSE and renders them inline. This uses the same element dict shape as above but is driven by the [RunEvent protocol](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/providers.md), not only `Message.send()`.

See **[Image Preview in Chat](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/image-preview-chat.md)** for the full architecture: detection (`media_utils`), provider bridge, persistence, and swappable backends.

# Chat Attachments

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/attachments

> Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are

Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are
read into the agent's prompt, images go to the model as multimodal input. The
default limit is 10 MB per file.

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Upload a file
RESP=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/chat/attachments \
  -F "file=@report.pdf;type=application/pdf" \
  -F "session_id=my-session")

# 2. Send chat with the attachment
ATT_ID=$(echo $RESP | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['id'])")
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/chat/send \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"content\":\"Summarize this document\",\"session_id\":\"my-session\",\"attachment_ids\":[\"$ATT_ID\"]}"
```

The agent receives the extracted PDF text before the user message. The reply
streams to WebSocket clients (see [Gateway Chat](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/gateway-chat.md)).

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["File Upload"] --> B["AttachmentManager"]
    B --> C{"Size and type"}
    C -->|"OK"| D["Save to temp dir"]
    C -->|"Rejected"| E["400 Error"]
    D --> F["Return metadata + id"]
    F --> G["Send chat with attachment_ids"]
    G --> H{"Content type?"}
    H -->|"PDF"| I["Extract text via pypdf"]
    H -->|"Image"| J["Pass to multimodal LLM"]
    H -->|"Other"| K["Read file contents"]
    I --> L["Prepend to agent prompt"]
    K --> L
```

## File Processing by Type

| Content type | Processing | What the agent sees |
|--------------|------------|---------------------|
| `application/pdf` | Text extracted with `pypdf` (a dependency of `aiui`) | `--- Attached PDF: name ---` block before the message |
| `image/*` | File path passed to the agent's `attachments` | The image, for vision-capable models |
| Anything else allowed | File read as text | `--- Attached File: name ---` block before the message |

## Allowed Types & Upload Encodings

`POST /api/chat/attachments` accepts **three encodings** so uploads work out of the box even without `python-multipart`:

1. **Raw binary body** with `X-Filename` header and file `Content-Type` (what `aiui.file_upload()` sends).
2. **JSON body** (`{"filename", "content_type", "data_base64", "session_id?"}`).
3. **`multipart/form-data`** with a `file` field (when `python-multipart` is installed; returns HTTP `415` otherwise).

| Category | MIME types |
|----------|------------|
| Text & Markup | `text/plain`, `text/csv`, `text/tab-separated-values`, `text/markdown` (`text/x-markdown` normalized), `application/xml`, `text/xml` |
| Data & Office | `application/json`, `application/pdf`, `.xlsx` (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`), `.docx` (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`) |
| Images | `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` |
| Audio | `audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav`, `audio/webm`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/mp4` |

Common OS MIME quirks (such as Windows sending `application/vnd.ms-excel` for `.csv`, or `application/octet-stream` for known safe data/media extensions) are normalized safely. Active web types (`text/html`, `image/svg+xml`, `application/javascript`) are always rejected with `400 {"error": "Type not allowed: ..."}`. Files over the size limit return `413` / `400`.

Files are stored under `<tmp>/praisonai_attachments/` with sanitized UUID filenames, automatic TTL eviction (default `3600` seconds) and capacity eviction (default `500` entries). Internal filesystem `path` values are **never** returned in HTTP responses — resolve them server-side with `aiui.get_uploaded_file()`.

## Page File Uploads (`aiui.file_upload` & `aiui.get_uploaded_file`)

On `@aiui.page` and `aiui.interface()` forms, use `aiui.file_upload()` to render a drag-and-drop uploader and resolve the uploaded handle safely in Python:

```python
def inspect_csv(doc):
    # aiui.interface() resolves file_upload inputs automatically via aiui.get_uploaded_file()
    if not doc:
        return "Upload a CSV file first."
    with open(doc["path"], "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        return aiui.code_block(f.read(1200))

aiui.interface(
    inspect_csv,
    inputs=[aiui.file_upload("Drop a CSV", name="doc", accept=".csv,.txt")],
    title="CSV Inspector",
)
```

Inside a manual `@aiui.register_page_action` handler, always resolve client handles via `meta = aiui.get_uploaded_file(data.get("doc"))` — it validates UUID syntax and looks up the file in the server's registry, blocking path traversal and expired/forged handles.

## Indexing into Knowledge

Add `-F "index_to_knowledge=true"` to the upload to also store the file in the
knowledge base. The response then carries `knowledge_indexed` (and
`knowledge_error` when it failed).

## Custom Limits

`AttachmentManager(storage_dir=None, max_size_mb=10, allowed_types=None)` takes
the limits. The server creates its default instance with
`praisonaiui.features.attachments.get_attachment_manager()`; there is no public
setter for a custom one yet.

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/chat/attachments` | POST | Upload a file (multipart: `file`, optional `session_id`, `index_to_knowledge`) |
| `/api/chat/attachments/{session_id}` | GET | List a session's attachments |
| `/api/chat/attachments/{attachment_id}` | DELETE | Delete an attachment |
| `/api/chat/media/{attachment_id}` | GET | Serve a stored generated-media file |

### Upload

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/chat/attachments \
  -F "file=@data.csv;type=text/csv" \
  -F "session_id=abc-123"
```

Response:

```json
{
  "id": "0b6c1f0e-5f7e-4c0a-9d0b-2f1d9e1a7c11",
  "filename": "data.csv",
  "content_type": "text/csv",
  "size": 34800,
  "session_id": "abc-123"
}
```

### List

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/chat/attachments/abc-123
```

## WebSocket

Over the WebSocket, put `attachment_ids` in the chat frame:

```json
{
  "type": "chat",
  "content": "Analyze this PDF",
  "session_id": "abc-123",
  "attachment_ids": ["0b6c1f0e-5f7e-4c0a-9d0b-2f1d9e1a7c11"]
}
```

`POST /run` (the chat's HTTP fallback when the WebSocket cannot open) takes
the same `attachment_ids` and handles them the same way.

## In a `@reply` callback

Text and PDF files are put before the message text. Every file of the
message is also on `message.attachments`, so an app can read images itself:

```python
@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    for f in message.attachments:  # [{id, name, content_type, path}]
        if f["content_type"].startswith("image/"):
            await aiui.say(f"Got the image {f['name']}")
```

- [Gateway Chat](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/gateway-chat.md): the chat interface
- [Sessions](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/sessions.md): session management

# Image Preview in Chat

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/image-preview-chat

> Protocol-driven inline media for agent-generated images (and other element types) during chat streaming. Any backend that implements BaseProvider can emit image

Protocol-driven inline media for agent-generated images (and other element types) during chat streaming. Any backend that implements `BaseProvider` can emit images without PraisonAI-specific code in chat or the frontend.

## Problem This Solves

Before this feature, PraisonAIUI could **render** images (`Message.add_image`, `ElementRenderer`) but the **wire protocol dropped media** during agent runs. ImageAgent / tool results appeared as JSON in the tool-call panel instead of inline `<img>` previews.

## Architecture

Modular layers — same pattern as [A2UI surfaces](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agent-ui-host.md):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Backend as Provider_or_Tool
    participant Detect as media_utils.py
    participant Protocol as RunEvent_MESSAGE_ELEMENT
    participant Chat as chat.py
    participant UI as chat.js_React

    Backend->>Detect: tool result or callback payload
    Detect->>Protocol: normalised element dict
    Protocol->>Chat: broadcast message_element
    Chat->>UI: WebSocket / SSE frame
    UI->>UI: appendMediaElement / ElementRenderer
    Chat->>Chat: persist elements in session history
```

### Layer responsibilities

| Layer | Module | Backend-agnostic? |
|-------|--------|-------------------|
| **Detection** | [`media_utils.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/media_utils.py) | Yes — normalises OpenAI, URL, b64, element dicts |
| **Protocol** | [`provider.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/provider.py) — `RunEventType.MESSAGE_ELEMENT` | Yes |
| **Adapter** | [`providers/__init__.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/providers/__init__.py) — PraisonAI bridge only | No — maps SDK/callback queue → protocol |
| **Transport** | [`chat.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/features/chat.py) — broadcast + persist | Yes |
| **Storage** | [`attachments.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/features/attachments.py) — `GET /api/chat/media/{id}` | Yes — reuses attachment store for b64 |
| **UI** | [`chat.js`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js), [`ElementRenderer`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/frontend/src/chat-engine/parts/media/MultimediaElements.tsx) | Yes — renders `{type, url, alt}` |

Detection and UI do **not** import PraisonAI. Only the provider adapter knows ImageAgent / OpenAI `{data: [{url}]}` shapes.

## Wire protocol

### Event type

```
type: "message_element"
element: { "type": "image", "url": "...", "alt": "..." }
session_id: "..."
run_id: "..."
```

Defined in Python as `RunEventType.MESSAGE_ELEMENT` and mirrored in [`types.ts`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/frontend/src/types.ts).

### Helper (any provider)

```python
from praisonaiui.provider import BaseProvider, RunEvent, RunEventType

yield BaseProvider.message_element_event({
    "type": "image",
    "url": "https://example.com/out.png",
    "alt": "Generated image",
})
```

Element shape reuses the existing [message element schema](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/message-elements.md) (`image`, `pdf`, `video`, `audio`, `file`, `code`).

## Data flow paths

### 1. Custom provider (swappable backend)

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiui.provider import BaseProvider, RunEvent, RunEventType

class MyImageProvider(BaseProvider):
    async def run(self, message, *, session_id=None, agent_name=None, **kw):
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_STARTED)
        # Call any image API here (OpenAI, Stability, local, etc.)
        yield BaseProvider.message_element_event({
            "type": "image",
            "url": image_url,
            "alt": "Generated image",
        })
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_COMPLETED, content="Here is your image.")

aiui.set_provider(MyImageProvider())
```

Example app: [`examples/python/30-image-preview/app.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/examples/python/30-image-preview/app.py).

### 2. Callback handler (`@aiui.reply`)

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiui import Message

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(msg):
    m = Message(content="Here is your image:")
    m.add_image("https://example.com/chart.png", alt="Chart")
    await m.send()
```

`PraisonAIProvider` maps queue events (`image`, `message` + `elements`) → `MESSAGE_ELEMENT`.

### 3. Tool results (automatic detection)

When a tool completes, `tool_completed_extra()` in [`a2ui_utils.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/a2ui_utils.py) calls `build_media_extra()` from `media_utils`. Supported shapes:

| Input shape | Example |
|-------------|---------|
| OpenAI / ImageAgent | `{"data": [{"url": "...", "b64_json": "...", "revised_prompt": "..."}]}` |
| Explicit element | `{"type": "image", "url": "..."}` |
| Plain URL string | `"https://cdn.example.com/out.png"` |
| Data URL | `"data:image/png;base64,..."` |
| Nested elements | `{"elements": [{"type": "video", "url": "..."}]}` |

`chat.py` broadcasts `message_element` for each detected element and attaches `elements` to the persisted assistant message.

### 4. ImageAgent direct mode

If the registered agent's `chat()` returns an OpenAI-shaped dict, `PraisonAIProvider._run_direct_mode` runs `extract_media_elements()` and emits `MESSAGE_ELEMENT` events before `RUN_COMPLETED`.

## Base64 storage

Large `b64_json` payloads are **not** stored inline in message history. They are decoded and saved via `AttachmentManager`, then served at:

```
GET /api/chat/media/{attachment_id}
```

If storage fails, the system falls back to a `data:image/png;base64,...` URL.

## Frontend rendering

| Surface | Handler |
|---------|---------|
| Dashboard chat (template) | `chat.js` — `case 'message_element': appendMediaElement()` |
| React chat | `streamingStore.ts` — `pendingElements` + `ElementRenderer` |
| Tool call panel | Thumbnail from `toolCall.elements` when expanded |
| Session reload | `elements` on messages from `/api/chat/history` and `/sessions/{id}/runs` |

See also [Message Elements](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/message-elements.md) for element properties and display modes.

## Deduplication

`_collect_element()` in `chat.py` dedupes by URL so the same image is not stored twice when both a `MESSAGE_ELEMENT` event and a tool completion carry the same URL.

## Out of scope

- **REST image generation** (`POST /v1/images/generations`) — separate OpenAI-compat endpoint; not wired into chat streaming
- **Canvas / A2UI surfaces** — separate feature for agent-driven UI catalogs
- **Auto-registering ImageAgent** — agents are configured explicitly by the user

## Tests

```bash
pytest tests/unit/test_media_utils.py \
       tests/integration/test_chat_image_preview.py -v -o addopts=
```

Coverage includes: detection normalisation, b64 fallback, provider callback bridge, `_run_and_broadcast` persistence, media serve route, ImageAgent dict responses, URL dedup.

## Related docs

- [Providers](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/providers.md) — provider protocol and inline media snippet
- [Message Elements](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/message-elements.md) — element types and Python API
- [Attachments](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/attachments.md) — user file uploads (separate from generated media serve path)
- [Gateway Chat](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/gateway-chat.md) — WebSocket event flow

# Media Analysis

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/media-analysis

> The media analysis feature uses the VisionAgent and OCRAgent from the PraisonAI SDK when available. Without the SDK, it returns simulated responses to allow fro

**Image understanding, OCR, and object detection** powered by VisionAgent — analyze uploaded images and documents.

## Quick Start

```bash
# List analysis capabilities
curl http://localhost:8083/api/media/capabilities

# Analyze an image
curl -X POST http://localhost:8083/api/media/analyze \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/photo.jpg","prompt":"What is in this image?"}'

# Extract text (OCR)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8083/api/media/ocr \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/document.png"}'
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Image Input\n(URL or base64)"] --> B{"VisionAnalysisManager"}
    B --> C{"SDK Available?"}
    C -->|Yes| D["praisonaiagents\nVisionAgent / OCRAgent"]
    C -->|No| E["Simulated Mode\n(metadata only)"]
    D --> F["Image Description\nOCR Text\nObject Detection"]
```

The media analysis feature uses the **VisionAgent** and **OCRAgent** from the PraisonAI SDK when available. Without the SDK, it returns simulated responses to allow frontend development without API keys.

### Capabilities

| Capability | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `image_description` | Natural language description of image contents |
| `ocr` | Extract text from images and documents |
| `object_detection` | Identify objects in images |
| `image_qa` | Answer questions about image contents |

## Configuration

```python
from praisonaiui.features.media_analysis import VisionAnalysisManager, set_analysis_manager

# Default: auto-detects SDK availability
set_analysis_manager(VisionAnalysisManager())
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/media/analyze` | POST | Analyze an image |
| `/api/media/ocr` | POST | Extract text via OCR |
| `/api/media/capabilities` | GET | List analysis capabilities |

### POST /api/media/analyze

```json
// Request
{"url": "https://example.com/photo.jpg", "prompt": "What is in this image?"}
// or
{"base64_data": "iVBORw0KGgo...", "mime_type": "image/png"}

// Response (SDK available)
{"analysis": "The image shows a sunset over mountains...", "status": "success", "provider": "sdk"}

// Response (simulated)
{"analysis": "[Simulated] Image analysis for: https://example.com/photo.jpg",
 "status": "simulated", "provider": "fallback",
 "note": "Install praisonaiagents for real analysis"}

// Response (no image → 400)
{"error": "No image provided", "status": "error"}
```

### POST /api/media/ocr

```json
// Request
{"url": "https://example.com/document.png"}

// Response
{"text": "Extracted text from the document...", "status": "success", "provider": "sdk"}
```

- [Attachments](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/attachments.md) — Upload images to analyze via media analysis

# Gateway Chat

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/gateway-chat

> The Chat page of the dashboard style (and of the app shell, which hosts the same view): real-time agent chat over a WebSocket, with markdown rendering, tool cal

The Chat page of the `dashboard` style (and of the app shell, which hosts the same view): real-time agent chat over a WebSocket, with markdown rendering, tool call cards and session history. The browser side is the vanilla `chat.js` view; the server side is the chat feature (`praisonaiui.features.chat`).

![The chat in the app shell, dark: an agent thought for two seconds, ran python3 --version, answered and now waits for approval to install numpy; the table and script it made sit under the answer](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/images/chat-interface.png)

## Quick Start

```python
# app.py
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("dashboard")

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")
```

```bash
aiui run app.py
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 and choose Chat in the sidebar
```

Without a `@aiui.reply` callback the chat runs the configured agents through
the PraisonAI provider (`pip install "aiui[praisonai]"`).

## How It Works

### Full Streaming Data Flow

A chat message travels through 5 layers before reaching the browser:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User (Browser)
    participant JS as chat.js
    participant WS as WebSocket /api/chat/ws
    participant CM as ChatManager<br/>(chat.py)
    participant PR as PraisonAIProvider<br/>(providers/__init__.py)
    participant SDK as Agent.chat()<br/>(praisonaiagents)

    U->>JS: User types message, hits Send
    JS->>WS: {type: "chat", content: "Hello"}
    WS->>CM: _run_and_broadcast(session_id, content)
    CM->>PR: provider.run(content, session_id)
    PR->>SDK: agent.chat(message, stream=True)

    rect rgb(40, 40, 60)
    note over SDK,JS: Streaming Phase
    SDK-->>PR: StreamEvent (DELTA_TEXT tokens)
    PR-->>CM: RunEvent(RUN_CONTENT, token="...")
    CM-->>WS: broadcast({type: "run_content", token: "..."})
    JS->>JS: appendDelta(token) — accumulate in single DOM element

    SDK-->>PR: StreamEvent (TOOL_CALL_START)
    PR-->>CM: RunEvent(TOOL_CALL_STARTED, name, args)
    CM->>CM: Dedup + enrich (icon, description, step_number)
    CM-->>WS: broadcast({type: "tool_call_started", ...enriched})
    JS->>JS: appendToolCall(data, 'running') — collapsible card

    SDK-->>PR: StreamEvent (TOOL_CALL_END + result)
    PR-->>CM: RunEvent(TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED, result)
    CM->>CM: Merge result into collected_tool_calls
    CM-->>WS: broadcast({type: "tool_call_completed", ...enriched})
    JS->>JS: updateToolCall(data, 'done') — show ✓ + result

    SDK-->>PR: StreamEvent (STREAM_END)
    PR-->>CM: RunEvent(RUN_COMPLETED, content=str(response))
    CM-->>WS: broadcast({type: "run_completed", content: "..."})
    JS->>JS: finalizeDelta(content) — replace streaming text with final
    end

    rect rgb(40, 50, 40)
    note over CM: Persistence Phase
    CM->>CM: Save to datastore: {role, content, toolCalls}
    end
```

### Key Files

| File | Layer | Responsibility |
|------|-------|----------------|
| `src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js` | Frontend | WS connection, DOM rendering, session history |
| `src/praisonaiui/features/chat.py` | Backend | ChatManager, `_run_and_broadcast`, history API |
| `src/praisonaiui/server.py` | Backend | SSE streaming path (`run_agent` endpoint) |
| `src/praisonaiui/providers/__init__.py` | Provider | SDK → RunEvent bridge, `_run_direct_mode` |
| `src/praisonaiui/datastore.py` | Storage | `MemoryDataStore` / `JSONFileDataStore` |
| `src/praisonaiui/provider.py` | Protocol | `RunEventType` enum definition |

## Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["ChatProtocol (ABC)"] --> B["ChatManager (Default)"]
    B --> C["send_message()"]
    B --> D["get_history()"]
    B --> E["abort_run()"]
    B --> F["broadcast()"]
    G["ChatFeature"] --> H["API Routes"]
    H --> I["POST /api/chat/send"]
    H --> J["GET /api/chat/history/{session_id}"]
    H --> K["POST /api/chat/abort"]
    H --> M["GET /api/chat/context-stats"]
    H --> L["WS /api/chat/ws"]
```

## Agent Tool Resolution

Agents created via YAML config, CRUD API, jobs, or channel bots automatically get tools resolved through the `ToolResolver`. Tool names in config are resolved to callable Python functions from 4 sources:

1. Local `tools.py` file (backward compatibility)
2. `praisonaiagents.tools.TOOL_MAPPINGS` (built-in tools)
3. `praisonai_tools` package (community tools)
4. Tool registry (programmatically registered tools)

### YAML Configuration

```yaml
# ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml (unified runtime config)
agents:
  researcher:
    instructions: "Research topics thoroughly."
    model: gpt-4o-mini
    tools:
      - internet_search        # Resolved to callable function
      - wikipedia_search
    reflection: true            # Enable self-reflection (default: true)
    role: "Senior Researcher"   # Optional CrewAI-style params
    goal: "Find accurate info"
    backstory: "Expert researcher"
```

### CRUD API

Agents created via `POST /api/agents` also support tools:

```json
{
  "name": "researcher",
  "instructions": "Research topics thoroughly.",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "tools": ["internet_search"],
  "reflection": true
}
```

### Where Tool Resolution Applies

| Component | Tool Resolution |
|-----------|----------------|
| Gateway `_create_agents_from_config()` | ✅ `ToolResolver` |
| Integration `create_gateway_from_yaml()` | ✅ `ToolResolver` |
| Provider `_get_or_create_agent()` | ✅ Default tools |
| Channel bot `_start_channel_bot()` | ✅ Default tools |
| Jobs `_execute_job()` fallback | ✅ `ToolResolver` |
| CRUD agents `_run()` fallback | ✅ `ToolResolver` |
| CRUD agents `_sync_to_gateway()` | ✅ `ToolResolver` |

## Features

### Markdown Rendering

Assistant messages are rendered with full markdown support:

- **Bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~
- Inline `code` and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting
- Ordered and unordered lists
- Links (auto-detected and rendered safely)

### Tool Call Display

![A tool call row (execute_command, Done in 0.3 s) above the answer, then an approval card for pip install numpy with Approve and Deny](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/images/tool-streaming.png)

When agents use tools, each call is displayed as a collapsible card:

- Tool name and status indicator (running/completed/failed)
- Input arguments (JSON)
- Output results (rendered in code blocks)

#### Tool Call Lifecycle

Tool calls go through 4 stages: **emit → enrich → dedup → persist**.

**1. Emit** — The SDK fires `TOOL_CALL_START` / `DELTA_TOOL_CALL` / `TOOL_CALL_END` events via `StreamEventEmitter`. The provider maps these to `RunEvent` types (`TOOL_CALL_STARTED`, `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED`).

**2. Enrich** — `_run_and_broadcast()` in `chat.py` enriches each tool call event with display-friendly fields via `_enrich_tool_payload()`:

| Field | Source | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `icon` | Mapped from tool name | 🔍, 📝, 💾 |
| `description` | Generated from name + args | "🔍 Searching for 'Django latest version'" |
| `step_number` | Auto-incrementing counter per run | 1, 2, 3 |
| `formatted_result` | Truncated result string | "✓ Done" |
| `tool_call_id` | SDK-assigned or UUID fallback | "call_abc123" |

**3. Dedup** — Both `DELTA_TOOL_CALL` (stream) and hook callbacks fire for the same tool call. The handler uses `_seen_tool_started` / `_seen_tool_completed` sets keyed by `tool_call_id` and `name` to suppress duplicates. A re-broadcast with `has_complete_args=True` is allowed to update the description with keyword-rich text.

**4. Persist** — After the run completes, all enriched tool calls are merged by `tool_call_id` into `collected_tool_calls` and saved alongside the assistant message:

```python
msg_data = {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": full_response,
}
if collected_tool_calls:
    msg_data["toolCalls"] = list(collected_tool_calls.values())
await _datastore.add_message(session_id, msg_data)
```

#### Reloading during a reply

The React chat asks for `run_attach` when it opens a session. A run whose tab
was reloaded comes back as the tab's own turn: the reply so far (the server
keeps each live run's events, consecutive tokens merged, up to 2,000 events),
the Stop button, and the composer waiting until the run ends. A run that
another open tab started shows read-only, also with the reply so far; both tabs
can keep sending.

#### Turn order

A reply is saved when its run ends, so two runs in one session (a second tab,
or a question sent after a reload while the first reply is still running)
finish out of order. A user message carries a `turn_id` and its reply a
`reply_to` with the same value; `GET /api/chat/history/{id}` lists each reply
right after its own question. History saved before these fields existed is
shown in the order it was saved.

#### Tool Call Persistence Schema

Tool calls are persisted alongside assistant messages in the datastore. When a session is reloaded from history, tool call steps are reconstructed from the `toolCalls` array on each assistant message.

Assistant message schema in the datastore:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "Final response text",
  "toolCalls": [
    {
      "name": "search_web",
      "description": "🔍 Searching for 'Django latest version'",
      "icon": "🔍",
      "step_number": 1,
      "args": {"query": "Django latest version"},
      "result": "...",
      "formatted_result": "✓ Done",
      "status": "done",
      "tool_call_id": "tc_abc123",
      "type": "tool_call_completed"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### History Reload Rendering

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser as chat.js
    participant API as GET /api/chat/history/{id}
    participant DS as DataStore

    Browser->>API: fetch('/api/chat/history/' + sessionId)
    API->>DS: get_messages(session_id)
    DS-->>API: messages (with toolCalls on assistant msgs)
    API-->>Browser: {messages: [...]}
    
    loop forEach message
        alt role == assistant
            Browser->>Browser: appendMessage('assistant', content)
            loop forEach toolCalls[]
                Browser->>Browser: appendToolCall(tc)
                Browser->>Browser: updateToolCall(tc, result)
            end
        else role == user
            Browser->>Browser: appendMessage('user', content)
        end
    end
```

### Session Management

- **New Session**: Click "New Chat" to create a fresh session
- **Session History**: Switch between sessions in the sidebar
- **Message History**: Full conversation history per session via REST API

### Message Abort

- Click the **Stop** button (or send `chat_abort` with the `run_id` over the WebSocket) to cancel a run
- Only the connection that started a run may stop it or answer its prompts (or any client, once that connection is gone)
- The partial response is preserved in history

### File Attachments

Upload files to include with your chat messages — see [Attachments](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/attachments.md) for details.

## Session Persistence

Chat history is stored through the `BaseDataStore` interface: by default the
praisonaiagents session store, or JSON files, memory or SQL with
`aiui run --datastore`. See [Session Management](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/sessions.md#data-persistence-options).
Each stored session holds its messages, with `toolCalls` on assistant messages:

```json
{
  "id": "session-uuid",
  "title": "Auto-generated from first user message",
  "created_at": "2026-03-17T08:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-17T08:01:00Z",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "..."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "...", "toolCalls": [...]}
  ]
}
```

### Response Content Strategy

The `content` field on assistant messages stores the SDK's final response from `agent.chat()` — the same text displayed by `finalizeDelta()` in the live view. This ensures the reloaded view matches what the user saw during streaming.

!!! important
    During streaming, text tokens are accumulated in `full_response`. When `RUN_COMPLETED` arrives with `event.content` (the SDK's authoritative return value), it **replaces** the accumulated tokens for storage. This prevents intermediate narrative text from being duplicated on reload.

## Chat Message Model

```python
@dataclass
class ChatMessage:
    role: str                          # "user" | "assistant" | "system" | "tool"
    content: str                       # Message text
    session_id: str                    # Session identifier
    message_id: str                    # Auto-generated UUID
    agent_name: Optional[str] = None   # Agent name
    timestamp: float                   # Unix timestamp
    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None    # Tool calls and other metadata
```

## WebSocket Protocol

On a server with auth on, the browser first exchanges its key for a
single-use ticket (`POST /api/auth/ws-ticket`) and connects with `?ticket=`;
see [Deployment](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md).

### Client → Server

```json
// Send a message (optional: agent_name, attachment_ids, client_turn_id, regenerate)
{"type": "chat", "content": "Hello!", "session_id": "abc-123"}

// Abort a run: answered with {"type": "chat_abort_result", "status": ..., "run_id": ...}
{"type": "chat_abort", "run_id": "run-1"}

// Answer an agent's question: answered with {"type": "ask_response_ack", "status": ...},
// status "received", "no_pending_ask" (nothing was waiting: the ask timed out or
// the run ended) or "forbidden" (another connection's run)
{"type": "ask_response", "session_id": "abc-123", "run_id": "run-1", "response": "5.1"}

// A tab that (re)opened a session: its live runs and their events so far,
// answered with {"type": "run_snapshot", "session_id": ..., "runs": [{"run_id",
// "client_turn_id", "question", "adoptable", "last_seq", "truncated", "events"}]}.
// "adoptable": the run's starting tab is gone, so this connection now owns it
// (it may stop or answer it). Every run event carries a per-run "seq"; skip
// the ones up to "last_seq", which the snapshot already holds.
{"type": "run_attach", "session_id": "abc-123"}

// Is a run still active?
{"type": "run_status", "run_id": "run-1"}

// Receive only these sessions' events (default: every session)
{"type": "subscribe", "session_ids": ["abc-123"]}
{"type": "unsubscribe", "session_ids": ["abc-123"]}

// Keepalive ping
{"type": "ping"}
```

A frame that is not a JSON object is answered with
`{"type": "protocol_error", "error": ...}`; the connection stays open.

### Server → Client

All events include `session_id` and `run_id`.

```json
// Streaming text token
{"type": "run_content", "token": "Hello", "session_id": "...", "run_id": "..."}

// Tool call started (enriched)
{
  "type": "tool_call_started",
  "name": "search_web",
  "tool_call_id": "call_abc123",
  "args": {"query": "Django"},
  "description": "🔍 Searching for 'Django'",
  "icon": "🔍",
  "step_number": 1
}

// Tool call completed (enriched)
{
  "type": "tool_call_completed",
  "tool_call_id": "call_abc123",
  "name": "search_web",
  "result": "Django 5.1 released...",
  "formatted_result": "✓ Done",
  "status": "done"
}

// Intermediate LLM narrative text (between tool calls)
{"type": "llm_content", "content": "Let me search for that..."}

// Reasoning step (thinking)
{"type": "reasoning_step", "step": "Analyzing the query..."}

// Agent asks for user input
{"type": "run_paused", "question": "Which version?", "options": ["5.0", "5.1"]}

// Memory updates
{"type": "memory_update_started"}
{"type": "updating_memory"}
{"type": "memory_update_completed"}

// Run completed (content = SDK's final response)
{"type": "run_completed", "content": "Here are the results..."}

// Error / Cancel
{"type": "run_error", "error": "..."}
{"type": "run_cancelled"}

// Team variants (multi-agent)
{"type": "team_run_started", "agent_name": "researcher"}
{"type": "team_run_content", "token": "..."}
{"type": "team_tool_call_started", ...}
{"type": "team_tool_call_completed", ...}
{"type": "team_run_completed", "content": "..."}

// Channel bot messages
{"type": "channel_message", "platform": "slack", "sender": "User", "content": "..."}
{"type": "channel_response", "platform": "slack", "content": "..."}

// Keepalive
{"type": "pong"}
```

## Frontend (chat.js)

The chat frontend is a vanilla JavaScript view,
`src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js`, shipped as-is with
the package (it is not generated by the frontend build).

### Core Functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|--------|
| `connectWebSocket()` | Open the WS (with a ticket when auth is on); reconnects on close |
| `handleWsMessage(data)` | Event dispatch — routes to rendering functions |
| `appendMessage(role, content, agentName)` | Render a complete message (history load) |
| `appendDelta(token, agentName)` | Streaming — append token to `currentDeltaEl` |
| `finalizeDelta(content, agentName)` | End streaming — replace with final content |
| `appendToolCall(data, status)` | Render tool call card |
| `updateToolCall(data, status)` | Update card with result |
| `appendReasoning(step)` | Render thinking step |
| `appendAskWidget(question, options, sessionId, runId)` | Render user-input prompt |
| `appendMemoryIndicator(text)` | Show memory update spinner |
| `loadSession(sessionId)` | Fetch history → render messages + tool calls |
| `restoreSessionHistory(sessionId)` | Same as above, on WS reconnect |
| `renderMarkdown(text)` | Custom zero-dependency markdown renderer |
| `escapeHtml(str)` | XSS prevention sanitizer |

### Streaming Text Model

During streaming, **all text tokens go into a single `currentDeltaEl` DOM element** — even across tool call boundaries. Tool call cards are sibling elements inserted alongside the text element. When `run_completed` arrives, `finalizeDelta(content)` **replaces** the accumulated text with the SDK's final response.

The chat UI supports dark and light themes via CSS custom properties — see [Theme System](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theme-system.md).

# Human-in-the-Loop Approvals

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/approvals

> Require explicit human approval before agents run sensitive tools, with inline chat cards, a dedicated Approvals queue and SSE updates.

When an agent is about to execute a sensitive tool (shell commands, deployments, payments, file deletions), PraisonAIUI pauses the run and asks a human to **Approve** or **Deny** — inline inside the chat thread and in the built-in **Approvals** page (`builtin.approvals`).

## How it works

1. The agent runtime or backend submits an approval request (`POST /api/approvals`).
2. Connected browsers receive it live over SSE (`GET /api/approvals/stream`) and show an inline approval card in chat plus an entry on the **Approvals** page.
3. Pair with `aiui.push_notification(..., action={"label": "Review now", "page": "approvals"})` so operators also get an immediate toast + unread badge in the header **Notification Bell** on the same dashboard.
4. A reviewer clicks **Approve** (`POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve`) or **Deny** (`POST /api/approvals/{id}/deny`), optionally updating reusable policy rules (`PUT /api/approvals/policies`).
5. The agent resumes or aborts cleanly, and the decision is recorded in `GET /api/approvals/history`.

Run the complete combined Python + YAML example locally (no API key needed):

```bash
cd examples/python/34-hitl-approvals-and-notifications
aiui run app.py
```

See [34-hitl-approvals-and-notifications](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/python/34-hitl-approvals-and-notifications) and [Notification Center](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/notifications.md).

## REST & SSE endpoints

All routes sit behind the server's active auth middleware (R8).

| Method & Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/approvals` | List all approvals (or `GET /api/approvals/pending` for open items) |
| `POST /api/approvals` | Create a new approval request |
| `POST /api/approvals/{approval_id}/approve` | Approve a pending request |
| `POST /api/approvals/{approval_id}/deny` | Deny a pending request |
| `GET /api/approvals/history` | Audit log of past decisions |
| `GET` / `PUT /api/approvals/policies` | Inspect or update automatic approval policies |
| `GET /api/approvals/stream` | Real-time SSE stream of approval events |

## Enable or disable

Approvals are enabled by default in the app shell. To hide the built-in Approvals page and disable its routes:

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled:
    - builtin.approvals
```

# Pre/Post Operation Hooks

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/hooks

> HooksFeature (builtin.hooks) exposes pre- and post-operation hooks over REST and the CLI, merging hooks defined in praisonaiagents.hooks (SDK hooks) with hooks

`HooksFeature` (`builtin.hooks`) exposes pre- and post-operation hooks over REST and the CLI, merging hooks defined in `praisonaiagents.hooks` (SDK hooks) with hooks registered dynamically through the API.

## REST API

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/hooks` | List all merged SDK and UI-registered hooks |
| `POST` | `/api/hooks` | Register a new hook (`name`, `event`, `type`: `"pre"` \| `"post"`, `enabled`) |
| `GET` | `/api/hooks/{hook_id}` | Fetch a UI-registered hook |
| `DELETE` | `/api/hooks/{hook_id}` | Delete a UI-registered hook |
| `POST` | `/api/hooks/{hook_id}/trigger` | Trigger a hook manually with optional `{"data": {...}}` payload |
| `GET` | `/api/hooks/log` | View recent hook executions (`?limit=50`) |

### Quick Example

```bash
# Register a pre-tool hook
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/hooks \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "audit_tool_calls", "event": "tool_call", "type": "pre"}'

# Trigger it manually and inspect the execution log
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/hooks/<hook_id>/trigger \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data": {"tool": "shell"}}'

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/hooks/log?limit=20
```

## CLI Commands

```bash
aiui hooks list
aiui hooks trigger <hook_id>
aiui hooks log
```

## Disabling

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled:
    - builtin.hooks
```

# Subagent Tree View

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/subagent-tree

> Visualize agent hierarchies — see which agents spawn subagents, track their status, and monitor the full execution tree.

Visualize **agent hierarchies** — see which agents spawn subagents, track their status, and monitor the full execution tree.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Get the subagent tree for a session
curl http://localhost:8000/api/subagents/my-session

# List all spawns across sessions
curl http://localhost:8000/api/subagents
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Orchestrator"] --> B["Researcher"]
    A --> C["Writer"]
    A --> D["Coder"]
    B --> E["Web Searcher"]
    C --> F["Editor"]
```

Each spawn is a record of parent agent, child agent and session in the
server's `SubagentManager`:

1. When `praisonaiagents` is installed, the manager subscribes to its `handoff`
   hook, so every agent handoff is recorded (parent, child and session id come
   from the hook payload; missing values become `parent`, `child` and
   `default`).
2. Your own code can record spawns with `register_spawn()`.
3. The tree for a session is built from its spawn records; an agent that is
   never a child is a root.

Records are kept in memory and cleared on restart. Every record has
`status: "running"`; completion is not tracked yet.

## Configuration

```python
from praisonaiui.features.subagents import get_subagent_manager

mgr = get_subagent_manager()  # the instance the REST API reads

# Register a spawn event
spawn_id = mgr.register_spawn(
    parent_agent="orchestrator",
    child_agent="researcher",
    session_id="my-session",
)

# Get the tree
tree = mgr.get_tree("my-session")
# {
#   "session_id": "my-session",
#   "roots": [{"name": "orchestrator", "children": [{"name": "researcher", ...}]}],
#   "total_spawns": 1
# }
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/subagents` | GET | All spawn records (`{"spawns": [...]}`) |
| `/api/subagents/{session_id}` | GET | Get tree for a session |

### Get Tree

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/api/subagents/my-session
```

```json
{
  "session_id": "my-session",
  "roots": [
    {
      "name": "orchestrator",
      "children": [
        {"name": "researcher", "children": []},
        {"name": "writer", "children": [
          {"name": "editor", "children": []}
        ]}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "total_spawns": 3
}
```

# Code Execution

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/code-execution

> 1. Code is submitted with a target language. A language outside the allowlist (default: python, javascript, bash) is a 400; so is any language other than Python

**Sandboxed code execution** with language allowlists, behind a human approval. Runs Python through the SDK's `execute_code` (`praisonaiagents.tools.python_tools`), which carries `@require_approval(risk_level="critical")`. Every run waits until someone approves it in the **Approvals** page.

## Quick Start

```bash
# List supported languages
curl http://localhost:8083/api/code/languages

# Execute code
curl -X POST http://localhost:8083/api/code/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"code":"print(\"Hello World\")","language":"python"}'
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["POST /api/code/execute"] --> F{"Language allowed<br/>and Python?"}
    F -->|No| G["400 error"]
    F -->|Yes| C{"praisonaiagents installed?"}
    C -->|No| E["503 degraded<br/>(nothing runs)"]
    C -->|Yes| H["SDK execute_code<br/>@require_approval critical"]
    H --> I["Pending entry in Approvals"]
    I -->|Approve| D["Runs in the subprocess sandbox → 200"]
    I -->|Deny or timeout| J["403 denied"]
```

1. Code is submitted with a target language. A language outside the **allowlist** (default: python, javascript, bash) is a 400; so is any language other than Python, because the SDK sandbox runs Python only.
2. Without `praisonaiagents` the response is `503` with `status: "degraded"`. Nothing runs, and nothing is simulated.
3. Otherwise the request goes through the SDK's own approval gate on `execute_code`, wired to the aiui approvals queue. A pending `execute_code` entry (risk `critical`, arguments = the exact code) appears in `GET /api/approvals/pending`, and the HTTP request waits for the decision without blocking the server.
4. **Approve** runs the code and returns `200`. **Deny**, or no answer within the SDK registry timeout (300 s by default), returns `403` with `status: "denied"`.

One run needs one approval. Only the entry the server created for that run counts: an entry created with `POST /api/approvals` does not unlock a run, and approving a run with `always: true` approves that run only (critical tools never get a standing approval).

To skip the human step on a trusted machine, opt out explicitly: add `execute_code` to the `auto_approve_tools` policy (`PUT /api/approvals/policies`; remove it to turn the gate back on) or set `PRAISONAI_AUTO_APPROVE=true` for the server process. Authentication is the server's job (`AUTH_ENFORCE`, `require_auth`, `AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN`): without credentials, the run and the approve/deny endpoints return 401.

## Configuration

```python
from praisonaiui.features.code_execution import SandboxExecutionManager, set_execution_manager

# Custom configuration
mgr = SandboxExecutionManager(
    sandbox=True,                              # Enable sandbox mode
    timeout=60,                                # Execution timeout
    allowed_languages=["python", "javascript"] # Only allow these languages
)
set_execution_manager(mgr)
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/code/languages` | GET | List supported languages |
| `/api/code/execute` | POST | Execute code in sandbox |

### POST /api/code/execute

```json
// Request
{"code": "print('hello')", "language": "python", "timeout": 30}

// Response after approval → 200 (a failing script is "failed", still 200)
{"language": "python", "status": "success", "output": "hello\n", "error": "",
 "result": null, "sandbox": true}

// Response when denied or timed out → 403
{"status": "denied", "language": "python",
 "error": "Not run: Execution of execute_code denied: ..."}

// Response without praisonaiagents → 503
{"language": "python", "status": "degraded", "sandbox": true,
 "error": "Code execution needs the praisonaiagents package (pip install praisonaiagents). Nothing was run."}

// Response (disallowed language → 400)
{"status": "error", "error": "Language 'ruby' not allowed",
 "allowed": ["python", "bash", "javascript"]}
```

- [Skills](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/features-api.md#skills) — Code execution tools in the skill catalog

# Model Fallback

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/model-fallback

> The model fallback feature (praisonaiui.features.model_fallback) lists the

The model fallback feature (`praisonaiui.features.model_fallback`) lists the
available models and stores an ordered fallback chain that the UI can show and
edit.

!!! note "The chain is stored, not applied"
    Nothing in PraisonAIUI reads the chain when it sends a request: the
    provider still calls the agent's own model, and a failed call is not retried
    on the next model. The chain is also kept in memory only, so a restart
    clears it. Use it as a setting your own provider or `@aiui.reply` callback
    reads (see below).

## Quick Start

```bash
# List available models and the current chain
curl http://localhost:8000/api/models

# Set the chain
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8000/api/models/fallback \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"models": ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-3-5-sonnet"]}'
```

## Model Discovery

The model list comes from `litellm.model_list` when LiteLLM is installed and
has models configured. Otherwise it is a short static list: `gpt-4o`,
`gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-3-5-sonnet` and `gemini-2.0-flash`.

## Reading the Chain

Use the server's shared manager, not a new `ModelFallbackManager()`, so you see
what the API set:

```python
from praisonaiui.features.model_fallback import get_fallback_manager

mgr = get_fallback_manager()

mgr.get_models()
# [{"id": "gpt-4o", "provider": "openai"}, ...]

mgr.set_fallback_chain(["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"])
mgr.get_fallback_chain()
# ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"]
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/models` | GET | Available models and the current fallback chain |
| `/api/models/fallback` | PUT | Set the chain (`{"models": [...]}`; 400 if not a list) |

### List Models

```json
{
  "models": [
    {"id": "gpt-4o", "provider": "openai"},
    {"id": "gpt-4o-mini", "provider": "openai"},
    {"id": "claude-3-5-sonnet", "provider": "anthropic"},
    {"id": "gemini-2.0-flash", "provider": "google"}
  ],
  "fallback_chain": ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"]
}
```

- [Providers](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/providers.md): LLM provider configuration

# MCP servers

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/mcp

> Give your agents the tools of any Model Context Protocol server, declared in YAML, over Streamable HTTP, SSE or stdio, with secrets kept on the server

The **MCP** page (`builtin.mcp`) connects the app to Model Context Protocol
servers so agents can use their tools. Declare servers once in the config;
they connect when the app starts. Users can add more from the page only where
you allow it. Install the client once: `pip install "aiui[mcp]"`.

## Declare servers

```yaml
mcp:
  servers:
    github:
      url: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
      headers:
        Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}
    files:
      command: npx
      args: [-y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."]
```

Put the block in the config the app starts with (`aiui run app.py --config
aiui.yaml`) or in the data-dir `config.yaml` (`AIUI_DATA_DIR`, default
`~/.praisonaiui`). `aiui validate` checks it. Each server has a `url` or a
`command`, not both:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Remote server (Streamable HTTP or SSE) |
| `command`, `args` | Local server started as a subprocess (stdio) |
| `env` | stdio: extra environment variables for the subprocess |
| `headers` | Remote: HTTP headers, for example `Authorization` |
| `transport` | `streamable-http`, `sse` or `stdio` (`type` works too). Usually not needed, see below |

`${NAME}` in `url`, `args`, `env` and `headers` reads the environment variable
`NAME`, so tokens stay out of the file. A list with a `name` per server
(`servers: [{name: github, url: ...}]`) works too; names must be unique.

The servers connect in the background at startup, all at once, so a slow
server never delays the app. One that fails shows its error on the page, with
a **Connect** button to try again. They disconnect when the app stops.

## Transports

| Server | What the app uses |
|---|---|
| `command` | stdio |
| `url` | Streamable HTTP; if the server does not answer it, SSE |
| `url` whose path ends in `/sse` | SSE |
| `transport: sse` or `transport: streamable-http` | Exactly that one, no fallback |

## What users may add

By default users can reconnect the declared servers but add nothing new. Open
it up with `allow`:

```yaml
mcp:
  allow:
    urls: ["*.example.com", "https://tools.partner.io/mcp/"]
    commands: [uvx]
```

| `allow.urls` entry | Admits |
|---|---|
| `mcp.example.com` | That host on its default port, `http` or `https` |
| `*.example.com` | Any subdomain of `example.com` |
| `https://h.example.com/mcp/` | That scheme and host, paths under `/mcp/` |
| `https://h.example.com:8443` | That port |
| `*` | Any public host |

A wildcard (`*`, `*.example.com`) never reaches a private, loopback or
link-local address, so users cannot reach your internal network or a cloud
metadata endpoint through the app. To allow an internal server, name its host:
`http://localhost:9000`.

`allow.commands` lists the executables users may start, matched exactly:
`npx` does not admit `/tmp/npx`. A user-added stdio server cannot set `env`.
Allowing `npx` or `uvx` lets users run any package they name, so list them
only for people you trust; `*` admits any command (the older
`PRAISONAIUI_ALLOW_REMOTE_MCP_STDIO=true` does the same). A user cannot reuse
a declared server's name for another target.

## Turn it off

`mcp: {enabled: false}`: nothing connects at startup and the page cannot add
servers. To remove the page and its routes: `extensions: {disabled: [builtin.mcp]}`.

## Secrets stay on the server

- `GET /api/mcp/servers` and the connect response show header and env names
  with `***` values, drop user and password from URLs, and mask query values
  (`?api_key=***`).
- Header and env values, every `${NAME}` value, and any `Bearer` token are
  redacted from the app's logs, tracebacks included.

## API

Every route needs the same credentials as the rest of the API in each auth mode.

| Route | Does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/mcp/servers` | Servers with `status`, `transport`, `tools`, `last_error`, `source` (`config` or `user`) and masked `connection_data`; plus `enabled` and `allow` |
| `POST /api/mcp/connect` | `{name}` connects a declared server. `{name, url, headers?, transport?}` or `{name, command, args?}` adds one that `allow` admits (403 otherwise, 409 for a declared name) |
| `POST /api/mcp/disconnect/{name}` | Disconnects a server |

From Python, `aiui.on_mcp_connect` and `aiui.on_mcp_disconnect` run when a
server's state changes. App code may call
`praisonaiui.features.mcp.connect_mcp_server({...})` directly; the `allow`
lists apply to users, not to your code.

# Text-to-Speech (TTS)

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/tts

> Synthesize speech from text using swappable backends — browser-native (zero cost) or OpenAI TTS API.

Synthesize speech from text using **swappable backends** — browser-native (zero cost) or OpenAI TTS API.

## Quick Start

```bash
# List available voices
curl http://localhost:8083/api/tts/voices

# Synthesize speech
curl -X POST http://localhost:8083/api/tts/synthesize \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hello from PraisonAI","voice":"default"}'
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Text Input"] --> B{"TTSProtocol"}
    B --> C["BrowserTTSManager\n(Web Speech API)"]
    B --> D["OpenAITTSManager\n(API Key Required)"]
    C --> E["Client-side\nspeechSynthesis"]
    D --> F["Server-side\nMP3 Audio"]
```

**Default**: `BrowserTTSManager` — uses the browser's built-in Web Speech API, requires no API key, runs entirely client-side.

**Optional**: `OpenAITTSManager` — uses OpenAI's TTS API for higher-quality voices (alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer). Requires `openai` package and API key.

## Configuration

```python
from praisonaiui.features.tts import set_tts_manager, OpenAITTSManager

# Switch to OpenAI TTS (requires OPENAI_API_KEY)
set_tts_manager(OpenAITTSManager())
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/tts/voices` | GET | List available voices |
| `/api/tts/synthesize` | POST | Synthesize speech from text |

```json
{
    "voices": [
        {"id": "default", "name": "Default", "lang": "en-US"},
        {"id": "google-us", "name": "Google US English", "lang": "en-US"},
        {"id": "google-uk", "name": "Google UK English", "lang": "en-GB"}
    ],
    "count": 3
}
```

### POST /api/tts/synthesize

```json

// Response (browser)
{
    "type": "browser_speech",
```

# Voice input in the chat

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/realtime-voice-input

> Talk instead of typing. When an app turns on voice input, the chat composer

Talk instead of typing. When an app turns on voice input, the chat composer
gets a microphone button. Press it, speak, and press it again: the recording
is turned into text and put in the message box, after anything already typed,
for you to read over and send.

Voice input belongs to the **realtime** feature (`builtin.realtime`). It is
off unless the app asks for it, so no other chat shows a microphone.

## Turn it on

Give aiui a realtime manager that can transcribe speech. The bundled
`OpenAIRealtimeManager` uses OpenAI speech to text (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, and
`OPENAI_BASE_URL` for a compatible server):

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiui.features.realtime import OpenAIRealtimeManager

aiui.set_realtime_manager(OpenAIRealtimeManager())
# Another speech-to-text model:
# aiui.set_realtime_manager(OpenAIRealtimeManager(transcribe_model="whisper-1"))
```

`aiui.OpenAIRealtimeManager` is the same class. There is no
`praisonaiui.realtime` module: import it from `praisonaiui` or
`praisonaiui.features.realtime`.

Your own backend works too. Subclass `RealtimeProtocol` and implement
`transcribe`:

```python
from praisonaiui.features.realtime import RealtimeProtocol

class MySpeech(RealtimeProtocol):
    async def transcribe(self, audio: bytes, *, mime_type: str) -> str:
        return await my_stt(audio, mime_type)   # mime_type: audio/webm, audio/mp4...
    # create_session, send_audio, receive_audio, call_tool, close_session as before

aiui.set_realtime_manager(MySpeech())
```

A manager without `transcribe` keeps the microphone hidden.
`aiui.set_realtime_manager(None)` turns voice input off again.

## In the browser

| State | What you see |
|---|---|
| At rest | A microphone icon button before Send ("Record a voice message") |
| Recording | A red stop button and a running time; screen readers hear "Recording". Press the button again to stop and transcribe, or Escape to discard |
| Transcribing | A spinner in the button |
| Done | The text in the message box, with the caret at its end |

The browser asks for the microphone the first time. If access is blocked, a
message says how to allow it in the browser's site settings; no microphone,
or one busy in another app, gets its own message. A recording stops by itself
after two minutes.

The button is keyboard accessible (Tab to it, Enter or Space to start and
stop, Escape to discard) and has a visible focus ring. Its code is a separate
chunk that loads only for an app with voice input on.

## API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/realtime/voice` | GET | `{"enabled": bool, "max_seconds": 120, "max_bytes": 8388608}`: whether the composer shows the microphone |
| `/api/realtime/transcribe` | POST | The recording as the raw body (`Content-Type: audio/*`). Returns `{"text": "..."}` |

`/api/realtime/transcribe` answers 404 while voice input is off, 415 for a
body that is not audio, 400 for an empty one, 413 over 8 MiB, 501 when the
manager cannot transcribe, and 502 when the speech service fails (its message
is logged by type only, never returned). Both routes need the same
credentials as every other `/api` route.

## Not included

The reply is text. Speaking it aloud (see [TTS](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/tts.md)) and a hands-free,
speech-to-speech session are not part of this feature.
