# Providers

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/providers

> PraisonAIUI uses a provider protocol — a simple abstraction that lets you plug in any AI backend.

PraisonAIUI uses a **provider protocol** — a simple abstraction that lets you plug in any AI backend.

## Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Frontend (React)"
        UI["Dashboard / Chat / Agents"]
        SSE["WebSocket or SSE stream"]
        API["REST API Client"]
    end

    subgraph "Server (server.py)"
        Routes["WS /api/chat/ws, /run, /sessions, /api/*"]
        Provider["get_provider()"]
    end

    subgraph "Provider Protocol (BaseProvider)"
        direction LR
        Run["run() → AsyncIterator[RunEvent]"]
        List["list_agents() → List[dict]"]
        Health["health() → dict"]
    end

    subgraph "Pluggable Backends"
        P1["PraisonAIProvider (default)"]
        P4["Your provider (aiui.set_provider)"]
    end

    UI --> API --> Routes --> Provider
    SSE --> Routes
    Provider --> Run
    Provider --> List
    Provider --> Health
    Run --> P1 & P4
```

The provider protocol is the **only contract** between the frontend and any AI backend. All dashboard pages (`/api/overview`, `/api/config`, `/api/logs`, etc.) are provider-agnostic — they always work regardless of which backend is active. The provider only handles agent execution (`run()`), agent listing (`list_agents()`), and health checks (`health()`).

## How It Works

1. The user sends a message: a `chat` frame on the WebSocket `/api/chat/ws`
   (the default for the chat page and the app shell), or `POST /run` (SSE)
2. The server calls `provider.run(message)` on the active provider
3. The provider yields `RunEvent` objects (start, content, tool calls, reasoning, completion)
4. The server sends each event as an SSE `data:` frame (`RunEvent.to_dict()`)
   or as a WebSocket message, and stores the finished turn in the datastore.
   The WebSocket adapter forwards only selected fields per event type (for
   example, reasoning events carry `step` but not `action`, `confidence` or
   `next_action`), so only SSE clients receive every serialized field
5. The frontend renders the events as they arrive

## Built-in Provider: PraisonAI

`PraisonAIProvider` is the default. When the app registers a `@aiui.reply`
callback, it runs the callback and turns its `aiui.say()`, `aiui.think()`,
`aiui.image()` and other calls into `RunEvent`s:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    # Your AI logic here — PraisonAIProvider handles the rest
    await aiui.say("Hello!")
```

Without a callback it runs a `praisonaiagents` `Agent` (install
`aiui[praisonai]`): the agent named in the request when one is defined through
the agents API or `config.yaml`, else a default assistant. Without
`praisonaiagents` it echoes the message.

### Agent Tools and Reflection

The default provider resolves tools for agents using `ToolResolver` from the `praisonai` package. Agents created via the CRUD API or `~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml` get their tool names (strings) automatically resolved to callable Python functions:

```python
# Agent definition with tools (via CRUD API or YAML):
# tools: ["internet_search", "wikipedia_search"]
#
# ToolResolver resolves these names from 4 sources:
# 1. Local tools.py file
# 2. praisonaiagents.tools.TOOL_MAPPINGS (built-in)
# 3. praisonai_tools package (community)
# 4. Tool registry (programmatic)
```

When an agent has no tools configured, the provider gives it the tools of the
SDK's `autonomy` profile (file operations, command execution, web search). The
default assistant runs with `reflection` off.

## Swapping Providers

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# Use a custom provider:
aiui.set_provider(MyCustomProvider())
```

## Writing a Custom Provider

Implement `BaseProvider.run()` — that's it:

```python
from praisonaiui.provider import BaseProvider, RunEvent, RunEventType

class EchoProvider(BaseProvider):
    """Echoes messages back — minimal example."""

    async def run(self, message, *, session_id=None, agent_name=None, **kw):
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_STARTED)
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_CONTENT, token=f"Echo: {message}")
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_COMPLETED, content=f"Echo: {message}")
```

### Inline media (images, video, files)

Any provider can attach rich media to chat messages using ``MESSAGE_ELEMENT``
events. The UI renders them inline and persists them in session history.

```python
class ImageProvider(BaseProvider):
    async def run(self, message, *, session_id=None, agent_name=None, **kw):
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_STARTED)
        # ... call your image API (OpenAI, Stability, custom, etc.) ...
        image_url = "https://example.com/generated.png"
        yield BaseProvider.message_element_event({
            "type": "image",
            "url": image_url,
            "alt": "Generated image",
        })
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_COMPLETED, content="Here is your image.")
```

Tool results from PraisonAI agents are also detected automatically when they
match OpenAI image shapes (``{"data": [{"url": "..."}]}``) or explicit element
dicts — no provider code required.

Callback handlers can use ``await aiui.image(url)`` (or dict entries in
``Message.elements``) and the default ``PraisonAIProvider`` maps those to
``MESSAGE_ELEMENT`` events. Typed elements from ``Message.add_image()`` are not
forwarded yet; see [Message Elements](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/message-elements.md).

Full architecture, data flows, and tests: [Image Preview in Chat](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/image-preview-chat.md).

### With Tool Calls and Reasoning

```python
class SmartProvider(BaseProvider):
    async def run(self, message, **kw):
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_STARTED)

        # Emit reasoning steps (shown in ThinkingSteps component)
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.REASONING_STARTED)
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.REASONING_STEP, step="Analyzing the question...")
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.REASONING_STEP, step="Searching knowledge base...")
        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.REASONING_COMPLETED)

        # Emit tool calls (shown in ToolCallDisplay component)
        yield RunEvent(
            type=RunEventType.TOOL_CALL_STARTED,
            name="web_search",
            args={"query": message},
        )
        yield RunEvent(
            type=RunEventType.TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED,
            name="web_search",
            result={"results": ["Found relevant info"]},
        )

        # Stream the response token by token
        for word in "Here is the answer".split():
            yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_CONTENT, token=word + " ")

        yield RunEvent(type=RunEventType.RUN_COMPLETED, content="Here is the answer")
```

## RunEvent Reference

Every event has a `type` field and optional payload fields:

| Field | Type | Used By |
|-------|------|---------|
| `type` | `RunEventType` | All events |
| `content` | `str` | `RUN_COMPLETED`, `RUN_CONTENT` |
| `token` | `str` | `RUN_CONTENT` (streaming) |
| `name` | `str` | `TOOL_CALL_*` |
| `args` | `dict` | `TOOL_CALL_STARTED` |
| `result` | `any` | `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED` |
| `tool_call_id` | `str` | `TOOL_CALL_*` (pairs start and completion) |
| `step` | `str` | `REASONING_STEP` (also `action`, `confidence`, `next_action`) |
| `query`, `references`, `time_ms` | `str`, `list`, `float` | `REFERENCES` (RAG sources) |
| `error` | `str` | `RUN_ERROR` |
| `agent_id`, `agent_name`, `team_id` | `str` | Multi-agent events |
| `extra_data` | `dict` | Custom payload (includes `element` for `message_element`) |

### Event Types (30 total)

=== "Agent Events"

    | Type | Description |
    |------|-------------|
    | `run_started` | Agent run begins |
    | `run_content` | Streaming token or content chunk |
    | `run_completed` | Agent run finished |
    | `run_error` | Error occurred |
    | `run_cancelled` | User cancelled |
    | `tool_call_started` | Tool invocation started |
    | `tool_call_completed` | Tool returned result |
    | `llm_content` | Narrative text between tool calls |
    | `reasoning_started` | Thinking begun |
    | `reasoning_step` | Individual reasoning step |
    | `reasoning_completed` | Thinking finished |
    | `memory_update_started` | Memory write begun |
    | `memory_update_completed` | Memory write done |
    | `updating_memory` | Memory being updated |
    | `run_paused` | Run paused (e.g. waiting for user) |
    | `run_continued` | Run resumed |
    | `references` | RAG source chunks for the answer |
    | `message_element` | Inline media element (image, video, file, etc.) — see [Image Preview in Chat](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/image-preview-chat.md) |

=== "Team Events"

    | Type | Description |
    |------|-------------|
    | `team_run_started` | Team run begins |
    | `team_run_content` | Team streaming content |
    | `team_run_completed` | Team run finished |
    | `team_run_error` | Team error |
    | `team_run_cancelled` | Team cancelled |
    | `team_tool_call_started` | Team tool call started |
    | `team_tool_call_completed` | Team tool call done |
    | `team_reasoning_started` | Team reasoning begun |
    | `team_reasoning_step` | Team reasoning step |
    | `team_reasoning_completed` | Team reasoning done |
    | `team_memory_update_started` | Team memory update started |
    | `team_memory_update_completed` | Team memory update done |

## API Summary

### `BaseProvider` (abstract)

Subclass and implement `run()` to create a custom provider.

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `run(message, *, session_id, agent_name, **kw)` | **Required.** Async generator yielding `RunEvent` objects |
| `list_agents()` | Optional. Returns list of available agents |
| `run_team(...)` | Optional. Multi-agent run |
| `health()` | Optional. Returns health check dict |
| `message_element_event(element)` | Static helper: a `MESSAGE_ELEMENT` event for an element dict |

### `RunEvent` (dataclass)

Structured event with `type: RunEventType` and optional payload fields (see
the table above). `to_dict()` serialises it to the JSON the frontend reads.

### `RunEventType` (enum)

30 string values matching the frontend `types.ts`; see the Agent Events and
Team Events tabs above.

### Helper Functions

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `praisonaiui.set_provider(provider)` | Set the active provider |
| `praisonaiui.get_provider()` | Get the active provider (lazy-inits `PraisonAIProvider`) |

# PraisonAI package integration

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/praisonai-package-integration

> How PraisonAIUI (aiui) connects to praisonai-package — the agent runtime, gateway, and CLI. For generic UI hosting see Agent UI host.

How **PraisonAIUI** (`aiui`) connects to **`praisonai-package`** — the agent runtime, gateway, and CLI. For generic UI hosting see [Agent UI host](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agent-ui-host.md).

## Division of labour

| Layer | Repo | Role |
|-------|------|------|
| Agent runtime | `praisonai-agents` | `Agent`, tools, memory, streaming |
| Gateway, jobs, CLI | `praisonai` | WebSocket `/ws`, `/api/v1/runs`, `praisonai claw` |
| Dashboard UI | **PraisonAIUI** | `dashboard.js`, `@aiui.page`, layout protocol |
| Work tracking | `praisonai-platform` | Issues API (optional board data source) |

Canonical app: `praisonai-package` → `src/praisonai/praisonai/claw/default_app.py`.

## Deployment shapes

### 1. Single process — `praisonai claw` (recommended)

```bash
praisonai claw   # → aiui run claw/default_app.py, default :8082
```

```text
Browser → create_app() (same process)
        → PraisonAISessionDataStore (sessions)
        → PraisonAIProvider (@aiui.reply / agents)
        → Built-in dashboard views
```

Use when: local dev, full dashboard, agents registered in Python.

### 2. Unified — `AIUIGateway`

```python
from praisonaiui.integration import AIUIGateway
gateway = AIUIGateway(port=8080)
gateway.register_agent(agent)
await gateway.start()   # create_app() + WebSocket /ws
```

Use when: you need **WebSocket gateway protocol** and dashboard on **one port**.

### 3. Split — gateway + UI

| Service | Default port | Endpoints |
|---------|--------------|-----------|
| `praisonai gateway start` | 8765 | `ws://…/ws`, `/health`, `/info` |
| `praisonai claw` or `aiui run` | 8082 | Dashboard, `/run` SSE, `/api/*` |

Use when: gateway runs headless; UI is a separate process. Point chat at gateway via provider config or run `AIUIGateway` instead.

## Wiring checklist

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonai.ui._aiui_datastore import PraisonAISessionDataStore

aiui.set_datastore(PraisonAISessionDataStore())
aiui.set_style("dashboard")
aiui.set_pages(["chat", "agents", "sessions", "config"])
aiui.set_dashboard(modules=["jobs"], sidebar=True, page_header=True)

# Optional: point jobs UI at package jobs server paths
aiui.set_jobs_api(api_base="/api/v1/runs", backend="praisonai")
```

Or via host bootstrap:

```python
from praisonai.integration.host_app import configure_host, create_host_app

configure_host(pages=[...], modules=["jobs"], agents=[...])
app = create_host_app()
```

## API surface

### Chat and agents (dashboard)

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `POST /run` | Stream agent run (SSE) |
| `GET /sessions`, `POST /sessions` | Session CRUD |
| `GET /agents`, `/api/agents/definitions` | Agent list / CRUD |
| `GET /api/health` | Sidebar health slot |

### Async jobs — two paths

| Backend | Base path | When |
|---------|-----------|------|
| **aiui** `JobsFeature` | `/api/jobs` | Default; in-process job store |
| **praisonai** jobs server | `/api/v1/runs` | Standalone `praisonai jobs` / FastAPI router |

Configure the dashboard jobs view:

```python
aiui.set_jobs_api(api_base="/api/jobs", backend="aiui")       # default
aiui.set_jobs_api(api_base="/api/v1/runs", backend="praisonai")
```

`/ui-config.json` exposes `jobs: { apiBase, backend }` for `jobs.js`.

**Response shapes:** both return `{ jobs, total }`. Praison uses `job_id`; aiui uses `id`. The jobs view normalises either field.

| Action | aiui | praisonai |
|--------|------|-----------|
| List | `GET /api/jobs` | `GET /api/v1/runs` |
| Detail | `GET /api/jobs/{id}` | `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}` |
| Cancel | `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel` | `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel` |
| Stream | `GET /api/jobs/{id}/stream` | `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/stream` |
| Delete | `DELETE /api/jobs/{id}` | Not on package router |

**Split jobs server (optional):** proxy aiui `/api/jobs/*` to an external jobs host:

```python
aiui.set_jobs_proxy("http://127.0.0.1:9000")  # forwards to /api/v1/runs/*
aiui.set_jobs_api(api_base="/api/jobs", backend="aiui")
```

The proxy forwards only to `/api/v1/runs/*` on that host: a path with a `.` or
`..` segment (encoded or not) is refused with 400. It never forwards aiui's own
credentials (`Authorization`, cookies, `X-API-Key`, `?token=`/`?api_key=`/`?ticket=`).
If the jobs server needs a credential, pass it:
`aiui.set_jobs_proxy("http://127.0.0.1:9000", token="<jobs server key>")`
sends `Authorization: Bearer <jobs server key>` upstream.

Use when the dashboard and jobs server run on different ports. Prefer `set_jobs_backend("praisonai")` when the browser can call `/api/v1/runs` on the same origin.

### REST invoke (automation)

| Path | Use |
|------|-----|
| `POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/invoke` | Sync invoke (n8n, scripts) — **package** `agent_invoke.py` |
| `POST /run` | Streaming chat — **dashboard** chat page |

Same agents if registered on both surfaces; different protocols.

### Discovery (package serve)

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /__praisonai__/discovery` | Serve-mode capability discovery |
| `GET /health`, `GET /info` | Gateway liveness and metadata |
| `GET /api/gateway/status` | aiui gateway feature status |

See **Feature Explorer** page in dashboard for live probes.

## Parallel UI protocols (not dashboard replacements)

Under `praisonaiagents/ui/`:

| Protocol | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| **A2A** | Agent cards, `/.well-known/agent.json`, external agent hosts |
| **AG-UI** | CopilotKit-style event stream (`POST /agui`) |
| **A2UI** | Declarative surfaces in chat/canvas |

Dashboard shell remains the ops console for `praisonai claw`. Use A2A/AG-UI/A2UI when embedding in other products.

## Two plugin systems

| System | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| **Agent plugins** | `~/.praisonai/plugins/` | Python agent extensions (`praisonaiagents.plugins`) |
| **Dashboard plugins** | `~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins/` | JS tabs + `manifest.json` for aiui shell |

Do not mix folders. Agent plugins extend runtime; dashboard plugins extend UI tabs only.

## Optional modules

```python
aiui.set_dashboard(modules=["jobs", "auth", "api"])
```

Loads `jobs.js`, `auth.js`, `api.js` into the plugin chain; their pages resolve to `views/<page id>.js` for built-in pages, from `/api/shell/manifest`. Enable only what your deployment exposes.

## Board / work tracking

Neither repo ships Hermes-style Kanban. Options:

1. **`aiui.board()`** — columns from `@aiui.page` handler (jobs by status, custom data).
2. **`praisonai-platform` issues** — map issue `status` → board columns (see `examples/python/platform-board/`). Set `PRAISONAI_PLATFORM_URL` and `PRAISONAI_PLATFORM_WORKSPACE_ID` (default workspace `default`); issues are fetched from `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/issues`.
3. **`dashboard-plugins`** — rich JS via `registerView` + `sdk.createBoard`.

Advanced board UX (drag-drop, WebSocket sync) is **deferred** — use polling via `sdk.createBoard({ pollMs })` or a custom plugin.

## Smoke checklist

After `praisonai claw` or `aiui run` with package bridges:

- [ ] `GET /api/health` → sidebar footer shows healthy
- [ ] Chat page sends message, streams reply
- [ ] Sessions page lists `~/.praisonai/sessions/` data
- [ ] Agents page CRUD (if agents registered)
- [ ] Jobs page (if `modules` includes `jobs` and jobs API configured)
- [ ] Explorer probes `/health`, `/ui-config.json`, `/api/dashboard/plugins`
- [ ] Auth/API pages (if `modules` includes `auth` / `api`)

# Standalone vs Integrated

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/standalone-vs-integrated

> This page summarises the expected install and runtime shape for PraisonAIUI in both modes.

This page summarises the expected install and runtime shape for PraisonAIUI in both modes.

## Install Matrix

| Mode | Package install | Runtime dependency | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone UI | `pip install praisonaiui` | Optional SDK packages absent | Uses built-in local managers and fallbacks |
| Integrated (PraisonAI) | `pip install praisonaiui praisonai praisonaiagents` | SDK and wrapper available | Uses injected backends and SDK-aware managers |

## Backend injection (integrated mode)

When hosted via `praisonai.integration.host_app.configure_host()`, the wrapper calls `praisonaiui.backends.set_backend()` for:

| Backend key | Feature area |
| --- | --- |
| `hooks` | Hooks dashboard |
| `workflows` | Workflow runs |
| `usage_query` / `usage_sink` | Usage analytics |
| `approvals_pending` / `approvals_policies` | HITL approvals |
| `jobs_store` / `jobs_executor` | Async jobs (optional) |
| `channel_bot` | Channel bots (optional) |
| `tool_resolver` | Agent tool name resolution (optional) |

Detect integrated mode in code: `praisonaiui.backends.is_integrated_mode()`.

## Documented SDK gaps (local fallback)

These features work standalone with in-memory stores. Health responses include `sdk_gap: true`:

| Feature | Gap | Standalone behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **nodes** | No cluster API in praisonaiagents | In-memory node registry |
| **auth** | No SDK auth module | In-memory API keys / sessions |
| **channels** | Bot runtime via praisonai wrapper | In-memory channel registry; bots need `praisonai[bot]` |
| **jobs** | Mock success only when standalone and agent missing | Integrated mode fails job instead of fake success |
| **realtime** | WebRTC needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Mock stream standalone; degraded error when integrated without key |
| **media / code** | SDK paths optional | `status: simulated` standalone; `status: degraded` integrated on failure |

View gaps in the dashboard sidebar footer (`GET /api/health` → `sdk_gaps` array).

## Practical Differences

- **Session/data handling**: standalone uses UI datastore fallback; integrated aligns with SDK-backed stores.
- **Feature backends**: standalone keeps in-memory/mock behaviour; integrated routes through injected factories.
- **Lifecycle hooks**: integrated mode can subscribe to SDK hooks (handoff, MCP lifecycle, tracing/eval stores).

## Recommendation

Use standalone mode for local UI-only workflows. Use integrated mode when you need shared runtime state with PraisonAI agents, tools, tracing, approvals, and schedules.

See also [backend-integration.md](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/backend-integration.md) and [praisonai-package-integration.md](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/praisonai-package-integration.md).

---

# Backend Integration Contract

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/backend-integration

> PraisonAIUI supports a four-layer integration model so standalone mode and SDK-integrated mode can share the same feature APIs.

PraisonAIUI supports a four-layer integration model so standalone mode and SDK-integrated mode can share the same feature APIs.

## Four Layers

1. **Feature API layer**
   Endpoints live in feature modules and expose stable HTTP/CLI behaviour.
2. **Feature manager layer**
   Each feature manager keeps local fallback logic for standalone operation.
3. **Backend factory layer**
   `praisonaiui.backends` provides optional injected factories (`get_workflow_runner()`, `get_hooks_lister()`, `get_usage_query()`, etc.).
4. **SDK/runtime layer**
   PraisonAI or praisonaiagents implementations are used when injected or importable.

## Injection Contract

- Injected backends are optional and must be callable.
- Features must keep local fallbacks when injected backends are absent or fail.
- Backend call signatures should remain minimal and dict/list based.
- Integration should not introduce hard imports in feature modules when a fallback already exists.

## Operational Rule

When integrated, wrappers should inject backend callables at startup; when standalone, features should run without any backend injection.

# Workflows, Hooks & OpenAI-Compatible API

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/workflows-and-openai-api

> Orchestrate multi-step agent workflows, trigger server lifecycle hooks and call your agents over an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint.

Beyond interactive chat, PraisonAIUI exposes automation and integration APIs so external tools, scripts and multi-agent pipelines can drive your agents directly.

## Workflows (`builtin.workflows`)

Define, trigger and inspect multi-step agent workflows over REST:

- `GET /api/workflows` / `POST /api/workflows` — List or create workflow definitions
- `POST /api/workflows/{workflow_id}/run` — Execute a workflow
- `GET /api/workflows/{workflow_id}/status` — Inspect workflow state
- `GET /api/workflows/runs` / `GET /api/workflows/runs/{run_id}` — Review run history and outputs

## Lifecycle hooks (`builtin.hooks`)

Register server-side hooks to react to platform events and inspect execution history:

- `GET /api/hooks` / `POST /api/hooks` — List or register hooks
- `POST /api/hooks/{hook_id}/trigger` — Trigger a hook manually
- `GET /api/hooks/log` — Inspect recent hook invocations

## OpenAI-compatible API (`builtin.api`)

Call your registered PraisonAIUI agents from any OpenAI-compatible client, SDK, or editor using the built-in `api` plugin (see the **API** page in the dashboard for ready-to-copy curl/SDK snippets and authentication headers). All requests honor the server's active auth middleware (R8).

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AIUI_API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model": "default", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

# AG-UI Protocol

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agui

> PraisonAIUI exposes an AG-UI SSE endpoint (POST /agui) so CopilotKit and any AG-UI-compatible frontend can stream runs directly from your PraisonAI agents.

PraisonAIUI exposes an [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/) SSE endpoint (`POST /agui`) so CopilotKit and any AG-UI-compatible frontend can stream runs directly from your PraisonAI agents.

## Requirements

The AG-UI encoder and runner come from `praisonaiagents`:

```bash
pip install "aiui[praisonai]"
```

When `praisonaiagents` is not installed (or no agent is available), `POST /agui` returns HTTP `503` and `GET /agui/status` reports `"status": "unavailable"`.

## Registering an Agent

Register an agent in your `app.py` (or configure one via the Agents page or PraisonAI gateway):

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiagents import Agent

assistant = Agent(
    name="assistant",
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant.",
)
aiui.register_agent("assistant", assistant)
```

`POST /agui` resolves the target agent in this order:

1. Explicitly registered agents (`aiui.register_agent(name, agent)`) matching `agent_name` in the JSON body or `?agent=<name>` query parameter (falls back to the registered agent when omitted).
2. Active `AIUIGateway` agents when running with `--backend praisonai`.
3. Existing provider agents, or lazily constructed agents from the Agents CRUD store when `praisonaiagents` is installed.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/agui` | Stream an AG-UI run (`text/event-stream`). Validates the body as `RunAgentInput` (`400` on invalid payload, `503` when no agent or `praisonaiagents` is available). |
| `OPTIONS` | `/agui` | CORS preflight for browser AG-UI clients. |
| `GET` | `/agui/status` | Check availability: `{"status": "available" \| "unavailable", "agent_registered": bool}`. |

### Example Request

```bash
curl -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/agui \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "threadId": "thread-1",
    "runId": "run-1",
    "messages": [{"id": "m1", "role": "user", "content": "Summarize today'\''s status"}]
  }'
```

Select a specific agent with `"agent_name": "researcher"` in the JSON body or `?agent=researcher` on the URL.

## Disabling AG-UI

AG-UI is shipped as the built-in plugin `builtin.agui`. To disable it:

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled:
    - builtin.agui
```

- [Features REST API](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/features-api.md#ag-ui)

# App & Dashboard Overview

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/app-ui/overview

> Combine chat with selectable layouts, Python or zero-code YAML data pages, a notification center, custom themes and plugins.

PraisonAIUI is more than a single chat window. In the default **React app shell** (`style: app`), you can pair conversational AI with live data pages, selectable layouts, a header Notification Center, custom themes and installable plugins — all from one server.

## Build custom pages in Python or YAML

Add KPI cards, filterable tables, charts, forms and Markdown runbooks next to your chat.

### Python (@aiui.page)

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.page("overview", title="Overview", icon="bar-chart-2", group="Workspace", badge="Live")
async def overview():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.columns([
            aiui.card("Active Users", value="1,420", footer="+12% this week"),
            aiui.card("Uptime", value="99.98%", footer="Last 30 days"),
        ]),
        aiui.table(
            headers=["Service", "Status"],
            rows=[["Chat Gateway", "Healthy"], ["Search Index", "Healthy"]],
        ),
    ])
```

### Zero-code YAML

Declare full pages in `app.yaml` — and split big apps across files with `$ref:`. Edits reload dynamically without restarting the server.

```yaml title="app.yaml"
style: app
branding:
  title: "Operations"
pages:
  - chat
  - id: overview
    title: "Overview"
    icon: "bar-chart-2"
    group: "Workspace"
    badge: "Live"
    components:
      - type: columns
        children:
          - type: metric
            label: "Active Users"
            value: "1,420"
            delta: "+12%"
          - type: card
            title: "Status"
            value: "Healthy"
```

Run it with `aiui run app.yaml`.

## Key building blocks

- [Selectable layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md)
  Switch one app between Chat + Canvas, Workbench, Command, Guided and Mission Control.
- [Server & YAML pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/server-pages.md)
  URL query filters, POST forms, lazy tabs, auto-refresh, live sidebar badges and YAML `$ref` pages.
- [Notification Center](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/notifications.md)
  Push real-time alerts over SSE to the header bell with read/unread state and deep links.
- [Theming & Plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md)
  Pick from 20+ color presets, light/dark modes, or ship full React pages as Python plugins.

## Built-in dashboard pages

When you want an out-of-the-box operations console for your agents, enable built-in pages with `aiui.set_pages("all")` (or pick specific IDs with `aiui.set_pages(["chat", "sessions", "agents", "logs"])`). Every page shares the same theme, navigation and authentication. See [Dashboard](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/dashboard.md) and [Focused app](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app.md).

# React App Shell (`style: app`)

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/react-shell

> The app shell is a React interface for the PraisonAIUI dashboard: a sidebar,

The app shell is a React interface for the PraisonAIUI dashboard: a sidebar,
a header with a command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K), a React chat and a host that
runs every existing dashboard page inside it. **It is the default style**
(owner decision, 2026-11-22): `create_app()`, `aiui run app.py` and an app
that registers pages all open it. The vanilla-JS `dashboard` is the legacy
UI; it still renders exactly as before when you ask for it:

| Where | Legacy dashboard |
|---|---|
| YAML config | `style: dashboard` |
| Python | `aiui.set_style("dashboard")` |
| CLI | `aiui run app.py --style dashboard` (prints a one-line legacy notice) |
| Environment | `AIUI_SHELL=legacy` |

## Turn it on explicitly

Any one of these:

| Where | How |
|---|---|
| YAML config | `style: app` |
| Python | `aiui.set_style("app")` before the server starts |
| CLI | `aiui run app.py --style app` |
| Environment | `AIUI_SHELL=app aiui run app.py` (alias: `AIUI_SHELL=react`) |

`AIUI_SHELL=app` only changes the `dashboard` style into
`app`. Other styles (`chat`, `docs`, `agents`, `playground`, `custom`) are
never rewritten.

### Kill switch

`AIUI_SHELL=legacy` turns `app` back into `dashboard`, whatever the config
says. It is the documented way back once the default flips (see
[flip criteria](#when-the-default-flipped)).

```bash
AIUI_SHELL=legacy aiui run app.py   # always the vanilla dashboard
```

## What you get

- **Every page you have today.** A page is resolved in this order:
    1. a React page registered through the SDK (built-in ports such as chat, or
       a [UI plugin](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md) page);
    2. a server-driven page (`register_page` with a handler, `@aiui.page`),
       rendered from its `_components` tree as blocks;
    3. otherwise the original dashboard view, mounted inside the shell.

  Nothing disappears: dashboard plugins (`kanban`, `sample-board`,
  `video-studio`), `set_custom_js` and `custom.js` `registerView` pages keep
  working as hosted pages.
- **React chat** over the WebSocket `/api/chat/ws` (streaming, tool calls,
  reasoning, inline approvals and questions, attachments, Stop, history).
  When the socket cannot open it falls back to Server-Sent Events (`POST /run`);
  on SSE an agent's question says that answering needs a live connection.
- **One markdown renderer** (Streamdown) for chat and docs, with lazy code
  highlighting (74 languages), Mermaid and KaTeX. In chat, external links open
  in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`, and remote images
  are shown as a click-to-load placeholder naming their host (same-origin,
  `data:image/` and `blob:` images load directly).
- **Approval toasts.** A new approval anywhere raises a toast with a
  "Review" button that opens the Approvals page. On the chat page the
  approval is shown in the thread instead.

## Compatibility

| Existing API | `dashboard` (default) | `app` (opt-in) |
|---|---|---|
| `register_page` with a handler / `@aiui.page` | unchanged | server-driven blocks page |
| `register_page` without a handler | unchanged | hosted `custom.js` `registerView` page |
| `register_page_action` | unchanged | the page's action endpoint |
| `set_pages`, `pages.enabled/disabled` | unchanged | applied |
| `set_custom_js` | unchanged | injected; runs when the hosted runtime loads |
| `set_custom_css` | unchanged | unchanged; HSL triples warn (see below) |
| `set_theme`, `set_brand_color`, `register_theme` | unchanged | converted to theme seeds |
| dashboard plugins | unchanged | hosted pages; `dashboard.plugins` allowlist honoured |
| `chat`, `docs`, `agents`, `playground`, `custom` styles | same app, now lazy-loaded with the new markdown renderer and tokens | n/a |
| `aiui build` static docs | same app; loads content-named copies `index-<hash>.js`/`.css` | n/a |

## Theme seeds (migration)

Colours now come from a small set of **seeds** (`--seed-accent`,
`--seed-ink`, `--seed-paper`, …). Everything else (`--background`,
`--primary`, sidebar and chart colours) is derived from them in CSS with
`color-mix()`, separately for light and dark. Python emits seeds only
(`praisonaiui.themes.get_seed_theme_css(preset, radius, accent, density)`):

- neutral presets (`zinc`, `slate`, `stone`, `gray`, `neutral`) are
  monochrome: the accent follows the ink;
- colour presets (`rose`, `blue`, …) seed the accent from the 600 shade in
  light mode, and the button text colour is picked automatically for
  at least 4.5:1 contrast;
- radius presets are unchanged.

`get_theme_css()` is kept for API compatibility but the compiler no longer
uses it. Runtime themes (`register_theme`, named presets) are converted to
seeds in the browser.

### Breaking change: bare HSL triples

Listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the release that ships the
app shell.

shadcn variables used to hold bare HSL triples that the stylesheet wrapped in
`hsl()`. They are now complete colours:

```css
/* before (no longer valid) */
:root { --primary: 221 83% 53%; }

/* after: any CSS colour */
:root { --primary: hsl(221 83% 53%); }

/* better: set the seed, and every derived colour follows in both modes */
:root { --seed-accent: hsl(221 83% 53%); }
```

`aiui validate` warns (code 5001) when `site.custom_css` sets one of these
variables to a bare triple. Custom CSS and runtime themes that still use
triples are converted in the browser where possible, but update the CSS.

## Caching and deploys

- Code chunks are content-hashed (`assets/<name>-<hash>.js`) and served with
  `Cache-Control: immutable`. `assets/index.js` and `assets/index.css` keep
  fixed names in the bundle; the server references them as `?v=<hash>`, so a
  release never mixes an old entry with new chunks.
- `aiui build` writes content-named copies of both,
  `assets/index-<sha256[:10]>.js` and `assets/index-<sha256[:10]>.css`, and
  loads them from `index.html` and every route page. A static host such as
  GitHub Pages ignores the query string, so `?v=` alone could pair a cached
  old page with the new entry. `index.js` and `index.css` stay in the build,
  so a page cached before the switch still loads, and the copies are listed in
  the site's `aiui-manifest.json` (keys `aiui-entry-copy:<file>`), so the
  deploy's carry-forward keeps them next to the chunks. When a chunk imports
  the entry module (none does today) the build keeps `index.js?v=`, which
  would otherwise load the entry twice.
- The docs deploy keeps the previous build's chunks, and with its ledger
  (`aiui-carried.json`) older builds' chunks for `--keep-days` (default 2)
  (`src/frontend/scripts/carry-forward-assets.mjs`), so a reader with an
  old page open can still load its lazy parts.
- A stale chunk that does fail to load triggers one automatic reload, and
  only when the server's HTML (fetched past the cache) names another build.
  The reload opens the page as `?aiui-build=<build>`, a URL no browser or CDN
  cache holds, and the boot removes the parameter again. When the boot
  chunks themselves cannot load, the page says so and offers Reload.
- A docs page never waits for good: each markdown request has a time limit
  for its headers and one for its body, a stalled request is sent again,
  and a page that still cannot load shows "Couldn't load this page" with
  Retry (`src/frontend/src/docs/docLoader.ts`). A retry also moves to a
  fresh connection (it switches between requests with and without
  credentials, which the browser keeps on separate connection pools), so a
  connection that a router dropped while idle does not cost the page. An
  attempt with no response headers after 1 s (0.4 s after 10 s without a
  request) also goes out on the other pool and the first answer wins; a
  request that fails outright switches at once. A visitor coming back after
  10 s without input sends one small request (`ui-config.json`) the same way,
  so the next click already uses a working connection.
  `python -m preqa netfault` reproduces the dead connection (budget 2.5 s;
  measured 0.15-0.19 s).
- Static files are sent gzip-compressed. Each file is compressed once per
  version (path, mtime, size) in a worker thread and kept in memory (at most
  64 MB), so a cold page load does not compress the bundle again on the
  event loop. Range requests get the plain bytes. The page HTML,
  `/api/shell/manifest`, `/api/pages` and dashboard-plugin files are
  compressed too.
- `aiui run app.py` serves the bundle from the installed package; it no
  longer copies it into `./aiui` on every start (a `./aiui` left by an older
  version is ignored for a chat app; delete it). A site built with
  `aiui run --config` is served gzip-compressed with `Cache-Control:
  no-cache`, like `aiui serve`, and its own `assets/` (for example
  `theme.css`) is looked up after the package's.
- `aiui serve` answers a page's canonical URL (`/docs/x`) from `docs/x.html`
  directly, without a redirect to `/docs/x/`.

## Quality gates

| Gate | Command (in `src/frontend`) | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Types | `npx tsc -b` | 0 errors |
| Unit tests | `npm test`, `npm run test:scripts` | all pass |
| Size (gzip) | `npm run size` | shell boot ≤ 151.3 kB, chat route ≤ 144,500 B, /chat first-screen JS ≤ 264,400 B, `index.css` ≤ 32 kB, Streamdown ≤ 100 kB, shikiPlugin ≤ 55 kB, legacy App path ≤ 250 kB, docs Try it chunk ≤ 7,566 B, Pro fonts (Geist + Geist Mono woff2) ≤ 58 kB, Paper fonts (Newsreader + Source Sans 3 + JetBrains Mono woff2) ≤ 140 kB, all assets ≤ 11,180,139 B uncompressed |
| First screen stays light | `npm run check:closure` | no Streamdown, Shiki, Mermaid, KaTeX or assistant-ui in the static closure of the entry, the shell or the legacy App |
| Committed bundle | `npm run check:bundle` | `templates/frontend` equals a fresh build (pull requests that touch the frontend only) |
| Browser suites | `npm run test:e2e` | see `src/frontend/e2e/README.md` |

The docs style preloads Streamdown before first paint (about 98 kB gzip on
that path). The HTML parser it needs for raw HTML and docs components
(rehype-raw, about 48 kB) is a chunk of its own that only pages whose
markdown has HTML load (`markdown/rehypeRawGate.ts`). This is an accepted
exception until docs pages are pre-rendered at build time.

## When the default flipped

The owner made `app` the default on 2026-11-22, before every criterion below
was met. The table is kept as the remaining work list:

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every page renders in the shell with status ready, 0 page errors and 0 leak delta in the Playwright sweep | **Not met.** Every manifest page is ready (a page that prints a JSON error body, or whose own data endpoint fails, now counts as an error; the Inspector was one and is fixed), 0 page errors, no page grows per visit, and every page opens by URL. Three pages keep a one-time residue after their first visit that does not grow, each listed with its reason in the sweep's `FIRST_VISIT_ALLOWANCE` (any other or larger residue fails): `chat` (13 window listeners and the composer's hidden measuring textarea), `chat-canvas` (one window listener) and `code-studio` (Monaco's interval, listener and two body nodes) |
| 2 | Chat parity complete | **Not met.** Done: streaming, tools, reasoning, approvals, ask, attachments, Stop, history, feedback, session rail, reconnect. Missing: message queue, channel messages with unread dots, context ring and compaction banner, cost chip, memory panel, floating and focus modes |
| 3 | Light mode correct on every page; owner signs off the light and dark screenshots | **Not met.** Awaiting owner review |
| 4 | Gates green: size, bundle-sync, entry closure, screenshots, pytest, tsc | **Partly.** All run green locally; screenshot comparison is not enforced in CI until Linux baselines exist |
| 5 | `set_custom_js`, `custom.js` `registerView` and the three bundled dashboard plugins work under `app` | **Met in this build.** The three dashboard plugins pass the sweep; the e2e app-shell server sets `set_custom_js` with a `registerView` for a page that also has a server handler, and the client view wins (as in the legacy dashboard) |
| 6 | One minor release with `app` opt-in, then two weeks with no open P1 from opt-in users | **Not met** |

## Plugins and trust

See [UI Plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md). Installing a plugin package means trusting it:
its Python runs in the server process and its JavaScript runs in the page
with no sandbox. An `iframe` page is the sandboxed option.

# Notification Center

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/notifications

> PraisonAIUI includes a modular, extendable Notification Center built into @aiui/sdk

PraisonAIUI includes a modular, extendable Notification Center built into `@aiui/sdk`
and shipped as a first-party plugin (`builtin.notifications`).

## Combined HITL Approvals + Notifications Example

See live notifications, header bell alerts, deep-link actions, and Human-in-the-Loop approvals working together on one dashboard in [34-hitl-approvals-and-notifications](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/python/34-hitl-approvals-and-notifications) (`aiui run app.py` or `aiui run app.yaml` — no API key required).

[
  {"type": "alert", "variant": "warning", "title": "Approval required: deploy_release", "message": "Agent paused before deploying v0.4.0 to production — click Review now in the header Notification Bell."},
  {"type": "timeline", "title": "Recent Notification Events", "items": [
    {"title": "Deployment v0.4.0 approved", "time": "just now", "status": "success", "description": "Agent resumed and completed rollout."},
    {"title": "Approval required: deploy_release", "time": "2m ago", "status": "warning", "description": "High-risk tool gate triggered from Chat."}
  ]}
]

## Zero-Code YAML Notifications

Declare startup or static notifications directly in `app.yaml`:

```yaml
style: app
notifications:
  - title: "Approval required: deploy_release"
    description: "Agent paused before rolling out v0.4.0"
    type: warning
    category: approvals
    action:
      label: "Open Approvals"
      page: "approvals"
```

## Architecture (DRY & Modular)

1. **Headless SDK store (`@aiui/sdk`: `notifications`, `useNotifications`)**
   - Holds the single client-side notification list, unread count, deduplication
     (`dedupeKey` / `id`), ring-buffer cap, and optimistic actions
     (`markRead`, `markUnread`, `markAllRead`, `remove`, `clear`, `sync`).
   - Automatically records calls to `notify(message, opts)` unless
     `opts.record === false`, so ephemeral toasts stay reviewable in the bell
     panel without duplicating code at call sites.
   - Extendable via `notifications.registerSource(id, source)` for custom
     transports (WebSockets, SSE, polling, webhooks).
2. **Header Bell plugin (`builtin.notifications`)**
   - Registers a lightweight bell trigger into the `header:actions` slot, so it
     appears in the Classic shell and selectable layout frames.
   - Lazily loads its popover panel on hover, focus, or click to keep boot
     bundles small.
   - Supports All / Unread / dynamic category filters, Mark all read, per-item
     read toggle & dismiss, safe SPA action links (`action.page` + `params`),
     keyboard `Escape`, and polite screen-reader announcements.
   - Disable it with `extensions: { disabled: ["builtin.notifications"] }` or
     replace it by registering your own `header:actions` slot component backed
     by `useNotifications()`.
3. **Python Feature & SDK (`praisonaiui.features.notifications`)**
   - Mounts authenticated REST and SSE endpoints (`/api/notifications`,
     `/api/notifications/read-all`, `/api/notifications/{id}/read`,
     `/api/notifications/{id}`, `/api/notifications/stream`).
   - Pluggable storage via `NotificationStoreProtocol` and
     `aiui.set_notification_store(store)`.

## Python Usage

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# Push a live notification from anywhere (background task, page handler, tool)
aiui.push_notification(
    "Deployment succeeded",
    "Production build v1.4 is live",
    type="success",
    category="deploy",
    dedupe_key="deploy-1.4",
    action={"label": "View logs", "page": "logs"},
)

# Inside a chat handler, optionally persist a toast to the Notification Center
await aiui.notify("Report ready", type="success", persist=True, category="chat")

# Inside a BlockPage handler, emit notifications alongside components
return aiui.layout(
    [aiui.card("Status", value="Synced")],
    notifications=[{"title": "Sync finished", "type": "success", "category": "sync"}],
)
```

## Browser Plugin SDK (`@aiui/sdk`)

```tsx
import { notifications, useNotifications } from '@aiui/sdk'

// Push from any browser plugin
notifications.push({
  title: 'Index rebuilt',
  description: '1,240 documents indexed',
  type: 'info',
  category: 'knowledge',
  dedupeKey: 'index-rebuild',
  action: { label: 'Open Knowledge', page: 'knowledge' },
  toast: true,
})

// Subscribe in a custom React component
export function UnreadPill() {
  const { unreadCount, markAllRead } = useNotifications()
  return <button onClick={() => markAllRead()}>Unread: {unreadCount}</button>
}

// Plug in a custom transport / source
const stop = notifications.registerSource('my-plugin', {
  connect(ctx) {
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      ctx.push({ dedupeKey: 'heartbeat', title: 'Worker healthy', type: 'info' })
    }, 60_000)
    return () => clearInterval(timer)
  },
})
```

# Layouts

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts

> A layout is the frame of the React app shell (style: app): the navigation,

A layout is the frame of the React app shell (`style: app`): the navigation,
the session list, the top bar, side panels and the phone chrome. The page
stays the page. Every page (chat, logs, config, a plugin page, a blocks page)
renders inside every layout, in the outlet the shell hands the frame. The
design is [ADR 0003](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-selectable-layouts.md).

Layouts exist only in the app shell. The legacy `dashboard` style is not
affected and renders exactly as before.

## The layouts

| Id | Title | What it is for | Opens on | Primary nav |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chat-canvas` (default) | [Chat and Canvas](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/chat-canvas.md) | Chat beside a canvas of the artifacts the agent makes | `chat` | chat, artifacts, agents, cron, knowledge, sessions, config |
| `chat` | Chat | The Chat and Canvas frame without the canvas or artifact cards (same Paper look); what `aiui run` opens | `chat` | chat, agents, cron, knowledge, sessions, config |
| `workbench` | [Quiet Workbench](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/workbench.md) | A quiet sidebar with your chats, and the page beside it | `chat` | chat, agents, knowledge, runs, config |
| `command` | [Command Deck](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/command.md) | Keyboard first: a command bar, session tabs and a run inspector | `chat` | chat, runs, agents, jobs, config |
| `guided` | [Guided Studio](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/guided.md) | Plain language and large buttons; every step explained | `start` | start, chat, agents, templates |
| `mission` | [Mission Control](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/mission.md) | Agents, runs and approvals at a glance | `overview` | overview, agents, approvals, chat, runs, sessions |

`classic` is not a layout. It is the core's own frame (the sidebar and header
the app shell had before layouts): always available, and the fallback.

A primary nav may name a page that is not there (a disabled record's page,
for example); the shell keeps only the ids the manifest carries.

Each built-in frame is its own design, built on the shared layout kit
(`src/frontend/src/app-layouts/kit/`: nav and session lists, page icons,
the connection line, phone sheet and tabs). Its page above has the regions,
keys, phone frame and the data it reads. The features only one layout uses
are lazy chunks of their own: the run inspector and command bar (Command
Deck), the step tracker (Guided Studio) and the mission board (Mission
Control). The Chat and Canvas frame shows the canvas of artifacts once the
artifacts feature (`layout-features/artifacts`, ADR track A) is in the
build; without it the canvas stays empty.

Each built-in layout is its own lazy chunk (`layout-<id>`), with the kit in
`layout-kit`. The browser downloads only the chunks of the layout on screen;
an inactive layout costs nothing.

## Configuration

Layouts apply to `style: app` only. A layout chosen under another style is
ignored, and the server logs one warning:
`layout ignored: style is 'dashboard'; use style: app`. Choosing a layout
never changes the style.

### YAML

`layout:` is the existing `LayoutConfig`. Its chat position keys (`mode`,
`width`, `height`) keep working. The layout keys are added next to them:

```yaml
style: app
layout: command                  # shorthand for {default: command}
```

```yaml
style: app
layout:
  default: command               # the layout a viewer starts with; classic = the shell's own frame
  available: [command, chat-canvas, workbench]   # offered, in picker order (default: all)
  user_choice: true              # alias userChoice; a viewer's own pick may override default
  primary: [chat, runs, agents, jobs, config]     # primary nav for every layout (at most 7 shown)
  options:                       # per-layout settings, keyed by layout id
    mission: {dailyBudget: 10, environment: prod}
```

- A layout id is lower-case letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter and
  has at most 40 characters. `classic` is reserved: it is a valid `default`,
  never an `available` entry.
- `layout: classic` keeps an app that already used `style: app` on the frame
  it had before.
- A malformed entry never fails the config. The server ignores it with a
  warning, and `aiui validate` reports it as **5103** (for example
  `layout: Bad_Id`, or `available: command` where a list goes). The rest of
  the section still applies.

### Python

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("app")
aiui.set_layout("command", available=["command", "chat-canvas"], user_choice=True)
aiui.set_layout(options={"mission": {"dailyBudget": 10}})   # only the arguments passed change
```

`set_layout(default=None, *, available=None, user_choice=None, primary=None, options=None)`
raises `ValueError` for a malformed id. Call it before the server starts.

### Environment

`AIUI_LAYOUT=<id>` or `AIUI_LAYOUT=classic` sets the default for one run. A
malformed value is ignored with a warning.

## Choosing a layout

**On the server**, the default is the first of these that is set:

1. `AIUI_LAYOUT`
2. `aiui.set_layout()`
3. YAML `layout:`
4. the `aiui run` default: `chat` (only under `aiui run`; `create_app()` and PraisonAI keep the style default)
5. the style default: `chat-canvas` for `style: app`

The shell manifest's `layouts` key carries the layouts the server offers
(`available`), its `default` and whether the viewer may choose
(`userChoice`). A shell that receives no `layouts` key (an older server)
renders the classic frame.

**In the browser**, the shell renders the first of these that the server
offers:

1. A `?layout=<id>` preview. It is kept for the tab (sessionStorage
   `aiui-layout-preview`), so it survives navigation and reload, and it is
   never saved as the viewer's choice. `?layout=classic` previews the classic
   frame. Use it for screenshots and support links.
2. The viewer's own choice (localStorage `aiui-layout`), only when the server
   allows a user choice.
3. The server's default.
4. The classic frame.

A layout the server does not offer is never chosen, whatever is stored.

**The viewer** switches with the command palette ("Switch layout: …", group
"Layout"; one command per offered layout, named after its manifest title, and
Classic; the group is listed after the pages, with Preferences and Theme,
until a query ranks it higher) or with **Settings → Appearance** (a select of the same list, shown
only when the server allows a user choice). The choice is saved in this
browser and applies at once, without a reload: the frame and the page
remount, and chat state is kept. When the server does not allow a choice,
the palette commands still switch, for this tab only. Saving the choice per
user across devices is **(planned)** (no server-side preference store yet).

### Unknown ids

- An `available` id that no enabled plugin declares is dropped, with one
  warning.
- A `default` that is not available falls back to `chat-canvas` when it is
  offered, otherwise to the first available layout, with one warning. With
  nothing available, the shell uses classic.
- `aiui validate` warns with code **5101** for an id that is not a built-in
  layout (a plugin may still provide it; plugin layouts are only known once
  the server runs), **5102** for a layout chosen while the style is not
  `app`, and **5103** for a malformed entry.

### Switching a layout off

Each built-in layout is a first-party record, `builtin.layout-<id>`:

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled: [builtin.layout-mission]
```

A disabled layout leaves the picker and takes its own pages with it.

## Layout pages

A page can belong to a layout. Such a page is `shell_only`, so it is never in
the page table, `GET /api/pages` or the dashboard. It is in the app shell
manifest only while a layout it names is offered. Its manifest row carries
`layouts` (and `replaces`, the page it stands in for while that layout is
active), and its `source` is the owning record, for example
`builtin.layout-guided`. The shell's nav shows such a page only while one of
its layouts is on screen; its URL renders under any layout.

Guided owns `start` (its Home, where `/` opens while Guided is the layout)
and `templates`. Mission's `ops-overview`, which replaces `overview`, arrives
with the Mission frame **(planned)**. A layout record adds a page only with
the frame that renders it.

### React pages inside every layout

Six built-in pages have a React page in the Pro design that renders inside
any layout frame (`src/frontend/src/app-pages/`, one lazy chunk each,
registered by `builtin.overview`, `builtin.sessions`, `builtin.agents`,
`builtin.knowledge`, `builtin.logs`, `builtin.config` and `builtin.cron` with the usual `registerPage`):

| Page | Design | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `overview` | ProOverview | A greeting and one sentence, "Today at a glance" tiles with sparklines, what needs your approval (the approvals feed plus the open chat's gates), agents, recent runs or chats, the model provider, a collapsible feature health list |
| `sessions` | ProList | Search (`/`), status chips, an agent filter, a sortable table (title, agent, messages, tokens, relative time, status), a detail panel, a labelled row menu, Delete with a confirmation |
| `agents` | ProList | Search (`/`), a model filter, one New agent button, a sortable table (monogram, name, description, model, tools, updated, status), a detail panel (temperature, tools, instructions, system prompt, Training history), Edit and New agent in that panel (name, description, model from `/api/agents/models`, temperature, instructions, system prompt), Duplicate, Delete with a confirmation, a skeleton while loading and Try again on an error; agents the app registers in code are read-only; on a phone the panel replaces the list |
| `knowledge` | ProList | A joined stat strip (entries, files, semantic or keyword search, the store with a status chip in plain words), search (`/`) with marked snippets and the relevance the store reports, "Add knowledge" for text or files (drop zone, drag and drop onto the page, per-file progress and errors), a table (name, type, size, added), a detail panel (facts, content, Copy, Delete with a confirmation), Clear all; on a phone the detail replaces the list |
| `logs` | ProLogs | Level toggles with counts, search with match navigation, Pause, Download, Clear with a confirmation |
| `cron` | ProList | Search, status chips, New schedule, a table (schedule in words and as cron, in UTC; next and last run; an enabled switch), a detail panel with recent runs, Run now, Edit and Delete, a builder (every N minutes or hours, daily, weekly, custom cron with the next runs) |
| `config` | ProSettings | A section list, a breadcrumb, shadcn Select / Switch / Input with help for each field, a masked API key with a show toggle, Test connection, a sticky "Unsaved changes" bar |

In the classic frame (`layout: classic`) these pages render their legacy
view exactly as before, and the default `dashboard` style never loads them.

The one layout page shipped today is `artifacts` (`layouts: [chat-canvas]`),
owned by the data record `builtin.artifacts` rather than a layout record: the
index of every chat's artifacts, where the canvas's Share links land. See
[Layout data](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layout-data.md).

## Data that only some layouts need

A first-party record can declare `for_layouts=("command", "mission")`. It is
mounted only while one of those layouts is offered, or while
`extensions.enabled` names it. Otherwise `GET /api/plugins?origin=builtin`
lists it as `disabled` with the reason `no layout needs it`, its routes answer
404 and its feature module is never imported.

## Follow-up suggestions

A reply handler can offer follow-up prompts for the answer it is writing.
They go out on the run's `run_completed` frame as `suggestions` (an optional
field; clients that do not know it ignore it), and a layout that shows
follow-up chips (Guided) renders them:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    await aiui.say("Here is the comparison.")
    aiui.suggest(["Show me a benchmark", "Explain timsort"])
```

A later call replaces the list and `aiui.suggest([])` clears it. Blank
entries are dropped, each prompt is cut to 200 characters and at most 8 are
kept. Outside a chat run the call does nothing.

## Plugin layouts

A plugin adds a layout with the same SDK call the built-ins use,
`registerLayout(id, meta, Frame | loader)`. Its Python side declares it with a
`layouts()` hook, the same way first-party records do:

```python
from praisonaiui import LayoutSpec

class DeckPlugin:
    name = "deck"

    def static_dir(self):
        return Path(__file__).parent / "static"

    def layouts(self):
        return [LayoutSpec(id="deck", title="Deck", module="deck.js", home="chat",
                           primary=("chat", "logs"))]
```

- `module` is required. A relative path resolves into the plugin's static dir
  (`/_plugins/deck/deck.js`, with an SRI hash). That module calls
  `registerLayout("deck", …)`, and the shell imports it only while the layout
  is active.
- An id that another plugin (or a built-in) already provides is ignored with
  a warning, and so is a `classic` or malformed id.
- On a remote or auth-enforced server, an entry-point plugin's layouts follow
  the same default-deny rule as its pages: list the plugin in
  `extensions.enabled`.
- Plugin pages may carry `layouts` and `replaces` too. `shell_only=True`
  keeps a `blocks` page out of `GET /api/pages`.

The browser module, the props a frame receives (`LayoutProps`: `Outlet`,
`nav`, `chrome`, `viewport`, `layout`) and a complete example are in
[UI Plugins → Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md#layouts). The fixture
`src/frontend/e2e/fixtures/layout-plugin/` is a working third-party layout
plugin.

In short, a frame:

- renders `<Outlet />` once, inside a `main` with `id={chrome.mainId}`;
- draws its navigation from `nav` (`primary` at most 7 items, `groups` for the
  rest, `footer`) and navigates with `nav.go(pageId)`;
- uses `chrome.openPalette()` for search and commands (there is one palette),
- lists the groups plugins declared (`nav.groups` entries with `declared: true`,
  kept in order and `folded` as given; the groups of the app's own pages and,
  under `set_pages("all")`, every group are marked the same way from the
  manifest's `layout.groups.shown`) even when it keeps other groups in
  More, and shows a settings entry calling `chrome.openSettings()` when it is
  set (only while some plugin contributes a settings section); the kit's
  `DeclaredNavGroups` and `PluginSettingsRow` draw both,
  and `chrome.Slot` for the shell's slots (`header:actions`, …);
- draws its phone frame when `viewport === 'phone'` (below 768 px), with touch
  targets of at least 44 px;
- reads data such as the session list with `useLayoutData('sessions')`, and
  renders without it when that returns null.

## When a layout fails

A layout whose module fails to import, or whose frame throws while
rendering, is replaced by the classic frame. The viewer sees one toast ("The
"…" layout failed to load"), and the shell fires one `aiui:plugin-error`
window event whose `detail.layout` is the layout id. Other layouts and the
pages are not affected. While a plugin layout is still loading, the shell
shows a frame skeleton; a selected layout that no plugin ever registers falls
back to the classic frame with a console warning.

## Isolation and budgets

These rules keep layouts independent (ARCHITECTURE.md R17):

- every layout lives in `src/frontend/src/app-layouts/<id>/` and is built as
  the chunk `layout-<id>`; shared pieces live in `app-layouts/kit/`
  (`layout-kit`), never copied; layout-specific features live in
  `src/frontend/src/layout-features/<name>/` (`lf-<name>`) **(planned: none
  exist yet)**;
- a layout never imports another layout or the shell, and loads a feature only
  with `import()`;
- the core (`shell/`, `sdk/`, `legacy/`, `blocks/`) names no layout id and
  imports neither folder (`shell/core-purity.test.ts`);
- the boot path loads no layout chunk, and a layout's closure contains no other
  layout, no feature, and no Streamdown, Shiki, Mermaid, KaTeX or
  `@assistant-ui` (`scripts/check-layout-isolation.mjs`, part of
  `npm run check:closure`); in the browser,
  `e2e/specs/layouts-host.spec.ts` checks that each layout downloads only its
  own chunks and the kit.

**Looks on first paint.** The server writes `data-aiui-tokens="pro"` on
the app shell's `<html>` when there is a default layout, and also the layout's
look (`data-aiui-look="paper"` for Chat and Canvas and Chat, from the
catalog record's `look`). The page then paints Paper and fetches only the
Paper fonts, never Geist first. An inline script drops the look before first
paint for a viewer who will not see it: one who chose plain Pro
("Switch look: Pro"), or one whose `?layout=`, tab preview or stored pick
(with `user_choice`) is another layout. The layout host clears it for a frame
without a look (the classic frame drops the Pro tokens, and the look's CSS
applies only with them).

Each layout, the kit and the `/chat` first screen with the default layout
have gzip budgets in `src/frontend/.size-limit.mjs` (listed in
ARCHITECTURE.md R10). `npm run size` fails when a budgeted layout or the kit
is missing from the build.

## The manifest

`GET /api/shell/manifest` has a top-level `layouts` key (`ShellLayouts` in
`src/frontend/src/sdk/manifest.ts`):

```json
{"default": "chat-canvas", "userChoice": true,
 "available": [{"id": "chat-canvas", "title": "Chat and Canvas", "description": "…", "order": 10,
                "home": "chat", "primary": ["chat", "artifacts", "…"], "source": "builtin"}]}
```

Outside `style: app` it is `{"default": "", "userChoice": true, "available": []}`, which the
shell reads as classic.

# Chat and Canvas layout

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/chat-canvas

> chat-canvas is the default layout of the React app shell (style: app).

`chat-canvas` is the default layout of the React app shell (`style: app`).
The chat is on the left; the tables, code and files the agent makes sit on a
canvas beside it, where you can sort, copy, download and compare versions.
See [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) for how layouts are chosen, and
[ADR 0003](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-selectable-layouts.md) for the design.

![The Chat and Canvas layout in dark mode, in its Paper look: the conversation on the left with a pending approval, and on the right the canvas split between the comparison table and the sort_demo.py script the agent wrote](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/images/app-shell-chat-canvas-dark.webp)

```yaml
style: app
layout: chat-canvas        # the default for style: app; this line is optional
```

## What is on screen

**Desktop and tablet**

| Region | What it holds |
|---|---|
| Sidebar (240 px) | The site name and a collapse button (⌘B / Ctrl+B); **New chat** (⌘N / Ctrl+N); the primary pages (chat, artifacts, agents, cron, knowledge, sessions, config; the Artifacts row shows how many artifacts exist across chats); **Chats**, your conversations as two-line rows (the title over "3 artifacts · now"), with a search button, the open one raised, a running one marked "Working…"; at the foot **Settings** (the config page), **More** (⌘K), which opens the command palette with every other page (the footer pages such as Inspector among them) and command, and the connection line ("Connected · local" when the server is this machine). |
| Top bar | On the chat page: the open chat's title over "Researcher · 3 artifacts · edited 2 min ago" (the agent of the latest answer, the chat's artifacts, their latest change; "reconnecting" joins it while the chat's connection is down). On other pages: the page title. Then **Search or run a command** (⌘K), on the chat page the **Canvas** toggle (pressed while the canvas is open, with the artifact count), **Share** (copies the link; a chat's link opens that chat) and the light/dark switch. |
| The page | Any page renders here. The chat page uses speech-bubble messages under a header with the agent's letter tile, name and time; each tool call is one compact row (the call in mono, "→" and the first line of its output, its state, how long it took); "Thought for 2s" is a quiet disclosure; explained approval cards (the tool and its risk with Details, "Researcher wants to run a command" and why, the exact `$ command`, then **Approve**, **Deny**, "Why am I asked?" and "Paused until you choose"); the composer has the message on two rows ("Ask a follow-up, or type @ to edit an artifact") above attach, **@**, the model and a round Send in the accent (lighter, and `aria-disabled`, while there is nothing to send); **@** (or typing @) lists this chat's artifacts, and a choice puts a plain-text mention such as `@"Model table"` in the message for the agent to read; and, when the artifacts feature is installed, the **Canvas** panel on the right. A new chat starts with the canvas collapsed; it opens once the chat has an artifact, and the toggle opens or closes it at any time. The "Chat + Canvas" page (`/chat-canvas`) is the same React chat in the app shell. |

Open, the canvas is the main surface: it takes about 58% of the chat page
and the chat a narrower column (never under about 400 px); with the canvas
closed the chat is a centred column. On a tablet the canvas starts closed.
Drag the gap between the chat and the canvas (or focus it and use the arrow
keys, Home and End) to resize it; the share is kept in this browser. Hiding the sidebar is kept in this browser too.

**Phone**

A header with the menu (the sidebar's contents in a sheet, with 44 px rows),
the chat title centred over "Mock · gpt-4o-mini" (the agent and the model the composer shows), and New chat. Approval cards
split the width into **Deny | Approve** (44 px), and the composer keeps the
model on its bottom row. On the chat page a
**Chat | Canvas (n)** switch flips between the conversation and the canvas.

## The look

The layout paints with its own look, **Paper** (the design board's palette
and type): warm paper neutrals with a navy accent in light and dark, titles,
the wordmark (and a serif "P" on the ink brand tile), artifact titles and table row headers in Newsreader, text in
Source Sans 3 and code in JetBrains Mono. The fonts ship with aiui (no font
CDN) and download only while the look is on. The `chat` layout (this frame
without the canvas) has the same look; every other layout, and the classic
frame, keep their own.

- Prefer the plain Pro look? Open the command palette (⌘K) and run
  **Switch look: Pro**; **Switch look: Paper** brings it back. The choice is
  saved in this browser.
- A brand colour (`theme.accent`, `aiui.set_brand_color(...)`) and the Pro
  accent presets replace the navy accent; the paper neutrals stay.
- Theme authors: the look is `<html data-aiui-look="paper">` with the tokens
  in `src/frontend/src/styles/paper.css`; see DESIGN.md "Looks".

## Artifacts and the canvas

The canvas, the artifact cards under each answer and the artifacts index page
come from the artifacts feature (`layout-features/artifacts`, record
`builtin.artifacts`). The layout loads that code only on the chat page, and
works without it: with the feature missing from the build, or switched off,
the chat page has no canvas and everything else stays.

The canvas (Canvas.dc.html): a tab per artifact with its kind icon, then
the split toggle, **+** (open another of this chat's artifacts below the
shown one, or All artifacts), expand and close. The shown artifact has its
title, kind and time, the version menu ("v2 · edited by Researcher"), Copy,
Download and Share; a table sorts by any column header; History (each
version, who made it, what changed, Restore) sits on the right, and folds
under the viewer on a phone. When the chat has code next to a table or a
document, the code docks below it (Run ⌘↵ and its Output strip, "Ran 1 min
ago · 0.02s", when the server can run it) until you close the split.

Each artifact shows once. While the canvas is there, a code block or table
that is an artifact (3+ lines of code, a table with 2+ rows)
leaves the reply: the reply shows its card ("Comparison table · Table ·
3 rows · v2 · edited by Researcher · In canvas"), and a card opens the
artifact in the canvas (on a phone, the Canvas side). Shorter snippets stay
in the reply. Choose `artifactsInChat: inline` to keep the blocks in the
reply as well, a long code block cut to its first 12 lines and a long table
to its first 6 rows (the rest scrolls inside the block):

```yaml
layout:
  default: chat-canvas
  options:
    chat-canvas: {artifactsInChat: inline, collapseLines: 20, collapseRows: 10}
```

The `chat` layout has no canvas and keeps every block in the reply.

## Turning parts off

- `extensions.disabled: [builtin.artifacts]`: no canvas, no Artifacts page;
  the rest of the layout is unchanged.
- `extensions.disabled: [builtin.approvals]`: no approval toasts; the
  approval card in the thread still decides the gate.
- `extensions.disabled: [builtin.layout-chat-canvas]`: the layout is not
  offered; the app shell opens on the next offered layout, or the classic
  frame.

## For plugin and theme authors

- The frame is the chunk `layout-chat-canvas`. It imports only the SDK,
  `components/ui`, `lib` and the layout kit, and loads the artifacts feature
  with `import()`.
- Styling hooks: `[data-aiui-layout-frame="chat-canvas"]` on the frame
  (`data-viewport` is `phone`, `tablet` or `desktop`), `[data-cc-title]` and
  `[data-cc-subtitle]` in the top bar, `[data-aiui-aside-slot]` (where the
  chat's aside toggle is portalled; without it the toggle stays in the chat's
  own header), `[data-cc-chat-meta]` on a chat row's second line, `[data-aiui-session]` on chat rows,
  `[data-aiui-nav-item]` on nav rows.
- The shell's `header:actions` slot is at the end of the top bar and
  `sidebar:footer` at the foot of the sidebar.
- `[data-in-canvas]` marks a reply block that is shown as its card
  (`data-cc-artifacts="card"` on the frame hides it); the window event
  `aiui:chat-aside` (`{open: true}` / `{open: false}`) opens or closes the
  chat's aside, as an artifact card does.
- The artifacts feature plugs in through files the layout looks for:
  `layout-features/artifacts/CanvasPanel.tsx` (the canvas, a chat region),
  `ArtifactCards.tsx` (the cards under an answer, a turn region) and
  `feed.ts` (the `artifacts` data feed, exported as `artifactsFeed` or as
  the default export).

# Quiet Workbench layout

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/workbench

> A calm sidebar with your chats, a focused top bar and the page beside it. It

A calm sidebar with your chats, a focused top bar and the page beside it. It
suits people who live in one conversation at a time and want nothing else on
screen. It is one of the [layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) of the React app shell
(`style: app`); the default `dashboard` style is not affected.

![The Quiet Workbench layout: the chats in a quiet sidebar and the conversation beside it](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/images/app-shell-workbench-light.webp)

```yaml
style: app
layout: workbench
```

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("app")
aiui.set_layout("workbench")
```

To try it without changing the server, open any page with
`?layout=workbench` (a preview for this browser tab), or pick
**Switch layout: Quiet Workbench** in the command palette (⌘K). `AIUI_LAYOUT=workbench`
sets it for the whole server.

## What is on screen

### Desktop and tablet (768 px and wider)

**Sidebar (256 px)**

- the site's logo and title, and a button that collapses the sidebar
  (⌘B; the choice is kept in this browser);
- **New chat** (⌘N);
- the layout's primary pages, each with its icon; the current one is
  highlighted. By default these are chat, agents, knowledge, runs and config;
  `layout.primary` in YAML replaces the list (at most 7 are shown, and only
  pages the server has);
- **Search and more** (⌘K), the one command palette;
- every other page through **Search and more ⌘K** (the palette), so nothing is out of reach and no bare "More (n)" row sits in the sidebar;
- **Chats**: a search box and your chats, newest first, each with when it
  was last active (Now, 2h, Yesterday, Mon, Jan 5). A chat with a reply in
  progress says *Running*; one with an approval waiting says *Waiting*;
- footer pages (if any), the connection line and the light or dark switch.

**Top bar (56 px)**

- the title: the open chat's title on the chat page (*New chat* before the
  first message), otherwise the page's title;
- on the chat page, the agent that answers and, when the agent has a
  definition with a model, the model (`Researcher · gpt-4o-mini`);
- the `header:actions` slot, so plugins can add buttons here;
- **Share**, which copies a link to the page, and **More**, which opens the
  palette.

### Phone (narrower than 768 px)

- a header with the menu button, the title with the agent and model under it,
  and a new chat button (all at least 44 px);
- the menu opens the sidebar as a sheet with the same contents, with 44 px
  rows and 15 px text. Opening a page or a chat closes it.

## The chat inside it

The layout asks the chat page to present itself quietly:

| Setting | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions` | `frame` | the chat page draws no session list of its own; the sidebar's **Chats** is the list |
| `thread` | `quiet` | your question sits in a full-width quiet box; the answer is plain prose; reasoning and tool steps are single ghost rows you can open |
| `approvals` | `inline` | an approval request appears in the answer with **Approve** and **Deny** |

The top bar names the open chat, so the chat page's own title is kept for
screen readers only, and its title row steps aside while the connection is
open. If the server offers agents to choose from, or the connection drops,
that row comes back with the agent picker or the connection badge.

## When a feature is off

The frame reads its data from the layout feeds (see
[Layout data](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layout-data.md)) and hides the part whose feed is off; it
never fails:

- with the chat page (`builtin.chat`) disabled there is no New chat button
  and no chat list, and the title is the page's;
- with approvals (`builtin.approvals`) disabled no chat is marked *Waiting*;
- with no agent definitions (`/api/agents/definitions` answering 404 or
  without a `model`), the top bar shows the agent without a model.

## Keyboard

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| ⌘N / Ctrl+N | New chat (also while typing). Some browsers keep this shortcut for a new window; the button always works |
| ⌘B / Ctrl+B | Collapse or expand the sidebar (desktop) |
| ⌘K / Ctrl+K | Search pages and commands |

## For developers

- Frame: `src/frontend/src/app-layouts/workbench/` (`Frame.tsx`, the view
  model in `model.ts`, `workbench.css`), built as the lazy chunk
  `layout-workbench`. It imports only the SDK, `components/ui`, `lib` and the
  layout kit (`app-layouts/kit`); see R17 in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- Descriptor: `src/frontend/src/builtin/layouts/workbench.ts` (title and the
  chat presentation above). The Python record is `builtin.layout-workbench`
  (`home: chat`, the primary list); `extensions.disabled:
  [builtin.layout-workbench]` removes the layout from the picker.
- Tests: `app-layouts/workbench/workbench.test.tsx` (view model, shortcuts,
  the frame on a desktop and a phone, with feeds off) and
  `e2e/specs/layout-workbench.spec.ts` (the scripted conversation on a
  desktop and a phone in light and dark, an inline approval, a page in the
  outlet, 44 px targets, network isolation and the leak probe).
- Design: `Main.dc.html` and `QuietPhone.dc.html`, drawn in the PraisonAI Pro
  tokens (`src/frontend/DESIGN.md`).
