# Command Deck layout

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/command

> The Command Deck (command) is the keyboard-first layout of the app shell

The Command Deck (`command`) is the keyboard-first layout of the app shell
(`style: app`). It has a command bar on top, an icon rail, session tabs, a
run inspector beside the chat and a status bar. Every page still renders in
its outlet. For layouts in general, see [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md).

```yaml
style: app
layout: command
```

Other ways to choose it: `aiui.set_layout("command")`, `AIUI_LAYOUT=command`,
`?layout=command` (a preview for this browser tab), Settings → Appearance, or
the palette command "Switch layout: Command Deck".

## What is on screen

| Region | What it does |
|---|---|
| Command bar | "Ask or run a command". Enter sends the text in the open chat (a new chat when none is open) and opens the chat page; a chat feed without `send` puts it in the composer instead. Typing `/` or `>` first opens the command palette with the rest typed in. ⌘K in the bar opens the palette with the bar's text. `/` anywhere outside a text field focuses the bar. The `@Agent` chip names the agent of the open chat. |
| Approvals button | "n approvals waiting", while any are pending. It opens the session the approval waits in, with the run panel. The layout shows approvals itself, so no approval toasts appear. |
| Icon rail | The layout's primary pages (at most seven; YAML `layout.primary` overrides them), each with a G-prefix key shown in its tooltip. "More" opens the palette for every other page. ⌘/ lists all shortcuts. The Runs item shows a count of active runs. |
| Session tabs (chat page) | The newest nine sessions, with the open one always included. An amber dot means the session waits for an approval; a blue dot means it is running. `+` starts a new chat. The right end shows the session id and the Run panel toggle. |
| Run inspector (chat page) | The open chat's latest run: status, run id and Stop; the pending approval with Approve, Deny and "Always allow"; elapsed time, tokens, cost and steps; the Steps timeline with a bar for each step; the files the run's tools touched. On a desktop it starts open, on a tablet closed. |
| Status bar | Online or offline and the host; the agent; active runs and pending approvals; today's tokens and cost; the ⌘K and ⌘/ hints. |

The chat page in this layout draws no session list of its own (the tabs are
the list). It uses the dense thread (the question as a `›` prompt line, a
monospace meta line with the run id, monospace tool rows) and the keyboard
approval strip ("Paused: … wants to run …", A and D).

## Keyboard

`mod` is ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. Single keys never fire
while you type in a field.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `mod` K | Commands and pages (the palette) |
| `/` | Focus the command bar |
| `mod` N | New chat |
| `mod` 1–9 | Switch to that session tab |
| `mod` I | Show or hide the run panel |
| `mod` / | All shortcuts |
| G, then a letter | Go to a rail page: G C Chat, G R Runs, G A Agents, G J Jobs, G S Config. Other pages take a free letter of their title. |
| J / K | Next or previous step in the run panel |
| Enter | Expand the focused step (its reasoning or tool result) |
| A / D | Approve or deny the pending approval |
| F | Jump to the files touched |
| Ctrl C | Stop the run (only when no text is selected) |

The palette also lists "Show or hide the run panel", "Keyboard shortcuts",
"Stop the run" while a run is going, and "Approve: …" and "Deny: …" for the
open chat's pending approval.

Browsers keep some of these combinations for themselves. For example,
Chrome uses ⌘N and ⌘1–9 itself. Where the browser takes a key first, use
the buttons or the palette instead.

## Phone

Below 768 px the deck becomes a phone frame (CommandPhone):

- The top row holds the menu, the command bar and New chat. The menu opens
  a sheet with any approvals waiting (each with Deny and Approve), the rail
  pages, the other pages, the sessions and the theme switch. An amber dot
  on the menu button means approvals are waiting.
- On the chat page, a switcher row shows the open session and an `n/m`
  counter. Tapping it opens the same sheet.
- The run inspector becomes a peek at the bottom: the run status, steps and
  cost, and the pending approval with 44 px Deny and Approve buttons. Tap
  the peek to expand it into the whole inspector.

Every touch target is at least 44 px, and body text is at least 15 px.

## Data and what happens when a part is off

The frame reads the shell's layout data feeds (`useLayoutData`):

| Feed | Provider | Without it |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions` | `builtin.chat` | No tabs, no switcher, no session list in the sheet |
| `chat` | `builtin.chat` | The run inspector shows "Run details appear here when chat is on"; Enter in the bar opens the palette instead |
| `approvals` | `builtin.approvals` | Approvals come only from the open chat's gates. "Always allow" is hidden. |
| run ledger | `builtin.run-ledger` (mounted only when `command` or `mission` is offered) | Tokens and cost read "—"; no usage in the status bar |

Tokens and cost come from the run ledger (`GET /api/runs/{id}`). The
inspector asks for them again whenever the run changes state, because
there is no wire event for usage. Steps and timings come from the chat
stream itself. Files touched are read from the tools' arguments: `path`,
`file`, `file_path` and similar keys, and shell writes (`>`, `tee`,
`touch`, `mkdir`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`).

## Code

| Part | Where | Chunk |
|---|---|---|
| Descriptor (eager, tiny) | `src/frontend/src/builtin/layouts/command.ts` | boot |
| Frame | `src/frontend/src/app-layouts/command/` | `layout-command` |
| Command bar | `src/frontend/src/layout-features/command-bar/` | `lf-command-bar` |
| Run inspector | `src/frontend/src/layout-features/run-inspector/` | `lf-run-inspector` |

The frame loads both features with `import()`. On the chat page the
browser downloads `layout-command`, `layout-kit`, `lf-command-bar` and
`lf-run-inspector`; on any other page, everything but `lf-run-inspector`.
No other layout's code is downloaded. The features never import the kit:
the frame passes them its typing check and platform. A feature that
imported the kit would split the kit into one more chunk for every layout.

Budgets (gzip, `npm run size`, measured plus 10%): `layout-command` 15.2 kB
(its closure minus boot, with the kit pieces it imports; ADR cap 24 kB),
`lf-run-inspector` 9.2 kB (cap 14 kB), `lf-command-bar` 1.6 kB (cap 6 kB).

The frame uses only part of the kit (not `BasicFrame` or `ShortcutHint`), so
Rollup splits the kit into chunks by which frames use which pieces (seven
with all five frames in the build); each frame's closure holds the ones it
imports. The kit's budget is 8.3 kB.

The tests are `app-layouts/command/*.test.ts(x)` (the frame model, the
render and the data helpers), `layout-features/run-inspector/*.test.ts(x)`
(steps, files, formats, the panel and the peek),
`layout-features/command-bar/bar.test.tsx`, and
`e2e/specs/layout-command.spec.ts` in the browser. That spec runs in the
`layouts-host` Playwright project, against the layouts server, with
`e2e/specs/layouts-host.spec.ts` (whose network-isolation case allows this
layout exactly `lf-command-bar` and `lf-run-inspector`):

```bash
cd src/frontend && npm run build
npx playwright test -c e2e/fixtures/layout-plugin/playwright.config.ts
```

## Not in this version

- **A Files destination.** The design's rail has one, but no files page
  exists. Files touched still appear in the inspector.
- **Per-step tokens.** The ledger records tokens per run, not per step, so
  the answer step shows a word count instead.

# Guided Studio layout

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/guided

> Guided Studio (guided) is the app shell layout for people new to AI

Guided Studio (`guided`) is the app shell layout for people new to AI
agents. It uses plain words and large buttons, and explains every step the
agent takes. It is one of the [selectable layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) of the
React app shell (`style: app`); the default `dashboard` style is not
affected.

```yaml
style: app
layout: guided
```

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("app")
aiui.set_layout("guided")
```

Or set `AIUI_LAYOUT=guided`, or preview it in one tab with `?layout=guided`.

## What it looks like

**Desktop.** A 280 px sidebar holds:

- the app name;
- a large **Start a new chat** button (⌘N / Ctrl+N);
- five destinations: **Home**, **Chat**, **My agents**, **Templates** and
  **Help**;
- **Your recent chats**, the newest five as cards ("Today, 2:14 pm · with
  Researcher"), with **See all** when the server has a sessions page;
- every other page, folded under **More tools**;
- **Settings** and a light/dark switch at the bottom.

The header names the open chat and who it is with: "Chatting with
Researcher · ready to help", or "working on it" and "waiting for your OK"
while a reply runs or waits. **Search ⌘K** opens the command palette.
**Change agent** opens the chat's agent picker, or My agents when the chat
offers no choice of agent.

**Phone** (narrower than 768 px). A 60 px header holds a menu button (your
chats, the other pages, Settings), the chat's title and a **Start a new chat**
button. Four bottom tabs follow the page: **Home**, **Chat**, **My agents**
and **Help**. Every target is at least 44 px and the text at least 15 px.

The layout paints with the PraisonAI Pro tokens. The pickable Pro accents
(Settings → Appearance, or the theme presets) recolour it.

## The chat

Guided changes how the chat page presents itself, not what it does.

| Part | What you see |
|---|---|
| Step tracker | Above each answer: "Here is what Researcher did", numbered steps in plain words, a short result for each step, and "All done in 3 seconds". **Show details** lists the raw calls: the tool, what it ran, what came back, and how long it took. |
| Approvals | The explained approval card, inside the answer right under its text and before the message actions (desktop and phone): the tool and its risk with **Details** for the arguments, what the agent wants to do, what it will run (a `$ command` line for a shell command), then **Approve** / **Deny** and **Why am I asked?**. The card is the tool's row, so the request is shown once; the step tracker shows the step as "Waiting for your OK". |
| Follow-up chips | Under the latest finished answer, "You could ask next" offers the run's suggestions. A chip puts its text in the message box, ready to send. |
| Empty chat | "Pick a template to get started" and four templates. |
| Thread | Larger type, a labelled "You" bubble, and an avatar on each answer. |

### Step labels

Each step gets a plain label. The first rule that matches wins:

1. The server's own label for the step (the tool event's `label`).
2. The tool's name:

| Tool name contains | Label |
|---|---|
| shell, exec, terminal, bash, command | Running a command |
| search, lookup (documents, memory, knowledge: "Searching your documents") | Searching the web |
| fetch, browse, visit, url, or a `url` argument | Visiting python.org |
| write, save, edit with file | Saving report.csv |
| read, open, load with file | Reading report.csv |
| anything else | Using Get weather |

Thinking is "Understanding your question" ("thought for 2s"). The answer is
"Writing the answer". An approval the agent waits on is "Waiting for your
OK". A step's short result is the first line of what it returned, cut at 40
characters. Machine output (JSON) is said as a count, such as "2 hits", or
left out; **Show details** still has the raw result.

### Follow-up suggestions

Chips appear only when the server sends suggestions with the finished run
(`run_completed.suggestions`). From Python:

```python
@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message):
    ...
    aiui.suggest(["Show a mergesort example", "Explain Big-O in plain words"])
```

With no suggestions, no chips are shown.

## Templates

Templates are the app's chat starters (`GET /starters`). Besides `label`
and `message`, a starter may carry three optional fields: `category`,
`description` and `icon` (an emoji). The Templates page groups starters by
`category`, and each card shows its `description` and `icon`.

```python
@aiui.starters
def starters():
    return [
        {"label": "Weekly metrics", "message": "Show this week's metrics",
         "category": "Analyse", "description": "Charts of the week", "icon": "📊"},
        {"label": "Draft a reply", "message": "Draft a friendly reply to ", "category": "Write"},
    ]
```

A starter without a `category` is listed under "More ideas". With no
starters configured, Guided offers a short plain-language set: summarise,
draft an email, explain, compare, plan, brainstorm, write code, and look at
numbers.

Using a template opens a new chat with the prompt in the message box. You
can change the words before you send. Nothing is sent for you.

## Pages

| Page | Id | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Home | `start` | A welcome, Start a new chat, popular templates, your recent chats, and how a chat works here |
| Templates | `templates` | Every template by category, with a search box and category filters |

Both are shell-only pages of `builtin.layout-guided`. They are never in the
dashboard or `/api/pages`. The nav lists them only while Guided is on, but
their URLs open under any layout. `/` opens on Home while Guided is the
layout; `layout.defaultPage` still wins.

## Options

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `layout.options.guided.helpUrl` | Where **Help** goes: an `http(s)` address (opens in a new tab) or a site path. Without it, Help opens the command palette. |
| `layout.primary` | Replaces the primary destinations (Home, Chat, My agents, Templates), at most 7. |

```yaml
style: app
layout:
  default: guided
  options:
    guided:
      helpUrl: https://docs.example.com/getting-started
```

## Switching it off

`extensions: {disabled: [builtin.layout-guided]}` removes the layout from
the picker and its two pages from the manifest.

With other records off, Guided degrades instead of failing:

- with `builtin.chat` off, there is no chat list and no Start a new chat;
- with `builtin.approvals` off, there are no approval toasts on other pages
  (the chat still shows its own approval card).

## Loading

Guided downloads only what is on screen:

| Chunk | When it loads |
|---|---|
| `layout-guided` | The frame, when Guided is the layout. Its chat regions and pages are their own chunks in the same group, fetched when shown. |
| `layout-kit` | Shared layout pieces, with the frame. |
| `lf-step-tracker` | With the first answer on screen. |

No other layout's code is fetched. The isolation gate
(`npm run check:closure`) and `e2e/specs/layout-guided.spec.ts` check this.

## Source

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Descriptor (meta, chat presentation, pages) | `src/frontend/src/builtin/layouts/guided.ts` |
| Frame, regions, pages, templates | `src/frontend/src/app-layouts/guided/` |
| Step tracker and its labels | `src/frontend/src/layout-features/step-tracker/` |
| Python record | `builtin.layout-guided` in `src/praisonaiui/builtin/catalog.py` |
| Designs | `Guided.dc.html`, `GuidedPhone.dc.html` (on the Pro tokens) |

# Mission Control layout

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts/mission

> Mission Control (mission) is the operations view of the app shell: every agent's status,

Mission Control (`mission`) is the operations view of the app shell: every agent's status,
today's runs and cost, and what waits on you, before anything else. It is one of the built-in
[selectable layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) (ADR 0003, record `builtin.layout-mission`).

```yaml
style: app
layout: mission                                   # or, with an environment badge:
layout: {default: mission, options: {mission: {environment: prod}}}
```

```python
aiui.set_style("app")
aiui.set_layout("mission", options={"mission": {"environment": "prod"}})
```

A viewer can also pick it from the palette ("Switch layout: Mission Control") or Settings →
Appearance, and `?layout=mission` previews it for one tab.

## What is on screen

| Where | Desktop (1024 px and up) | Phone (under 768 px) |
|---|---|---|
| Top | Site title, the `environment` badge, search (opens the command palette), provider health, the approvals bell with its count, theme | Site title with health and environment, search, the approvals bell (44 px buttons) |
| Navigation | A 216 px column: the layout's primary pages with counts (agents, runs today, waiting approvals as a warning badge), the other pages folded under 11px uppercase group headers, "More pages ⌘K"; the top bar's pill is the one status indicator ("Connected") | Bottom tabs: the first four primary pages (Overview, Agents, Approvals with its badge, Chat) and More, which opens a sheet with the rest of the nav and the recent chats |
| Home (`/overview`) | The ops overview: approval request cards, today's KPI strip, the agents (waiting first), recent runs | Approval cards first, then the KPI strip and "Tap an agent to open its chat" |
| Chat | The ops column (KPI strip, agent cards, the selected agent's sessions and New chat) beside the chat; a chat header with the session title, Running / Waiting for approval, the agent, run id and start time, Open runs and Stop run | The chat, with the approval banner above it |
| Any page | The approval banner while something waits; the page renders in the frame's outlet under a title row | The approval banner, then the page |

Tablet widths use the desktop frame without the ops column.

### Approvals everywhere

Mission sets `meta.approvals: 'frame'`, so `builtin.approvals` stops toasting while Mission is on
screen: the frame shows every pending approval itself.

- **Banner**, on every page except the overview (which lists them) and the approvals page: the
  oldest pending approval ("Coder needs your approval to continue", the exact call, its risk, how
  long it has waited, how many more wait) with Review, Deny and Approve. When nothing is listed in
  `/api/approvals` but a run is paused on a gate in the open chat, the banner shows that gate on
  the other pages with Open chat. The banner is a region named by its title, and only the title
  is live: a screen reader announces it when an approval appears, not each tick of the timer.
- **Nav badge and bell**: the number of pending approvals.
- **Agent card**: an agent with a pending approval (listed, or a gate in the open chat) shows as
  "Waiting for approval" with the call and a waiting timer, and is listed first.
- **Overview**: one request card per pending approval ("Needs approval · Coder wants to run a
  command", the call, the reason, Deny / Approve, in the banner's order).
- **Thread**: the chat draws gates as approval cards (`meta.chat.approvals: 'card'`).

<kbd>⌘</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>J</kbd> moves focus to the banner's Approve button;
<kbd>⌘</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>N</kbd> starts a new chat. In a browser tab most browsers keep
<kbd>⌘</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>N</kbd> for a new window and the page never sees it; use the
ops column's New chat button there (the shortcut works in an installed app window).

### Run timeline

Above each answer the chat shows the run's steps (`meta.chat.turnHeader`): Think, each tool by
name, Answer, Handoff → *agent* and Approval pending, each as wide as the time it took, with its
duration (a waiting gate counts up as `0:42`). The steps are derived in the browser from the
turn's own parts and their timing, so the timeline needs no server call.

## Data it reads

| Data | Source | When it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| KPIs (runs today and the change, success rate, cost against the FinOps daily budget, p50 / p95 latency), agent status, recent runs | The `runs` layout data kind. Until a browser built-in provides it, the mission board reads the run ledger's routes itself (`GET /api/runs/kpis?window=today`, `/api/runs/agents`, `/api/runs?limit=10`), every 5 s while the tab is visible and on approval events, and stops when Mission is switched away | `builtin.run-ledger` off (the routes answer 404): "Run history is off on this server", no counts in the nav |
| Pending approvals | The `approvals` layout data kind (`builtin.approvals`, its own `/api/approvals/stream`) | No banner, no badge |
| Sessions and the open chat | The `sessions` and `chat` kinds (`builtin.chat`) | No session list or chat header details |
| Health pill | `GET /api/provider/health` every 30 s | "Status unknown" |

See [layout data](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layout-data.md) for the run ledger's routes and gating: it is mounted while
`command` or `mission` is on offer.

## Chat presentation

| `meta.chat` | Value |
|---|---|
| `sessions` | `frame` (the ops column draws the agent's sessions) |
| `thread` | `dense` |
| `approvals` | `card` |
| `turnHeader` | the run timeline (`RunTimeline`, from the mission board's entry) |

## Code and chunks

| Piece | Path | Chunk | Loaded |
|---|---|---|---|
| Descriptor | `src/frontend/src/builtin/layouts/mission.ts` | boot (a few lines) | always (registers the layout; downloads nothing) |
| Frame | `src/frontend/src/app-layouts/mission/` | `layout-mission` | when Mission is on screen |
| Mission board | `src/frontend/src/layout-features/mission-board/` | `lf-mission-board` (one chunk) | with `import()` the first time the frame shows a board part (the run feed, the ops column, the overview, the banner or the run timeline); cached after that |

The frame imports only the SDK, `components/ui`, `lib` and the layout kit, and the board only with
`import()` of its one entry, `mission-board/index.ts` (R17), so the board builds as a single chunk:
one request, not one per part. Budgets (`.size-limit.mjs`, gzip): `layout-mission` 13.2 kB (kit included),
`lf-mission-board` 11.8 kB. Every board part sits behind its own error boundary: a part that fails to load
or render disappears and the frame keeps working.

## The ops overview page

The home of Mission is `overview`. While no catalog page replaces it, the frame shows the ops
overview there itself. The `ops-overview` page record (`shell_only`, `layouts: [mission]`,
`replaces: overview`) is **(planned)**: once the catalog carries it, `/overview` resolves to it under
Mission (shell `resolveRoutePage`) and the frame shows the same board for it.

# Layout data: run ledger and artifacts

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layout-data

> Two built-in records serve data that only the selectable layouts read. Each lives in

Two built-in records serve data that only the selectable [layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) read. Each lives in
its own feature module and mounts only while a layout that needs it is on offer:

| Record | Module | Serves layouts | Routes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `builtin.run-ledger` | `features/run_ledger.py` | `command`, `mission` | `/api/runs*` |
| `builtin.artifacts` | `features/artifacts.py` | `chat-canvas` | `/api/artifacts*` |

## When they are mounted

- Under `style: app` every layout is on offer by default, so both records are on.
- `layout.available` (YAML) or `aiui.set_layout(available=[...])` narrows the offer. With
  `available: [chat-canvas]` only `builtin.artifacts` mounts, and with `available: [mission]` only
  `builtin.run-ledger` does.
- Under any other style (`dashboard`, the standalone default, or `chat`) no layout is on offer.
  Both records are then `disabled` with the reason `no layout needs it` in
  `/api/plugins?origin=builtin`. Their modules are never imported and their routes answer 404.
- `extensions.enabled: [builtin.run-ledger]` mounts a record whatever the layouts are.
- `extensions.disabled` always wins.

`builtin.artifacts` owns one page, `artifacts` (`shell_only`, `kind: native`,
`layouts: [chat-canvas]`): every chat's artifacts, newest first, with their versions. The React
page is `layout-features/artifacts/ArtifactsPage` (chunk `lf-artifacts`), registered lazily by the
browser built-in `builtin.artifacts` (`src/frontend/src/builtin/artifacts.ts`) only while the
manifest lists the page. The shell shows it in the nav while Chat and Canvas is the frame, and its
URL (where Share links land, `/artifacts?session=…&artifact=…&v=…`) renders under any layout. Like
every `shell_only` page it reaches the app shell manifest only, never `/api/pages` or the
dashboard. `builtin.run-ledger` adds no page.

Every route is authenticated in all three auth modes, like any other `/api/*` route. None is
public.

## Run ledger

The ledger keeps one record per chat run: its session, agent, start and end, status
(`running`, `waiting`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`), its steps (`reasoning`, `tool`,
`text`, `approval`, `handoff`), and the tokens, cost and model of the run's usage records. It adds
no wire event. A client reads the ledger after `run_completed`.

| Route | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/runs?after=&agent=&session_id=&limit=` | `{runs: RunSummary[], count}`, newest first (`limit` 1–500, default 50) |
| `GET /api/runs/{run_id}` | `RunDetail` with its steps, or 404 |
| `GET /api/runs/kpis?window=today\|24h\|7d` | `RunKpis`; any other window is 400 |
| `GET /api/runs/agents` | `{agents: AgentStatus[]}`, running and waiting agents first |

The shapes are the ones in `src/frontend/src/sdk/layoutTypes.ts`: camelCase keys, times in epoch
milliseconds.

`RunKpis` holds:

- `runs` and `runsDelta`, the change against the previous window of the same length;
- `successRate`, from 0 to 1, with cancelled runs left out;
- `cost` and `budget`;
- `p50Ms` and `p95Ms`, the latency of completed runs.

`budget` is `finops.daily_cost_budget_usd` from the runtime config (Settings, FinOps & Budgets),
multiplied by 7 for the `7d` window. It is left out when that value is unset or 0, or when
`finops.enabled` is `false`.

**Tokens and cost per run.** `usage.track_usage()` takes `run_id=`. When it is not given, it uses
the run the calling task is serving, from the `praisonaiui.features.chat.current_run_id` context
variable. The chat sets that variable for the whole run, and `PraisonAIProvider` passes it on.
`POST /api/usage/track` accepts `run_id` in its body. A provider that records usage without a run
id is joined to the run by session and time window instead, and the run then carries
`approximate: true`.

**Storage.** Finished runs are held in memory (the newest 1000) and appended to
`<data dir>/runs/ledger.jsonl`. The data dir is `PRAISONAI_HOME`, else `AIUI_DATA_DIR`, else
`~/.praisonaiui`.
The append runs on a single writer thread, so the chat broadcast never waits on the disk. The
file is read back the first time a `/api/runs*` route is called, and it is compacted once it holds
more than twice the ring size.

### Observing chat events

The ledger is fed by a hook that any server-side code can use:

```python
from praisonaiui.features.chat import add_event_observer

def on_event(session_id: str, event: dict) -> None:
    if event["type"] == "run_closed":
        print(event["run_id"], event["status"])  # completed | failed | cancelled

remove = add_event_observer(on_event)   # call remove() to stop observing
```

The observer sees every event that `ChatManager.broadcast` sends, whether or not a client is
connected. After each run it also gets one `run_closed` event, which clients never see. By the
time it arrives, the provider has finished and its usage is tracked. Observers run inline on the
event loop, so they must be quick and must not change `event`. An observer that raises is logged
and skipped.

## Artifacts

The browser derives artifacts from the chat: fenced code, tables, file and media elements, and
A2UI surfaces. The extraction rules live only in the client. The server stores what the client
sends: the index for each session, so the nav can count artifacts across sessions, and the
versions the user edited.

| Route | Does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/artifacts?session_id=&limit=` | The latest version of every key, newest first, without content: `{artifacts, count, sessions}` |
| `GET /api/artifacts/{session_id}` | Every version, with content: `{sessionId, artifacts}` |
| `PUT /api/artifacts/{session_id}/{key}` | Upserts a derived version, or adds a user edit: `{artifact}` |
| `DELETE /api/artifacts/{session_id}/{key}[?version=N]` | Removes one key, or one version of it |
| `DELETE /api/artifacts/{session_id}` | Removes the whole session |

Deleting a chat (`DELETE /sessions/{id}`, which the chat, the Sessions page and
`aiui sessions delete` use) also deletes its artifacts.

The body of a `PUT` is an `Artifact`. `kind` is one of `code`, `table`, `markdown`, `file`,
`image`, `pdf`, `video` or `a2ui`.

- With `edited: true`, or with no `version`, the `PUT` adds the next version.
- With a `version`, it replaces that version. If the user edited that version, the `PUT` is
  refused with 409.

The limits are 512 KB of content for each version, 50 versions for each key (unedited versions
are dropped first), and 500 keys for each session.

`url` must be a relative or same-origin path, or an `http:`, `https:`, `blob:` or `data:image/`
URL, the same rule chat markdown uses. The server first normalises the URL the way a browser
does: it drops tab, CR and LF, and strips leading and trailing control characters and spaces. So
`java\nscript:` is refused like `javascript:`. The normalised form is the one stored.

Each session is one JSON file under `<data dir>/artifacts/`, named by a hash of the session id.
Each write goes to a temporary file that is then renamed into place.

---

# Dashboard

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/dashboard

> style: dashboard is the legacy vanilla UI. New apps use the React app

!!! note "Legacy UI"
    `style: dashboard` is the legacy vanilla UI. New apps use the React app
    shell, the default style, with the same `@aiui.page` pages: see
    [Build a focused app](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app.md). This page documents the
    legacy style, which keeps working when you ask for it.

Build rich admin panels with **zero HTML/CSS/JS**. Register pages from Python, compose UIs with the component API, and the SDK renders everything.

## Quick Start

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiui.server import create_app

aiui.set_style("dashboard")

@aiui.page("analytics", title="Analytics", icon="📊")
async def analytics():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.columns([
            aiui.card("Users", value=142, footer="+12% this week"),
            aiui.card("Revenue", value="$1,500"),
        ]),
        aiui.table(
            headers=["Agent", "Tasks", "Status"],
            rows=[["Researcher", 15, "Active"]],
        ),
    ])

app = create_app()
```

```bash
aiui run app.py
# → Dashboard with sidebar, "Analytics" page with cards + table
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["@aiui.page()"] --> B["/api/pages"]
    B --> C["dashboard.js"]
    C --> D["Sidebar + Pages"]
    E["aiui.layout()"] --> F["/api/pages/{id}/data"]
    F --> C
    C --> G["Cards / Tables / Charts"]
```

1. **`@aiui.page()`** registers a page with the server
2. **`dashboard.js`** fetches `/api/pages` and `/ui-config.json` once each on load, builds the sidebar automatically
3. When a page is selected, it fetches `/api/pages/{id}/data`
4. If the data contains `_components`, they render as real UI elements (cards, tables, etc.)

The Chat page highlights code with highlight.js, which it loads from
`cdnjs.cloudflare.com` the first time a reply contains a code block. A chat
with no code never contacts the CDN; without internet access, code shows
unhighlighted.

## Registering Pages

### Basic Page

```python
@aiui.page("status", title="Status", icon="🟢")
async def status_page():
    return {"status": "healthy", "uptime": "99.9%"}
```

Pages without component layouts render as formatted JSON.

### Page with Components

```python
@aiui.page("metrics", title="Metrics", icon="📈", group="Monitoring")
async def metrics_page():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.columns([
            aiui.card("CPU", value="12%"),
            aiui.card("Memory", value="324 MB"),
            aiui.card("Disk", value="45 GB free"),
        ]),
        aiui.text("Last updated: 30 seconds ago"),
    ])
```

### Page Groups

Pages are grouped in the sidebar by the `group` parameter:

```python
@aiui.page("agents", title="Agents", icon="🤖", group="Agent")
@aiui.page("config", title="Config", icon="⚙️", group="Settings")
@aiui.page("logs",   title="Logs",   icon="📜", group="Settings")
```

In the app shell, `icon` can also name any lucide icon, or point at an image.
Every layout's sidebar draws it; a lucide icon outside the shell's small built-in
set loads on demand, so it does not add to the first page load:

```python
@aiui.page("people", title="People", icon="users", group="Team")
@aiui.page("brand",  title="Brand",  icon="/static/logo.svg", group="Team")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `page_id` | `str` | ✅ | Unique identifier (URL-safe) |
| `title` | `str` | ✅ | Display name in sidebar |
| `icon` | `str` | ❌ | Sidebar icon: a [lucide](https://lucide.dev/icons) name (`"users"`, `"film"`), an emoji, or an image URL (`https://…` or a root path `/…`). Default `📄` means none chosen: the app shell shows a placeholder (the title's first letter in layouts) |
| `group` | `str` | ❌ | Sidebar group name |
| `description` | `str` | ❌ | Subtitle below the title |

## Component API

Build dashboard UIs entirely from Python — no HTML needed. **81 component builders** are available across layout, data display, inputs, feedback, overlays, and media.

> See the full [Component API Reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/components.md) for all components and parameters.

### Cards & Metrics

```python
# Simple cards
aiui.card("Total Users", value=142, footer="+12% this week")

# Metric cards with delta indicators
aiui.metric("Requests", value="12.3k", delta="+15%")
aiui.metric("Errors", value=23, delta="+3", delta_color="inverse")
```

### Columns

Arrange components side-by-side in a responsive grid:

```python
aiui.columns([
    aiui.card("Users", value=42),
    aiui.card("Tasks", value=18),
    aiui.card("Uptime", value="99.9%"),
])
```

### Tables

Data tables with headers and rows:

```python
aiui.table(
    headers=["Name", "Role", "Status"],
    rows=[
        ["Alice", "Engineer", "Active"],
        ["Bob", "Designer", "Idle"],
    ],
)
```

### Tabs & Accordion

Organize content in tabs or collapsible sections:

```python
aiui.tabs([
    {"label": "Overview", "children": [aiui.text("Tab 1")]},
    {"label": "Details",  "children": [aiui.table(headers=["K","V"], rows=[["a","b"]])]},
])

aiui.accordion([
    {"title": "FAQ", "content": "Answer here"},
])
```

### Alerts & Badges

```python
aiui.alert("Deploy complete!", variant="success", title="Done")
aiui.badge("New")
aiui.progress_bar("Upload", value=73)
```

### Text & Code

```python
aiui.text("Simple text block.")
aiui.markdown_text("**Bold** and `code`.")
aiui.code_block("print('hello')", language="python")
aiui.json_view({"key": "value"})
```

### Form Inputs

```python
aiui.text_input("Name", placeholder="Enter name")
aiui.select_input("Country", options=["USA", "UK", "Canada"])
aiui.slider_input("Volume", value=65, min_val=0, max_val=100)
aiui.checkbox_input("I agree", checked=True)
aiui.switch_input("Enable notifications")
aiui.radio_input("Language", options=["Python", "JS", "Go"])
```

### Charts

```python
aiui.chart("Revenue Over Time", data=[
    {"month": "Jan", "value": 1200},
    {"month": "Feb", "value": 1800},
], chart_type="line")
```

Kinds, reference lines, value formats and every option: `aiui.chart` in the [Component API Reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/components.md).

### Layout

Wrap all components in a layout container:

```python
aiui.layout([
    aiui.columns([...]),
    aiui.table(...),
    aiui.text("Footer note"),
])
```

The `layout()` function adds the `_components` key that tells the frontend to render structured components instead of raw JSON.

## Built-in Pages

Built-in plugins (`src/praisonaiui/builtin/catalog.py`) auto-register pages across four sidebar groups (`Agent`, `Work`, `Control`, and `Settings`). Use `aiui.set_pages("minimal" | "agent" | "ops")` or `aiui.set_pages([...])` to show only what your app needs (`aiui pages ids` prints every active ID):

| Group | Built-in Pages |
|-------|----------------|
| **Agent** | `chat` (Chat), `chat-canvas` (Chat + Canvas), `canvas` (Canvas), `channels` (Channels), `inbox` (Channel Inbox), `agents` (Agents), `skills` (Skills), `marketplace` (Marketplace), `memory` (Memory), `knowledge` (Knowledge), `mcp` (MCP), `guardrails` (Guardrails), `cron` (Cron). In `style: app`, `connect`, `artifacts` (Chat + Canvas), and `start`/`templates` (Guided) also appear. |
| **Work** | `work` (Work Hub), `kanban` (Kanban), `jobs-board` (Jobs Board) |
| **Control** | `overview` (Overview), `nodes` (Nodes), `sessions` (Sessions), `replay` (Replay), `runs` (Runs), `feedback` (Feedback), `usage` (Usage), `eval` (Eval), `training` (Training), `jobs` (Jobs), `approvals` (Approvals), `code-studio` (Code Studio), `api` (API), `inspector` (Inspector). In `style: app`, `api-reference` (API Reference) also appears. |
| **Settings** | `config` (Config), `security` (Security), `auth` (Auth), `logs` (Logs), `telemetry` (Telemetry), `traces` (Traces), `debug` (Debug), `theme-picker` (Theme) |

Custom pages added via `@aiui.page()` appear alongside built-in pages.

## Agent Run Button

Each agent card on the **Agents** page includes a **▶ Run** button. Clicking it navigates to the **Chat** page with that agent automatically pre-selected in the agent dropdown.

### How It Works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant A as Agents View
    participant D as Dashboard
    participant C as Chat View

    U->>A: Click "▶ Run" on agent card
    A->>D: pushState('/chat?agent=X')
    A->>D: dispatch popstate
    D->>C: selectPage('chat') → render()
    C->>C: loadAgents() → populate dropdown
    C->>C: Read ?agent=X → pre-select agent
    C->>C: replaceState('/chat') → clean URL
```

1. The Run button reads the agent name from its `data-id` attribute
2. It pushes `/chat?agent=<name>` to browser history and dispatches `popstate`
3. The dashboard's `popstate` listener calls `selectPage('chat')`, loading the Chat view
4. Chat's `render()` calls `loadAgents()`, then checks `URLSearchParams` for `?agent=`
5. If found, it sets the dropdown value and `currentAgentName`, then cleans the URL

## Test Panel

Every dashboard includes a **Test All Features** link at the bottom of the sidebar. It auto-discovers all registered features from `/api/features` and tests each endpoint, showing pass/fail results in a grid.

```python

@aiui.page("analytics", title="Analytics", icon="📊", group="Custom")

            aiui.card("API Calls", value="3,847", footer="Last 24h"),
            aiui.card("Avg Latency", value="47ms", footer="-5ms"),
            aiui.card("Success Rate", value="99.2%", footer="✓ Healthy"),
        ]),
        aiui.table(
            headers=["Agent", "Tasks Completed", "Status"],
            rows=[
                ["Researcher", 15, "Active"],
                ["Code Writer", 8, "Idle"],
                ["Reviewer", 12, "Active"],
            ],
        ),
    ])

@aiui.page("metrics", title="Metrics", icon="📈", group="Custom")
```

## Client-Side Extension API

The dashboard provides a JavaScript API for registering custom views from the client side.

### `window.aiui.registerView(pageId, renderFn, cleanupFn)`

Register a custom view renderer for a page ID.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `pageId` | `string` | Page ID to handle (e.g. `"my-custom-page"`) |
| `renderFn` | `async (container: HTMLElement) => void` | Async function that renders into the container |
| `cleanupFn` | `() => void` | Optional cleanup function called when navigating away |

```javascript
// Register a custom view
window.aiui.registerView('my-analytics', async (container) => {
    const data = await fetch('/api/my-data').then(r => r.json());
    container.innerHTML = `
        <div class="db-card">
            <div class="db-card-title">Custom Analytics</div>
            <div class="db-card-value">${data.total}</div>
        </div>
    `;
}, () => {
    // Cleanup (optional) — called when user navigates away
    console.log('Cleaning up my-analytics view');
});
```

### View Resolution Priority

When a page is selected, the dashboard resolves views in this order:

1. **Custom registered views** — `window.aiui.registerView()` (highest priority)
2. **Built-in view modules** — `views/<page id>.js` for built-in pages, from
   `/api/shell/manifest`: a page whose `source` is `builtin` (kind `legacy` or
   `native`) loads `<legacy.viewsBase><page id>.js`. A page an app
   (`register_page` / `@aiui.page`), a plugin or a dashboard-plugin folder
   provides never gets a built-in view, even under a built-in id: it renders its
   own content, in the dashboard style too. When the manifest cannot be read,
   every page `/api/pages` lists is tried by the same file name.
3. **Generic JSON viewer** — Falls back to rendering `_components` or raw JSON

### `window.aiui.views`

Access the view registry directly:

```javascript
// Check if a view is registered
if (window.aiui.views['my-page']) {
    console.log('my-page view is registered');
}

// List all registered views
console.log(Object.keys(window.aiui.views));
```

### Built-in Views

A built-in page's view is the file named after its page id
(`views/<page id>.js`); there is no list in `dashboard.js`. Some of them:

| Page ID | View Module | Description |
|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `chat` | `chat.js` | Chat interface |
| `overview` | `overview.js` | Dashboard overview |
| `agents` | `agents.js` | Agent management |
| `sessions` | `sessions.js` | Session management |
| `memory` | `memory.js` | Memory viewer |
| `knowledge` | `knowledge.js` | Knowledge base |
| `logs` | `logs.js` | Real-time logs |
| `cron` | `cron.js` (re-exports `schedules.js`) | Scheduled jobs |
| `config` | `config.js` | Runtime config |
| `approvals` | `approvals.js` | Tool approvals |
| `usage` | `usage.js` | Token usage |
| `channels` | `channels.js` | Messaging channels |
| `skills` | `skills.js` | Agent skills |
| `nodes` | `nodes.js` | Execution nodes |
| `guardrails` | `guardrails.js` | Safety guardrails |
| `eval` | `eval.js` | Agent evaluation |
| `telemetry` | `telemetry.js` | Performance metrics |
| `traces` | `traces.js` | Distributed tracing |
| `security` | `security.js` | Security monitoring |

`runs`, `cron`, `work` and `training` are one-line modules that re-export
`run-recorder.js`, `schedules.js`, `work-hub.js` and `training-lab.js` under the
page id.

### Light and dark mode

The dashboard picks its colour mode in this order:

1. the viewer's choice, stored under `aiui-theme-preference` (`light`, `dark` or
   `system`; the Theme page and the app shell write the same key);
2. the app's default: `aiui.set_theme(dark_mode=True|False)`, else YAML
   `site.theme.mode` (`light`, `dark`, `system`) or `site.theme.darkMode`;
3. the OS (`prefers-color-scheme`), when neither chose a mode
   (`/ui-config.json` then sends `site.themeDefault: "system"`).

A change of the OS scheme or of the stored choice in another tab applies at once.

# Agents, Memory & Skills Management

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agents-memory-skills

> Create and run agents from the UI, inspect agent memory stores and manage agent skills via built-in pages and REST APIs.

When running in multi-agent or dashboard mode (`aiui.set_pages("all")` or explicit page IDs), PraisonAIUI provides built-in pages and REST APIs for managing your agent fleet without restarting the server.

## Built-in plugins & endpoints

| Plugin | Page ID | Capabilities & Endpoints |
|---|---|---|
| **Agents (`builtin.agents`)** | `agents` | Create, edit, duplicate, delete and run agent definitions (`GET`/`POST /api/agents/definitions`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/agents/definitions/{id}`, `POST /api/agents/duplicate/{id}`, `POST /api/agents/run/{id}`, `GET /api/agents/models`). |
| **Memory (`builtin.memory`)** | `memory` | Browse, search and manage short-term, long-term and entity memory entries (`GET`/`POST /api/memory`, `GET /api/memory/search`, `DELETE /api/memory/{id}`). Install `pip install "aiui[memory]"` for vector backends. |
| **Skills (`builtin.skills`)** | `skills` | Discover, register, configure and toggle reusable agent skills (`GET`/`POST /api/skills`, `GET /api/skills/categories`, `POST /api/skills/{id}/toggle`, `PUT /api/skills/{id}/config`). |

## Enable selectively in your app

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_pages(["chat", "agents", "memory", "skills", "knowledge"])
```

Or register agents directly from Python with `aiui.register_agent("researcher", agent)` (see [Python API](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python.md#aiuiregister_agentname-agent)) and manage knowledge bases in [Knowledge & embeddings](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/knowledge-embeddings.md).

# Schedules, Background Jobs & Kanban Boards

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/schedules-and-jobs

> Run recurring agent schedules (cron), monitor async background jobs and track tasks on built-in Kanban boards.

PraisonAIUI ships three built-in operational plugins for long-running and recurring agent work:

- **Schedules (`builtin.cron`)**: Recurring agent tasks with natural-language or cron schedules (`hourly`, `daily`, `*/30m`, `cron:0 9 * * 1-5`, `at:ISO`), backed by `config.yaml` and wired into agent schedule tools.
- **Jobs (`builtin.jobs`)**: Async job submission, progress tracking, live stats and cancellation.
- **Work / Kanban (`builtin.work`)**: Built-in task board (`work`, `jobs-board`, `kanban`) plus the composable `aiui.board(columns=[...])` component for custom pages.

## API overview

| Feature | Key endpoints |
|---|---|
| **Schedules** | `GET /api/schedules`, `POST /api/schedules`, `POST /api/schedules/{id}/run`, `POST /api/schedules/{id}/stop`, `GET /api/schedules/{id}/stats` |
| **Jobs** | `GET /api/jobs`, `POST /api/jobs`, `GET /api/jobs/stats`, `GET /api/jobs/{id}`, `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel` |
| **Kanban** | `GET /api/kanban`, `POST /api/kanban/cards`, `PUT /api/kanban/cards/{id}`, `DELETE /api/kanban/cards/{id}` |

## Build a custom status or board page

Combine `aiui.status()` (with `refresh_every`) and `aiui.board()` in any `@aiui.page` handler:

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui


@aiui.page("workboard", title="Workboard", icon="kanban", group="Work", refresh_every=5)
async def workboard():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.status("Nightly report", state="running", detail="Summarizing 12 channels", progress=65),
        aiui.board(columns=[
            {"title": "Queued", "cards": [aiui.card("Audit docs", footer="scheduled")]},
            {"title": "Running", "cards": [aiui.card("Nightly report", footer="65%")]},
            {"title": "Done", "cards": [aiui.card("Sync index", footer="ok")]},
        ]),
    ])
```

Show the built-in pages in your sidebar with `aiui.set_pages(["chat", "cron", "jobs", "work"])` or `aiui.set_pages("all")`.

# Work Hub, Kanban & Jobs Board

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/work-hub-and-kanban

> PraisonAIUI ships a multi-agent task tracking workspace under the Work sidebar group with three built-in views:

PraisonAIUI ships a multi-agent task tracking workspace under the **Work** sidebar group with three built-in views:

| Page ID | Title | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `work` | **Work Hub** | Full-bleed workspace combining the kanban board, card details, chat, and job log |
| `kanban` | **Kanban** | Multi-agent task board with drag-and-drop columns and live SSE sync |
| `jobs-board` | **Jobs Board** | Async jobs (`GET /api/jobs/board`) grouped by execution status |

All three pages belong to the built-in plugin `builtin.work`, backed by `KanbanFeature` (`/api/kanban/*`).

## Board Columns

Every board organizes cards across seven workflow columns (plus `archived`, hidden unless `?archived=true`):

`triage` → `todo` → `ready` → `running` → `blocked` → `review` → `done`

Each task card tracks `title`, `status`, `assignee`, `priority`, `tenant`, `board`, `body`, `comments`, `meta`, and optional child subtask progress (`children` or `meta.progress`).

## REST & Live SSE API

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/kanban/board` | Get columns and cards (`?board=default&tenant=...&archived=false`) |
| `GET` | `/api/kanban/boards` | List available board names |
| `POST` | `/api/kanban/tasks` | Create a task (`201`) |
| `POST` | `/api/kanban/tasks/bulk` | Move multiple `task_ids` to a target `status` |
| `GET` | `/api/kanban/tasks/{task_id}` | Fetch full task details |
| `PATCH` | `/api/kanban/tasks/{task_id}` | Update task fields |
| `DELETE` | `/api/kanban/tasks/{task_id}` | Delete a task |
| `POST` | `/api/kanban/tasks/{task_id}/move` | Move a task to a new column (`{"status": "review"}`) |
| `POST` | `/api/kanban/tasks/{task_id}/comments` | Append a comment (`{"text": "...", "author": "..."}`) |
| `GET` | `/api/kanban/events` | SSE stream (`text/event-stream`) of task changes (`?board=default&since=0`) |
| `GET` | `/api/kanban/health` | Store health, task count, and board list |

### Quick Example

```bash
# Create a task
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/kanban/tasks \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title": "Audit Q4 metrics", "status": "todo", "assignee": "analyst", "priority": "high"}'

# Move it to running
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/kanban/tasks/<task_id>/move \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "running"}'
```

## Custom Storage Backends

By default `KanbanFeature` uses `SimpleKanbanStore` (in-memory, zero dependencies). Subclass `KanbanStoreProtocol` from `praisonaiui.features.kanban` to persist boards in SQL, Redis, or an external issue tracker, and register a factory via `praisonaiui.backends.set_kanban_store_factory(...)`.

## Disabling

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled:
    - builtin.work
```

# Guardrails, Evals, Traces, Usage & Logs

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/observability-and-guardrails

> Monitor token usage, latency telemetry, execution traces, live logs, safety guardrails and evaluation scores from built-in pages.

Production AI apps need visibility into cost, latency, safety checks and quality regressions. PraisonAIUI includes six modular observability and safety plugins you can enable individually or all at once.

## Built-in plugins at a glance

| Plugin | Page ID | What it tracks | Key endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Usage (`builtin.usage`)** | `usage` | Token counts, model breakdown, session/agent totals and estimated costs | `GET /api/usage/summary`, `/models`, `/sessions`, `/agents`, `/timeseries`, `/costs`, `POST /api/usage/track` |
| **Traces (`builtin.traces`)** | `traces` | End-to-end execution traces and nested tool/LLM spans | `GET /api/traces`, `GET /api/traces/spans`, `GET /api/traces/{trace_id}`, `POST /api/traces/record` |
| **Telemetry (`builtin.telemetry`)** | `telemetry` | Runtime latency metrics, performance snapshots and profiling | `GET /api/telemetry`, `/metrics`, `/performance`, `/profiling`, `POST /api/telemetry/record` |
| **Logs (`builtin.logs`)** | `logs` | Live searchable server and agent log stream | `GET /api/logs`, `GET /api/logs/stream` |
| **Guardrails (`builtin.guardrails`)** | `guardrails` | Active safety rules and recorded policy violations | `GET /api/guardrails`, `/violations`, `POST /api/guardrails/register`, `DELETE /api/guardrails/{id}` |
| **Evals (`builtin.eval`)** | `eval` | Automated judges, evaluation runs and quality scores | `GET /api/eval`, `/judges`, `/scores`, `POST /api/eval/run` |

## Turn them on or off

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# Show only the observability pages your team uses
aiui.set_pages(["chat", "usage", "traces", "logs", "guardrails"])
```

To disable any non-required plugin and skip importing its backend module (R2/R4), list it under `extensions.disabled:` in `aiui.yaml` (e.g. `builtin.eval`, `builtin.telemetry`).

# Training Lab

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/training

> The Training page (training, under the Control sidebar group) lets you inspect praisonai-train agent training sessions, compare iteration scores, and apply the

The **Training** page (`training`, under the **Control** sidebar group) lets you inspect [`praisonai-train`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAI) agent training sessions, compare iteration scores, and apply the best training profile to any registered agent.

## Storage & Optional Dependency

Training sessions are read from JSON files in the first directory that applies:

1. `$PRAISON_TRAIN_DIR` environment variable
2. `<configured data dir>/train` (when `$AIUI_DATA_DIR` or `--datastore` sets a data directory)
3. `~/.praison/train` (default `praisonai-train` directory)

`praisonai-train` is an **optional** dependency:

- **Without `praisonai-train`:** Listing sessions and viewing full iteration reports still work directly from the JSON files; `POST /api/training/sessions/{session_id}/apply` returns HTTP `503` with an install hint (`pip install praisonai-train`).
- **With `praisonai-train` installed:** Clicking **Apply** (or calling `/apply`) runs `praisonai_train.train.agents.apply_training()` on the selected agent definition.

## REST API

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/training/status` | Package availability, version, storage directory, session count, and warnings |
| `GET` | `/api/training/sessions` | List session summaries sorted by newest first (`?limit=50&agent_id=...`) |
| `GET` | `/api/training/sessions/{session_id}` | Full report, per-iteration scores, `best_iteration`, early-stop info, and scenarios |
| `POST` | `/api/training/sessions/{session_id}/apply` | Apply the best (or specified `iteration`) training profile to `agent_id` |

### Apply a Training Profile

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/training/sessions/session_01/apply \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"agent_id": "agent_abc", "iteration": 3}'
```

Omit `iteration` to automatically select the highest-scoring iteration.

## Disabling

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled:
    - builtin.training
```

- [Agents, Memory & Skills](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agents-memory-skills.md)
- [Observability & Guardrails](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/observability-and-guardrails.md)
- [Features REST API](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/features-api.md#training-lab)

# Execution Nodes & Presence

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/nodes

> The Nodes page (nodes, under the Control sidebar group) monitors execution nodes and live server/worker instances connected to your PraisonAIUI deployment.

The **Nodes** page (`nodes`, under the **Control** sidebar group) monitors execution nodes and live server/worker instances connected to your PraisonAIUI deployment.

On startup, `NodesFeature` automatically registers the `local` host node and server instance so the Nodes page immediately reflects the current machine's OS, Python version, and online status.

## REST API

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/nodes` | List registered execution nodes and total count |
| `POST` | `/api/nodes` | Register a new execution node (`201`, returns generated auth `token`) |
| `GET` | `/api/nodes/{node_id}` | Fetch node details |
| `PUT` | `/api/nodes/{node_id}` | Update `name`, `host`, `agents`, or `approval_policy` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/nodes/{node_id}` | Remove a node |
| `GET` | `/api/nodes/{node_id}/status` | Check node health, status, and last heartbeat |
| `GET` / `PUT` | `/api/nodes/{node_id}/agents` | Inspect or assign agents bound to a node |
| `GET` | `/api/nodes/instances` | List connected instances (alias: `GET /api/instances`) |
| `POST` | `/api/instances/heartbeat` | Record an instance presence heartbeat |

### Registering a Worker Node

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/nodes \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "gpu-worker-1",
    "host": "10.0.0.14",
    "platform": "Linux",
    "agents": ["researcher"],
    "approval_policy": "deny"
  }'
```

## Custom Backends

Implement `NodeProtocol` from `praisonaiui.features.nodes` (`list_nodes`, `register_node`, `get_node`, `delete_node`, `heartbeat`) to back node presence with your own orchestrator or service registry.

## Disabling

```yaml
extensions:
  disabled:
    - builtin.nodes
```

# Agent UI host — modular dashboard shell

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/agent-ui-host

> PraisonAIUI can host any AI agent backend behind a modular dashboard shell: pages, views, layout components, optional plugins, and branding — without forking th

PraisonAIUI can host any AI agent backend behind a **modular dashboard shell**: pages, views, layout components, optional plugins, and branding — without forking the frontend.

## Architecture

```text
YAML / Python config → server (pages API, plugins.json) → dashboard.js shell
                              ↓
  registerView / views/<page id>.js (built-in pages) / layout JSON / registerComponent
                              ↓
                    renderComponent() + theme (--db-*)
```

**Extension priority** (first match wins):

1. `window.aiui.registerView(pageId, …)`
2. Dashboard manifest plugins (`dashboard-plugins/*/manifest.json`)
3. Built-in view modules: `views/<page id>.js` for built-in pages, from `/api/shell/manifest` (a page's `source` and `kind` there decide; an app page under a built-in id renders its own content, also in the dashboard style)
4. Server `aiui.layout()` JSON from `@aiui.page()`
5. `window.aiui.registerComponent(type, …)` inside `renderComponent`
6. Generic JSON fallback viewer

## Quick start (external agent)

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
from praisonaiui.server import create_app

aiui.set_style("dashboard")
aiui.set_branding(title="Acme Agents", logo="A")
aiui.set_pages(["chat", "tasks", "sessions", "config"])
aiui.set_dashboard(modules=["jobs"], sidebar=True, page_header=True)

@aiui.page("tasks", title="Tasks", icon="📋", group="Work")
async def tasks_page():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.board(columns=[
            {"id": "todo", "title": "Todo", "cards": [aiui.card("Review PR", footer="agent-a")]},
            {"id": "done", "title": "Done", "cards": [aiui.card("Ship feature")]},
        ]),
    ])

app = create_app()
```

See [`examples/python/external-agent-dashboard/app.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/examples/python/external-agent-dashboard/app.py).

## `window.aiui` extension API

| API | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `version` | Shell protocol version (`'1'`) |
| `registerView(pageId, renderFn, cleanup?)` | Replace or add a full page renderer |
| `registerComponent(type, renderFn)` | Override a layout component type |
| `registerSurfaceRenderer(surfaceId, renderFn)` | Custom A2UI surface renderer |
| `selectPage(pageId)` | Navigate programmatically (e.g. open full canvas) |
| `registerSlot(name, renderFn)` | Inject DOM into named slots |
| `sdk.fetchJSON(url, opts?)` | Authenticated fetch helper |
| `sdk.el(tag, attrs?, children?)` | Small DOM builder |
| `sdk.themeVar('--db-*', fallback?)` | Read theme CSS variables |
| `sdk.createBoard(root, { fetch, pollMs? })` | Live board with optional polling |

### Slots

| Slot id | Where it renders |
|---------|------------------|
| `shell:sidebar:footer` | Bottom of sidebar (default: health hint) |
| `page:{pageId}:toolbar` | Right side of page header |

Register only what you need; omit slots you do not use.

## Layout components (Python → JS)

Define pages with `@aiui.page()` returning `aiui.layout([...])`. Types are implemented once in [`ui.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/ui.py) and [`dashboard.js`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/dashboard.js).

**Kanban / board:** use `aiui.board(columns=[...])`. Columns contain `id`, `title`, and `cards` (from `aiui.card()` or dicts). The shell renders via `renderBoard`, composing existing card renderers (DRY).

## A2UI surfaces (agent-driven UI)

Three tiers work together:

| Tier | Mechanism | Use case |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Dashboard | `aiui.layout()` → `_components` | Python-authored pages |
| A2UI | `send_a2ui_messages` → `SurfaceHost` | Agent-generated UI in chat/canvas |
| AG-UI | `POST /agui` SSE | CopilotKit / external clients |

Register an empty canvas page:

```python
@aiui.page("agent-canvas", title="Agent Canvas", icon="🖼️")
async def agent_canvas():
    return {"_surface": {"id": "main", "messages": []}}
```

Or use `@aiui.surface_action("main")` for button callbacks.

**Full guide:** [A2UI canvas](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/a2ui-canvas.md) — chat-canvas split view, `send_a2ui_messages`, HTTP/CLI, `coerce_a2ui_tool_messages`, troubleshooting. Example: [`examples/python/30-a2ui-canvas/`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/examples/python/30-a2ui-canvas/app.py).

## Optional dashboard modules

Load heavy built-ins only when listed:

```python
aiui.set_dashboard(modules=["jobs", "auth", "api"])
```

```yaml
dashboard:
  modules: [jobs]
```

This adds `jobs.js`, `auth.js`, or `api.js` to the plugin chain; their pages resolve to `views/<page id>.js` for built-in pages, from `/api/shell/manifest`. `feedback` is always available as a built-in view when the page is enabled.

## Third-party dashboard plugins

Place folders under:

- `~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins/{name}/`
- Or `src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/dashboard-plugins/{name}/` (shipped examples)

Each plugin needs `manifest.json` + `index.js` (optional `styles.css`):

```json
{
  "name": "my-board",
  "label": "My board",
  "icon": "📋",
  "tab": { "path": "/my-board" },
  "entry": "index.js"
}
```

The server exposes:

- `GET /api/dashboard/plugins` — manifest list
- `GET /dashboard-plugins/{name}/{path}` — static assets

Plugins register views in `index.js`:

```javascript
window.aiui.registerView('my-board', async (container) => {
  window.aiui.sdk.createBoard(container, {
    fetch: async () => ({ columns: [...] }),
  });
});
```

Sample: [`sample-board`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/dashboard-plugins/sample-board/).

## Agent plugins vs dashboard plugins

| System | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Agent plugins | `~/.praisonai/plugins/` | Python agent extensions |
| Dashboard plugins | `~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins/` | JS UI tabs |

See [PraisonAI package integration](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/praisonai-package-integration.md) for backend wiring, jobs API, and deployment.

## Granular control — opt-in / opt-out

| What you control | How | Example |
|------------------|-----|---------|
| UI mode | `aiui.set_style(...)` | `"dashboard"`, `"chat"`, `"docs"` |
| Sidebar pages | `aiui.set_pages([ids])` whitelist | `["chat", "sessions"]` |
| Hide built-ins | YAML `pages.disabled: [...]` | Blacklist in server |
| Sidebar on/off | `set_dashboard(sidebar=False)` | Chat-only full width |
| Page title bar | `set_dashboard(page_header=False)` | Cleaner surface |
| Optional modules | `set_dashboard(modules=[...])` | `["jobs"]` only |
| Third-party tabs | Install chosen `dashboard-plugins/` folders | Manifest per plugin |
| Shell chrome | `registerSlot` | Header/footer widgets |
| Look only | `set_theme`, `set_branding`, `set_custom_css` | White-label |
| Replace one page | `registerView(pageId, ...)` | Override built-in |
| Board UI | `aiui.board()` or plugin | Not in default nav |

**Note:** `@aiui.page()` custom pages are **not** filtered by `set_pages()` — only built-in dashboard pages are. Remove custom pages from code to hide them.

### Example profiles

```python
# Chat-only
aiui.set_style("dashboard")
aiui.set_pages(["chat"])
aiui.set_dashboard(sidebar=False, page_header=False)

# Ops console — no chat
aiui.set_pages(["sessions", "agents", "logs", "config", "usage", "approvals"])
```

```yaml
style: dashboard
pages:
  enabled: [chat, agents, memory, sessions]
dashboard:
  sidebar: true
  pageHeader: true
  modules: [jobs]
  plugin_dirs: [/opt/my-agent/plugins]
```

CLI: `aiui pages ids` lists built-in page ids for whitelists.

## DRY rules for contributors

1. Add new layout types in **`ui.py`** and one `case` in **`dashboard.js`**.
2. Page-specific UI belongs in **`plugins/views/*.js`**, delegating to shared modules (`jobs.js`, etc.) via thin wrappers.
3. Reuse **`_helpers.js`** (`pageToolbar`, `filterChips`, `searchInput`, `modalShell`, `toast`).
4. Boards compose **`card`** / **`columns`** — do not duplicate card markup in plugins.

## Related files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [`praisonai-package-integration.md`](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/praisonai-package-integration.md) | Praison backend wiring |
| [`server.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/server.py) | Pages API, `set_dashboard`, plugin chain |
| [`dashboard_plugins.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/dashboard_plugins.py) | Manifest discovery and static routes |
| [`dashboard.js`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/dashboard.js) | Shell, registries, renderers |
| [`schema/models.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/schema/models.py) | `DashboardConfig.modules`, `plugin_dirs` |

# Replay

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/replay

> at what cost. It works for finished runs and for runs that are still going.

**PraisonAI Replay** shows a recorded agent run as a story: who did what, when, why, and
at what cost. It works for finished runs and for runs that are still going.

## Record a run, then open it

```bash
praisonai replay view agents.yaml      # records the run and opens Replay on it
```

or from Python:

```python
from praisonai.replay import record

with record(live=True):
    team.start()
```

Every recorded run is a file `<id>.jsonl` in the traces folder. Replay reads it from
the first of these that applies:

1. `$PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR`
2. `$PRAISON_HOME/traces`
3. `<data dir>/traces`, when a data directory is configured with `$PRAISONAI_HOME`
   (checked first) or `$AIUI_DATA_DIR`
4. `~/.praison/traces`, where the PraisonAI CLI writes runs

The PraisonAI CLI always records to `~/.praison/traces`. A server started with
`AIUI_DATA_DIR` or `PRAISONAI_HOME` (Docker with `AIUI_DATA_DIR=/data`, for example)
reads its own `<data dir>/traces` instead and does not show those CLI runs. To show
them, set `PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR=~/.praison/traces`.

To open aiui on Replay yourself:

```bash
aiui run "$(python -c 'import praisonaiui.replay_app as m; print(m.__file__)')" \
    --style dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8090
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8090/replay?run=<id>
```

`/#/replay?run=<id>` works too. In a full dashboard, Replay is in the sidebar under
**Control**.

## Watch a run live: the Run button

For learning, demos and debugging, open a page with a **Run** button. Each click records
a new run, and the page draws it as it happens:

```python
from praisonai.replay import watch

watch(flow, input="solar sails")   # an Agent, AgentTeam, AgentFlow or agents.yaml
```

```bash
praisonai replay watch agents.yaml
```

On the **Map**, each step and agent shows where the run is: dashed means not reached,
blue (pulsing) means running now, green means done and red means failed. After a run,
**▶ Play** moves through it again one step at a time, and the map rewinds with it. One
run goes at a time. Each run of a team starts its tasks afresh; an Agent keeps its chat
history between runs.

## Show progress inside your own app

`create_replay_app()` is the same view as a small ASGI app, without the dashboard. Mount
it in any FastAPI or Starlette app:

```python
from praisonai.replay import record, replay_app

app.mount("/replay", replay_app())         # read-only: shows recorded runs

# wherever your app starts work:
with record(run_id, live=True):
    team.start()
```

Then show one run, live, in your page, for example in an `<iframe>`:

```html
<iframe src="/replay/?run=RUN_ID" style="width:100%;height:640px"></iframe>
```

| URL | Shows |
|---|---|
| `/replay/` | The run list and the selected run |
| `/replay/?run=<id>` | Only that run, no list. A run that has not started yet is waited for. |

`replay_app(team)` adds the Run box to the mounted page. Without the PraisonAI wrapper,
pass any `run(input, run_id)` callable to `praisonaiui.features.replay.create_replay_app`;
it must record the run under `run_id`. For a page you build yourself, the view is one
module:

```html
<div id="progress"></div>
<script type="module">
  import { render } from "/replay/replay.js";
  render(document.getElementById("progress"), { base: "/replay", run: "RUN_ID", approve: false });
</script>
```

`render()` options: `base` (where the API is mounted), `run` (show only this run),
`runner` (`{input, placeholder, ask}` to show the Run box) and `approve` (`false` hides
the approve and deny buttons; the embedded app has no approvals API, so answer approvals
where your app asks for them).

Anyone who can reach the mounted app can read the runs, and with a runner can start one.
Keep it on localhost or behind your app's login. `POST /api/replay/run` only accepts
`Content-Type: application/json`, so another website cannot start a run from a visitor's
browser.

## What you see

| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Runs** | Recorded runs, newest first. A run that is still being written has a **Live** badge. |
| **Timeline** (default) | One lane per agent, plus **Manager** and **You**. Time runs left to right. LLM calls and tool calls are blocks in their agent's lane. Arrows show hand-offs, delegation, routing and approval requests. Parallel branches get their own sub-lanes. A call or step repeated back to back is one block marked ×N. Tasks and steps run across the top. |
| **Map** | The team or flow as a graph, drawn from the graph recorded at the start of the run and fitted to the page (−, Fit and + zoom; drag to pan). Agents that took part but are not in the graph, for example after a hand-off to an agent outside the team, appear in an **Outside the team** group with their hand-offs. Older recordings without a graph get a "who talked to whom" map built from the events. Each node shows its state at the cursor: dashed means not reached, blue means running, green means done (×N when it ran more than once) and red means failed; the node the cursor is on has a bold outline. |
| **What happened** | One plain sentence per step, for example *"Researcher asked web_search for 'solar sail facts' — 1.2 s, $0.002."* Hovering or focusing a sentence highlights its block, and the other way round. |
| **Details** | Three tabs for the selected step. **What happened**: when, who, how long, cost, tokens, output. **Why**: only what the recording holds, such as the input given to a tool, the context passed in a hand-off and its reason, the manager's task snapshot, the route a step chose, and an approval's decision and where an automatic approval came from. **Raw JSON**: the events themselves. |
| **Cost & latency** | Adds a bar under each block (taller and darker means more cost, or more time) and per-agent totals in the lane labels. |

Shapes always carry meaning as well as colour: agents are circles, tools are rounded
rectangles, you are a diamond and the manager is a square. In each lane, LLM calls sit on
the top row and that agent's tool calls on a thinner row under them, so a long LLM call
never hides its tools. Labels that do not fit end in "…"; hover or focus a block to see the
whole label.

The **Theme** menu follows your system's light or dark setting by default; choose Light or
Dark to override it. On a phone the run list, timeline and steps stack in one column.

## Moving through a run

Replay opens at the end of the run, so you see everything. Move the cursor to replay it:
anything after the cursor is drawn as an outline.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| ← → | Previous / next step |
| ↑ ↓ | Previous / next step in the step list; previous / next node in the map |
| Home / End | First / last step |
| Enter or Space | Open the focused block or node |
| ← → in the tabs | Switch between What happened, Why and Raw JSON |

The scrubber under the timeline does the same with a mouse or touch, and **▶ Play** steps
through on its own. On a live run the
cursor follows new events; if you step back, **Jump to live** takes you to the latest.

## Approving from Replay

When an agent asks for approval and the run uses aiui's approval store, a **Waiting for
you** card appears above the timeline:

- **Approve** or **Deny**, with an optional reason.
- **Edit arguments…** opens the arguments as JSON (taken from the server, not the redacted
  recording when the server has them). The JSON must be an object; mistakes are shown
  as you type. **Approve with these arguments** sends them as `modified_args`.

These buttons call `POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve` and `/deny`. The agent waits until
you answer, and is denied if nobody answers before the approval timeout.

## Sharing a run as one file

`praisonai replay export RUN --format html` writes a single HTML file with the run and
this viewer inside. It needs no server and no network. Approvals cannot be answered from
an exported file.

## HTTP API

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/replay/runs` | `[{run_id, session_id, path, started_at, ended_at?, status, kind, name, agents, events, cost_usd, live}]`, newest first |
| `GET /api/replay/runs/{id}/events?after_seq=N` | `{events, graph, run}`; `after_seq` keeps only events with a larger `sequence_num`; `wait=1` answers `{events: [], graph: null, run: null}` instead of 404 for a run that has not started yet |
| `GET /api/replay/runs/{id}/stream` | Server-sent events: `event: ctx` per trace event (with `id:` = `sequence_num`), `ping` every 15 s, `end` once the run has finished and gone quiet for 2 s. Honours `after_seq` and `Last-Event-ID`. |

With a runner (`create_replay_app(run=...)`), `POST /api/replay/run` with
`{"input": "..."}` starts a run and returns `{run_id}` (409 while one is going).

Run ids must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`. Replay never writes trace files itself. Half-written last lines, unknown fields and unknown event types are skipped
safely, and schema 1.0 recordings still open.

The **Traces** page reads the same files: each run is a trace, and its spans come from
matching start and end events.

# Browser Automation

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/browser-automation

> Expose browser agent capabilities (CDP, Playwright) through the dashboard — run browser tasks from the UI.

Expose **browser agent capabilities** (CDP, Playwright) through the dashboard — run browser tasks from the UI.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Check browser automation status
curl http://localhost:8083/api/browser/status

# Run a browser task
curl -X POST http://localhost:8083/api/browser/run \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task": "Go to example.com and extract the page title", "url": "https://example.com"}'
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Dashboard UI"] --> B["POST /api/browser/run"]
    B --> C["BrowserAutomationManager"]
    C --> D{"Backend Available?"}
    D -->|Playwright| E["Playwright Browser"]
    D -->|CDP| F["Chrome DevTools Protocol"]
    D -->|None| G["Error: Install praisonai[browser]"]
    E --> H["Execute Task"]
    F --> H
    H --> I["Return Result"]
```

## Prerequisites

Browser automation requires `praisonai[browser]`:

```bash
pip install praisonai[browser]
```

This installs the Playwright and/or CDP backends.

## Status

The status endpoint reports which backends are available:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8083/api/browser/status
```

```json
{
  "available": true,
  "tasks_run": 5,
  "backends": ["playwright", "cdp"]
}
```

# Channel-to-Chat Bridge

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/channel-chat-bridge

> Bridge channel bot conversations (Slack, Discord, Telegram) into the Chat UI in real-time.

Bridge channel bot conversations (Slack, Discord, Telegram) into the Chat UI in real-time.

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PU as Platform User
    participant Bot as SlackBot / DiscordBot / TelegramBot
    participant Bridge as _attach_chat_bridge()
    participant CM as ChatManager.broadcast()
    participant WS as Chat WebSocket (/api/chat/ws)
    participant UI as chat.js (Chat View)

    Note over Bridge: Attached BEFORE bot.start()
    Note over Bridge: All broadcasts via asyncio.create_task<br/>(fire-and-forget, zero perf impact)

    PU->>Bot: "Hello" (platform message)
    Bot->>Bridge: on_message hook fires
    Bridge->>CM: broadcast({type: "channel_message", ...})
    CM->>WS: send to connected clients
    WS->>UI: _handleChannelMessage() renders with platform badge

    Bot->>Bot: agent processes message
    Bot->>Bridge: _wrapped_chat() returns response
    Bridge->>CM: broadcast({type: "channel_response", ...})
    CM->>WS: send to connected clients
    WS->>UI: _handleChannelResponse() renders as assistant
```

## How It Works

### Backend (`channels.py`)

`_attach_chat_bridge(channel_id, bot, platform)` is called in `_start_channel_bot()` right before the bot task is launched:

1. **`on_message` hook** — Captures incoming platform messages and broadcasts `channel_message` events with sender name, platform, and icon
2. **`_session.chat()` wrapper** — Wraps the agent's chat method so responses are also broadcast as `channel_response` events
3. **Persistence** — All messages saved to the datastore under session `channel-{channel_id}` for history on reload

### Frontend (`chat.js`)

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `_handleChannelMessage(data)` | Renders incoming platform user messages; auto-switches to channel session if on fresh chat |
| `_handleChannelResponse(data)` | Renders agent responses from channel bots |
| `_appendChannelMsg(role, data)` | Creates message DOM with platform badge, icon, sender name |
| `_markSessionUnread(sessionId)` | Adds unread dot to sidebar for inactive channel sessions |

## Performance

Every broadcast is dispatched via `asyncio.create_task()` — the original bot message handling is **never blocked**. Errors in broadcasting are logged at `debug` level and swallowed — the bot continues normally even with zero Chat UI clients connected.

## Session Naming

Each channel gets a dedicated session: `channel-{channel_id}`. Platform icons:

| Platform | Icon |
|---|---|
| Slack | 💬 |
| Discord | 🎮 |
| Telegram | ✈️ |
| WhatsApp | 📱 |

## WebSocket Events

### `channel_message`

```json
{
  "type": "channel_message",
  "session_id": "channel-abc123",
  "channel_id": "abc123",
  "platform": "slack",
  "icon": "💬",
  "content": "Hello from Slack!",
  "sender": "john.doe",
  "timestamp": 1773033464.37
}
```

### `channel_response`

```json
{
  "type": "channel_response",
  "session_id": "channel-abc123",
  "channel_id": "abc123",
  "platform": "slack",
  "icon": "💬",
  "content": "Hi! How can I help?",
  "agent_name": "assistant",
  "timestamp": 1773033465.12
}
```
