# Settings, Themes, Multi-Surface & Pages

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/settings-and-pages

> Configure A2UI chat previews, themes, catalogs, custom renderers, same-page multi-surface, and multi-page workspaces.

Configure how A2UI surfaces appear, style them to match your brand, and decide whether to show everything on **one page** or across **multiple pages**.

## 1. All A2UI Settings

| Setting | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `aiui.set_chat_preview(enabled=True, surface_id="main", width="40%")` | Python startup | Enables the split Chat + Canvas right-hand preview panel |
| `theme={"primaryColor": "#2563eb", "font": "Inter"}` | `createSurface` | Surface-level theme configuration |
| `catalog_id` | `createSurface` | Catalog URI (`"basic"`, v0.9 `catalogs/basic/catalog.json`, v0.10, or custom) |
| `send_data_model=True` | `createSurface` | Include client data-model state on user actions |
| `window.aiui.registerSurfaceRenderer(id, fn)` | Browser JS | Override rendering for a specific surface or custom catalog |

## 2. Same Page vs Different Pages

### Option A — Try everything on ONE page (Multi-Surface)

The built-in **Canvas** page (`/canvas`) includes a live **Surface selector** populated from `GET /api/surfaces`, so you can push several independent surfaces (`"main"`, `"form"`, `"metrics"`) and switch between them on the same page without reloading.

You can also embed a surface directly inside any custom `@aiui.page`:

```python
@aiui.page("studio", title="A2UI Studio", group="A2UI")
async def studio_page():
    return {"_surface": {"id": "main", "messages": build_studio_surface()}}
```

### Option B — Split across DIFFERENT pages

Combine dedicated pages in one app so users can chat alongside a live preview, open a full-screen workspace, and inspect settings separately:

```python
aiui.set_chat_preview(enabled=True, surface_id="main", width="40%")
aiui.set_pages([
    "chat-canvas",   # Split view: Chat left + live A2UI canvas right
    "canvas",        # Full-page multi-surface canvas with surface switcher
    "agent-canvas",  # Custom pre-seeded A2UI page
    "a2ui-settings", # Capabilities & catalog inspector page
])
```

Open any specific surface directly via query string: `/canvas?surface=checkout`.

## 3. Protocol Versions & v0.8 → v0.9 Compatibility

PraisonAIUI accepts **v0.8**, **v0.9**, and **v0.10** messages seamlessly:

| v0.8 (Upgraded automatically) | v0.9 / v0.10 (Native) |
|---|---|
| `beginRendering` (`styles`, `root`) | `createSurface` (`theme`, `catalogId`, `sendDataModel`) |
| `surfaceUpdate` (`{component: {Text: {...}}}`) | `updateComponents` (`{component: "Text", ...}`) |
| `dataModelUpdate` (`contents: [{key, valueString}]`) | `updateDataModel` (`path`, `value`) |
| `deleteSurface` | `deleteSurface` |
| `userAction` | `action` |

Use `aiui.v08_to_v09(messages)` in Python anytime you want to inspect or persist the upgraded v0.9 payload.

## 4. Custom Catalogs & Custom Renderers

If an agent uses a custom catalog URI (for example `https://acme.example/a2ui/shop.json`), register a custom renderer in custom JS (`aiui.set_custom_js(...)`):

```js
window.aiui.registerSurfaceRenderer("shop", (host, messages) => {
  host.textContent = `Custom catalog received ${messages.length} message(s)`;
});
```

## 5. HTTP API & CLI Reference

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/surfaces` | List all active surfaces and message counts |
| `GET` | `/api/surfaces/capabilities` | Return A2UI supported versions, catalog IDs, 18 components, and 14 functions |
| `GET` | `/api/surfaces/{id}` | Fetch surface messages and metadata (returns empty list if not yet created) |
| `POST` | `/api/surfaces/{id}/messages` | Append or replace (`"replace": true`) messages (v0.8 / v0.9 / v0.10) |
| `POST` | `/api/surfaces/{id}/action` | Submit user action (`/actions` alias also supported) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/surfaces/{id}` | Delete surface |

```bash
aiui surface capabilities
aiui surface list
aiui surface get main --json
aiui surface push main --file surface.jsonl --replace
aiui surface clear main
aiui surface status
```

# Interactive Response Examples

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/response-examples

> Live interactive simulations of every response type an AI agent can render when a user sends a message — KPIs, forms, approvals, charts, tables, workflows, boards, and copyable outputs.

# Interactive Agent Response Examples

When a user sends a message in Chat, an agent does not have to reply with plain text alone. Using **A2UI surfaces** (`a2ui_surface` / `send_a2ui_messages`) or **UI component blocks** (`aiui.*`), agents can stream rich interactive UI directly into the chat thread or split Canvas.

Every example below shows the **user prompt**, a **live interactive simulation** you can click and test right here, and the **code / A2UI JSON** that produces it.

## 1. KPI & System Health Card Response

**User sends:** `"Show today's system health and active traffic."`

[
  {
    "type": "stat_group",
    "stats": [
      {"type": "metric", "label": "Active Sessions", "value": "1,420", "delta": "+12.4%", "sparkline": [980, 1080, 1210, 1340, 1420]},
      {"type": "metric", "label": "P95 Latency", "value": "118 ms", "delta": "-14 ms", "sparkline": [148, 138, 130, 122, 118]},
      {"type": "metric", "label": "Success Rate", "value": "99.94%", "delta": "+0.08%"}
    ]
  },
  {"type": "alert", "variant": "success", "title": "All Systems Operational", "message": "4 worker pools healthy across us-east and eu-west."}
]

### A2UI v0.9 JSON

```json
[
  {"createSurface": {"surfaceId": "health", "catalogId": "basic"}},
  {"updateComponents": {"surfaceId": "health", "components": [
    {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["h1", "row"]},
    {"id": "h1", "component": "Text", "text": "System Health", "variant": "h2"},
    {"id": "row", "component": "Row", "children": ["c1", "c2"]},
    {"id": "c1", "component": "Card", "child": "m1"},
    {"id": "m1", "component": "Text", "text": "Active Sessions: 1,420 (+12.4%)"},
    {"id": "c2", "component": "Card", "child": "m2"},
    {"id": "m2", "component": "Text", "text": "P95 Latency: 118 ms (-14 ms)"}
  ]}}
]
```

### Python

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.layout([
    aiui.stat_group([
        aiui.metric("Active Sessions", value="1,420", delta="+12.4%", sparkline=[980, 1080, 1210, 1340, 1420]),
        aiui.metric("P95 Latency", value="118 ms", delta="-14 ms"),
    ]),
    aiui.alert("4 worker pools healthy.", variant="success", title="All Systems Operational"),
])
```

## 2. Interactive Form & Parameter Tuning Surface

**User sends:** `"Let me configure my research agent's model, temperature, and memory."`

{
  "type": "form_action",
  "action": "save_agent_config",
  "submit_label": "Apply Settings",
  "children": [
    {"type": "select_input", "label": "Model", "options": ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-3.7-sonnet", "gemini-2.5-flash"], "value": "gpt-4o", "name": "model"},
    {"type": "slider_input", "label": "Temperature", "value": 0.3, "min_val": 0, "max_val": 1, "step": 0.1, "name": "temperature"},
    {"type": "switch_input", "label": "Enable cross-session memory", "checked": true, "name": "memory"}
  ]
}

### A2UI v0.9 (Python)

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

msgs = aiui.a2ui_surface(
    surface_id="agent-config",
    components=[
        {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["model", "temp", "mem", "save"]},
        {"id": "model", "component": "ChoicePicker", "label": "Model", "value": {"path": "/model"},
         "options": [{"label": "gpt-4o", "value": "gpt-4o"}, {"label": "gpt-4o-mini", "value": "gpt-4o-mini"}]},
        {"id": "temp", "component": "Slider", "label": "Temperature", "min": 0, "max": 1, "value": {"path": "/temp"}},
        {"id": "mem", "component": "CheckBox", "label": "Enable memory", "value": {"path": "/memory"}},
        {"id": "save-txt", "component": "Text", "text": "Apply Settings"},
        {"id": "save", "component": "Button", "child": "save-txt", "variant": "primary",
         "action": {"event": {"name": "save_agent_config", "context": {"model": {"path": "/model"}}}}},
    ],
    data={"model": "gpt-4o", "temp": 0.3, "memory": True},
)
```

### Action Handler

```python
@aiui.surface_action("agent-config")
async def on_config(action: dict):
    aiui.push_notification("Agent updated", f"Saved {action.get('context')}", type="success")
    return {"ok": True}
```

## Test 1 — Push a second surface and switch live on `/canvas`

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/surfaces/checkout/messages \

  -d '{
    "replace": true,

      {"version": "v0.9", "createSurface": {"surfaceId": "checkout", "catalogId": "basic", "theme": {"primaryColor": "#0f766e"}}},
      {"version": "v0.9", "updateComponents": {"surfaceId": "checkout", "components": [
        {"id": "root", "component": "Card", "child": "col"},
        {"id": "col", "component": "Column", "children": ["hdr", "picker", "pay"]},
        {"id": "hdr", "component": "Text", "text": {"path": "/title"}, "variant": "h2"},
        {"id": "picker", "component": "ChoicePicker", "label": "Plan", "value": {"path": "/plan"},
         "options": [{"label": "Monthly ($19)", "value": "monthly"}, {"label": "Annual ($190)", "value": "annual"}]},
        {"id": "pay-lbl", "component": "Text", "text": "Continue"},
        {"id": "pay", "component": "Button", "child": "pay-lbl", "variant": "primary",
         "action": {"event": {"name": "checkout_submit", "context": {"plan": {"path": "/plan"}}}}}
      ]}},
      {"version": "v0.9", "updateDataModel": {"surfaceId": "checkout", "path": "/", "value": {"title": "Upgrade Plan", "plan": "annual"}}}
    ]
  }'
```

Open `/canvas`, click **Refresh**, and pick **`checkout`** from the **Surface** selector—or open `/canvas?surface=checkout` directly.

## Test 2 — Verify v0.8 backwards compatibility

Push a legacy **v0.8** payload (`surfaceUpdate` + `dataModelUpdate` + `beginRendering`) to surface `"legacy"`:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/surfaces/legacy/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "messages": [
      {"surfaceUpdate": {"surfaceId": "legacy", "components": [
        {"id": "hero", "component": {"Text": {"text": {"path": "/headline"}, "usageHint": "h1"}}}
      ]}},
      {"dataModelUpdate": {"surfaceId": "legacy", "path": "/", "contents": [
        {"key": "headline", "valueString": "Upgraded automatically from A2UI v0.8!"}
      ]}},
      {"beginRendering": {"surfaceId": "legacy", "root": "hero"}}
    ]
  }'
```

PraisonAIUI automatically upgrades it to v0.9 and renders it on `/canvas?surface=legacy`.

## Test 3 — Stream JSONL with the CLI

```bash
cat <<'EOF' > demo.jsonl
{"version":"v0.9","createSurface":{"surfaceId":"main","catalogId":"basic"}}
{"version":"v0.9","updateComponents":{"surfaceId":"main","components":[{"id":"root","component":"Text","text":{"path":"/msg"},"variant":"h2"}]}}
{"version":"v0.9","updateDataModel":{"surfaceId":"main","path":"/","value":{"msg":"Streamed from JSONL!"}}}
EOF

aiui surface push main --file demo.jsonl --replace --server http://127.0.0.1:8099
aiui surface capabilities --server http://127.0.0.1:8099
```

## Test 4 — Clear a surface with `deleteSurface`

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/surfaces/legacy/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages": [{"version": "v0.9", "deleteSurface": {"surfaceId": "legacy"}}]}'
```

# Content Sources

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-sources

> content.docs tells aiui build where your Markdown lives. Each file becomes a

`content.docs` tells `aiui build` where your Markdown lives. Each file becomes a
page under `site.routeBaseDocs` (default `/docs`).

## Docs Directory

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: "./docs"
```

The path is relative to the config file.

## Include/Exclude Patterns

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: "./docs"
    include:            # default: ["**/*.md", "**/*.mdx"]
      - "**/*.md"
    exclude:
      - "drafts/**"
      - "_*.md"
```

`include` patterns are globs relative to `dir`. An `exclude` pattern matches
the path relative to `dir`, a folder holding it (`drafts`, `drafts/`) or, with
no `/`, any file or folder name (`*.tmp`). A leading `/` anchors it to `dir`;
`!pattern` brings back a file an earlier pattern left out.

Excluded files are not published at all: `aiui build` copies neither the
pages nor the images next to them, and it lists what it left out.

The same patterns can live in an `.aiuiignore` file next to `aiui.yaml`, one
per line (`#` starts a comment); they add to `exclude`:

```text
# .aiuiignore
drafts/
internal/
*.secret.md
```

## Index Files

`index.md` and `README.md` (any case) are the page of their folder:
`guides/index.md` is served at `/docs/guides`. `indexFiles` is accepted in the
config, but other file names are not treated as index pages yet.

## Frontmatter

```markdown
---
title: "Custom Title"
order: 1
description: "One sentence for search results."
---

# Page Content
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `title` | Page title in the navigation; default: the first `#` heading, then the slug |
| `order` | Sort order within the folder (lower first); `0` or missing falls back to a number prefix |
| `description` | Meta description; default: the first paragraph of 20 or more characters, cut at 160 |
| `noindex` | `true` adds `robots: noindex, nofollow` and leaves the page out of the sitemap |
| `layout` | `home` on `docs/index.md` draws the [home page layout](#home-page-layout) |

The frontmatter block is not shown on the page.

## Home Page Layout

Frontmatter `layout: home` on the docs home page (`docs/index.md`) puts a
hero and a feature grid above the page's own Markdown, the way VitePress does:

```markdown
---
title: Acme
layout: home
hero:
  name: Acme                          # the page heading, in the accent colour
  text: Ship your agent's UI today    # the large headline
  tagline: One sentence that says what it is and who it is for.
  image: images/app-light.webp        # optional, relative to this page
  imageDark: images/app-dark.webp     # optional, shown in dark mode instead
  imageAlt: The app with a conversation open
  actions:
    - text: Quick start
      link: getting-started/quickstart.md
    - text: GitHub
      link: https://github.com/acme/acme
      theme: alt                      # brand (default) or alt
features:
  - title: Chat
    icon: message-square
    details: Streaming replies, tool calls and approvals.
    link: guides/chat.md
    linkText: Chat guide
---

## Install

The Markdown below the frontmatter renders under the hero.
```

- The hero image keeps a 16:10 box until the file arrives, so nothing below it
  jumps as it loads; once loaded it takes the image's own shape. Screenshots
  at 16:10 (1600 × 1000, say) never move the page. Only the image for the
  colour mode on screen downloads at first; the other one waits until the
  reader switches.
- `aiui build` adds `<link rel="preload" as="image">` for the hero to the home
  page's HTML, so the download starts with the page instead of after the app
  has drawn the hero. With `site.theme.mode: system` (or no mode) each image
  gets the matching `prefers-color-scheme` media query; a fixed `light` or
  `dark` preloads only that image. A reader whose saved light/dark choice
  differs from the system setting downloads both.

- Links and images resolve against the home page like Markdown links, and
  links to other sites open in a new tab.
- `icon` is one of `message-square`, `panels-top-left`, `layout-dashboard`,
  `book-open`, `plug`, `shield-check`, `code`, `terminal`, `bot`, `zap`,
  `rocket` and `palette` (lucide line icons); any other name shows no icon.
- Up to 4 actions and 12 features are kept. Every value is plain text.
- Only the docs home page reads `layout: home`; on other pages it does nothing.

## Numbered Prefixes

```
docs/
├── 01-introduction.md   # order 1, served at /docs/introduction
├── 02-installation.md   # order 2
└── 03-quickstart.md     # order 3
```

A leading number gives the order when the frontmatter sets none, and the
`NN-` prefix is stripped from the URL. Only a prefix at the start of a folder or
file name counts: digits inside a name stay (`ui-reset-2026-11.md` is served at
`/docs/ui-reset-2026-11`). A link that names the file (`01-introduction.md`)
opens the page at its URL.

## Static Hosting

`aiui build` writes a site any static host can serve, with no rewrite rules:

| File | Why |
|------|-----|
| `index.html` | The site root; it shows `docs/index.md` (the docs home page). `/docs` and `/docs/index` open the same page and move to `/`, the home page's one URL (also in the sitemap, `llms.txt` and canonical links) |
| `docs/<page>.html` | `/docs/<page>` on hosts that map a path to `<path>.html` (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages) |
| `docs/<page>/index.html` | `/docs/<page>/` on hosts that do not (S3, `python -m http.server`); the page drops the trailing slash |
| `docs/<page>.md` | The markdown the page loads, also for index pages (`guides/index.md` → `docs/guides.md`) and numbered files |
| `404.html` | Any other path loads the site, which opens the page the URL means (`/guides/setup` opens `/docs/guides/setup`) or shows "Page not found" with links home and to search |

## Related

- [Navigation](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md): how pages become the sidebar
- [SEO](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/seo.md): meta tags, sitemap and `robots.txt`

# Navigation

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation

> aiui build turns the docs folder into the sidebar (docs-nav.json). YAML

`aiui build` turns the docs folder into the sidebar (`docs-nav.json`). YAML
`navigation.tabs` then splits that sidebar into tabs.

## The Generated Sidebar

Each folder becomes a section and each Markdown file an entry:

- Inside a folder, pages sort by frontmatter `order`, then by file name (see
  [Content Sources](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-sources.md#frontmatter)).
- A folder's section takes the title of its `index.md` (or another
  `indexFiles` name) and links to it; a folder without one is titled with
  its name, title-cased. Link a folder's index page by the folder (`notes/`).
- An entry's title is the frontmatter `title`, else the first `#` heading.

The generated tree looks like this:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "title": "Getting Started",
      "path": "/docs/getting-started",
      "children": [
        { "title": "Installation", "path": "/docs/getting-started/installation" },
        { "title": "Quick Start", "path": "/docs/getting-started/quickstart" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`content.docs.nav.mode` picks between this generated sidebar (`auto`, the
default) and one you list in YAML (below). Options for the generated sidebar:

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    indexFiles: [index.md, README.md, _index.md]   # files that name their folder
    nav:
      sort: alpha        # filesystem (default) | alpha (title) | date (frontmatter `date`, newest first)
      collapsible: false # groups never fold (default: true)
      directory: card    # card | accordion: list each folder's pages (Directory Listings)
```

Frontmatter `order` wins over `sort`. A folder's index page is its section's
own page (the label links there).

## A Sidebar at the Root

`navigation.pages` and `navigation.groups` list the sidebar in order, with no
tab or `nav.mode` needed:

```yaml
navigation:
  pages:
    - index                   # a top-level page
    - group: "API"
      root: api/overview      # the group's own page: its label and breadcrumb link there
      tag: "New"              # a badge after the label (up to 24 characters)
      pages:
        - api/auth
        - group: "Errors"
          expanded: false     # starts folded
          pages: [api/errors]
  groups:
    - group: "Guides"
      directory: card         # list the group's pages on its page
      pages: [guide/setup, guide/deploy]
```

These group keys work in tab groups too.

## Folding Groups

Every group folds: click its label, or the chevron beside a label that links
to a page. Each reader's choice is remembered across reloads and visits. The
group holding the current page always opens. `interaction.drilldown: true`
makes a group label with no page of its own open the group's first page.

```yaml
interaction:
  drilldown: true
```

## Directory Listings

`directory: card` (a card grid) or `accordion` (a row per page) lists a
group's pages with their descriptions at the end of the group's page. A group
with no `root` gets a generated page at `/docs/<group-slug>` (`Guides` is
`/docs/guides`), or uses the page already there. `content.docs.nav.directory`
does this for every folder of the generated sidebar.

## Breadcrumbs

The line above a page title is the page's group. `styling.eyebrows:
breadcrumbs` shows every group above it, each with a page of its own linked.
Every page's HTML carries a schema.org `BreadcrumbList` for search engines.

```yaml
styling:
  eyebrows: breadcrumbs   # section (default) | breadcrumbs
```

## Checks

`aiui validate` and `aiui build` warn about a listed page name that matches no
page (code 2101, with the closest name; `aiui validate --strict` fails), a tab,
anchor or dropdown with nothing to open (2102) and about keys that
do nothing yet (1004: `nav.maxDepth`, `i18n.fallbackLocale`, `translationsDir`).

## A Sidebar You List (`mode: manual`)

With `content.docs.nav.mode: manual` the sidebar comes from the tab groups:
each group is a section holding the pages it lists, in that order, whatever
folder they live in. A `pages` entry may itself be a group, which nests a
section (one level is the usual choice).

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: "./docs"
    nav:
      mode: manual

navigation:
  tabs:
    - tab: "Guides"
      groups:
        - group: "App"
          pages:
            - features/styles
            - group: "Layouts"          # a nested section
              pages:
                - features/layouts
                - features/layouts/chat-canvas
        - group: "Deployment"
          pages:
            - features/deployment
            - health-endpoints          # a page at the docs root
    - tab: "Project"
      groups:
        - group: "Decisions"
          pages:
            - adr/index
            - adr/0001-replay-view      # the file name works too
```

- A page is named by its URL path under the docs base (`features/layouts`),
  its file path without `.md` (`adr/0001-replay-view`, `adr/index`) or
  `index` for the home page. A name that matches no page is skipped (and
  reported, see Checks).
- A page listed twice appears once, where it is first listed.
- Frontmatter `nav_title` gives a page a shorter sidebar title than its
  heading (`nav_title: CLI` on a page titled "CLI API Reference").
- Pages no group lists are still built and reachable by URL, but hidden: not
  in any sidebar, search, `sitemap.xml` or `llms.txt` (see
  [Hidden pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/seo.md#hidden-pages)). Leave a page out of the site with
  `content.docs.exclude` (see [Content Sources](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-sources.md#includeexclude-patterns)).
- `hidden: true` on a group hides its pages the same way; on a tab it also
  drops the tab from the header.
- `boost: 2` on a group ranks its pages higher in site search (0.1 to 10; a
  page's own `boost` wins; see [Search](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#search)). With
  tabs, search results can be filtered by tab.
- The active tab is the one whose groups list the page; for a page no group
  lists, the folder `prefix` decides as in auto mode, then the first tab.

## Sidebar Icons

A group's `icon:` in the navigation YAML, or a page's frontmatter `icon:`,
puts a 16px line icon before its title in the sidebar and the phone drawer.

```yaml
navigation:
  tabs:
    - tab: "Get started"
      groups:
        - group: "Get started"
          icon: rocket
          pages:
            - getting-started/quickstart
```

```markdown
---
title: CLI
icon: terminal
---
```

- Any [lucide icon](https://lucide.dev/icons) name (`flag`, `house`, or an
  old name such as `home`), an emoji (`icon: "🚀"`) or an image URL
  (`https://…` or `/icons/x.svg`). See [Icons](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#icons).
  `aiui validate` warns (7009) about a name that is not an icon.
- Page icons work in both modes; group icons need `mode: manual`.

## Tabs

`navigation.tabs` groups the sidebar sections into tabs in the header. A
section belongs to the first group whose `group` name matches its title, whose
`prefix` is its folder, or whose `pages` list one of its pages. The sidebar
shows only the active tab's sections, in the order of its groups; the active tab
follows the URL.

```yaml
navigation:
  tabs:
    - tab: "Documentation"
      groups:
        - group: "Getting Started"
          icon: "rocket"
          prefix: "getting-started"
          pages:
            - getting-started/installation
            - getting-started/quickstart
        - group: "Features"
          prefix: "features"
    - tab: "API Reference"
      groups:
        - group: "API"
          prefix: "api"
```

A section that no group of any tab claims is not shown while tabs are set.
In manual mode the groups are the sections, so each one belongs to its tab.

Clicking a tab opens its first page; the active tab follows the page you
are on. On phones the tabs move into the navigation drawer, where tapping
one shows its sidebar without leaving the page.

### Tab options

```yaml
navigation:
  tabs:
    - tab: "Guides"
      icon: book-open                  # any icon (see Sidebar Icons)
      pages: [index, quickstart]       # pages straight in the tab, no group needed
    - tab: "Blog"
      href: "https://example.com/blog" # a link out (opens in a new tab)
    - tab: "API"
      menu:                            # a small dropdown under the tab
        - item: "REST"
          description: "HTTP endpoints"
          icon: globe
          groups:
            - group: "REST"
              pages: [api/rest/users]
        - item: "SDKs"
          pages: [api/sdk/python, api/sdk/node]
        - item: "Status"
          href: "https://status.example.com"
```

| Key | On | Does |
|-----|----|------|
| `icon` | tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown | an icon before the name |
| `href` | tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown | a link instead of a sidebar (`url` still works on a tab) |
| `pages` | tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown | pages listed straight in it (before its `groups`) |
| `groups` | tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown | its sidebar sections |
| `hidden` | tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown | leaves the header and sidebar; its pages stay routable |
| `menu` | tab | items, each with its own sidebar or `href`; the tab opens the list |
| `description` | menu item, dropdown | a second line under the name |
| `tabs` | dropdown | header tabs shown while that dropdown is open |

## Anchors

Anchors are links pinned at the top of the sidebar on every page. An anchor
with `href` links out; one with `pages` or `groups` opens its own sidebar,
like a tab. `navigation.global.anchors` takes the same entries and lists
them first.

```yaml
navigation:
  global:
    anchors:
      - anchor: "Community"
        icon: users
        href: "https://example.com/forum"
  anchors:
    - anchor: "Changelog"
      icon: newspaper
      pages: [changelog]
```

## Dropdowns (Product Switcher)

`navigation.dropdowns` (also spelled `products`, with `product:` names) puts
a switcher at the top of the sidebar. Each entry opens its own sidebar, or
brings its own header `tabs`, so one site can hold several products.

```yaml
navigation:
  dropdowns:
    - dropdown: "Cloud"
      description: "Hosted service"
      icon: cloud
      tabs:
        - tab: "Guides"
          groups: [{ group: "Cloud", pages: [cloud/start, cloud/deploy] }]
        - tab: "API"
          pages: [cloud/api]
    - dropdown: "Self-hosted"
      description: "Run it yourself"
      icon: server
      groups:
        - group: "Install"
          pages: [self/install]
```

Tabs, menu items, anchors and dropdowns share one rule: each part with
pages or groups gets its own sidebar, and the page you are on decides which
one is open. `aiui validate` warns about one with no pages, groups or
`href` (code 2102) and about a listed page that does not exist (2101).

## Versions

`navigation.versions` publishes several versions of the docs side by side.
The default version is served at the docs root; every other version comes
from its own folder, with no page list needed:

```yaml
navigation:
  versions:
    - { version: v2, default: true, tag: Latest }   # docs/**  ->  /docs/...
    - { version: v1, tag: Deprecated }              # docs/v1/** ->  /docs/v1/...
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `version` | the name in the switcher; also the folder and URL segment (`v1`, `2.x`) |
| `default` | the version at the docs root (default: the first one) |
| `tag` | a badge after the name (`Latest`, `Beta`, `Deprecated`), up to 24 characters |
| `index` | `true` keeps an older version in the sitemap and `llms.txt` (default: only the default version) |
| `groups`, `pages`, `tabs` | the version's own sidebar and header tabs (with `nav.mode: manual`); without them the folder's pages form the sidebar |
| `hidden` | left out of the switcher; its pages stay routable |

A switcher at the top of the sidebar (and of the phone drawer) names the open
version. Picking another one opens the same page in it (`/docs/guide/setup`
and `/docs/v1/guide/setup`), or that version's first page when it has no
such page. The sidebar, the pager, the header tabs and the site search show
the open version only; the top-level `tabs` and `dropdowns` belong to the
default version, and anchors show in every version.

An older version's page names the default version's same page as its
canonical URL and carries `robots: noindex`, so search engines send readers
to the current docs; its pages stay out of `sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt`
unless the version sets `index: true`. A page's own `canonical` or `robots`
front matter wins. `aiui validate` reports two versions with one name, more
than one default, and a version that lists a page from another version's
folder (code 7018).

## Languages

`navigation.languages` publishes translated docs. The default language is
served at the docs root; every other one comes from its own folder, named by
its code, with no page list needed:

```yaml
navigation:
  languages:
    - { language: en, default: true }   # docs/**     ->  /docs/...
    - { language: fr }                  # docs/fr/**  ->  /docs/fr/...
    - { language: pt-BR, label: Português }
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `language` | the language code (`fr`, `pt-BR`); also the folder and URL segment |
| `label` | the name in the switcher (default: the language's own name, `Français`) |
| `default` | the language at the docs root (default: the first one) |
| `index` | `true` lists its pages in `llms.txt` too (default: only the default language) |
| `groups`, `pages` | its own sidebar (with `nav.mode: manual`); without them its folder's pages form the sidebar |
| `hidden` | left out of the switcher and the translation links; its pages stay routable |

A switcher in the header (an icon on phones) opens the same page in the
other language (`/docs/guide/setup` and `/docs/fr/guide/setup`), or that
language's first page when the page is not translated yet. The sidebar, the
pager and the site search show the open language only. The reader's pick is
remembered, and on a first visit to the docs home the reader's browser
language (`fr-CA` finds `fr`) opens its translation; crawlers and other
automated browsers always get the default language. `navigation.languageRedirect: false`
turns that redirect off.

Every page carries `<html lang>` and, when it has translations, a
`<link rel="alternate" hreflang>` for each (with `x-default` on the default
language's page); `sitemap.xml` lists the same alternates. `llms.txt` and
`llms-full.txt` hold the default language, and each other language gets its
own `llms-<code>.txt`.

With `navigation.versions` too, a language folder sits inside its version's
folder: `docs/v1/fr/` is served at `/docs/v1/fr/...`, and both switchers keep
the page. `aiui validate` reports two languages with one code, more than one
default, and a version folder inside a language folder such as `docs/fr/v1/`
(code 7020).

## Header Links

`navbar` adds links and one primary button to the header. On phones they move
into the navigation drawer.

```yaml
navbar:
  links:
    - label: "Blog"
      href: "https://example.com/blog"
      icon: newspaper       # optional: any icon value (lucide name, image URL, emoji)
    - type: discord         # github | discord: the network's mark; no label needed
      href: "https://discord.gg/your-server"
  primary:
    type: github            # button (default) | github | discord
    href: "https://github.com/your/repo"
```

A link with `type` and no `label` shows the network's mark alone, named for
screen readers. Links to another site open in a new tab.

The star count needs no setup: the browser asks the public GitHub API once and
keeps the answer for six hours. If it cannot get one, the button shows the mark
and the label.

## Footer

`footer.socials` maps a network to a URL and draws its mark; `footer.links`
adds columns of links above the bottom line.

```yaml
footer:
  socials:
    github: "https://github.com/your/repo"
    x: "https://x.com/you"
    discord: "https://discord.gg/your-server"
    status: "https://status.example.com"   # any key: a globe named "status"
  links:
    - header: "Company"                    # optional
      items:
        - label: "About"
          href: "https://example.com/about"
```

Known keys: `github`, `gitlab`, `x` (or `twitter`), `discord`, `slack`,
`linkedin`, `youtube`, `bluesky`, `mastodon`, `reddit`, `telegram`,
`facebook`, `instagram`, `threads`, `medium`, `hacker-news`, `npm`,
`website`, `email` (a `mailto:` URL), `rss` and `podcast`. Any other key whose
URL is on one of those sites gets that mark (`community:
https://discord.gg/x` shows Discord); the rest get a globe. Each mark is a link
named for its network.

## Banner

`banner` puts a strip above the header on every docs page:

```yaml
banner:
  content: "Version 2 is out. [Read the notes](/changelog)"   # Markdown
  dismissible: true      # a close button (default false)
  type: warning          # info (default) | warning | success
```

`banner: "Version 2 is out."` is the short form. A closed banner stays closed
for that reader until its content changes, so a new announcement shows again
with no key to bump.

# Templates & Layouts

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/templates

> Learn how templates and layouts work in PraisonAIUI.

Learn how templates and layouts work in PraisonAIUI.

## Overview

A template, used by the docs site (`aiui build`), combines:

- a **layout**: the structure around the page content
- **slots**: the components for the header, footer and table of contents (see
  [Slots & Components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/slots.md))
- optional **zones**: widgets around the content (see
  [Widget Zones](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/widget-zones.md))

Routes pick the template for a URL (see [Configuration](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#routes)).
These are docs-site layouts; the layouts of the React app shell are a different
thing (see [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md)).

## Layouts

Every layout sits between the site header and footer.

| Layout | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `ThreeColumnLayout` | Sidebar + content + TOC (the default) |
| `TwoColumnLayout` | Sidebar + content (no TOC) |
| `CenteredLayout` | Centered content, no sidebar; `hero` zone |
| `FullWidthLayout` | Sidebar when there is navigation, wide content; `hero` zone |
| `FlexibleLayout` | Sidebar (or `leftSidebar` widgets), content, TOC, and widget zones |

### ThreeColumnLayout

The classic documentation layout with sidebar and TOC.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Header                     │
├───────┬─────────────────────────┬───────────┤
│ Left  │          Main           │   Right   │
│(Side) │        (Content)        │   (TOC)   │
├───────┴─────────────────────────┴───────────┤
│                   Footer                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### TwoColumnLayout

Sidebar + Content without the right TOC column.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Header                     │
├───────┬─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Left  │              Main                    │
│(Side) │           (Content)                  │
├───────┴─────────────────────────────────────┤
│                   Footer                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### CenteredLayout

Centered content with no sidebar, ideal for articles/blogs.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Header                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Main (Centered)                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                   Footer                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### FullWidthLayout

The content takes the remaining width; the sidebar shows only when the site
has docs navigation.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Header                     │
├───────┬─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Left  │        Main (Full Width)             │
│(Side) │                                      │
├───────┴─────────────────────────────────────┤
│                   Footer                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Defining Templates

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "ThreeColumnLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "my_header" }
      left: { ref: "sidebar" }
      main: { type: "DocContent" }
      right: { type: "Toc" }
      footer: { ref: "my_footer" }
```

## Slot Assignment

Slots can be assigned in two ways:

### Reference (ref)
Point to a component defined in the `components` section:
```yaml
slots:
  header: { ref: "my_header" }
```

### Direct Type
Use a component type directly:
```yaml
slots:
  main: { type: "DocContent" }
```

### Null (hide)
`right: null` hides the table of contents (the only slot the renderer hides):
```yaml
slots:
  right: null
```

---

# Slots & Components

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/slots

> A template names a component for each slot of its layout. In the docs site that

A template names a component for each slot of its layout. In the docs site that
`aiui build` produces, the React renderer reads three slots; the others are
validated and compiled into the manifest but do not change the page.

## Slot System

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "ThreeColumnLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "main_header" }
      left: { type: "DocsSidebar" }
      main: { type: "DocContent" }
      right: { type: "Toc" }
      footer: { ref: "main_footer" }
```

| Slot | Effect in the docs site |
|------|-------------------------|
| `header` | Its component's props (`logoText`, `logoImage`, `links`, `cta`) fill the header. YAML `navbar` links and CTA win over `links`/`cta`, but `logoImage` wins over YAML `logo.light`/`logo.dark` |
| `footer` | Its component's props (`text`, `links`) fill the footer bottom row, next to YAML `footer` |
| `right` | `null` hides the table of contents; any other value shows it |
| `left`, `main` | No effect: the sidebar is always the generated navigation and the main area the page's Markdown |

Without a `header` or `footer` slot, the components named `header` and
`footer` are used. `aiui validate` checks that every `ref` names a component.

## Built-in Components

### Header

```yaml
components:
  my_header:
    type: "Header"
    props:
      logoText: "My Site"
      logoImage: "/logo.svg"
      links:
        - label: "Docs"
          href: "/docs"
        - label: "Blog"
          href: "/blog"
      cta:
        label: "Get Started"
        href: "/docs/quickstart"
```

### Footer

```yaml
components:
  my_footer:
    type: "Footer"
    props:
      text: "© 2024 My Company"
      links:
        - label: "GitHub"
          href: "https://github.com"
```

### DocsSidebar, DocContent, Toc

These name the generated navigation, the page content and the table of
contents. They take no props the renderer reads.

```yaml
slots:
  left: { type: "DocsSidebar" }
  main: { type: "DocContent" }
  right: { type: "Toc" }
```

## Custom Components

The docs site renderer has no hook for your own slot components. The separate
TypeScript runtime in the repository (`src/praisonaiui-ts`, see
[TypeScript](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/typescript.md)) has a `SlotRegistry` for apps that render
the manifests themselves. Pages in the React app shell are added with plugins
instead (see [Plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md)).

---

# Widget Zones

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/widget-zones

> Widget zones place small built-in widgets (stats cards, links, banners) around

Widget zones place small built-in widgets (stats cards, links, banners) around
the page content of a docs site (`aiui build`, `style: docs` or `custom`),
configured per template in YAML.

## Zone Layout

`FlexibleLayout` renders these zones:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              HERO                       │
├─────────┬───────────────────┬───────────┤
│  LEFT   │                   │   RIGHT   │
│ SIDEBAR │   page content    │  SIDEBAR  │
├─────────┴───────────────────┴───────────┤
│            BOTTOM NAV                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              FOOTER                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Configuration

Use the `zones` property in your template configuration:

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "FlexibleLayout"
    zones:
      hero:
        - type: "HeroBanner"
          props:
            title: "Welcome to Our Docs"
            subtitle: "Beautifully designed documentation"
            ctaLabel: "Get Started"
            ctaHref: "/docs/quickstart"
      
      rightSidebar:
        - type: "StatsCard"
          props:
            title: "Active Users"
            value: "15,231"
            change: "+20.1%"
            changeType: "positive"
        - type: "QuickLinks"
          props:
            title: "Resources"
            links:
              - label: "API Reference"
                href: "/docs/api"
              - label: "Examples"
                href: "/docs/examples"
      
      footer:
        - type: "Newsletter"
          props:
            title: "Stay Updated"
        - type: "SocialLinks"
          props:
            links:
              - platform: "GitHub"
                href: "https://github.com"
              - platform: "Twitter"
                href: "https://twitter.com"
        - type: "Copyright"
          props:
            text: "© 2024 My Company"
```

## Available Zones

| Zone | Location | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| `hero` | Above the content | Banners, announcements |
| `leftSidebar` | Left column | Replaces the docs navigation when set |
| `rightSidebar` | Right column | Below the table of contents |
| `bottomNav` | Below the content | Related links |
| `footer` | Bottom | Footer widgets, above the site footer |
| `header`, `topNav`, `main` | | Accepted by the schema; no layout renders them yet |

A `Toc` entry in `rightSidebar` is skipped: the table of contents is always
drawn there when the page has headings. When the config defines a component
named `sidebar`, `header` or `footer` and a template leaves the matching zone
(`leftSidebar`, `header`, `footer`) empty, the build fills the zone with that
component.

## Built-in Widgets

### StatsCard
Display metrics and statistics.

```yaml
- type: "StatsCard"
  props:
    title: "Downloads"
    value: "42,891"
    change: "+12%"
    changeType: "positive"  # or "negative"
```

### QuickLinks
Navigation links widget.

```yaml
- type: "QuickLinks"
  props:
    title: "Quick Links"
    links:
      - label: "API Reference"
        href: "/docs/api"
```

### Newsletter
Email subscription form.

```yaml
- type: "Newsletter"
  props:
    title: "Subscribe"
    buttonText: "Sign Up"
```

### HeroBanner
Landing page hero section.

```yaml
- type: "HeroBanner"
  props:
    title: "Welcome"
    subtitle: "Build amazing docs"
    ctaLabel: "Get Started"
    ctaHref: "/docs"
```

### SocialLinks
Social media links.

```yaml
- type: "SocialLinks"
  props:
    links:
      - platform: "GitHub"
        href: "https://github.com"
```

### Copyright
Copyright notice.

```yaml
- type: "Copyright"
  props:
    text: "© 2024 Company Name"
```

### Other widgets

| Widget | Props |
|--------|-------|
| `Progress` | `label`, `value` (0 to 100), `showPercent` (default true) |
| `Announcement` | `title`, `message`, `type` (`info`, `warning`, `success`) |
| `RecentPosts` | `title`, `posts` (list of `title`, `href`, `date`) |
| `BadgeList` | `title`, `badges` (list of strings) |

## Layouts Supporting Zones

| Layout | Zones rendered |
|--------|----------------|
| `FlexibleLayout` | `hero`, `leftSidebar`, `rightSidebar`, `bottomNav`, `footer` |
| `ThreeColumnLayout` (default) | `rightSidebar` |
| `CenteredLayout` | `hero` |
| `FullWidthLayout` | `hero` |
| `TwoColumnLayout` | none |

## Example

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "FlexibleLayout"
    zones:
      rightSidebar:
        - type: "StatsCard"
          props: { title: "Users", value: "15k" }
        - type: "StatsCard"
          props: { title: "Revenue", value: "$42k" }
      bottomNav:
        - type: "QuickLinks"
          props:
            title: "Related"
            links:
              - label: "Previous: Setup"
                href: "/docs/setup"
```

# Hot Reload

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/hot-reload

> Two commands reload during development: aiui dev for a docs site and

Two commands reload during development: `aiui dev` for a docs site and
`aiui run --reload` for an app.

## Docs sites: `aiui dev`

Run it in the folder that holds `aiui.yaml`:

```bash
aiui dev
```

```
⏳ Building aiui.yaml...
✓ Built in 0.4s

🚀 Preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
Edits rebuild and reload the page. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
```

It builds the site, serves it and opens it in the browser. Save a page, a
snippet or `aiui.yaml` and the site rebuilds and the open tab reloads by
itself, at the same scroll position (the URL keeps the `#heading`).

- **No configuration needed to start.** A folder with only a `docs/` folder of
  Markdown files works: the site is built with the defaults and titled after
  the folder.
- **A broken edit never takes the preview down.** The error is printed in the
  terminal and shown over the page, and the last good build stays up until you
  save a fix.
- **Warnings** from the build (content checks) print once each in the terminal.
- **Production output is untouched.** Each build goes to a temporary folder,
  removed on exit. The few lines of script that listen for rebuilds are added
  to pages as they are served, so `aiui build` output never contains them.
- The preview is served the way `aiui serve` serves the build: the same
  routes, cache rules and base path.

```bash
aiui dev --port 3000 --no-open       # another port; do not open a browser tab
aiui dev --config site/aiui.yaml     # a configuration elsewhere
aiui dev --base-path /               # preview at the root whatever basePath says
```

The tab listens on `/__aiui/dev` (Server-Sent Events) with a script served
from `/__aiui/dev.js`, so the preview runs under the site's
[Content Security Policy](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-security-policy.md). It only answers on this
machine unless you pass `--host`; build errors include file paths, so expose it
only on a network you trust. Every option is in the
[CLI reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/cli.md#aiui-dev).

## `aiui serve --watch`

`aiui serve --watch` rebuilds the site into the output folder on every change
in the configuration's folder, without reloading the browser. Use it when you
want the built files on disk; `aiui dev` is the writing loop.

## Apps: `aiui run --reload`

```bash
aiui run app.py --reload
```

Uvicorn restarts the server when a file in the folder of `app.py` changes, and
the restarted server loads `app.py` again with the same style, datastore and
config.

## Examples dashboard: `aiui dev --examples`

`aiui dev --examples` serves a small dashboard (default port 9000) that
switches between the example projects in a folder (each a directory with an
`aiui.yaml`, or the old name `aiui.template.yaml`):

```bash
aiui dev --examples examples --port 9000
```

## Related

- [Config Hot-Reload](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/config-hot-reload.md): reloading the runtime config of a
  running server
- [CLI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/cli.md)

# Internationalization (i18n)

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/i18n

> Key-based UI strings with locale switching and {name} interpolation, served by the i18n feature (praisonaiui.features.i18n). English, Spanish and French ship bu

Key-based UI strings with locale switching and `{name}` interpolation, served by the i18n feature (`praisonaiui.features.i18n`). English, Spanish and French ship built in.

## Quick Start

```bash
# List available locales
curl http://localhost:8000/api/i18n/locales

# Get strings for a locale
curl http://localhost:8000/api/i18n/strings/es

# Translate a key
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/i18n/translate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"key":"app.welcome","locale":"fr"}'
```

## How It Works

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Frontend"] -->|"t('app.welcome', 'es')"| B{"I18nProtocol"}
    B --> C["JSONLocaleManager"]
    C --> D["en: Welcome to PraisonAI"]
    C --> E["es: Bienvenido a PraisonAI"]
    C --> F["fr: Bienvenue sur PraisonAI"]
```

The i18n system uses a **key-based** translation approach:

1. Each string has a dotted key (e.g., `app.welcome`, `chat.send`)
2. Keys are grouped by prefix: `app`, `chat`, `skills`, `finops`, `nav`, `error`
3. `{name}` placeholders are replaced at lookup time
4. An unknown key returns the key itself; an unknown locale falls back to English

## Built-in Locales

| Locale | Language | Strings |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `en` | English | 36 |
| `es` | Spanish (Español) | 36 |
| `fr` | French (Français) | 36 |

## Configuration

```python
from praisonaiui.features.i18n import JSONLocaleManager, set_i18n_manager

mgr = JSONLocaleManager(default_locale="es")
set_i18n_manager(mgr)

# Translate
mgr.t("app.welcome")          # "Bienvenido a PraisonAI"
mgr.t("app.welcome", "fr")    # "Bienvenue sur PraisonAI"
mgr.t("chat.memory.chip", count=3)  # "3 recuerdos"
```

A different backend implements `I18nProtocol` (`t`, `list_locales`,
`get_strings`, `get_locale`, `set_locale`) and is installed with
`set_i18n_manager()`.

## Locale Switcher (React styles)

The React styles read a YAML `i18n` block. With more than one locale, the header
shows a locale switcher; picking a locale loads its strings from
`/api/i18n/strings/{locale}` and sets the server locale. A locale in
`rtlLocales` switches the page to right-to-left.

```yaml
i18n:
  defaultLocale: en
  locales: [en, es, fr]
  rtlLocales: []
```

## REST API

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/i18n/locales` | GET | List available locales |
| `/api/i18n/strings/{locale}` | GET | Get all strings for a locale |
| `/api/i18n/translate` | POST | Translate a key with optional variables |
| `/api/i18n/locale` | GET | Get current default locale |
| `/api/i18n/locale` | POST | Set default locale |

### GET /api/i18n/strings/es

```json
{
    "locale": "es",
    "strings": {
        "app.title": "PraisonAI",
        "app.welcome": "Bienvenido a PraisonAI",
        "chat.send": "Enviar",
        "...": "..."
    },
    "count": 36
}
```

An unknown locale returns 404; a malformed one 400.

### POST /api/i18n/translate

```json
// Request
{"key": "app.welcome", "locale": "fr"}

// Response
{"key": "app.welcome", "text": "Bienvenue sur PraisonAI"}
```

Pass `"variables": {"count": 3}` to fill placeholders.

# OpenAPI

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/openapi

> Point the docs site at an OpenAPI spec; aiui build loads, bundles and checks it.

Name your spec in `aiui.yaml`; `aiui validate` and `aiui build` load and check it.

```yaml
api:
  openapi: openapi.yaml   # or https://api.example.com/openapi.json
```

- A file (relative to `aiui.yaml`) or an `http(s)` URL; `http://localhost:8080/openapi.json` works with no flag.
- JSON or YAML, OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2. Swagger 2.0 is an error.
- A `$ref` to another file (`paths/pets.yaml`, `../common.yaml#/components/schemas/Error`)
  resolves relative to the file naming it, URLs too, and is bundled in: no pre-bundling.
  Recursive schemas, across files too, stay finite.
- 3.0 specs are normalised to 3.1 rules for rendering (`nullable`, boolean
  `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum`, schema `example`); the published file keeps your version.

`openapi` also goes on a navigation tab or group: a path or URL, `{source, directory}` or a
list of either. A spec named twice loads once. `directory`: the URL folder of its endpoint pages
(default `api-reference`).

```yaml
navigation: {tabs: [{tab: API, openapi: [v2.yaml, {source: admin.yaml, directory: api/admin}]}]}
```

## Checks

Each problem names its file, line and JSON pointer (`openapi.yaml:42: $ref '#/x' does not
resolve (at #/components/schemas/Pet/properties/owner)`). Errors fail `validate` and
`build`: an unreadable file or URL, YAML/JSON syntax, a missing or unsupported `openapi`
version, `info` without `title`/`version`, a `$ref` that does not resolve, a path not
starting with `/`, a duplicate `operationId`. Warning: a `{param}` with no path parameter.

## Output

`aiui build` writes `openapi/<slug>.json` (the spec bundled into one file, `x-excluded`
operations removed; `<slug>`: file name, `-2` on a clash), `openapi/index.json`
(`{"specs": [{source, file, title, openapi, version, operations}]}`), an "OpenAPI specs"
section in `llms.txt` and an [RFC 9727](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9727) API catalog at
`/.well-known/api-catalog` (each API's base URL, spec and first endpoint page).

## Endpoint pages

Every operation and 3.1 webhook gets a docs page, generated at build time as Markdown with
the [API field components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#api-fields): the endpoint bar with [Try it](#try-it), server URL,
deprecation notice, path / query / header / cookie parameters, request body,
each response ([schemas](#schemas) with `oneOf`/`anyOf` tabs, constraints and conditional
requirements), [request examples](#request-examples) in several languages, [response examples](#response-examples), callbacks and a link to the spec. They publish like hand-written pages: agent `.md`, `llms.txt`,
`llms-full.txt`, sitemap and site search (which also matches `METHOD /path`, the
`operationId` and every parameter and body field name).

| Spec | Result |
|---|---|
| `api.openapi` only | an "API Reference" group at the end of the sidebar |
| `openapi` on a tab | its tag groups join the tab ("API Reference" for untagged operations) |
| `openapi` on a group | its tag groups go inside that group |
| `tags` | one sidebar group per operation's first tag; label: `x-group`, `x-displayName`, `summary`, then `name`; 3.2 `parent` nests groups; a tag with another `kind` (`badge`) makes no group |
| untagged webhook | a "Webhooks" group |
| `x-hidden: true` | page built and routable, not in the sidebar or indexes |
| `x-excluded: true` | no page, and removed from the published spec |
| `deprecated: true` | a deprecation notice |

URL: `/docs/<directory>/<tag name>/<slug>`, the slug from the `operationId` (`listPets` ->
`list-pets`, so rewording a summary keeps the URL), else the summary, else method and path
(`get-pets-id`). `x-aiui: {href: /reference/pets}` sets the whole path (kebab-cased, `..`
dropped; see [page settings](#page-settings-in-the-spec)). A slug already taken (by a hand-written page or another endpoint) gets `-2`, `-3`.
The title is the `summary` as written, else the `operationId` in words. `aiui validate`
warns about a duplicate tag, an unknown `parent` and a `parent` cycle.

### Schemas

Each field shows what the schema says, at build time, in the page Markdown (so agents and
search see it too):

| Schema | On the page |
|---|---|
| `$ref`, `allOf` | followed and merged into one field list |
| `oneOf` / `anyOf` | tabs, one per choice, titled by its `title`, else its `$ref` name, else its type, else "Option n"; at the top of a body or response too |
| `nullable: true`, `type: [x, "null"]`, `anyOf: [X, {type: "null"}]` | `x \| null` in the type; the field still expands to X's properties |
| `object[]`, nested objects | properties nested under "Show properties", a recursive schema stops one level down |
| `enum`, `const` | "Available options: `card`, `bank`", "Allowed value: `card`" |
| `minimum`/`maximum` (exclusive too), `minLength`/`maxLength`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, `pattern` | "Required range: `1 <= x < 100`", "Required string length: `16 - 19`", "Required array length: `>= 1` elements", "Pattern: `^[0-9]+$`" |
| `examples` / `example` on a field | "Example: `5`" (short values) |
| `additionalProperties`, `not` | "Additional properties: `string`", "Must not match: `integer`" |
| `if`/`then`/`else`, `dependentRequired`, `dependentSchemas` (also inside `allOf`) | a pill on each affected field: "required if method = card", "required unless method = card", "required if owner is set"; an `if` that tests more than sibling `const` / `enum` / `required` shows "conditionally required" |

```yaml
api:
  openapi: openapi.yaml
  params: {expanded: all}   # nested properties start open (default: closed)
```

### Response examples

The side column's response example has one tab per status code, content type (when a response
has several) and named example (its `summary`, else its key). This gives the tabs
`200 · application/json · A small cat`, `200 · application/json · big` and `200 · application/xml`:

```yaml
responses:
  "200":
    content:
      application/json:
        examples:
          small: {summary: A small cat, value: {name: Tom}}
          big: {value: {name: Garfield}}
      application/xml: {example: "<cat/>"}
```

Per content type: the `examples` map (`value`, 3.2 `dataValue` / `serializedValue`, or the
`externalValue` URL), else `example`, else for JSON an example built from the schema. JSON is
pretty-printed (a JSON string too); XML, HTML, YAML and CSV are highlighted; other types are text.

### Request examples

The side column shows the request as code, one tab per language: cURL, Python and
JavaScript by default. A pick is remembered, so every endpoint page opens on the reader's
language. Each sample is built at build time from the spec: the server URL (variables set to
their defaults; a relative or missing server is joined to `https://api.example.com`), path
parameters (their example, else a `{name}` placeholder), required query, header and cookie
parameters and any with an example, the first security requirement as a placeholder
(`Bearer <token>`, `Basic <encoded-value>`, an API key `<api-key>` in its header, query or
cookie) and the body (its first example, else one made from the schema without `readOnly`
fields). JSON, form-urlencoded and plain-text bodies work in every language; `multipart/form-data`
in cURL, Python and JavaScript (a `format: binary` field is sent as a file).

```yaml
api:
  openapi: openapi.yaml
  examples:
    languages: [curl, python, go]   # or all; [] shows only the spec's own samples
```

Languages: `curl`, `python`, `javascript`, `go`, `java`, `ruby`, `php`, `csharp`, `rust`,
`swift` (also `shell`, `node`, `js`, `py`, `c#`, `dotnet`, ...). `aiui validate` names an
unknown one.

Your own samples, from an SDK say, go in the operation's `x-codeSamples` (or `x-code-samples`).
They come first, in their order; one in a generated language replaces that sample, any other
language adds a tab. `label` is the tab title (default: the language's name).

```yaml
x-codeSamples:
  - {lang: python, label: Python SDK, source: "client.pets.list(limit=10)"}
  - {lang: kotlin, source: "client.pets().list(10)"}
```

The agent `.md` export, `llms-full.txt` and the page source keep every sample as a fence.

### Try it

Under the title, every endpoint page has an endpoint bar (method, path, copy) and **Try it**: a
request form with a server menu (operation, path, then spec `servers`) and an input per server
variable, an input per path, query, header and cookie parameter (`enum` and boolean as menus,
arrays comma-separated, empty `required` ones named before sending) and the body to edit
(`multipart/form-data` as a JSON object of its fields). Inputs start with `x-default`, else the
example (`example`, `examples`, `default`, `const`, first `enum` value); the body with its first
example, else one made from the schema. Beside them: the curl command for exactly what will be
sent, live, with copy, and after Send the status, time, size, headers and body (JSON
pretty-printed). A relative or missing server URL means the site the docs are served from.

```yaml
api:
  playground:
    display: interactive   # simple: the bar without Try it; none: method and path as plain text;
                           # auth: Try it only for readers signed in to the aiui server
  examples:
    prefill: true          # false: inputs start empty, the example as placeholder
```

With `auth`, the bar asks `GET /api/auth/status` once per page load and shows Try it only when it
answers `authenticated: true` (an `aiui serve` or `create_app` site whose reader is signed in;
without sign-in configured, every reader counts as signed in). On a static host it acts like
`simple`.

Webhooks have no Try it. Front matter `playground:` (same values) sets the display of one
[`openapi:` or `api:` page](#endpoints-on-your-own-pages), `x-aiui` `metadata.playground` of
one generated page.

The request goes straight from the reader's browser to your API: no proxy, so it works on a
static host and keys never pass through a third party, and the browser's CORS rules apply. The
API must allow the docs site's origin (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; for custom headers or a
JSON body, a preflight `OPTIONS` with `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`). A blocked request says it
"did not reach the API" (the curl command still works in a terminal). Response headers other
than the CORS-safelisted ones show only when listed in `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`; a cookie
parameter goes only into the curl command (a browser sends just the cookies it holds).

`aiui build` writes each page's form data to `openapi/try/<page>.json`; the form is a lazy chunk
loaded on the first hover, focus or click of Try it. In the page source the bar is
`<ApiPlayground method="GET" path="/pets" src="/openapi/try/....json" />` (without `src`, the bar
alone, usable on a hand-written page); the agent `.md` keeps `` `GET` `/pets` ``.

#### Authentication

An operation's `security` (else the spec's) becomes an **Authorization** section on its page (a
field per scheme, required when every alternative needs it, OAuth2 scopes listed) and inputs in
Try it: `apiKey` in a header, query or cookie, `http` `bearer` (and any other scheme name),
`http` `basic` (username and password, base64-encoded for you), `oauth2` and `openIdConnect` (paste
an access token; sent as `Bearer`). With several alternatives a menu picks one (`{}` in the list
adds "None"); `security: []` turns it off; `mutualTLS` is left out (a browser cannot send it).
A scheme's `x-default` prefills its input.

```yaml
components:
  securitySchemes:
    token: {type: http, scheme: bearer, bearerFormat: JWT, x-default: test-token}
    key: {type: apiKey, in: query, name: api_key}
security: [{token: []}, {key: []}]
```

Values are kept in the browser tab's `sessionStorage` per docs site (gone when the tab closes,
never `localStorage`) and sent only with the request itself. The curl command shows them as
`********` until **Show values**; the request examples on the page keep placeholders
(`Bearer <token>`).

#### Files and streams

- `multipart/form-data`: a file input per part with `format: binary` / `byte` or a
  `contentMediaType`; the chosen file replaces that field (curl `--form 'photo=@cat.png'`).
- A body that is a file (`application/octet-stream`, `image/*`, `audio/*`, `video/*`, PDF, or a
  `format: binary` schema): one file input, sent as the body (curl `--data-binary`).
- A JSON field with `format: byte` or `contentEncoding: base64` / `base64url`: a file input
  that writes the file's encoding into the body.
- A `text/event-stream`, NDJSON or JSON Lines response is shown as it arrives: server-sent events
  as a list (event name, id, data with JSON pretty-printed), other streams as text. **Stop**
  ends it; reading stops at 10 MB; a broken connection says "Stream interrupted."

**(planned)**: method and `kind: badge` pills in the
sidebar, a choice picker for `any` fields, `api.optional`, and showing image, audio and video responses inline.

## Endpoints on your own pages

Name an operation in a page's front matter and the page shows it: the endpoint bar and Try it
under your `#` title, your Markdown, then the generated parameters, body, responses and
request and response examples.

```markdown
---
openapi: "GET /users"
---

# Listing users

Paging works like this...
```

- `"GET /users"` looks in every spec the config names; `"admin.yaml POST /users"` in that file
  (its name is enough; a file only pages name is loaded, relative to `aiui.yaml`, and published);
  `"webhook user-created"` names a webhook.
- `title`, `description` and search keywords come from the operation unless the page sets them;
  the spec's description shows only when the page has no text of its own.
- The operation gets no generated page of its own: your page replaces it.
- `playground: simple` (or `none`) on the page changes its Try it display.

### Pages without a spec

`api:` makes an endpoint page from the page alone: the bar, and Try it with an input per
`<ParamField>` (`placeholder`, else `default`, as the example), per `{param}` in the path, and a
JSON body of the `body` fields.

```markdown
---
api: "POST /v1/users"
---

<ParamField body="name" type="string" placeholder="Ada" required>The name.</ParamField>
```

```yaml
api:
  server: https://api.example.com     # or a list: a menu in Try it
  auth: {method: key, name: X-API-Key}  # bearer (default), basic, key or none: Try it's Authorization inputs
```

### Endpoints in navigation

A `pages:` entry can be an operation: `"GET /users"`, `"admin.yaml POST /users"` or
`"webhook user-created"`. Without a file it comes from the nearest group or tab with `openapi`,
else `api.openapi`, else any spec. When a spec's own group (or `api.openapi`) lists operations,
only the listed ones get pages, each where it is listed, and no tag groups are added. An entry
for an operation a page shows (`openapi:` front matter) links that page.

```yaml
navigation:
  groups:
    - group: Users
      openapi: openapi.yaml
      pages: [guides/users, "GET /users", "POST /users", "webhook user-created"]
```

`aiui validate` names a reference that matches no operation (7012).

### Page settings in the spec

An operation's `x-aiui` sets its generated page: `metadata` is front matter (`title`,
`sidebarTitle`, `description`, `playground`, `tag`, `og:*`, ...), `content` is Markdown shown
above the description (any docs component works) and `href` the page URL. The `x-mint` key
other docs tools write is read too; `x-aiui` wins where both set a value.

```yaml
x-aiui:
  metadata: {title: Create a user, sidebarTitle: Create, tag: NEW}
  content: "<Note>Needs an admin key.</Note>"
```

From Python, `praisonaiui.compiler.openapi.load_spec("openapi.yaml")` returns an `ApiSpec`
(`ok`, `issues`, `document`, `operations`, `dereference(node)`).

# Python API reference

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/api-reference-python

> One line in a docs page and aiui build writes the reference for a Python module, class or function from its docstrings.

Write one line in a docs page and the build turns it into the reference for
that Python module, class or function:

```markdown
::: mypkg.client
```

No extra tool or build step. The source is read as text (Python's `ast`), so
the package does not have to be installed and nothing is imported. `aiui dev`
rebuilds the page when you save a `.py` file. The reference goes in where the
line is, in the same pass as [snippets](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#reusable-snippets-and-variables),
so the page, its agent `.md`, `llms-full.txt`, search and `aiui validate` all see it.

## What a block shows

| You write | You get |
|---|---|
| `::: mypkg.client` | The module docstring, then its public members: `__all__` in order when there is one (re-exports followed), else every public class and function |
| `::: mypkg.client.Client` | The class: constructor signature and parameters, bases, attributes (annotated or documented, properties, `Field(default=, description=)`), then its public methods |
| `::: mypkg.client.connect` | One function or method |

Each object gets a heading anchored by its dotted path with dashes
(`#mypkg-client-Client-fetch`) and its signature with type hints and defaults.
Names starting with `_` are left out. From the docstring:

- **Parameters**: [`<ParamField>`](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#api-fields) rows with the
  type and default from the signature, `required` when there is no default,
  and the text; documented `**kwargs` keys get rows too. **Attributes**:
  `<ResponseField>` rows.
- **Returns**, **Yields**, **Raises**: lists of types with their text.
- `>>>` examples, `::` blocks and `.. code-block::`: highlighted code.
  **Notes**, **Warnings**, `.. note::`, `.. warning::`: callouts.

Google (`Args:`), NumPy (`Parameters` over `----------`) and reST (`:param x:`,
`:type x:`, `:returns:`, `:rtype:`, `:raises E:`) styles all work. reST roles
become code, and `<` is escaped so text never turns into a tag.

## Options

YAML on the indented lines under the block (an `options:` mapping works too):

```markdown
::: mypkg.client.Client
    members: [connect, close]
    heading_level: 3
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `members` | all public | Only these members, in this order; `false`: the object alone |
| `private` | `false` | Also `_name` members (not `__dunder__`) |
| `show_source` | `false` | A collapsed "Source code" block under each object |
| `heading_level` | `2` | Heading level of the block's own object (`1` to `6`) |

## Where modules are found

`mypkg.client` is `mypkg/client.py`, `mypkg/client/__init__.py` or a `.pyi`, in
`src/`, then the project folder. Change the folders, searched in order:

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: docs
    reference:
      paths: [src, packages/sdk]
```

## Checks

A block naming no module or member, a file that is not valid Python, or an
unknown option is 7016 in `aiui validate` and fails `aiui build` with the page
and line. A `:::` line inside a code fence is left alone.

## Example

The class behind this page, from `::: praisonaiui.compiler.python_api.PythonApi`
with `members: [markdown]` and `heading_level: 3`:

### `PythonApi` {#praisonaiui-compiler-python_api-PythonApi}

```python
PythonApi(root: Path, paths: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_PATHS)
```

Finds and renders the objects ``:::`` blocks name.

**Parameters**

- `root` (Path, required): The project folder.

- `paths` (list[str] | tuple[str, ...], default: DEFAULT_PATHS): Folders under ``root`` searched in order for a module's file.

#### `PythonApi.markdown()` {#praisonaiui-compiler-python_api-PythonApi-markdown}

```python
def markdown(target: str, opts: dict) -> str
```

The Markdown for one ``::: target`` block.

**Parameters**

- `target` (str, required): A dotted module path, optionally followed by a class, function or method.

- `opts` (dict, required): The block's options (``members``, ``private``, ``show_source``, ``heading_level``).

**Returns**

- `str`: Headings, signatures and field rows for the docs Markdown pipeline.

**Raises**

- `ApiReferenceError`: When ``target`` names nothing, or a listed member does not exist.
