# SEO

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/seo

> Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

## Configuration

Top-level `seo` block in `aiui.yaml`:

```yaml
seo:
  siteUrl: "https://ui.praison.ai"
  titleTemplate: "%s | %s"
  defaultImage: "/icon.svg"
  robots:
    index: true          # false: the whole site is noindex (see below)
    follow: true
  indexing: navigable    # or `all`: index hidden pages too
  trailingSlash: false   # true: canonical, og:url, sitemap and llms URLs end in /
  ogImages: true         # a generated social card per page (needs Pillow); false: defaultImage
  contentSignals:        # optional robots.txt Content-Signal line
    search: true
    aiInput: true
    aiTrain: false
  twitter:
    handle: "@yourhandle"
  metatags:              # extra head tags on every page
    google-site-verification: "abc123"
    og:locale: en_GB
  paths:                 # head tags for the pages under a folder
    - path: v1           # or /docs/v1, v1/*; the longest matching path wins
      metatags:
        robots: noindex
  organization:          # the JSON-LD publisher (default: site title, siteUrl, logo)
    name: Acme Inc
    logo: /logo.svg
    sameAs: [https://github.com/acme]
```

Every key is optional; the defaults are what most sites want.

`siteUrl` is needed for absolute canonical URLs and `sitemap.xml`. Without it
the build falls back to a `CNAME` file next to the config (or in `docs/`), and
without either there is no sitemap and `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` use
root-relative links. What the build publishes for agents (agent-ready `.md`
pages, `llms.txt` by nav group, `markdown.instructions`):
[AI-ready docs](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md).

## Build outputs

`aiui build` automatically generates:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `sitemap.xml` | All doc URLs with `lastmod` dates |
| `robots.txt` | Crawl rules + sitemap pointer |
| `llms.txt` | AI crawler index ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org)), one section per nav group |
| `llms-full.txt` | Every page as agent-ready Markdown, in one file |
| `docs/**/*.html` | Per-route HTML with meta tags + crawl nav |
| `.nojekyll` | GitHub Pages Jekyll bypass |

No extra flags are needed: the files are written whenever `content.docs` is
configured (the site-URL ones only when a site URL is known, see above).

A `robots.txt` or `sitemap.xml` next to `aiui.yaml` is published as it is,
instead of the generated one.

## Who gets indexed

One rule decides the sitemap, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, site search and
the page's robots meta, so they never disagree:

| Page | Sidebar | Sitemap, llms, search | `<meta name="robots">` |
|------|---------|-----------------------|------------------------|
| normal | yes | yes | `index, follow` |
| `noindex: true` | yes | no | `noindex` |
| hidden | no | no (yes with `seo.indexing: all`) | `noindex` (`index, follow` with `all`) |
| any, with `seo.robots.index: false` | as above | no sitemap or llms files; search kept | `noindex` |
| `searchable: false` | yes | sitemap and llms yes; site search no | `index, follow` |

Each page has exactly one robots meta tag. `noindex` does not add `nofollow`:
crawlers still follow the page's links to the pages that are indexed.

With `seo.robots.index: false`, robots.txt says `Disallow: /`, and no
`sitemap.xml` or `llms*.txt` is written (one left from an earlier build is
removed).

### Hidden pages

```markdown
---
title: Beta feature
hidden: true
---
```

A hidden page is built and reachable by its URL (share the link), but it is
not in the sidebar, the previous / next links or search, and not indexed.
In `content.docs.nav.mode: manual`, `hidden: true` on a group or tab hides
all its pages, and pages no group lists are hidden too
([Navigation](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md#a-sidebar-you-list-mode-manual)).

A folder without an `index.md` is a sidebar section only, never a page: it
gets no route and no sitemap entry.

### Content signals

`seo.contentSignals` writes a [Content-Signal](https://contentsignals.org)
line into robots.txt, saying how crawlers may use the pages: `search`
(search results), `aiInput` (answers grounded on the page) and `aiTrain`
(model training). Keys you leave out are left out of the line; with no
`contentSignals` there is no line.

```text
User-agent: *
Allow: /
Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no
```

## Page-level overrides

Use frontmatter on any markdown page:

```markdown
---
title: "Custom Page Title"
description: "Custom meta description for search snippets"
noindex: true    # keep it in the sidebar, out of search engines and site search
hidden: true     # keep it out of the sidebar too (see Hidden pages)
---

# Page Content
```

If `description` is omitted, the first paragraph is used automatically.
Component and HTML tags are left out of it: a page that opens with
`<Note>` or a multi-line `<img>` gets its first sentence of prose.

Any Open Graph, Twitter or article tag, the canonical URL, the robots value
and keywords can be set per page (quote keys that have a colon):

```markdown
---
title: Install
canonical: https://example.com/original/install
robots: noindex, nofollow
keywords: [install, setup]
'og:image': /images/install-card.png
'twitter:card': summary
---
```

Each tag is decided once, in this order (later wins): the built defaults,
`seo.metatags`, `seo.paths` (shorter paths first), the page's frontmatter.
Then `og:url` follows the canonical and `twitter:image` the `og:image`
(unless set themselves), and `twitter:card` is `summary_large_image` when the
page has an image. Root-relative URLs (`/images/x.png`) become absolute.
A noindex page keeps `noindex` whatever the overrides say, and a `robots`
value with `noindex` (from frontmatter or a `seo.paths` folder) also leaves
the page out of the sitemap, `llms.txt` and search, so they never disagree.
Open Graph keys (`og:`, `article:`) are written as `property=`, the rest as
`name=`; every value is HTML-escaped. `aiui validate` rejects a
`seo.metatags` key that is not a tag name.

## Social cards

Install Pillow and every docs page gets its own share image, with no config:

```bash
pip install pillow
aiui build
```

The build draws a 1200x630 PNG per page and publishes it at
`/og/<page route>.png` (`/og/docs/guide/install.png`). Each card shows the
page title (sized to fit, up to three lines), its sidebar group, as much of
the description as fits, the site name with its logo and the site's host,
in the theme's accent and colour mode (`site.theme.preset`, `accent`,
`accentDark`, `mode`; preset `paper` gets the paper colours). A PNG, JPEG,
WebP or GIF `logo` is drawn as is; an SVG or emoji logo becomes the site's
initial on an accent tile. Latin text uses the UI's own font; other scripts
use a system font (Noto Sans CJK, Arial Unicode, Noto Sans or DejaVu Sans).

The card becomes the page's `og:image` and `twitter:image`, with a
`summary_large_image` card, in the built HTML and when the docs app moves
between pages, and the site root shares the docs home's card.

Which image a page gets, first match wins:

| Set by | Image |
|--------|-------|
| `'og:image'` in the page's frontmatter or a `seo.paths` folder | that image, no card drawn |
| `og:image` in `seo.metatags` | that image on every page, no cards drawn |
| `seo.ogImages: false`, or Pillow not installed | `seo.defaultImage` |
| otherwise | the page's generated card |

Cards are cached by a hash of what they show (in `$AIUI_DATA_DIR/og-cards`,
else `~/.praisonaiui/cache/og-cards`), so `aiui dev` and repeat builds only
draw the pages that changed, and new cards are drawn in parallel. Without
Pillow, `aiui build` prints one note saying how to turn them on.

## Per-page HTML includes

Each route HTML file contains:

- `<link rel="canonical">` (absolute HTTPS)
- `<meta name="description">`
- Open Graph tags (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:type`, `og:site_name`, `og:image`: the page's [social card](#social-cards) by default), each once
- Twitter Card tags (`summary_large_image` with an image)
- Your `seo.metatags`, `seo.paths` and frontmatter tags
- One JSON-LD `@graph`: `Organization`, `WebSite` (with a `SearchAction`: `?q=` opens site search),
  `TechArticle` (publisher, `dateModified` with `content.docs.lastUpdated`, keywords, image) and a
  `BreadcrumbList` from the sidebar groups
- Static `<nav>` with links to every doc page (for non-JS crawlers)
- `<noscript>` pre-rendered page content

## Runtime (SPA navigation)

When users navigate via the sidebar, React updates title, canonical, OG, Twitter, robots, and JSON-LD to match the current page, with the same tags, overrides and order as the built HTML (`docs-nav.json` carries each page's `seo` map). The built page's JSON-LD graph stays while it is the page shown.

## Deploy

See [GitHub Pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/github-pages.md) for publishing the build. Submit your sitemap in [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console):

```
https://your-domain.com/sitemap.xml
```

# Redirects and the not-found page

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/redirects

> Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and

Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and
choose what readers see on a URL with no page.

## Redirects

List moved pages under `redirects:` at the top level of `aiui.yaml`:

```yaml
redirects:
  - source: /docs/getting-started
    destination: /docs/quickstart
  - source: /docs/v1/:slug*          # everything under /docs/v1
    destination: /docs/:slug*
  - source: /blog/:year/:post
    destination: /news/:post
  - source: /docs/beta
    destination: /docs/preview
    permanent: false                 # 302 instead of 301
  - source: /support
    destination: https://example.com/help
```

| Key | Meaning |
|-----|---------|
| `source` | A site path starting with `/`. `:name` matches one path segment; a final `:name*` matches the rest of the path, including nothing (`/docs/v1/:slug*` matches `/docs/v1` and `/docs/v1/a/b`). |
| `destination` | A site path or a full URL. It can reuse the names from `source`. |
| `permanent` | `true` (default) answers with 301, `false` with 302. |

The first matching rule wins. Leave out the `--base-path` prefix: rules use
site paths and the build adds the base path.

### Where each kind of rule works

`aiui build` publishes every rule whose source is not a published page:

| Host | Exact source (`/docs/old`) | Wildcard source (`/docs/v1/:slug*`) |
|------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `aiui serve` | 301 / 302 | 301 / 302 (a file at the path wins) |
| Netlify, Cloudflare Pages | 301 / 302 from the `_redirects` file | 301 / 302 from `_redirects` |
| GitHub Pages, any static host | A stub page at the old URL (meta refresh, a canonical link, a script redirect) | The docs app follows the rule from the page-not-found view |

The query string and the `#section` carry over unless the destination sets
its own. A stub never replaces a real file; it has `noindex` and a canonical
link to the new URL. The [link check](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/cli.md#aiui-docs-check-links)
treats every source as a valid link.

### Checks

`aiui validate` warns when an exact rule loops or ends at a docs path with no
page (7010), or when a page is still published at its source (7011).

## The not-found page

A URL with no page shows "Page not found", a link home, the search, and up
to three pages from the sidebar whose names are close to the URL (a typo
such as `/docs/instalation` offers Installation), unless a `redirects:` rule
matches first. Set the heading and text under `errors:`:

```yaml
errors:
  404:                     # or notFound
    title: This page moved
    description: |
      Most pages from the old site are now under **Guides**.
      [Contact us](https://example.com/help) if you can't find yours.
    redirect: false        # true: send readers to the home page instead
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `title` | `Page not found` | The heading and the browser tab title |
| `description` | A line naming the missing path | Markdown under the heading |
| `redirect` | `false` | `true` sends readers to the home page instead of showing the page |

# AI-ready docs

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs

> Every page as clean Markdown for agents, llms.txt by nav group, llms-full.txt, agent instructions, Visibility, Accept text/markdown, an MCP server and Ask AI with cited answers.

`aiui build` publishes each docs page twice: the page people read, and the
same page as clean Markdown for AI agents. Nothing to configure, and it works
on any static host.

| URL | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `/docs/<page>.md` | the page as agent-ready Markdown (below) |
| `/llms.txt` | the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) index: one `##` section per nav group, each page linked as its `.md` |
| `/llms-full.txt` | every indexed page's agent-ready Markdown in one file |
| `/.well-known/llms.txt`, `/.well-known/llms-full.txt` | copies, where some agents look first |

Each page's HTML names its Markdown (`<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="…/docs/guide/install.md">`).
Links are absolute with a site URL (`seo.siteUrl` or a `CNAME`, see
[SEO](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/seo.md)), root-relative otherwise. Hidden and `noindex` pages stay out
of the llms files. An `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt` next to `aiui.yaml` is
published as it is.

## The agent-ready Markdown

| In the source | In the `.md` |
|---|---|
| front matter | `# Title`, then `> description` |
| `<Note>`, `<Warning title="…">`, … | a blockquote with a bold label: `> **Note:** …` |
| `<Tabs>` / `<Tab title="pip">` | one heading per tab, a level under the heading above |
| `<Steps>` / `<Step title="Install">` | a numbered list: `1. **Install**` |
| `<Card title="Guide" href="guide.md">` | a list item: `- [Guide](https://…/docs/guide.md)` |
| `<ParamField>`, `<ResponseField>` (in `<Expandable>`), `<RequestExample>`, `<Panel>` | `` - `user_id` (path, string, required): … `` (nested one level); a bold "Request example" over its fences; the content |
| `<Accordion>`, `<Frame>`, other tags, comments | their content (a bold title, an italic caption); comments removed |
| links to pages (`setup.md`, `/docs/setup`) | absolute `.md` URLs; other links absolute URLs |

Code is never changed. **Copy page**, **View as Markdown** and **Open in
ChatGPT / Claude** use this version; the browser renders the untouched source,
published as `/docs/<page>.source.md`. `.mdx` pages work the same way, and are
in search and `llms-full.txt`.

## Agent instructions

```yaml
markdown:
  instructions:            # or one string
    - Cite the page URL you used.
    - Prefer the `aiui` CLI over editing generated files.
```

Every `.md`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` then carries, under the title, a
`> ## Agent instructions` quote block with these lines.

## Content for people or for agents only

```mdx
<Visibility for="humans">Click **Deploy** in the top bar.</Visibility>
<Visibility for="agents">Run `aiui build` and upload the output folder.</Visibility>
```

`for="humans"` shows on the page and in site search only; `for="agents"` only
in the `.md` and the llms files.

## Accept: text/markdown

`aiui serve` answers a page URL with its Markdown when `Accept` ranks
`text/markdown` at least as high as `text/html` (browsers still get the page):

```bash
curl -H "Accept: text/markdown" http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs/guide/install
```

## MCP server

`aiui serve` and `aiui dev` also run an
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the site at `/mcp`, so an
editor's agent can search and read the docs while it works, and tell you when
a page let it down. Nothing to install or configure:

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `search_docs(query, limit=10)` | the best matching pages and sections (ranked as the search dialog ranks them), each with its path, URL and a snippet |
| `read_page(path)` | one page's agent-ready Markdown; `path` is a page path (`/docs/guide/install`) or URL |
| `list_pages()` | every page by nav group (`llms.txt`) |
| `submit_feedback(path, helpful, comment?)` | stores a vote on a page, like a reader's "Was this page helpful?", with `source: agent` |

The first three are read-only. `submit_feedback` lets an agent report a page
that is wrong, outdated, unclear or missing what it needed, so docs problems
reach you from the agents reading them. Reports land in the same
store as readers' votes, so `aiui docs feedback` counts them together (in the
CSV and JSON exports `source` tells them apart), under the same limits as the page's vote
button: 20 a minute per client (shared with `/api/docs/feedback`), 4 KiB, a
1,000-character comment, and only for pages that exist. The tool is not
listed when [page feedback](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#page-feedback) is off
(`feedback: false`) or posted to your own `endpoint`.

Connect from the page menu (**Copy MCP server URL**, **Connect to Cursor**,
**Connect to VS Code**), or add it by hand:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "acme-docs": { "url": "https://docs.acme.dev/mcp" } } }
```

Agents also find it on their own: `/.well-known/mcp` (also `mcp.json` and
`mcp/server-card.json`) serves a server card with the endpoint and the tools,
and `llms.txt` ends with an "MCP server" section linking it.

The transport is Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC over `POST`, protocol versions
2025-03-26 to 2025-11-25) and stateless. Requests whose `Host` is
not a name the server answers to (DNS rebinding; behind a reverse proxy on the
same machine list the public name in `AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS`) or that come from
another site's page (`Origin`; allow one with `--cors-origins` or
`AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) are refused. To turn the server off:

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: docs
    mcp: false
```

A static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) runs no server, so it has no `/mcp`
and the menu shows no MCP items; the `.md` pages and llms files above still
work there.

## Ask AI

`aiui serve` and `aiui dev` also answer questions about the docs, with the
sections each answer came from. Set a model key in the environment and
serve; there is nothing to configure:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
aiui serve
```

The server ranks the build's sections for the question (the same ranking as
search, widened so a long question still finds its pages), sends the best six
to the model and streams a Markdown answer that cites them as `[1]`, `[2]`.
Your key stays on the server: it is read from the environment and never logged
or sent to the browser.

| Model setting | Where |
|---|---|
| `content.docs.assistant.model`, else `AIUI_ASSISTANT_MODEL`, else `OPENAI_MODEL_NAME`, else `gpt-4o-mini` | which model answers |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | any OpenAI-compatible API, including a local server (`OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1` needs no key) |
| a `provider/model` name such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` | goes through LiteLLM when it is installed, with that provider's key |

Without a key the endpoint still answers: it returns the best matching
sections and says AI answers are not set up, so readers never hit an error.

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: docs
    assistant:
      starters: ["How do I install it?", "How do I change the theme?"]
      instructions: Call the product Acme, never "the tool".
      # model: gpt-4o-mini
      # endpoint: https://docs-api.acme.dev/api/docs/ask   # static host only
```

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `starters` | none | up to six questions offered before the reader asks |
| `instructions` | none | extra rules for every answer (tone, names, scope); up to 4,000 characters |
| `model` | see above | the model |
| `endpoint` | none | on a static host, the ask URL of an `aiui serve` running the same build |

`assistant: false` turns it off. The build writes these settings into
`ui-config.json`, which is public: keep secrets out of `instructions`.

### What readers see

When the server has a model, the docs header shows **Ask AI**. It opens a
side panel with your starter questions; answers stream in, cite their
sections as `[1]` links that open the page at that section, list the sections
under the answer, and can be copied or stopped. Follow-up questions keep the
conversation. Other ways in:

| Entry point | What it does |
|---|---|
| ⌘I / Ctrl+I | opens the panel |
| `?assistant=<question>` on any page URL | opens the panel and asks; the parameter leaves the address bar |
| select a passage in a page | an **Ask about this** chip quotes it in the question |
| search (⌘K) | an **Ask AI: <query>** row under the results |
| a page with `mode: assistant` | the page's text, then the panel inline: a full "Ask the docs" page |
| `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('aiui:docs-ask', { detail: { question, context } }))` | from your own JavaScript |

A server without a key shows none of this (the API above still returns the
best sections). A static host shows it only when `endpoint` names an
`aiui serve` running the same build; allow the site's origin there with
`--cors-origins https://docs.acme.dev`.

### The HTTP API

`POST /api/docs/ask` with `{"question": "...", "context": "...", "page": "/docs/x", "history": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]}`
(only `question` is required; `context` is a quoted passage, `history` the
earlier turns) answers with Server-Sent Events:

| Event | Data |
|---|---|
| `sources` | `[{"n": 1, "title", "heading", "path", "url", "snippet"}]`, the sections the answer may cite as `[n]` |
| `text` | `{"text": "..."}`, the next piece of the Markdown answer |
| `done` | `{}` |
| `unavailable` | `{"message": "..."}` instead of `text` when no model is set up |
| `error` | `{"message": "..."}` when the model call failed |

`GET /api/docs/search?q=install&limit=10` returns `{"results": [{"title", "heading", "anchor", "path", "url", "snippet"}]}`,
ranked as the search dialog ranks them, and each page's Markdown is at
`/docs/<page>.md`, so another app can embed docs search and answers.

The endpoints are public like the site, so they are guarded: 10 questions a
minute per client, a 32 KiB body, a 2,000-character question, the same `Host`
and `Origin` checks as the MCP server, and `application/json` or `text/plain`
bodies (a static site on another origin posts `text/plain`, allowed with
`--cors-origins` or `AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`). Answers spend your key, so put a
public site behind your own rate limits too.

---

# Analytics, support chat and cookie consent

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/analytics

> Add web analytics or a support chat widget to a docs site with one line per

Add web analytics or a support chat widget to a docs site with one line per
provider, and ask readers for consent before anything loads.

```yaml
integrations:
  plausible: docs.example.com      # one id is enough
  intercom: abc12345
  consent: true                    # ask first, with the built-in banner
```

`aiui build` adds them to every page (the home page, each docs page and
`404.html`). Each client-side page change counts as a page view.

## Providers

A provider takes its main id as a plain value (`ga4: G-ABC1234`) or a block
with more settings. The build checks every id and URL and stops on a bad one.

| Key | Settings (first one is the main id) | Page views on navigation |
|-----|-------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `ga4` | `measurementId` (`G-...`) | Counted by GA4's enhanced measurement (page changes based on browser history, on by default) |
| `gtm` | `tagId` (`GTM-...`) | Pushes `{event: "aiui.pageview", page_path, page_title}` to the data layer |
| `posthog` | `apiKey` (`phc_...`), `apiHost` (default `https://us.i.posthog.com`), `sessionRecording` (default `false`) | Counted by PostHog (`history_change`) |
| `plausible` | `domain`, `server` (default `https://plausible.io`, or your own instance) | Counted by Plausible |
| `fathom` | `siteId` | Counted by Fathom (`data-spa="auto"`) |
| `umami` | `websiteId` (a UUID), `src` (default `https://cloud.umami.is/script.js`) | Counted by Umami |
| `segment` | `key` (the write key) | `analytics.page()` |
| `mixpanel` | `projectToken`, `region` (`us`, `eu` or `in`) | Counted by Mixpanel (`track_pageview: "url-with-path"`) |
| `scripts` | A list of `https://` script URLs for any other tool | Up to the tool |

Support chat widgets load when the browser is idle, so they never slow the first paint:

| Key | Settings |
|-----|----------|
| `intercom` | `appId` (calls `Intercom('update')` on each page change) |
| `crisp` | `websiteId` (a UUID) |
| `front` | `chatId` |

```yaml
integrations:
  posthog: { apiKey: phc_abc123def456, apiHost: https://eu.i.posthog.com, sessionRecording: true }
  mixpanel: { projectToken: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef, region: eu }
  scripts: [https://cdn.example.com/tracker.js]
```

## Cookie consent

With `consent`, nothing loads until the reader accepts. A small banner at the
bottom of the page offers **Decline** and **Accept**, the same size and style,
so declining is as easy as accepting. The choice is remembered in the
browser's local storage (`aiui-consent`: `granted` or `denied`). The banner
uses the site's theme colours in light and dark mode and fits a phone screen.

```yaml
integrations:
  ga4: G-ABC1234
  consent:
    text: We use cookies to see which pages help and which need work.
    decline: No thanks             # and accept: for the other button
    policy: /docs/privacy          # adds a link after the text
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `required` | `true` | `consent: true` is short for this; `false` loads without asking. |
| `banner` | `true` | `false`: no built-in banner; your own consent tool decides (below). |
| `text`, `accept`, `decline` | an English sentence, `Accept`, `Decline` | The banner's words. |
| `policy`, `policyLabel` | none, `Privacy policy` | A link to your privacy page (a site path or URL). |

**Change of mind.** Any link to `#cookie-settings` opens the banner again, for
example in the footer: `[Cookie settings](#cookie-settings)`. Declining after
accepting reloads the page, so the trackers that were running stop.

**Your own consent tool.** Set `banner: false` and tell the page the reader's
choice from the tool's callback:

```js
window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('aiui:consent', { detail: { granted: true } }))
```

## Privacy and previews

Readers whose browser sends Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track get no
analytics (support chat still loads); `respectDoNotTrack: false` counts them
anyway. `aiui dev` leaves integrations out so previews are not visits;
`dev: true` under `integrations` loads them there too.

## Content Security Policy

No inline script is emitted: the settings are a JSON data block and the loader
is a file at the site root (`/aiui-integrations.js`). The build's
[Content Security Policy](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-security-policy.md) adds each provider's
hosts per directive by itself (`Compiler(config).external_origins()` lists
them). A tag manager container (`gtm`) loads whatever tags you add to it, so
with `gtm` the policy is report-only until you add their hosts under
`site.csp` and set it to enforce.

---

# Docs sign-in

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/docs-auth

> Put a docs site behind a password, keep some pages open to everyone, and limit

Put a docs site behind a password, keep some pages open to everyone, and limit
others to a group of readers. `aiui serve` and `aiui dev` enforce it; there is
nothing to install and no account system to run.

## A password for the whole site

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: docs
    auth:
      password: env:DOCS_PASSWORD
```

```bash
aiui build
DOCS_PASSWORD='a long passphrase' aiui serve
```

Every page now asks for the password. A reader who opens any page gets a sign-in
page in the site's own theme, at that URL, and lands on the page they asked for.
The session lasts seven days. `/__aiui/login` shows who is signed in and a
**Sign out** button (link to it from `navbar.links` if you want one).

Passwords are always written `env:NAME`: the build stores the variable's name,
never the password. Change the variable and restart to change the password;
every reader signed in with the old one is signed out.

## Open pages

Most docs want a public home and quickstart and the rest behind sign-in:

```yaml
auth:
  password: env:DOCS_PASSWORD
  public: ["/", quickstart, "guides/*"]
```

`public` lists page paths relative to the docs (`/` is the home page,
`/docs/quickstart` also works) and patterns (`*` matches any part of a path). A
page can also say it in its front matter:

```markdown
---
title: Pricing
public: true
---
```

`public: false` keeps a page behind sign-in when a pattern would open it, so
`public: ["*"]` plus `public: false` on a few pages protects only those.

## A password per reader

```yaml
auth:
  password: env:DOCS_PASSWORD          # optional: a shared password
  users:
    alice: env:ALICE_PASSWORD
    bob: env:BOB_PASSWORD
```

Readers sign in with their password alone; it tells the server who they are.

## Groups

Give readers groups, then name the groups a page is for:

```yaml
auth:
  users:
    alice: {password: env:ALICE_PASSWORD, groups: [partners]}
```

```markdown
---
title: Partner API
groups: [partners]
---
```

A page with `groups` is for readers in at least one of them. To any other
signed-in reader it does not exist: a 404, and it is missing from their sidebar,
search, `llms.txt`, MCP and Ask AI. A signed-out reader who opens it gets the
sign-in page (they may be a member).

## What is protected

A page's rule covers everything made from it: its HTML (including the copy
inside `<noscript>`), its `.md` and `.source.md` files and `Accept:
text/markdown` answer, its social card under `/og/`, its Try it data and its RSS
feed. `docs-nav.json`, `search-index.json`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` (and
their `/.well-known/` copies) hold only the pages the reader may read (so the
pages do not carry the navigation, as they do on a site without sign-in, and
the build writes no split search index, `search-index/`: search reads the cut
`search-index.json`), and the
[MCP server](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#mcp-server), [Ask AI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#ask-ai),
`/api/docs/search` and page feedback see only those pages. An AI tool that
connects to `/mcp` without the browser's cookie reads the open pages. The
sitemap lists only open pages.

Code, styles, fonts, images and `ui-config.json` are open to anyone, so open
pages render (do not put a secret in an image). Any other file (OpenAPI specs, a
nav group's generated page, files you copied in) needs sign-in.

## Security

- Protected answers carry `Cache-Control: private`, so a shared cache never
  hands one reader's page to another.
- The session cookie is `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Secure` over HTTPS
  (also behind a proxy that sets `X-Forwarded-Proto`). It is signed with a key
  derived from the reader's password.
- Passwords are compared in constant time. Ten wrong passwords from one address
  in ten minutes block that address for the rest of the ten minutes (429).
- Sign-in and sign-out only accept a form posted from the site itself
  (`AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` adds origins, as for the rest of aiui).
- A password variable that is not set is logged as a warning; that reader
  cannot sign in.

## Static hosts

Sign-in needs the aiui server. A static host (GitHub Pages, a CDN) serves every
file of the build, so `aiui build` warns (7017) on a site with
`content.docs.auth`; serve it with `aiui serve` ([deployment](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md)).
`aiui validate` reports front matter `public` or `groups` on a site without
`content.docs.auth`, and a group no reader is in (7017). A docs folder served by `aiui run` uses the app's own
sign-in instead ([deployment](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md#auth-enforcement)).

---

# Content Security Policy

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-security-policy

> A docs site built with aiui build ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy

A docs site built with `aiui build` ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy
and needs no configuration. The policy allows the scripts the site runs and
nothing else, so injected markup cannot run a script, and only your own site
can show the docs in a frame.

## What you get

`aiui build` works the policy out from what the site actually loads:

| Source | Directive |
|--------|-----------|
| The site's own files (app, chunks, fonts, `customCss`/`customJs` files, the `site.components` module and its import map's hash) | `'self'` |
| The small inline scripts the build writes (theme, URL, redirect stubs) | `script-src 'sha256-…'`, one hash each |
| The JSON the build inlines in each page (its Markdown, the navigation and route manifest) | nothing: `type="application/json"` is data the browser never runs |
| Google Fonts and font, stylesheet and script URLs in `site.theme.fonts`, `customCss`, `customJs` | `style-src`, `font-src`, `script-src` |
| [Integrations](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/analytics.md) (analytics, support chat) | each provider's hosts |
| YouTube, Vimeo and Loom embeds on a page | `frame-src` (the privacy-friendly player) |
| The `servers` of your OpenAPI specs (Try it) | `connect-src` |
| `assistant.endpoint`, `feedback.endpoint` on a static host | `connect-src` |
| A navbar `primary` button of `type: github` (the star count) | `connect-src https://api.github.com` |

Everything else stays strict: no `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'` for
scripts, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `form-action 'self'`.
Images and media load from `'self'`, `data:`, `blob:` and any `https:` host,
so Markdown images and badges keep working. Styles allow `'unsafe-inline'`:
the app's code highlighting, diagrams and dialogs set inline styles.

The policy goes out three ways:

- **Every built page** carries it as `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">`,
  right after `<meta charset>`. This works on any static host, GitHub Pages
  included.
- **`_headers`** in the build folder sends it as a header on Netlify and
  Cloudflare Pages, with `frame-ancestors 'self'` added (a meta tag cannot
  carry `frame-ancestors`).
- **`aiui serve` and `aiui dev`** send the `/*` headers of `_headers`, so the
  preview behaves like the host. The `aiui dev` reload script is a file
  (`/__aiui/dev.js`), so it runs under the same policy.

On another host (nginx, S3 with CloudFront, a CDN), copy the header line from
`_headers` into its configuration.

## Configure

```yaml
site:
  csp:
    connect-src: https://api.example.com     # add sources to a directive
    frame-ancestors: ["https://app.example.com"]
```

| `site.csp` | Effect |
|------------|--------|
| unset | On for a docs build (reported only when `integrations.gtm` is set, see below); off for other builds |
| `true` | On, enforced |
| `false` | Off: no meta tag, no `_headers` |
| `report-only` | Only `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` in `_headers` and from `aiui serve`: the browser logs what the policy would block, and blocks nothing |
| a map | On, with extra sources per directive (a string or a list). A list with `'none'` replaces the directive (`frame-ancestors: ["'none'"]` forbids every frame). `report-only: true` in the map reports instead of enforcing. `report-uri` sets where the browser posts reports |

Directive names are lower-case words (`script-src`, `connect-src`, ...) and
sources contain no spaces, `;` or `,`: anything else is a config error, so
the value is always a valid header.

## When to add sources

- **`customJs` that calls another server** (`fetch`, a WebSocket, a widget):
  add its origin under `connect-src`, `frame-src` or `script-src`.
- **Raw HTML in a page** needs no sources: the page renders YouTube, Vimeo
  and Loom `<iframe>` players, `<img>` and `<video>` (all allowed above), shows
  any other `<iframe>` as a link and removes `<script>`, `<form>` and similar
  elements before the policy is ever involved. `aiui validate` names each one
  (finding 7019; see [raw HTML](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#raw-html)). Inline event
  handlers (`onclick="…"`) never run.
- **Tag Manager (`integrations.gtm`)** runs whatever tags the container holds,
  which the build cannot see, so the default there is `report-only`. Add the
  hosts of your tags and set `site.csp: true` to enforce.
- **Legacy `site.plugins`**: `mermaid` and `syntax-highlight` load from their
  CDN, which the policy allows when they are listed. Other dashboard plugins
  are not meant for docs pages.

To find what a page needs, open the browser console: every blocked load or
script is logged with the directive that blocked it. `report-only` shows the
same messages without blocking anything.

# Chat & Agent Examples

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/examples/basic

> Curated, modern Python chat and AI agent examples you can run in one command.

Every example below lives in [`examples/`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples) and runs with one command (`aiui run app.py`) in the default **React app shell** (`style: app`).

> **Tip:**
> New to PraisonAIUI? Follow the [6-step progressive learning path](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/tutorials/first-chat.md) to build an app one feature at a time, or browse [Apps, Components & A2UI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/examples/app-and-components.md) and [Zero-Code YAML & Plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/examples/yaml-and-plugins.md).

## Agent UI & Streaming

| Example | What it demonstrates | Run |
|---|---|---|
| [01-chat](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/python/01-chat) | Minimal 5-line chat (`@aiui.reply` + `aiui.say()`) | `aiui run app.py` |
| [02-chat-app](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/python/02-chat-app) | Full lifecycle (`@welcome`, `@on_chat_start`, `@step`, `@profiles`, `@starters`, `@button`, `notify(persist=True)`) | `aiui run app.py` |
| [03-chat-with-ai](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/python/03-chat-with-ai) | Live OpenAI token streaming, per-chat memory and feedback | `aiui run app.py` |

## Minimal 5-Line Starter

```python title="app.py"
import praisonaiui as aiui

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(message: str):
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message}")
```

```bash
aiui run app.py
```

# Zero-Code YAML & Plugin Examples

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/examples/yaml-and-plugins

> Run chat apps, A2UI surfaces, UI component pages, docs sites, and installable UI plugins from YAML.

PraisonAIUI has full **Python ↔ YAML ↔ CLI parity**—you can declare chat apps, UI component pages, live A2UI surfaces, notifications, and static docs sites directly in YAML without writing Python.

## Zero-Code YAML Chat & App Configs

Run any folder in [`examples/yaml/`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml) with `aiui run chat.yaml`:

| Example | What it demonstrates | Run |
|---|---|---|
| [01-chat](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml/01-chat) | Minimal zero-code YAML chat agent | `aiui run chat.yaml` |
| [02-profiles](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml/02-profiles) | Multi-persona agent switching via `profiles:` | `aiui run chat.yaml` |
| [03-clean-chat](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml/03-clean-chat) | Focused sidebar-free chat (`dashboard.sidebar: false`) | `aiui run chat.yaml` |
| [04-tools](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml/04-tools) | Built-in tool registration in YAML | `aiui run chat.yaml` |
| [05-features](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml/05-features) | Feature flags and dashboard options | `aiui run chat.yaml` |
| [13-playground](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/tree/main/examples/yaml/13-playground) | Multi-profile playground (`--style agents`) | `aiui run chat.yaml --style agents` |

## Zero-Code YAML App with A2UI, Rich Components & Notifications

Save as `app.yaml` and run `aiui run app.yaml`—editing the file updates blocks, badges, and surfaces live without restarting:

```yaml
style: app
chat:
  preview:
    enabled: true
    surfaceId: main
    width: "40%"
notifications:
  items:
    - title: "Workspace ready"
      type: success
      pinned: true
pages:
  - chat-canvas
  - canvas
  - id: live-surface
    title: Live A2UI
    group: A2UI
    surface:
      id: main
      theme:
        primaryColor: "#2563eb"
      components:
        - id: root
          component: Text
          text: { path: /headline }
          variant: h2
      data:
        headline: "Zero-code A2UI surface from YAML"
  - id: release-status
    title: Release Status
    group: Workspace
    components:
      - type: stepper
        active: 1
        steps:
          - { title: "Build" }
          - { title: "Verify" }
          - { title: "Ship" }
      - type: copy_field
        label: "Install Command"
        value: "pip install aiui"
```

# Advanced Examples

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/examples/advanced

> Docs-site configurations beyond a single template. Every snippet here passes

Docs-site configurations beyond a single template. Every snippet here passes
`aiui validate --strict`.

## Multiple Templates

A centered landing page with a hero banner, and the three-column layout for
the docs:

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "ThreeColumnLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "header" }
      left: { type: "DocsSidebar" }
      main: { type: "DocContent" }
      right: { type: "Toc" }
      footer: { ref: "footer" }

  landing:
    layout: "CenteredLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "header" }
      footer: { ref: "footer" }
      right: null
    zones:
      hero:
        - type: "HeroBanner"
          props:
            title: "My Project"
            subtitle: "Docs for everyone"
            ctaLabel: "Get Started"
            ctaHref: "/docs/getting-started/quickstart"

routes:
  - match: "/docs/**"
    template: "docs"

  - match: "/"
    template: "landing"
```

The layouts and the zones each renders are in [Templates](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/templates.md)
and [Widget Zones](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/widget-zones.md).

## Route-Level Overrides

A route's `slots` can override the `right` slot (the table of contents); header
and footer always come from the template. The first matching route wins, so put
the specific route first:

```yaml
routes:
  - match: "/docs/changelog"
    template: "docs"
    slots:
      right: null  # Hide TOC on the changelog

  - match: "/docs/**"
    template: "docs"
```

## Custom Components

The docs site renderer has no hook for your own header or sidebar component;
the `Header` and `Footer` props cover branding (see
[Slots & Components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/slots.md)). For full control, scaffold the
React frontend with `aiui init --frontend` and change it there.

## Custom Colors

```yaml
site:
  title: "My Project"
  theme:
    preset: "emerald"
    radius: "lg"
    darkMode: true
```

`site.customCss` applies to both the runtime server (`aiui run`, CSS text) and
the static docs output of `aiui build` (CSS text, files and URLs); see
[Theming](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md#custom-css-and-js).

# CLI Reference

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/cli

> Every aiui command and option. aiui --help prints the same

Every `aiui` command and option. `aiui <command> --help` prints the same
information from the installed version. The wheel also installs the command
as `praisonaiui`.

For a short tour of the commands you will use most, see
[CLI Usage](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/getting-started/cli.md).

## Run and build

### `aiui run`

Run the server for a Python app (`app.py`) or a YAML chat agent (`chat.yaml`).

```bash
aiui run APP_FILE [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `APP_FILE` | required | A Python file that registers callbacks, or a `.yaml`/`.yml` chat config |
| `--port, -p` | `8000` | Port. If it is taken, the next free port (up to 10 further) is used. The port is bound before the URL is printed and the server serves that socket, so two apps started together never get the same port |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Address to bind to |
| `--reload, -r` | off | Restart when files change |
| `--style, -s` | detected | `app` (the React app shell, default), `chat` (the classic chat), `docs`, `agents`, `playground`, `dashboard` (legacy) or `custom` |
| `--preset` | `minimal` for `app.py` | Page preset: `minimal` (Chat + your pages), `agent` (Chat, Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory), or `ops` (all built-in ops pages) |
| `--pages` | none | Explicit comma-separated page IDs (e.g. `chat,sessions`), `all`, or a preset name (`minimal`, `agent`, `ops`) |
| `--backend, -b` | `standalone` | `standalone`, or `praisonai` to use the PraisonAI WebSocket gateway |
| `--datastore, -d` | `sdk` | Session storage: `sdk` (shared with PraisonAI Agents), `sdk:/path`, `json`, `json:/path` or `memory`. Without the flag, a chat YAML's `datastore:` key is used |
| `--config, -c` | none | A docs-site YAML to build before serving (optional) |
| `--output, -o` | `aiui` | Folder the UI files are written to; by default next to `APP_FILE` |

Style: for a Python app `--style` wins, then `aiui.set_style()`; for a YAML
app its `style:` key wins over `--style`. Without any of them `aiui run`
detects one: `@aiui.profiles` plus registered agents gives `agents`, and
anything else (including `@aiui.reply` and `@aiui.page`) opens `app` (the React
app shell). For Python `app.py` files that do not call `aiui.set_pages()`,
`aiui run` defaults to the `minimal` preset (Chat + your own pages) unless
`--preset`, `--pages`, or `AIUI_PAGES` is set. In `app`, `aiui run` opens the
`chat` layout (the chat without a canvas) unless `AIUI_LAYOUT`,
`aiui.set_layout()` or YAML `layout:` picks another. See
[UI Styles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/styles.md), [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md), and
[Build a focused app](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app.md).

A chat YAML's top-level keys: `name`, `instructions`, `model`, `welcome`,
`goodbye`, `starters`, `profiles`, `tools`, `features`, `datastore`, `style`,
`theme`, `branding`, `dashboard`, `pages`, `layout` and `extensions`.
`layout:` takes a layout id (`layout: command`) or the same block as
`aiui.yaml` (`default`, `available`, `user_choice`, `primary`, `options`);
`extensions:` takes `enabled:` / `disabled:` lists, as in `aiui.yaml`. Any
other key prints a warning naming it, since it would otherwise be ignored
without a word.

`aiui run` loads `~/.praisonai/.env` and then `./.env` before starting,
without overriding variables that are already set.

```bash
aiui run app.py                         # style detected; a chat app opens the app shell
aiui run app.py --style chat            # the classic chat style
aiui run app.py --port 3000 --reload
aiui run app.py --datastore json        # sessions under ~/.praisonaiui
aiui run chat.yaml                      # YAML-defined agent (needs praisonaiagents)
aiui run app.py --backend praisonai
```

### `aiui init`

Scaffold a starter Python Agent UI (`app.py`) or a Docs UI config (`aiui.yaml`)
in the current folder. Refuses to overwrite existing files unless `--force` is
given.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--template, -t` | `minimal` | App templates (writes `app.py`): `agent`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `langgraph`, `crewai`, `pydantic-ai`, `praisonai`, `dashboard`. Docs templates (writes `aiui.yaml`): `minimal`, `docs`, `marketing` |
| `--force, -f` | off | Overwrite existing files |
| `--frontend` | off | Also scaffold a Vite + React + shadcn frontend project |

```bash
aiui init --template agent        # runnable starter app.py with starters + send_block
aiui init --template openai       # OpenAI streaming chat app.py
aiui init --template langgraph    # LangGraph agent app.py
aiui init --template dashboard    # split-pane workspace (chat_panel) + File Inspector (aiui.interface)
aiui init --template docs         # docs-site aiui.yaml
```

For docs templates, the file's first line (`# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json`)
gives autocomplete and hover docs in editors ([Editor setup](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#editor-setup)).
Create the folder it points to (for the `docs` template, `./docs` with at least
one `.md` file) before `aiui build`.

### `aiui validate`

Check a docs-site configuration and its pages.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--config, -c` | `aiui.yaml` | Configuration file ([lookup](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#config-file-name)) |
| `--strict` | off | Unknown keys, broken links, nav entries without a page and content issues (7xxx) become errors (exit 1) |
| `--format` | `text` | `json` prints `{valid, errors, warnings}`, each with `code`, `file`, `line`, `message`, `suggestion` |

Each finding prints as `[category] code file:line: message` with a fix hint
under it:

```text
  [content] 7005 docs/guide/setup.md:14: heading jumps from h2 to h4
    💡 Use ### here; screen readers navigate by heading level
```

| Code | Finding |
|------|---------|
| 1003 | unknown key (ignored); in a `$ref` file the file is named |
| 1004 | key accepted but has no effect; unknown component tag in a page |
| 2101 | a nav entry names no docs page |
| 2102 | a navigation tab, menu item, anchor or dropdown with no pages, groups or `href` |
| 5001, 51xx, 5201 | theme, layout and search settings that are ignored |
| 6001, 6002 | broken link or missing image (`aiui docs check-links`); OpenAPI spec problems |
| 7000 | page front matter is not valid YAML (the page loses its title) |
| 7001 | front matter key has the wrong type ([keys](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#front-matter)) |
| 7002 | image without alt text (`![](x.png)`, `<img>` with no `alt`; `alt=""` marks a decorative image) |
| 7003 | two files publish the same page URL (`intro.md` and `01-intro.md`) |
| 7004 | two sidebar entries in one folder have the same title |
| 7005 | heading skips a level (`##` then `####`) |
| 7006 | page has nothing beyond its headings |
| 7007 | `{{name}}` with no value under `variables:` ([variables](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#reusable-snippets-and-variables)) |
| 7008 | snippet not found, outside the project folder, or including itself (fails `aiui build`) |
| 7009 | `icon` (front matter, navigation, a component's `icon="…"`) that is not a [lucide](https://lucide.dev/icons) name, an emoji or an image URL, with the nearest name |
| 7010 | a redirect loops, or ends at a docs path with no page ([redirects](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/redirects.md#checks)) |
| 7011 | a page is published at a redirect's source, so the redirect never runs |
| 7012 | front matter `openapi:` / `api:` or a navigation `METHOD /path` entry that names no operation in the loaded specs ([OpenAPI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/openapi.md#endpoints-on-your-own-pages)) |
| 7013 | front matter `related` names a page that does not exist ([related pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#related-pages)) |
| 7014 | a `site.customCss`, `site.customJs`, `site.theme.fonts` or `site.theme.codeLanguages` file that is not in the project folder ([fonts and custom files](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md#fonts)) |
| 7015 | `site.theme.code` names a theme that is not bundled (with the nearest name), or a `site.theme.codeLanguages` file is not a TextMate grammar ([code blocks](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md#code-blocks)) |
| 7016 | a `::: module` block names no module or member, or has an unknown option (fails `aiui build`; [Python API reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/api-reference-python.md#checks)) |
| 7017 | `content.docs.auth` is set, and only `aiui serve` / `aiui dev` enforce it (`aiui build`); front matter `public` / `groups` without `content.docs.auth`, or a group no reader is in ([docs sign-in](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/docs-auth.md)) |
| 7018 | two `navigation.versions` with the same name, more than one marked `default: true`, or a version that lists a page of another version's folder ([versions](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md#versions)) |
| 7019 | raw HTML a page shows differently than written: an `<iframe>` that is not a YouTube, Vimeo or Loom video (shown as a link; the host is named), or `<script>`, `<style>`, `<link>`, `<form>`, `<audio>`, `<object>`, `<embed>` (removed). Also an `aiui build` warning ([raw HTML](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#raw-html)) |
| 7020 | two `navigation.languages` with the same code, more than one marked `default: true`, or a version folder inside a language folder (`docs/fr/v1/`; [languages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md#languages)) |
| 7021 | `site.components` is not a `.js` / `.mjs` file in the project folder, or the build finds no component tag in it ([your own components](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#your-own-components)) |
| 7022 | a class on a component tag or raw HTML that docs pages drop (not a docs utility class; the nearest allowed one is suggested), or a `style` attribute (always removed). Also an `aiui build` warning ([styling with classes](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#styling-with-classes)) |
| 7101 | `site.theme.accent` under WCAG AA 3:1 contrast on the light or dark background, with a shade that passes |
| 7102 | `logo`, `favicon` or `site.theme.background` image that is not a file in the project folder ([branding](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md#branding-a-docs-site)) |

Without `--config`, `validate`, `build` and `serve` read `./aiui.yaml`. The
old name `aiui.template.yaml` still works: when it is the only one there it is
used, with a one-line hint on stderr to rename it, and the exit code is
unchanged. When both files exist, `aiui.yaml` wins. An explicit `--config`
always wins and prints no hint. See
[Config file name](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#config-file-name).

### `aiui schema`

Print the JSON Schema of `aiui.yaml`, generated from the `Config` model of the
installed version; `--output, -o <file>` writes it to a file. The schema is
also published at `https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json`; see
[Editor setup](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#editor-setup).

### `aiui build`

Build a static docs site from the configuration.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--config, -c` | `aiui.yaml` | Configuration file ([lookup](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#config-file-name)) |
| `--output, -o` | `aiui` | Output folder |
| `--minify` | off | Minify the JSON manifests |
| `--strict` | off | Stop with exit code 1 on a broken link (without it, broken links are warnings) |

The output holds `index.html`, `404.html`, the UI bundle (`assets/`,
`aiui-manifest.json`), the manifests (`ui-config.json`, `docs-nav.json`,
`route-manifest.json`), one HTML file and the Markdown source per page,
`robots.txt` and `.nojekyll`. `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`
are added when the site URL is known (`seo.siteUrl`, or a `CNAME` file next to
the configuration or in `docs/`).

### `aiui docs check-links`

Find broken page links, `#anchor`s, images, component `href`s and nav entries
before you deploy. Prints `file:line: target: reason (did you mean X?)` and
exits `1` when a link is broken. See
[Writing docs pages → Check links](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#check-links).

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--config, -c` | `aiui.yaml` | Configuration file |
| `--external` | off | Also request every `http(s)` URL (HEAD, then GET; 16 at a time) |
| `--timeout` | `10` | Seconds to wait for each external URL |
| `--json` | off | Print `{"checked", "pages", "broken": [{file, line, target, reason, suggestion}]}` |

### `aiui serve`

Build (unless `--no-build`) and serve a docs site.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--config, -c` | `aiui.yaml` | Configuration file ([lookup](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#config-file-name)) |
| `--output, -o` | `aiui` | Folder to serve |
| `--port, -p` | `8000` | Port (next free port if taken) |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Address to bind to |
| `--no-build` | off | Serve the existing output without building |
| `--watch, -w` | off | Rebuild when a file in the configuration's folder changes (reload the page yourself; `aiui dev` reloads it for you) |
| `--cors-origins` | empty | Comma-separated allowed origins; empty means same-origin only |
| `--ssl-certfile` | none | Certificate file for HTTPS |
| `--ssl-keyfile` | none | Private key file for HTTPS |
| `--open / --no-open` | auto | Open the site in a browser. Auto opens it only when run from a terminal; never in CI, under a test runner or from a script ([when a browser opens](#when-a-browser-opens)) |

Paths without a file extension fall back to the single-page app. Paths that
try to leave the output folder are refused. Every response carries the `/*`
headers of the build's `_headers` file, which holds the site's
[Content Security Policy](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-security-policy.md).

#### When a browser opens

`aiui serve`, `aiui dev` and `aiui dev --examples` open a browser tab only for a
person at a terminal. With neither flag, the tab opens when standard output is a
terminal and no CI or test runner is detected (`CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`,
`GITLAB_CI`, `BUILDKITE`, `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST`). `--open` forces it,
`--no-open` skips it, and `AIUI_NO_BROWSER=1` turns it off everywhere, for
scripts and coding agents that start these servers.

### `aiui dev`

Preview the docs site while you write it: build, serve, and reload the open
browser tab on every save. A failed build is shown in the terminal and over
the page while the last good build stays up. Run it in the folder that holds
`aiui.yaml`, or in a folder with only a `docs/` folder. See
[Hot Reload](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/hot-reload.md).

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `--config, -c` | `aiui.yaml` | Configuration file ([lookup](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration.md#config-file-name)) |
| `--port, -p` | `8000` | Port (next free port if taken) |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | Address to bind to |
| `--open / --no-open` | auto | Open the preview in a browser; auto as for `aiui serve` ([when a browser opens](#when-a-browser-opens)) |
| `--base-path` | as `aiui build` | URL path to preview the site under |
| `--examples, -e` | none | Run the examples dashboard for this folder instead (default port `9000`) |

`aiui dev --examples examples` is the older dashboard that lists the example
projects in a folder and switches between them. In a folder with no
configuration and no `docs/` but an `examples/` folder, plain `aiui dev` still
opens it.

## Diagnostics

| Command | Options | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `aiui doctor` | `--server, -s` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8000`), `--json` | Structured diagnostics against a running server. The first two checks need no server: `aiui Version` (the imported version against PyPI's latest) and `aiui Install` (the version and folder actually imported; warns when pip's metadata names another version, as a stale editable install does, and prints the reinstall command) |
| `aiui health-check` | `--server, -s`, `--detailed, -d` | Server health; `--detailed` shows each feature |
| `aiui health` | same | Alias of `health-check` |
| `aiui test <suite>` | `--server, -s` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8082`) | Integration tests against a running server: `chat`, `memory`, `sessions`, `endpoints`, `features`, `all`. See [API Testing](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/testing.md) |

## Plugins

```bash
aiui plugins list [--json] [--config FILE]       # installed UI plugins, version, status, load error
aiui plugins doctor [--config FILE] [--no-builtin]
```

`--config` applies the `extensions:` policy from that YAML. `doctor` checks the
entry point, the SDK version gate, `static_dir` and SRI hashes, and (unless
`--no-builtin`) page ids that a built-in page shadows. A plugin's own commands
run as `aiui <plugin> ...` or `aiui plugins <plugin> ...`;
`AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` turns that lookup off. See
[UI plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md).

## Management commands

These talk to a running server over HTTP. Every one takes
`--server, -s URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8000`).

### `sessions`

```bash
aiui sessions list
aiui sessions create
aiui sessions get SESSION_ID
aiui sessions delete SESSION_ID
aiui sessions messages SESSION_ID
```

### `session-ext`

```bash
aiui session-ext state SESSION_ID
aiui session-ext save-state SESSION_ID --key K --value V
aiui session-ext labels SESSION_ID
aiui session-ext usage SESSION_ID
aiui session-ext compact SESSION_ID
aiui session-ext reset SESSION_ID
```

### `memory`

```bash
aiui memory list [--type short|long|entity|all]
aiui memory add TEXT [--type long]
aiui memory search QUERY [--limit 10]
aiui memory context QUERY [--limit 5]    # memory text for prompt injection
aiui memory clear [--type all]
aiui memory status
```

### `provider`

```bash
aiui provider status     # active provider and its health
aiui provider health
aiui provider agents
```

### `features` and `pages`

```bash
aiui features list       # registered feature protocols
aiui features status     # health summary
aiui pages list          # sidebar pages with group and icon
aiui pages ids           # page ids, for aiui.set_pages()
```

### `config`

Runtime configuration (stored in `config.yaml` under the data directory).

```bash
aiui config get [KEY]          # all keys when KEY is omitted
aiui config set KEY VALUE
aiui config list
aiui config history [--limit 20]
```

### `approval`

```bash
aiui approval list [--status all|pending|resolved]
aiui approval pending
aiui approval resolve APPROVAL_ID [--approved | --denied] [--reason TEXT]
```

### `schedule`

```bash
aiui schedule list
aiui schedule add NAME MESSAGE [--every 60]    # interval in seconds
aiui schedule remove JOB_ID
aiui schedule status
```

### `skills`, `hooks`, `workflows`

```bash
aiui skills list | status | discover
aiui hooks list

aiui hooks log [--limit 20]
aiui workflows list | status | runs
aiui workflows run WORKFLOW_ID
```

### `eval` and `traces`

```bash

aiui traces list [--limit 20]

```

### `surface`

A2UI surfaces for the agent canvas; see [A2UI Overview](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/a2ui/overview.md).

```bash
aiui surface list | status

aiui surface push [SURFACE_ID] --file surface.jsonl [--replace]
aiui surface action [SURFACE_ID] ACTION [--component ID] [--data '{}']
aiui surface clear [SURFACE_ID]
```

### `notifications`

Manage in-app notifications (`NotificationStoreProtocol`, REST + SSE); see [Notifications](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/notifications.md).

```bash

```

### `telemetry`

Inspect live HTTP latency, throughput, memory, and recorded metrics.

```bash

aiui telemetry status
aiui telemetry metrics [--json]
```

### `auth`

`aiui auth create-secret` prints a new session secret (offline; see
[Sessions](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md#sessions)); `aiui auth create-key --name my-app` creates an
API key on the running server and prints it once.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Invalid configuration, failed request or other error |
| `2` | File or folder not found, or an unknown `--style` |
| `3` | Build failed |
| `4` | No free port near the requested one |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `AIUI_DATA_DIR` | Data directory (default `~/.praisonaiui`): sessions, runtime `config.yaml`, plugin state |
| `AIUI_SHELL` | `app` turns the `dashboard` style into the React app shell; `legacy` turns `app` back into `dashboard` |
| `AIUI_LAYOUT` | Default app-shell layout id; see [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) |
| `AIUI_TEMPLATES_DIR` | Serve or build with another frontend bundle folder |
| `AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Origins allowed for cross-site requests and WebSockets (comma-separated, or `*`) |
| `AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Extra host names a loopback or private-address server answers |
| `AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN` | Require the URL token on every request |
| `AUTH_ENFORCE` | `true` gates every route and WebSocket behind auth |
| `AIUI_AUTH_SECRET` | Session signing secret (comma-separated to rotate: first signs, all verify); default a generated `<data dir>/auth_secret` |
| `AIUI_SESSION_LIFETIME` | How long a sign-in lasts while unused (`14d` default, `12h`, `3600`); overrides YAML `auth.sessionLifetime` |
| `AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD` | `1` stops loading plugin CLI commands |
| `PRAISONAI_MODEL` | Default model for built-in agent features (default `gpt-4o-mini`) |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Used by agent features and examples that call OpenAI |

The security variables are described in
[Deployment](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md).

## Python equivalent of `aiui build`

```python
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from praisonaiui.compiler import Compiler
from praisonaiui.schema import Config

config = Config.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(Path("aiui.yaml").read_text()))
result = Compiler(config, base_path=Path(".")).compile(output_dir=Path("aiui"), minify=False)
print(result.success, result.files, result.error)
```
