# Python SDK API

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/python

> Reference for import praisonaiui as aiui.

Reference for `import praisonaiui as aiui`.

## Server Configuration

These functions configure the server. Call them at module level in your `app.py`, before the server starts.

### `aiui.set_style(style)`

Set the UI style.

| Parameter | Type | Values |
|-----------|------|--------|
| `style` | `str` | `"app"` (the React app shell), `"chat"` (the classic chat), `"dashboard"`, `"agents"`, `"playground"`, `"docs"`, `"custom"` |

```python
aiui.set_style("dashboard")
```

Priority under `aiui run`: CLI `--style`, then `set_style()`, then
auto-detection (a plain chat app gets `app`). See
[UI Styles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/styles.md).

---

### `aiui.set_pages(page_ids)`

Choose which pages the app shows besides its own, in every style. The list
covers built-in pages, the app shell's layout pages (`start`, `artifacts`,
`templates`, `connect`, `api-reference`, ...) and dashboard-plugin folders,
including the ones in `~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins` that every app on the
machine would otherwise share. Pages the app registers itself
(`@aiui.page()`, `register_page`, `register_plugin`) and installed
entry-point plugins always appear. Without `set_pages` every page shows.

```python
aiui.set_pages("minimal")         # preset: Chat + your own pages (default for aiui run app.py)
aiui.set_pages("agent")           # preset: Chat, Sessions, Approvals, Usage, Memory + your pages
aiui.set_pages("ops")             # preset: all built-in ops pages (alias of "all")
aiui.set_pages(["chat"])          # explicit list: Chat plus the app's own pages
aiui.set_pages([])                # only the app's own pages
aiui.set_pages([
    "chat", "agents", "memory", "knowledge",
    "skills", "sessions", "usage", "config", "logs",
])
```

An id that names no page is reported with a warning at startup. Use
`aiui pages ids` to see all available page IDs, or inspect `aiui.PAGE_PRESETS`
for the built-in preset definitions (`minimal`, `agent`, `ops`).

`aiui.set_pages("all")` / `aiui.set_pages("ops")` (or `aiui run app.py --preset ops` / `--pages all`) shows every page
and makes every layout's sidebar list them all, grouped (Agent, Work,
Control, ...), as the legacy dashboard did: each page in its React version
where there is one, otherwise the legacy view inside the app shell. The
layout picker keeps working. `aiui run --pages chat,sessions` is the same as
`set_pages(["chat", "sessions"])`.

The app's own pages (`register_page`, `@aiui.page`) are listed in their group
in every layout's sidebar, not only under More (⌘K).

### `aiui.only_my_pages(*keep)`

Shorthand for `set_pages(list(keep))`: `aiui.only_my_pages()` shows only the
app's own pages, `aiui.only_my_pages("chat")` adds Chat.

---

### `aiui.create_shell_app(*, config=None, pages=None, plugins=None, routes=None, csp=None, require_auth=False, config_path=None)`

Build a minimal Starlette ASGI app that mounts **only** the React app shell,
selected pages, plugin assets/routes, and caller-supplied `routes` — without
mounting agent server endpoints (`/sessions`, `/run`, `/agents`, `/teams`,
`/api/chat/*`) or the 48 backend agent features (unmatched paths return `404`).

Pass `csp="strict"` (a directive dict, or `(html, hashes) -> str`) to attach a
strict `Content-Security-Policy` header with exact `'sha256-…'` hashes for the
shell's executable inline scripts. Related helpers:

- `aiui.render_shell_html(request=None, *, style="app")` → `(html, inline_script_hashes)`
- `aiui.shell_inline_script_hashes(html)` → sorted `'sha256-…'` tuple (skips `type="application/json"` and `src="…"`)
- `aiui.shell_csp_header(html, *, base=None, extra=None)` → rendered `Content-Security-Policy` header value

See [Build a focused app → Mount only the shell](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/guides/focused-app.md#mount-only-the-shell-no-agent-endpoints).

---

### `aiui.set_branding(title, logo)`

Configure the sidebar branding (title text and logo).

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `title` | `str` | `"PraisonAI"` |
| `logo` | `str` | `""` (no logo: the PraisonAI brand glyph) |

`logo` is an image URL or path (`/static/logo.svg`, `https://…`, `data:image/…`)
or a short text mark. Left empty, every UI draws the PraisonAI glyph on the
accent tile.

```python
aiui.set_branding(title="MyApp", logo="/static/logo.svg")
```

Also configurable via `config.yaml`:
```yaml
site:
  title: MyApp
  logo: /static/logo.svg
```

---

### `aiui.set_datastore(store)`

Set the persistence backend for sessions and messages.

```python
# JSON files under ~/.praisonaiui (or AIUI_DATA_DIR)
aiui.set_datastore(aiui.JSONFileDataStore())

# In-memory (no persistence)
aiui.set_datastore(aiui.MemoryDataStore())
```

Without a call, the server uses the SDK store shared with PraisonAI Agents
(`SDKFileDataStore`, from `praisonaiui.datastore_sdk`), falling back to
`JSONFileDataStore`. `aiui run --datastore` sets the same thing from the
command line.

---

### `aiui.set_provider(provider)`

Set the AI provider for chat completions.

```python
aiui.set_provider(aiui.PraisonAIProvider())
```

---

### `aiui.register_agent(name, agent)`

Register an agent object (for example a PraisonAI Agents `Agent`) under a
name. Together with an `@aiui.profiles` callback, registered agents make
`aiui run` pick the `agents` style.

```python
from praisonaiagents import Agent

aiui.register_agent("researcher", Agent(name="Researcher", instructions="You research topics."))
```

Agents created in the dashboard's Agents page are a separate store
(`/api/agents/definitions`).

---

### `aiui.remove_page(page_id)`

Remove a page from the sidebar.

```python
aiui.remove_page("debug")
```

---

### `aiui.set_chat_mode(mode, *, position, size, resizable, minimized)`

Configure chat window display mode — full page, floating window, or sidebar panel.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `mode` | `str` | `"fullpage"` | `"fullpage"`, `"floating"`, or `"sidebar"` |
| `position` | `tuple[int, int]` | `(20, 20)` | (bottom, right) pixel offset for floating mode |
| `size` | `tuple[int, int]` | `(400, 500)` | (width, height) initial size for floating mode |
| `resizable` | `bool` | `True` | Allow resizing the floating window |
| `minimized` | `bool` | `False` | Start minimized (floating mode only) |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# Full page chat (default)
aiui.set_chat_mode("fullpage")

# Floating chat window
aiui.set_chat_mode("floating", position=(20, 20), size=(420, 550))

# Sidebar panel
aiui.set_chat_mode("sidebar")
```

---

### `aiui.set_sidebar_config(*, collapsible, default_collapsed, width, min_width, max_width)`

Configure sidebar behavior and dimensions.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `collapsible` | `bool` | `True` | Allow sidebar to be collapsed |
| `default_collapsed` | `bool` | `False` | Start with sidebar collapsed |
| `width` | `int` | `260` | Default sidebar width in pixels |
| `min_width` | `int` | `200` | Minimum width when resizing |
| `max_width` | `int` | `360` | Maximum width when resizing |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_sidebar_config(collapsible=True, width=280)
aiui.set_sidebar_config(default_collapsed=True)  # Start collapsed
```

---

### `aiui.set_brand_color(color)`

Set the brand/primary accent color. Overrides the theme's default accent.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `color` | `str` | Hex color (e.g. `"#6366f1"`) or CSS color value |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_brand_color("#818cf8")  # Indigo-400
aiui.set_brand_color("#22c55e")  # Green-500
```

---

### `aiui.set_chat_features(*, history, streaming, file_upload, audio, reasoning, tools, multimedia, feedback)`

Configure which chat features are enabled in the UI.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `history` | `bool` | `True` | Show session history sidebar |
| `streaming` | `bool` | `True` | Enable streaming responses |
| `file_upload` | `bool` | `False` | Show file upload button |
| `audio` | `bool` | `False` | Show audio input button |
| `reasoning` | `bool` | `True` | Show reasoning/thinking steps |
| `tools` | `bool` | `True` | Show tool call displays |
| `multimedia` | `bool` | `True` | Enable multimedia rendering |
| `feedback` | `bool` | `False` | Show feedback buttons |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# Minimal chat — no history sidebar, no file upload
aiui.set_chat_features(history=False, file_upload=False)

# Full-featured chat
aiui.set_chat_features(
    history=True,
    streaming=True,
    file_upload=True,
    audio=True,
    feedback=True,
)
```

---

### `aiui.set_dashboard(*, sidebar, page_header, modules, plugin_dirs, plugins, groups)`

Configure dashboard layout options.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `sidebar` | `bool` | `True` | Show the left sidebar navigation |
| `page_header` | `bool` | `True` | Show the page title/description header |
| `modules` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Optional dashboard JS modules (`jobs`, `auth`, `api`) |
| `plugin_dirs` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Extra directories to scan for dashboard plugins |
| `plugins` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Allowlist of dashboard plugin names. `None` = all discovered (bundled, `~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins`, `plugin_dirs`); `[]` = none |
| `groups` | `dict \| None` | `None` | Sidebar group order and folding in the app shell (YAML `dashboard.groups`) |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_style("dashboard")
aiui.set_dashboard(sidebar=False)       # Chat-only dashboard, no sidebar
aiui.set_dashboard(page_header=False)   # Hide page titles
aiui.set_dashboard(plugins=[])          # No auto-discovered dashboard plugins
```

`plugins` filters both the sidebar pages (`/api/pages`) and the browser plugin
manifest (`/api/dashboard/plugins`), so disabled plugin scripts are never loaded.
It scopes navigation only — it is **not** an authorization boundary for API routes.

---

### `aiui.set_chat_preview(enabled, *, surface_id, width)`

Configure the **chat + canvas** split preview (`chat-canvas` page). The vanilla `chat` page is unchanged.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | `bool` | `True` | Expose preview settings in `/ui-config.json` |
| `surface_id` | `str` | `"main"` | Default A2UI surface id for the preview panel |
| `width` | `str` | `"40%"` | CSS width of the preview column (e.g. `"38%"`, `"420px"`) |

```python
aiui.set_chat_preview(enabled=True, surface_id="main", width="38%")
aiui.set_pages(["chat-canvas", "chat", "canvas"])
```

See [A2UI canvas](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/a2ui-canvas.md).

---

### `aiui.set_theme(preset="zinc", dark_mode=True, radius="md")`

Set the colour palette, colour mode and corner radius. Takes priority over
YAML `site.theme`.

| Parameter | Type | Values |
|-----------|------|--------|
| `preset` | `str` | `zinc`, `slate`, `stone`, `gray`, `neutral`, `red`, `orange`, `amber`, `yellow`, `lime`, `green`, `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `sky`, `blue`, `indigo`, `violet`, `purple`, `fuchsia`, `pink`, `rose`, or a name from `register_theme()` |
| `dark_mode` | `bool \| None` | `True` dark, `False` light, `None` leaves it to YAML or the viewer and the OS |
| `radius` | `str` | `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` |

```python
aiui.set_theme(preset="blue", dark_mode=None, radius="lg")
```

See [Theming](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md).

---

### `aiui.set_custom_css(css)`

Add a CSS string to the page as an inline `<style>` tag.

```python
aiui.set_custom_css(":root { --db-accent: #22c55e; }")
```

---

### `aiui.set_layout(default=None, *, available=None, user_choice=None, primary=None, options=None)`

Choose the React app shell's layout (`style: app`). See
[Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md).

---

### `aiui.register_theme(name, variables)`

Register a custom theme preset. The theme becomes available in the theme picker UI and via `/api/theme`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `name` | `str` | Unique theme name (e.g. `"ocean"`, `"sunset"`) |
| `variables` | `dict[str, str]` | Dict with at least `{"accent": "#hexcolor"}` |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# Register a custom theme
aiui.register_theme("ocean", {"accent": "#0077b6"})

# With explicit RGB (auto-derived if omitted)
aiui.register_theme("sunset", {
    "accent": "#ff6b35",
    "accentRgb": "255,107,53",
})

# Apply the custom theme
aiui.set_theme(preset="ocean")
```

See [CSS Architecture](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/css-architecture.md) for all available CSS variables.

---

### `aiui.set_custom_js(path)`

Inject a local JavaScript file into the UI. Reads the file at `path` and
serves it at `/custom.js`. A `<script src="/custom.js">` tag is injected
into the host HTML **after** the plugin loader, so `window.aiui` and all
registry APIs (`registerView`, `registerComponent`) are ready when your
code runs.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `path` | `str \| Path` | Local filesystem path to a `.js` file |

Raises `FileNotFoundError` if the path does not exist.

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.set_custom_js("plugin.js")
```

Where `plugin.js` uses the client-side extension APIs:

```javascript
// plugin.js
window.aiui.registerComponent('timeline', function(comp) {
    const el = document.createElement('div');
    (comp.events || []).forEach(ev => {
        const row = document.createElement('div');
        row.textContent = `${ev.time} — ${ev.label}`;
        el.appendChild(row);
    });
    return el;
});
```

---

### `aiui.register_component_schema(component_type, schema)`

Register a JSON Schema contract for a component dict. Built-in schemas
are auto-derived from every `aiui.ui.*` builder at startup; user schemas
take priority and are merged on top.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `component_type` | `str` | Component type string (e.g. `"timeline"`) |
| `schema` | `dict` | JSON Schema dict (Draft 2020-12 compatible) |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

aiui.register_component_schema("timeline", {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["type", "events"],
    "properties": {
        "type": {"const": "timeline"},
        "events": {"type": "array"},
    },
})
```

### `aiui.get_component_schemas()`

Returns the merged registry as a `dict[str, dict]`. Also available as a
JSON endpoint: `GET /api/components/schemas`.

```python
schemas = aiui.get_component_schemas()
print(sorted(schemas))   # ['accordion', 'alert', ..., 'timeline', ...]
```

---

### `aiui.prompt(question, *, options=None, timeout=300.0)`

Pause the agent and wait for the user to answer. Preferred entry point
for interactive agent flows — supersedes the legacy `AskUserMessage`
class.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `question` | `str` | Text shown to the user. |
| `options`  | `list[str] \| None` | Optional list of choices. When given, the user picks one; otherwise they type free text. |
| `timeout`  | `float` | Seconds to wait before giving up. Default 300 (5 min). |

Returns a `PromptResult` dataclass (`text`, `choice`, `message_id`).
The result is truthy when the user answered, falsy on timeout.

The answer comes back over the chat WebSocket (`ask_response`), so a
question needs the WebSocket transport; the HTTP fallback (`POST /run`) can
show it but not answer it. Time spent waiting for the answer does not count
against the `@reply` inactivity timeout (`AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT`).
`aiui.ask` and `AskUserMessage` work the same way.

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

@aiui.reply
async def on_message(msg: str):
    name = await aiui.prompt("What's your name?")
    if name:
        await aiui.say(f"Hi {name.text}!")

    pick = await aiui.prompt("Pick a colour", options=["red", "blue"])
    if pick:
        await aiui.say(f"You picked {pick.choice}")
```

---

### `aiui.error(content, *, details=None)`

Emit an error message to the chat. A thin helper around `Message` with
`metadata={"kind": "error"}` — keeps the public surface small.

```python
try:
    data = await fetch()
except Exception as exc:
    await aiui.error("Couldn't load data", details=str(exc))
```

---

### `aiui.configure(*, datastore=None, branding=None, theme=None, chat=None, custom_css=None, custom_js=None, style=None)`

One call for the common setters. Every keyword is optional; each one is
forwarded to the matching `set_*` function, which you can still call directly.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `datastore` | `str` | Storage backend: `"memory"`, `"json"`, `"json:/path"`, `"sdk"`, `"sdk:/path"`. |
| `branding`  | `dict` | Forwarded to `set_branding(...)`. Keys: `title`, `logo` (any other key raises `TypeError`). |
| `theme`     | `dict` | Forwarded to `set_theme(...)`. Keys: `preset`, `dark`/`dark_mode`, `radius`; `brand_color` goes to `set_brand_color()`. |
| `chat`      | `dict` | `feedback` goes to `set_feedback_enabled()`, `mode` to `set_chat_mode()`, other keys to `set_chat_features()`. |
| `custom_css`| `str` | CSS text, passed to `set_custom_css()` unchanged. It is not read from a file: pass `Path("styles.css").read_text()` to use one. |
| `custom_js` | `str \| Path` | Path to a JS file; same as `set_custom_js`. |
| `style`     | `str` | UI style — `"chat"`, `"dashboard"`, etc. |

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

from pathlib import Path

aiui.configure(
    branding={"title": "My App", "logo": "🎨"},
    theme={"preset": "blue", "dark": True, "radius": "md"},
    chat={"feedback": True, "mode": "floating"},
    datastore="json",
    custom_css=Path("styles.css").read_text(),
    custom_js="plugin.js",
)
```

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui

# In-memory (volatile)
aiui.configure(datastore="memory")

# JSON files at ~/.praisonaiui/sessions/
aiui.configure(datastore="json")

# JSON files at custom path
aiui.configure(datastore="json:/tmp/my-sessions")

# SDK-backed store shared with PraisonAI Agents (the default)
aiui.configure(datastore="sdk")
```

---

## Callback Decorators

### `@aiui.reply`

Handle incoming chat messages. This is the core callback.

```python
@aiui.reply
async def on_reply(message):
    await aiui.think("Thinking...")
    await aiui.say(f"You said: {message.text}")
```

Annotate the parameter as `str` (`async def on_reply(message: str)`) to get
the text only. Otherwise the callback gets a `MessageContext` with:

- `message.text` (alias `message.content`): the user's text
- `message.session_id`: the session id
- `message.agent_name`: the selected agent, if any
- `message.attachments`: the files sent with the message,
  `[{id, name, content_type, path}]` (see [Attachments](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/attachments.md))

How a reply ends:

- If the callback raises, the run ends with one `run_error` frame carrying the
  exception text. The chat shows the error under whatever was streamed, the
  reply is saved with `status: "error"` (so it is still there after a
  reload), the run ledger counts it as failed, and the traceback is logged.
- Stop (`chat_abort`, `POST /api/chat/abort`, `POST /cancel`) cancels the
  callback task: the callback gets `asyncio.CancelledError` at its next
  `await`, so an LLM call or tool it is waiting on stops too.
- A callback that sends nothing (no token, message, step or tool event) for
  `AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 600) is cancelled and the run
  fails with a timeout. Set `AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0` for no limit.

---

### `@aiui.welcome`

The greeting on a new, empty chat.

```python
@aiui.welcome
async def on_welcome():
    await aiui.say("Welcome! How can I help you today?")
```

The chat runs it through `POST /welcome` once per page load and shows what
it says (`aiui.say`, or streamed tokens) as plain text on the empty thread:
in the app shell's chat and every layout, the `chat` style and the
dashboard's chat. In a layout's new-chat hero (the site's mark and name)
the greeting takes the place of the generic "Ask anything…" line, with the
starters below it. It is not saved to the conversation. A chat YAML's
`welcome:` key registers one for you.

---

### `@aiui.goodbye` / `@aiui.on_chat_end`

Runs when a chat's last browser connection closes, after any reply still
running there finishes, as that chat (`aiui.user_session` is readable): use it
for clean-up. Nobody is listening any more, so what it sends is dropped.

```python
@aiui.on_chat_end
async def end():
    await close_connection(aiui.user_session.get("db"))
```

---

### Chat lifecycle

Each moment of a chat has a handler. The names are aliases: `@aiui.on_message`
and `@aiui.reply` register the same handler (the last one registered wins).

| Decorator | Runs | Same as |
|---|---|---|
| `@aiui.on_message` | For each message the user sends; gets the `MessageContext` (`message.content`). | `@aiui.reply` |
| `@aiui.on_chat_start` | Once per chat, right before its first reply (again after `on_chat_end` ran for it). | |
| `@aiui.on_stop` | When the user presses Stop, as the stopped chat. | `@aiui.cancel` |
| `@aiui.on_chat_end` | When the chat ends (above). | `@aiui.goodbye` |
| `@aiui.author_rename` | Maps an author (agent) name to the name the chat shows. | |
| `@aiui.welcome` | The greeting on an empty chat, once per page load (no chat yet). | |

Every handler may be `async def` or a plain `def`.

```python
@aiui.on_chat_start
async def start():
    aiui.user_session["agent"] = build_agent()   # per-chat setup
    await aiui.say("Ready when you are.")         # opens the first reply

@aiui.on_message
async def main(message):
    await aiui.say(await aiui.user_session["agent"].run(message.content))

@aiui.author_rename
def rename(name: str) -> str:
    return {"researcher": "Research assistant"}.get(name, name)
```

`on_chat_start` runs in the reply's task (so `aiui.say` and `aiui.Message`
work) and needs a reply handler; if it raises, that turn fails with the error
and the next turn runs it again. `author_rename` is called once per name per
reply (a failing handler keeps the name); the display name goes on every frame
of the reply (`agent_name`) and the saved reply, never on the agent the user
picked. `@aiui.resume` is not called yet (below).

---

### `@aiui.starters`

Define conversation starters shown to new users.

```python
@aiui.starters
async def on_starters():
    return [
        {"label": "What can you do?", "message": "Tell me about your capabilities"},
        {"label": "Help me write", "message": "Help me draft an email"},
    ]
```

---

### `@aiui.profiles`

Define chat profiles (agent personas users can choose).

```python
@aiui.profiles
async def on_profiles():
    return [
        {"name": "Expert", "description": "Expert mode", "icon": "🎓"},
        {"name": "Creative", "description": "Creative writer", "icon": "✍️"},
    ]
```

---

### `@aiui.page(id, *, title, icon="📄", group="Custom", description="", order=100, refresh_every=None, badge=None)`

Register a custom page. The callback's return value is the page data
(`GET /api/pages/<id>/data`); return `aiui.layout([...])` to render UI blocks
inside the React app shell (the default). Use `@aiui.register_page_action(id)`
to handle form submissions, editable `aiui.sheet(..., action=...)` saves, or
streaming `yield` generators (`application/x-ndjson`).

```python
@aiui.page("analytics", title="Analytics", icon="bar-chart-2", group="App", order=10)
async def analytics_page():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.card("Revenue", value="$12,345"),
        aiui.chart("Signups", data=[{"name": "Mon", "value": 4}, {"name": "Tue", "value": 7}], chart_type="line"),
    ])
```

`aiui.register_page(id, *, title, ...)` registers a page without a decorator.

---

### `aiui.interface(fn, *, inputs=("text",), outputs="auto", title="App", id=None, description="", icon="sparkles", group="Apps", submit_label="Run", order=10)`

Register a 5-line Gradio-style interactive page backed by a single Python
function (sync, `async def`, sync generator, or async generator `yield`).
Accepts shorthand input names (`"text"`, `"textarea"`, `"number"`, `"checkbox"`,
`"file"`) or full `aiui.*` input blocks (including `aiui.file_upload()`).
Uploaded files are resolved automatically via `aiui.get_uploaded_file()` and
unverified/forged handles resolve to `None`.

```python
async def summarize(text: str, tone: str = "Brief"):
    acc = ""
    for word in f"**{tone}:** {text[:120]}".split():
        acc = f"{acc} {word}".strip()
        yield acc

aiui.interface(
    summarize,
    inputs=["textarea", aiui.select_input("Tone", name="tone", options=["Brief", "Detailed"], value="Brief")],
    title="Summarizer",
)
```

---

### `aiui.get_uploaded_file(attachment_or_id)`

Resolve an attachment UUID (or handle dict submitted by `aiui.file_upload()`)
to verified server file metadata (`{id, filename, content_type, size, path, session_id}`),
or `None` if unknown, malformed, or expired. Always use this instead of trusting
client-supplied paths.

---

### `@aiui.on(event)`

Register a handler for a named event. The server dispatches `feedback`
(a thumbs up or down on a message) to it:

```python
@aiui.on("feedback")
async def on_feedback(event):
    print(event["session_id"], event["message_id"], event["value"], event["comment"])
```

---

### `@aiui.login`, `@aiui.settings`, `@aiui.resume`

These decorators register a handler, but the server does not call them yet,
so do not rely on them. Sign-in is configured with YAML `auth:` or
`create_app(require_auth=...)`; see [Deployment](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md).

---

### `@aiui.surface_action(surface_id)`

Handle user actions from an A2UI surface (button clicks, form submits).

```python
@aiui.surface_action("main")
async def on_surface_action(action: dict):
    # action includes component_id, action name, data, session_id
    return {"status": "ok"}
```

---

### `@aiui.on_shared_view` / `@aiui.on_shared_thread_view`

Control read-only access to shared thread links (`GET /shared/{token}`). Returns `True` to allow access, `False` to deny (default: deny when unregistered).

```python
@aiui.on_shared_view
async def can_view_shared(thread_id: str, viewer) -> bool:
    return viewer is not None
```

Related helpers: `aiui.create_share_token(thread_id, created_by)`, `aiui.get_thread_by_share_token(token)`, `aiui.revoke_share_token(thread_id, user_id)`, `aiui.list_share_tokens(user_id)`, and `aiui.get_share_url(token, base_url="")`. See [Session Management → Thread Sharing](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/sessions.md#thread-sharing).

## Message Functions

Async functions for sending messages to the user. Call inside callback handlers.

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `await aiui.say(content)` | Send a complete message |
| `await aiui.send_block(block, *, name=None, id=None)` | Render any of the 81 UI blocks, `aiui.layout([...])`, pandas/Polars DataFrame, or Plotly figure inline inside chat |
| `await aiui.stream_token(token)` | Append a token to the streaming reply |
| `await aiui.stream(token)` | Same as `stream_token` |
| `await aiui.think(step)` | Show a reasoning step |
| `await aiui.ask(question, options=None, timeout=300.0)` | Ask the user and wait; returns the answer text |
| `await aiui.image(url, alt="")` | Send an image |
| `await aiui.audio(url)` | Send audio |
| `await aiui.video(url)` | Send video |
| `await aiui.file(url, name="")` | Send a file |
| `await aiui.action_buttons(buttons)` | Show buttons; handle clicks with `@aiui.button(name)` |
| `await aiui.tool(name, args=None, result=None)` | Show a tool call and its result |

## UI Components

Build custom page layouts with UI components.

```python
@aiui.page("my-dashboard", title="My Dashboard", icon="📊")
async def my_dashboard():
    return aiui.layout([
        aiui.columns([
            aiui.card("Metric A", value="42"),
            aiui.card("Metric B", value="98%", footer="+5% this week"),
        ]),
        aiui.table(headers=["Name", "Value"], rows=[["Alpha", 100], ["Beta", 200]]),
        aiui.chart("Trend", data=[{"name": "Q1", "value": 10}, {"name": "Q2", "value": 30}], chart_type="line"),
    ])
```

| Component | Usage |
|-----------|-------|
| `aiui.layout(children)` | Root container for a page |
| `aiui.card(title, *, value=None, footer=None)` | Metric card |
| `aiui.columns(children)` | Horizontal column layout |
| `aiui.chat_panel(*, title="Agent Chat", agent=None, height=520, session_id=None, welcome=None)` | Embedded Agent Chat panel for split-pane workspaces |
| `aiui.chart(title, *, data=None, chart_type="bar")` | Chart; `data` accepts a list of dicts or pandas/Polars DataFrame |
| `aiui.plotly_chart(fig, title="", *, height=None, caption=None)` | Convert a Plotly figure to a native Recharts `chart` block |
| `aiui.table(data=None, *, headers=None, rows=None, row_ids=None, actions=None)` | Data table; accepts pandas/Polars DataFrames, dict lists, or headers + rows |
| `aiui.file_upload(label="Upload file", *, name="files", accept=None, multiple=False, max_size_mb=10)` | Drag-and-drop file uploader backed by `/api/chat/attachments` |
| `aiui.sheet(title, *, headers=None, rows=None, tabs=None, action=None, save_label="Save")` | Editable multi-tab spreadsheet with optional Save action callback |
| `aiui.text(content)` | Text block |

See the [Component API Reference](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/components.md) for the other builders
(metrics, alerts, tabs, forms and more).

# YAML Configuration

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/configuration

> The aiui.yaml schema: what aiui validate checks and aiui build

The `aiui.yaml` schema: what `aiui validate` checks and `aiui build`
compiles. The source of truth is
[`schema/models.py`](https://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAIUI/blob/main/src/praisonaiui/schema/models.py)
(`Config`). The runtime state file of a running server is a different file; see
[Runtime Persistence](#runtime-persistence-configyaml) below.

## Config file name

`aiui validate`, `aiui build` and `aiui serve` find the file in this order:

1. `--config <path>`, when given. It always wins and prints nothing extra.
2. `./aiui.yaml`.
3. `./aiui.template.yaml`, the old name. It still works; the command prints one
   dim line on stderr and its exit code does not change:
   `Using aiui.template.yaml; rename it to aiui.yaml (the old name keeps working).`

When both files exist, `aiui.yaml` is used and the command says so in one line
(`Using aiui.yaml; aiui.template.yaml is also here and is ignored.`). With
neither, the command stops with `Configuration file not found: aiui.yaml`.
`aiui init` writes `aiui.yaml` and refuses to overwrite either name without
`--force`. `aiui dev` reads either name, and `aiui dev --examples` accepts either name in each example folder. `aiui.yml`
is not looked up; pass it with `--config`.

## Split the config with `$ref`

Any mapping can live in its own file. `$ref` names a YAML (or JSON) file,
relative to the file that holds the `$ref`:

```yaml
# aiui.yaml
site:
  title: My Docs
navigation:
  $ref: ./config/nav.yaml
```

```yaml
# config/nav.yaml
tabs:
  - tab: Guides
    groups:
      - $ref: ./groups/guides.yaml
```

- Included files can include others; keys written next to `$ref` override the
  included ones.
- Paths stay inside the folder of `aiui.yaml`; a file that includes itself,
  directly or through others, is an error (`$ref cycle: aiui.yaml ->
  config/nav.yaml -> aiui.yaml`).
- Errors name the file and line of the `$ref` (`aiui.yaml:6: $ref
  './config/nav.yaml' not found`); a YAML error or an unknown key inside an
  included file names that file. `validate`, `build`, `serve`, `docs
  check-links` and the server all read includes.

## Editor setup

`aiui init` starts `aiui.yaml` with this line:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json
```

Editors that run the YAML language server (VS Code with the Red Hat YAML
extension, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, Zed) then complete keys, show each key's
description on hover and underline wrong values as you type; add the line to
an existing `aiui.yaml` for the same. The schema is generated from the
`Config` model, so it never drifts from `aiui validate`. For the exact
installed version (offline, or pinned), run `aiui schema -o aiui.schema.json`
and use `$schema=./aiui.schema.json`.

## Overview

| Key | What it sets | Page |
|-----|--------------|------|
| `schemaVersion` | Schema version (`1`) | below |
| `site` | Title, description, theme, logo, custom CSS | below, [Theming](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/theming.md) |
| `style` | UI style (`docs` by default for a site) | [UI Styles](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/styles.md) |
| `content` | Where the Markdown lives | [Content Sources](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/content-sources.md) |
| `components`, `templates`, `routes` | Layout of each page | below, [Templates](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/templates.md), [Slots](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/concepts/slots.md) |
| `navigation`, `navbar`, `footer`, `logo`, `search` | Docs site chrome | [Navigation](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md) |
| `seo`, `i18n`, `a11y` | Meta tags, locales, accessibility switches | [SEO](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/seo.md), [i18n](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/i18n.md) |
| `layout` | Chat position, and the app shell's layouts | [Layouts](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/layouts.md) |
| `chat`, `auth`, `dashboard`, `widgets`, `extensions` | Chat, sign-in, dashboard and plugin settings | [Deployment](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/deployment.md), [Plugins](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/plugins.md) |
| `dependencies` | shadcn components to install at build time | below |

`aiui validate --strict` turns unknown keys into errors.

## Schema Version

Always specify the schema version:

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1
```

## Site Configuration

```yaml
site:
  title: "My Documentation"          # Required
  description: "Site description"    # Optional
  routeBaseDocs: "/docs"             # Default: /docs
  ui: "shadcn"                       # Theming hint (shadcn | mui | chakra)
  theme:
    preset: "zinc"                   # Any Tailwind color (22 options)
    radius: "md"                     # none | sm | md | lg | xl
    darkMode: true
```

> **Note**: The `ui` field is a theming hint. Components are UI-agnostic and use CSS classes you can style with any framework.

## Component Dependencies

Auto-install shadcn components at build time:

```yaml
dependencies:
  shadcn:
    - accordion
    - tabs
    - dialog
```

When you run `aiui build`, missing components are installed with
`npx shadcn@latest add <name>` into the frontend source (`src/frontend` in a
repository checkout). This only matters when you build the frontend yourself;
the bundled React app does not change.

## Content Sources

```yaml
content:
  docs:
    dir: "./docs"                    # Path to docs folder
    include:                         # Glob patterns
      - "**/*.md"
      - "**/*.mdx"
    exclude:                         # Excluded patterns
      - "**/drafts/**"
    editLink:                        # "Edit this page" under each page
      pattern: "https://github.com/acme/site/edit/main/docs/:path"
      text: "Edit this page"         # optional
    lastUpdated: true                # the date of the page's last commit
    feedback:                        # "Was this page helpful?" (on by default; false: off)
      issues: "https://github.com/acme/site/issues/new"  # optional
      code: true                     # optional: a flag on each code block
      endpoint: "https://hooks.example.com/votes"  # optional: static hosting
    related: 5                       # related pages under each page (default 3; false: none)
    mcp: false                       # no MCP server on aiui serve (default: on)
    assistant:                       # Ask AI on aiui serve (default: on; false: off)
      starters: ["How do I install it?"]
      instructions: "Call the product Acme."
```

`editLink`, `lastUpdated` and `feedback` draw the page footer; see
[Writing docs pages → Page footer](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#page-footer).
`related` is the [related pages](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/writing-docs.md#related-pages) list.
`mcp` is the [docs MCP server](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#mcp-server) and
`assistant` is [Ask AI](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/ai-ready-docs.md#ask-ai).

`indexFiles` and `nav` (`mode`, `sort`, `collapsible`, `maxDepth`) are accepted
but not read by the build yet; see [Navigation](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/navigation.md).

## Components

Define reusable components:

```yaml
components:
  my_header:
    type: "Header"
    props:
      logoText: "My Site"
      cta:
        label: "Get Started"
        href: "/docs"

  my_footer:
    type: "Footer"
    props:
      text: "© 2024"
```

### Built-in Component Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `Header` | Site header with logo, nav, CTA |
| `Footer` | Site footer |
| `DocsSidebar` | Documentation sidebar navigation |
| `Toc` | Table of contents |
| `DocContent` | Rendered markdown content |

## Templates

Templates combine a layout with slot assignments:

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "ThreeColumnLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "my_header" }     # Reference a component
      left: { ref: "sidebar_docs" }
      main: { type: "DocContent" }     # Direct type assignment
      right: { type: "Toc" }
      footer: { ref: "my_footer" }
```

### Layouts

| Layout | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `ThreeColumnLayout` | Sidebar + Content + TOC |
| `TwoColumnLayout` | Sidebar + Content |
| `CenteredLayout` | Centered content, no sidebar |
| `FullWidthLayout` | Full width content |
| `FlexibleLayout` | WordPress-style widget zones |

## Widget Zones

Place widgets in layout zones without modifying markdown:

```yaml
templates:
  docs:
    layout: "FlexibleLayout"
    zones:
      rightSidebar:
        - type: "StatsCard"
          props:
            title: "Users"
            value: "15,231"
            change: "+20%"
      footer:
        - type: "Newsletter"
        - type: "Copyright"
          props:
            text: "© 2024"
```

Zones, the widgets and which layouts render them:
[Widget Zones](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/widget-zones.md).

## Routes

Map URL patterns to templates:

```yaml
routes:
  - match: "/docs/changelog"
    template: "docs"
    slots:
      right: null                      # Override: hide TOC

  - match: "/docs/**"
    template: "docs"
```

Route matching uses glob patterns:
- `*` - one path segment
- `**` - any number of segments

The first matching route wins, so list specific routes before broad ones.
A route's `slots` can override only the `right` slot in the docs site
(`right: null` hides the table of contents); header and footer are read from
the template, so per-route overrides of them have no effect.

## Complete Example

```yaml
schemaVersion: 1

site:
  title: "PraisonAI Docs"
  ui: "shadcn"
  theme:
    darkMode: true

content:
  docs:
    dir: "./docs"

components:
  header:
    type: "Header"
    props:
      logoText: "PraisonAI"

  footer:
    type: "Footer"
    props:
      text: "© 2024 Praison Limited"

  sidebar:
    type: "DocsSidebar"
    props:
      source: "docs-nav"

templates:
  docs:
    layout: "ThreeColumnLayout"
    slots:
      header: { ref: "header" }
      left: { ref: "sidebar" }
      main: { type: "DocContent" }
      right: { type: "Toc" }
      footer: { ref: "footer" }

routes:
  - match: "/docs/**"
    template: "docs"
```

## Runtime Persistence (`config.yaml`)

> **Single source of truth** for all runtime feature state.

In addition to `aiui.yaml` (which drives static site generation), PraisonAIUI uses a **unified runtime config file**, `config.yaml` in the data directory (`AIUI_DATA_DIR`, default `~/.praisonaiui/`). This file stores all feature state — agents, channels, guardrails, schedules, and runtime settings — in a single YAML file that persists across server restarts.

This is compatible with the `gateway.yaml` schema used by `praisonai gateway start --config`.

### Schema

```yaml
# ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml (auto-generated)
schemaVersion: 2

server:
  host: "127.0.0.1"
  port: 8003

provider:
  name: "openai"
  model: "gpt-4o-mini"

gateway:
  host: "127.0.0.1"
  port: 8765

# Agent definitions (same schema as gateway.yaml)
agents:
  personal:
    name: "Personal Assistant"
    instructions: "You are a friendly personal assistant."
    model: "gpt-4o-mini"
    tools: ["internet_search"]

# Messaging channels
channels:
  telegram_bot:
    name: "My Bot"
    platform: "telegram"
    config:
      bot_token: "env:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"

# Runtime configuration (set via /api/config/runtime)
runtime_config:
  model: "gpt-4o"
  temperature: 0.7

# Guardrail definitions
guardrails:
  registry:
    polite_check:
      description: "Output must be polite"

# Scheduled jobs
schedules:
  jobs:
    daily_report:
      name: "Daily Report"
      schedule:
        kind: every
        every_seconds: 86400
```

### How It Works

All CRUD operations (dashboard, REST API, CLI) **automatically write back** to this file:

| Feature | Section | Written On |
|---------|---------|------------|
| Config Runtime | `runtime_config` | PATCH, PUT, DELETE, apply |
| Guardrails | `guardrails` | Register |
| Channels | `channels` | Add, update, delete |
| Schedules | `schedules` | Add, remove, update |
| Agents | `agents` | Create, update, delete |

- **Atomic writes**: a temp file and `os.replace()` prevent corruption.
- **Hot reload**: the [Config Hot-Reload](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/features/config-hot-reload.md) watcher, once started, reloads this file after external edits.
- **Secrets**: channel secrets are written as `env:VAR_NAME` references (a `<key>_ref` key works too); the server refuses an inline token that looks like a secret and redacts secrets in API responses.

Rule of thumb: secrets (API keys, tokens) go in environment variables;
preferences (model, theme, branding) in the config file.

### Relationship to `aiui.yaml`

| File | Purpose | Used By |
|------|---------|---------|
| `aiui.yaml` | Static site layout, components, routes | `aiui build`, `aiui serve`, `aiui validate` |
| `$AIUI_DATA_DIR/config.yaml` | Runtime feature state (agents, channels, config) | `aiui run`, dashboard API |
| `gateway.yaml` | Subset of `config.yaml` (legacy compatibility) | `praisonai gateway start` |

# Component API Reference

Source: https://ui.praison.ai/docs/api/components

> Python functions for building app and dashboard UIs. Each function returns a plain dict that the frontend renders as a real UI block — 81 builders organized by

Python functions for building app and dashboard UIs. Each function returns a plain dict that the frontend renders as a real UI block — **81 builders** organized by category (usable on `@aiui.page`, in zero-code YAML, and inline inside chat via `await aiui.send_block(...)`). Looking for visual examples in both Python and zero-code YAML? Browse the [UI Components gallery](https://ui.praison.ai/docs/components/overview.md).

```python
import praisonaiui as aiui
```

---

## Core Components

### `aiui.layout(children)`

Wrap components in a renderable container.

```python
aiui.layout([
    aiui.card("Users", value=42),
    aiui.table(headers=["A"], rows=[["x"]]),
])
# Returns: {"_components": [...]}
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `children` | `Sequence[dict]` | ✅ | List of component dicts |
| `refresh_every` | `float` | ❌ | App shell: re-fetch the page every N seconds while visible (`_refresh_every`) |
| `params` | `dict` | ❌ | In an action reply: values written into the page URL's query string (`_params`) |

**Returns:** `dict` with `_components` key — triggers structured rendering in the frontend.

### `aiui.card(title, *, value, footer)`

A metric/stat card.

```python
aiui.card("Revenue", value="$1,500", footer="+8% this month")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | `str` | ✅ | Card header label |
| `value` | `Any` | ❌ | Main display value |
| `footer` | `str` | ❌ | Small text below the value |

### `aiui.columns(children)`

Arrange components in a responsive grid row.

```python
aiui.columns([
    aiui.card("A", value=1),
    aiui.card("B", value=2),
    aiui.card("C", value=3),
])
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `children` | `Sequence[dict]` | ✅ | Component dicts to lay out side-by-side |

### `aiui.table(*, headers, rows, columns=None, ...)`

A data table. In the app shell it sorts by header click, formats typed
columns, and can search, page, link rows and open a row in a side panel. The
old call shape keeps working unchanged.

```python
aiui.table(
    headers=["Name", "Role"],
    rows=[["Alice", "Engineer"], ["Bob", "Designer"]],
)
```

A larger table with typed columns, dict rows and search:

```python
aiui.table(columns=[
    {"key": "name", "label": "Channel", "type": "link", "href_key": "url"},
    {"key": "subs", "label": "Subscribers", "type": "number", "format": "compact"},
    {"key": "status", "type": "badge", "tones": {"growing": "success", "down": "error"}},
], rows=channels, searchable=True, caption="Channels")  # rows: [{"name", "url", "subs", ...}]
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `headers` | `Sequence[str]` | ✅ unless `columns` | Column header labels |
| `rows` | `Sequence[Sequence \| dict]` | ✅ | Row arrays in column order, or dicts keyed by column `key` (sent as arrays) |
| `columns` | `Sequence[str \| dict]` | — | Column config (below). Gives the headers when `headers` is not set |
| `row_ids` | `Sequence[str]` | — | Stable unique ID per row. Makes rows selectable by click, Enter or Space |
| `actions` | `Sequence[str]` | — | Row action button labels (requires `row_ids`) |
| `searchable` | `bool` | — | A search box that keeps the rows holding every typed word (in the browser) |
| `page_size` | `int` | — | Rows per page; `0` shows every row. Unset: 50 per page once there are more than 100 rows |
| `sortable` | `bool` | — | `False` turns header sorting off. Default on |
| `row_href_key` | `str` | — | Key (in dict rows, or a column key) holding each row's link. The first cell becomes the link and a click on the row opens it |
| `row_detail` | `bool` | — | A click (or Enter) on a row opens a side panel listing the row's fields |
| `detail_key` | `str` | — | Key in dict rows holding a list of block dicts the side panel renders instead of the fields (implies `row_detail`) |
| `detail_load_key` | `str` | — | Key in dict rows holding a lazy section key loaded via `POST /api/pages/{id}/action` (`{"_lazy": key, "_params": ...}`) when that row's side panel opens (implies `row_detail`) |
| `detail_load` | `str` | — | Prefix for lazy row detail keys (`f"{detail_load}{row_id_or_index}"`; implies `row_detail`) |
| `max_height` | `int \| str` | — | Height of the scrolling body (px or CSS length, `0` for none). Default `70vh`, so the header stays in view |
| `caption` | `str` | — | Accessible name of the table and its search box |

Column dict keys: `key`, `label`, `type`, `format`, `decimals`, `tones`,
`tone_above`, `tone_below`, `thresholds`, `href_key`, `width` (px or CSS length),
`align` (`left`, `center`, `right`) and `sortable` (`False` for one column). A
plain string is a column whose key and label are that string.

| `type` | Cell value | Shows |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| `auto` (default) | anything | Text as sent; a column of numbers lines up at the end; `{"text", "href"}` is a link and `{"src", "alt"}` an image |
| `text` | any | The value as text |
| `number` | number (or `{"value", "tone"}`) | Right-aligned, tabular figures. `format`: `compact` (1.2k, 3.4M), `percent` (a fraction: 0.123 → 12.3%), `multiplier` or `x` (2.3x), `fixed` (exactly `decimals`, default 2); none groups digits. `decimals` sets the fraction digits. Optional threshold colouring: `tone_above` (number or `[n, tone]`, default `success`), `tone_below` (number or `[n, tone]`, default `error`), or ordered `thresholds: [{"gte": 1, "tone": "success"}, {"lt": 0.5, "tone": "error"}]` |
| `link` | `{"text", "href", "external"}` or a URL; or text with the column's `href_key` | A link. Only http(s), mailto, tel and relative URLs are kept |
| `badge` | text, or `{"text", "tone"}` | A badge; `tones` maps a value to `success`, `warning`, `error` or `info` |
| `tag` | a list (or comma-separated text) | One badge per item, toned like `badge` |
| `image` | URL, or `{"src", "alt"}` | A small rounded thumbnail (`format: "wide"` for 16:9); `alt` defaults to the column label |
| `progress` | 0..1 | A bar and its percent |
| `date` | ISO text, or epoch seconds or ms | `Nov 22, 2026` in UTC; `format: "datetime"` adds the time, `"iso"` gives `2026-11-22`. Sorts by time |
| `sparkline` | a list of numbers | A small trend line (no axes); sorts by the last point |

A header click sorts ascending, descending, then back to the server's order:
stable, numeric-aware (`1,234`, `1.2k`, `12%`, `2.5x`), empty cells last;
headers are buttons with `aria-sort`. On a phone the table scrolls sideways.
The legacy `dashboard` style draws the dict as a plain text table.

With `row_ids`, the dashboard renderer emits bubbling DOM events from the table, so
a custom view can own query state (search, filters, page, sort) and react to rows:

| Event | `detail` |
|-------|----------|
| `aiui:table-select` | `{rowId, index}` |
| `aiui:table-action` | `{action, rowId}` |

Because events carry the stable `rowId`, selection stays correct after the server
re-sorts or filters rows. Loading, empty and error states compose from existing
components (`aiui.skeleton()`, `aiui.empty()`, `aiui.alert()`):

```js
// Custom view: server-paged, searchable table using only documented APIs.
window.aiui.registerView('companies', (container) => {
  const state = { q: '', page: 1 };
  const show = (comps) => { container.replaceChildren(...comps.map(window.aiui.renderComponent)); };
  async function load() {
    show([{ type: 'skeleton', variant: 'card' }]);
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/companies?q=${encodeURIComponent(state.q)}&page=${state.page}`);
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
      const { rows, total } = await res.json();   // [{id, name, status}], count
      if (!rows.length) return show([{ type: 'empty', text: 'No results' }]);
      show([{ type: 'table', headers: ['Name', 'Status'],
              rows: rows.map(r => [r.name, r.status]),
              row_ids: rows.map(r => r.id), actions: ['Edit'] },
            { type: 'caption', text: `${total} companies` }]);
    } catch (e) {
      show([{ type: 'alert', variant: 'error', message: 'Could not load companies. Try again.' }]);
    }
  }
  container.addEventListener('aiui:table-select', (e) => openDetail(e.detail.rowId));
  container.addEventListener('aiui:table-action', (e) => editRow(e.detail.rowId));
  // On search/filter change: state.q = value; state.page = 1; load();
  load();
});
```

### `aiui.text(content)`

A text block.

```python
aiui.text("Last updated 30 seconds ago.")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `content` | `str` | ✅ | Text content |

### `aiui.chart(title, *, data, chart_type, x, y, ...)`

A chart with tooltips, colours from the theme's `--chart-1..5` tokens (light
and dark) and the full width of its column, down to a phone. The chart
library loads in its own chunk the first time a page shows a chart.

```python
# Horizontal bars with a reference line; bars below it are muted.
aiui.chart(
    "Median lift by day", chart_type="barh",
    data=[{"day": "Mon", "lift": 1.4}, {"day": "Tue", "lift": 0.8}],
    x="day", y="lift",
    reference={"value": 1, "label": "usual"}, color_by_reference=True,
    y_format="multiplier",
)

# A line with faint count bars behind it, on a scale of their own.
aiui.chart(
    "Usual views per month", chart_type="line",
    data=[{"month": "Jan", "views": 12000, "posts": 4}, {"month": "Feb", "views": 15400, "posts": 7}],
    x="month", y="views", y2="posts", labels={"views": "Usual views", "posts": "Posts"},
    y_format="compact",
)

aiui.chart("Retention", chart_type="area", data=points, x="t", y="share", y_format="percent", y_domain=[0, 1])
aiui.chart("Formats mix", data=rows, x="quarter", y=["video", "carousel", "text"], stacked=True)
aiui.chart("Reach", chart_type="scatter", data=channels, x="subs", y="ratio", label="channel")
aiui.chart("Spread of lift", chart_type="histogram", data=[0.4, 1.2, 0.9, 2.5], bins=12)

# A heatmap: rows x columns from {x, y, value} rows, coloured low to high.
aiui.chart("When posts land", kind="heatmap", data=slots, x="hour", y="weekday", value="posts")

# A sparkline: a tiny line with no axes (plain numbers work).
aiui.chart("Views, last 30 days", kind="sparkline", data=[120, 140, 90, 210, 180])

# Small multiples: one small chart per platform, all on the same value scale.
aiui.chart("Views by platform", chart_type="line", data=rows, x="month", y="views", facet="platform")
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | `str` | `""` | Chart title |
| `data` | `list[dict]` | `[]` | Rows, e.g. `[{"month": "Jan", "views": 1200}]`. A histogram also takes plain numbers |
| `chart_type` | `str` | `"bar"` | `bar` (columns), `barh` (horizontal bars), `line`, `area`, `scatter`, `pie`, `donut`, `histogram`, `heatmap`, `sparkline` |
| `kind` | `str` | — | Alias of `chart_type` |
| `x` | `str` | first text column | Category key. Scatter: the x value (default: first numeric column). Histogram: the measured value |
| `y` | `str \| list[str]` | every numeric column | Series key, or keys for several series |
| `y2` | `str` | — | A secondary series drawn as faint bars on its own scale (`bar`, `barh`, `line`, `area`) |
| `labels` | `dict[str, str]` | — | Display names for keys in the legend and tooltip |
| `label` | `str` | — | Scatter: key naming each point in the tooltip |
| `tooltip` | `list[str \| dict]` | — | Extra row keys (or `{"key", "label", "format"}` dicts) shown in the tooltip (including scatter & heatmap) |
| `stacked` | `bool` | `False` | Stack the series (`bar`, `barh`, `area`) |
| `reference` | number, list of numbers, `{value, label}` or a list of them | — | Dashed reference lines (a vertical line on `barh`) |
| `color_by_reference` | `bool` | `False` | Bars at or above the first reference keep the series colour; bars below it are muted |
| `x_format`, `y_format` | `str` | — | `number` (1,234.5), `compact` (1.2k, 3.4M), `percent` (0.25 → 25%), `multiplier` (1.5x), `duration` (seconds → 1:05). Axis ticks default to `compact`, tooltips to `number` |
| `x_domain`, `y_domain` | `[min, max]` | auto | X / value axis range, e.g. `x_domain=[1e3, 1e7]` on scatter or `y_domain=[0, 1]` with `y_format="percent"` |
| `x_scale`, `y_scale` | `str` | `"linear"` | `"linear"` or `"log"` (non-positive values are omitted safely) |
| `clip` | `bool \| number \| [min, max]` | — | Clamp outliers to `x_domain`/`y_domain` (`True`), an upper cap (number), or `[min, max]` (histogram edge bins show `≤`/`+`; heatmap colour scale clamps to bounds) |
| `bins` | `int` | Sturges' rule (max 30) | Histogram bin count |
| `height` | `int` | 240 | Plot height in px; `barh` grows with its rows, pie and donut are 260 |
| `caption` | `str` | — | A line of muted text under the chart |
| `legend` | `bool` | more than one series | Show the legend |
| `value` | `str` | `"value"` | Heatmap: the cell value key. `x` is the column key and `y` the row key (defaults `x` and `y`) |
| `facet` | `str` | — | Key whose values split the rows into small charts in a responsive grid (at most 24 panels) |
| `facet_scales` | `str` | `"shared"` | `"shared"` (one value scale across all panels) or `"free"` (each panel scales to its own data) |

**Heatmap.** Columns and rows keep the order they first appear in `data`,
so sort the rows (Mon..Sun, 0..23) before passing them; a repeated cell
sums. Cells are coloured on a sequential scale from the theme's first chart
colour (light and dark), empty cells are outlined, `y_format` formats the
values in the tooltip and the colour scale under the grid, and `y_domain`
fixes the scale. Cells keep a minimum width, so a wide grid scrolls sideways
inside the chart on a phone.

**Sparkline.** One series, no axes, the last value printed beside it;
`height` defaults to 48 px. A number list under a metric is
`aiui.metric(..., sparkline=[...])`.

**Small multiples.** With `facet`, each panel is 160 px high (48 for a
sparkline) unless `height` is set, panels follow first-seen order, and the
legend is shown once. `y_domain` overrides the shared scale.

An unknown `chart_type` or format raises `ValueError`. A dict written by hand
(`{"type": "chart", "data": [...], "chart_type": "line"}`) works too: missing
keys are inferred from the first row, and `column`, `hbar` and `doughnut` are
accepted as kind names. At most 5,000 rows are drawn. The legacy `dashboard`
style shows a summary card instead of the chart.

---

## Essential Components

### `aiui.metric(label, *, value, delta, delta_color, caption, sparkline, benchmark, benchmark_label)`

A metric card with optional delta indicator and caption.

```python
aiui.metric("Requests", value="12.3k", delta="+15%")
aiui.metric("Errors", value=23, delta="+3", delta_color="inverse")
aiui.metric("Lead time", value="4 d", delta="-3 days", delta_color="inverse", caption="median")
aiui.metric("Posts", value=51, caption="in the last 30 days")
aiui.metric("Engagement", value=0.024, benchmark=0.41, benchmark_label="median")  # "17x below median (0.41)"
aiui.metric("Views", value="12.3k", sparkline=[8200, 9100, 10400, 12300])
```

`benchmark` compares a numeric `value` with a reference: a ratio of 2 or
more reads as a multiple ("17x below median"), a smaller one as a percentage
("25% above median"), and it is coloured like a delta (`delta_color`
applies, so `"inverse"` makes "above" the loss). `sparkline` draws the
numbers as a tiny trend line under the value.

A `delta` that starts with `+`/`↑` or `-`/`↓` (or a signed number) is coloured
as a gain or a loss. Use `caption` for a neutral note under the value, so a
subtitle such as "-2 from plan" is not coloured by accident.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | `str` | ✅ | — | Metric label |
| `value` | `Any` | ✅ | — | Main metric value |
| `delta` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Change indicator (e.g. "+5%") |
| `delta_color` | `str` | ❌ | `"normal"` | `"normal"` (rise is good), `"inverse"` (fall is good, e.g. `"-3 days"`), or `"off"` (never coloured) |
| `caption` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Neutral note under the value, never coloured. `help` is an alias |
| `sparkline` | `list[float]` | ❌ | `None` | Numbers drawn as a tiny trend line under the value |
| `benchmark` | `float` | ❌ | `None` | Reference the value is compared with ("17x below median") |
| `benchmark_label` | `str` | ❌ | `"benchmark"` | Name of the benchmark in that line |

## Form Input Components

### `aiui.text_input(label, *, value, placeholder)`

| `placeholder` | `str` | ❌ | `""` | Placeholder text |

### `aiui.number_input(label, *, value, min_val, max_val, step)`

```python
aiui.number_input("Age", value=28, min_val=0, max_val=150, step=1)
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | `str` | ✅ | — | Input label |
| `value` | `int\|float` | ❌ | `0` | Default value |
| `min_val` | `int\|float` | ❌ | `None` | Minimum allowed |
| `max_val` | `int\|float` | ❌ | `None` | Maximum allowed |
| `step` | `int\|float` | ❌ | `1` | Increment step |

### `aiui.select_input(label, *, options, value, name, searchable, auto_submit, options_url, placeholder, selected_label)`

```python
aiui.select_input("Country", options=["USA", "UK", "Canada"], value="USA")
aiui.select_input("Channel", options=channels, name="channel")  # 1,000+ options: searchable
aiui.select_input(
    "Creator",
    options_url="/api/creators/search",
    value=creator_id,
    selected_label=creator_name,
    placeholder="Search creators...",
    name="creator",
)
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | `str` | ✅ | — | Input label |
| `options` | `Sequence[str \| dict]` | ❌ | `()` | Option strings, or `{"value", "label"}` dicts (optional when `options_url` is set) |
| `value` | `str` | ❌ | `""` | Default selected |
| `name` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Submit key in a form (else `label`) |
| `searchable` | `bool` | ❌ | `None` | `True`: a type-to-search list (combobox). `None`: searchable when there are more than 20 options or `options_url` is set. `False`: always a plain dropdown |
| `auto_submit` | `bool` | ❌ | `False` | Submit the enclosing form when the value changes |
| `options_url` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Endpoint queried with `?q=<text>` (debounced 200 ms) returning `[{"value", "label"}]`, `["str"]`, or `{"options": [...]}` |
| `placeholder` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Placeholder text shown when no value is selected |
| `selected_label` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Display label for the initial `value` when `options_url` is used and `options` is omitted |

In the app shell the searchable list filters as you type (names that start
with the text first) and renders at most 100 rows, with a "N more: type to
narrow" line, so a list of a thousand options opens instantly. When
`options_url` is set, typing queries the server endpoint with `?q=...` and
remembers chosen labels across searches. Arrow keys, Enter and Escape work as
in any listbox; the value posts by `name` like a plain select.

`auto_submit=True` is also accepted by `text_input` (debounced 400 ms),
`number_input`, `slider_input`, `textarea_input`, `checkbox_input`,
`switch_input`, `radio_input`, `date_input`, `time_input` and
`color_picker_input`.

### `aiui.multiselect_input(label, *, options, value, name, placeholder, auto_submit, options_url, selected_labels)`

```python
aiui.multiselect_input("Tags", options=["AI", "ML", "NLP"], value=["AI"], name="tags")
aiui.multiselect_input("Topics", options_url="/api/topics/search", value=["t1"], selected_labels={"t1": "AI"}, name="topics")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | `str` | ✅ | — | Input label |
| `options` | `Sequence[str \| dict]` | ❌ | `()` | Choices: strings or `{"value", "label"}` dicts (optional when `options_url` is set) |
| `value` | `Sequence[str]` | ❌ | `()` | Default selections |
| `name` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Submit key in a form (else `label`) |
| `placeholder` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Text of the add button while nothing is chosen |
| `auto_submit` | `bool` | ❌ | `False` | Submit the form when the selection changes |
| `options_url` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Endpoint queried with `?q=<text>` (debounced 200 ms) for remote options |
| `selected_labels` | `dict[str, str]` | ❌ | `None` | Initial `{value: label}` map so chips show labels before a search runs |

Chosen values show as chips with a remove button; "Add" opens a searchable
list. In a form it posts a **list** of the chosen values.

### `aiui.tags_input(label, *, value, name, placeholder, auto_submit)`

```python
aiui.tags_input("Tags", value=["ai"], name="tags")
```

Free-text tags: Enter or a comma turns the typed text into a chip (pasted
`a, b, c` makes three), Backspace in the empty box removes the last one.
Blank and duplicate tags are dropped. Posts a **list** of strings.

### `aiui.date_range_input(name, *, label, start, end, presets, auto_submit)`

```python
aiui.date_range_input("posted", label="Posted", presets=[7, 30, 90, 365])
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | `str` | ✅ | — | Submit-key prefix |
| `label` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Label above the control |
| `start` / `end` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Default ISO dates |
| `presets` | `Sequence[int\|dict]` | ❌ | `(7, 30, 90, 365)` | Day counts, or `{"days": 14, "label": "2 weeks"}`; `()` hides them |
| `auto_submit` | `bool` | ❌ | `False` | Submit the form when the range changes |

Preset buttons and two native date fields. It posts **`<name>_start`** and
**`<name>_end`** (`"2026-01-31"`, or `""` for an open side). A preset sets
the end to today and the start that many days earlier, in the browser's local
date; the preset whose range matches is shown as pressed.

### `aiui.segmented_input(name, options, *, label, value, multi, auto_submit)`

A row of toggle pills (`aria-pressed`). Single choice posts the value (the
first option when `value` is empty); `multi=True` posts a **list**.

### `aiui.link_button(label, href, *, variant, external)` and `aiui.page_link(page_id, label, *, variant, params)`

`link_button` is a link drawn as a button (`variant`: `"outline"` default,
`"primary"`, `"secondary"`, `"ghost"`, `"link"`). `page_link` links to another
page of the app by id; in the app shell a click opens it in place (no reload),
Ctrl/Cmd-click still opens a new tab, `params` appends query parameters to the
target URL, and `variant` draws it as a button. Both return a `link` dict, so
the legacy dashboard shows a plain link. Gallery items, `card_grid` cards,
breadcrumbs, table `link` cells and `button_group` items also accept `page`
with optional `params` (and same-origin `/page?k=v` hrefs navigate in place in
the app shell).

```python
aiui.link_button("Open report", "/files/report.html", variant="primary", external=True)
aiui.page_link("sync", "Go to Sync")
aiui.page_link("creators", "Browse creators", variant="outline", params={"tier": "top"})
```

### `aiui.video_player(src, *, autoplay, poster, title)`

```python
aiui.video_player("/video/demo.mp4", poster="/img/thumb.jpg", title="Product demo")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `src` | `str` | ✅ | — | Video file URL |
| `autoplay` | `bool` | ❌ | `False` | Auto-play (muted, as browsers require) |
| `poster` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Poster image URL |
| `title` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Caption under the player, also its accessible name |

### `aiui.file_download(label, *, href, filename, variant)`

A download button (a link with the `download` attribute).

```python
aiui.file_download("Download Report", href="/files/report.pdf", filename="report.pdf")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | `str` | ✅ | — | Button label |
| `href` | `str` | ✅ | — | File URL |
| `filename` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Suggested filename |
| `variant` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Button look (`"outline"` when unset, `"primary"`, `"secondary"`, `"ghost"`) |

### `aiui.gallery(items)`

An image/media gallery grid.

```python
aiui.gallery([
    {"src": "/img/1.jpg", "alt": "Photo 1", "caption": "Sunset"},
    {"src": "/img/2.jpg", "title": "Docs", "href": "https://docs.praison.ai", "target": "_blank"},
    {"src": "/img/launch.jpg", "title": "Launch video", "video": "/video/launch.mp4"},
    {"title": "Sync status", "page": "sync"},
])
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `Sequence[dict]` | ✅ | List of `{"src": str, "alt": str, "caption": str}` |

Optional per item: `title`, `subtitle`, `tag`, `description`, and a link that
makes the whole tile clickable and keyboard focusable: `href` (+ `target`, e.g.
`"_blank"`), `page` (an app page id, opened in place, with optional `params`) or
`video` (a video URL: the thumbnail gets a play mark and opens it, in a new tab
unless `target` is set). When both `title` and `caption` are given, `caption`
renders visibly under the title alongside any `subtitle`.

### `aiui.card_grid(items, *, columns)`

A responsive grid of entity cards (a person, channel, product, ...). It shows
`columns` cards per row on a wide page, two at medium width and one on a phone.

```python
aiui.card_grid([{
    "title": "Ada Lovelace", "subtitle": "@ada", "avatar": "/img/ada.png", "badges": ["Top 10"],
    "stats": [{"label": "Median views", "value": "41k"}, {"label": "Lift", "value": "2.4x"}],
    "page": "creator-ada",
}], columns=3)
```

`columns` (1-6, default 3) is the number per row on a wide page. Item keys: `title` (required), `subtitle`, `description` (two lines),
`image` (cover image), `avatar` (round image URL; `True` shows the title's
initials), `badges` (strings or `{"text", "variant"}`), `stats`
(`[{"label", "value"}]`), and `href` (+ `target`) or `page` to make the whole
card a link.

### `aiui.list_detail(*, rows, columns, title, page_size, search, empty)`

A list with a detail panel beside it (below it on a phone): a dense table with
a sticky header, a search box, keyboard selection (Up and Down move, Enter
opens, Escape closes) and pages. Selecting a row shows its other columns and
its `detail` dict as key facts.

```python
aiui.list_detail(
    title="Sessions",
    columns=["title", {"key": "tokens", "align": "end"}],
    rows=[{"id": "s1", "title": "Sorting", "tokens": 3412, "detail": {"Cost": "$0.02"}}],
)
```

| Key | Type | Description |
|-----|------|-------------|
| `title` (or `label`) | `str` | Accessible name, also used in the search label. Default `Items` |
| `columns` | `list[str \| dict]` | `{"key", "label", "align"}` (`align`: `end` or `right` for numbers), or plain keys. Unset: the keys of the first row except `id` and `detail` |
| `rows` | `list[dict]` | One dict per row: `id` (default: its index), a value per column key, and an optional `detail` dict shown in the panel |
| `page_size` | `int` | Rows per page. Default 25 |
| `search` | `bool` | Show the search box even when every row fits on one page (it shows by itself past one page) |
| `empty` | `str` | Text shown when there are no rows |

Use `aiui.table(...)` instead when the list needs typed cells or header
sorting (`row_detail=True` or `detail_key` give it a side panel).

### `aiui.html(content, *, height, csp, trusted, title)`

App HTML or SVG (a chart, a styled box, a small interactive widget), isolated
from the page.

```python
aiui.html("""
<svg viewBox="0 0 120 40" width="100%">
  <rect width="80" height="12" rx="3" fill="var(--aiui-accent)"/>
  <text x="0" y="32" fill="var(--aiui-muted)" font-size="10">80% done</text>
</svg>""")
aiui.html(table_html, height=320, title="Top posts")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `content` | `str` | ✅ | — | HTML string; may hold `<svg>`, `<style>` and `<script>` |
| `height` | `int\|str` | ❌ | `None` | Fixed height (pixels or a CSS length such as `"20rem"`). Default: fit the content |
| `csp` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Content-Security-Policy for the frame, replacing the default below |
| `trusted` | `bool` | ❌ | `False` | Render inline in the page instead of in a frame, sanitised (see below) |
| `title` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Accessible name of the frame (default "Embedded content") |

!!! danger "Security model"
    **Default (sandboxed frame).** In the app shell the content renders in an
    `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` built from `srcdoc`, without
    `allow-same-origin`. Its scripts run in an opaque origin: they cannot read
    or change the app's page, cookies, `localStorage` or session, cannot call
    `/api/*` as the signed-in user, cannot open pop-ups, submit forms or
    navigate the top window. A `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">`
    also blocks network access. The default policy is
    `default-src 'none'; img-src data: https:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`.
    Pass `csp=` to tighten or loosen it; the frame sizes itself with a small
    inline script, so a policy without `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` needs a
    fixed `height`.

    **`trusted=True` (inline).** The content is placed in the page through
    the sanitised Markdown pipeline (`rehype-sanitize`): scripts, event
    handlers, `style`, `<iframe>` and `<svg>` are removed. Use it for simple
    markup (tables, lists, links) that should flow with the page text; use
    the default frame for SVG and anything with scripts.

    **Never put untrusted text into raw HTML yourself.** Escape values you
    interpolate (`html.escape(...)`) even inside the frame: an injected
    script cannot reach the app, but it can still change what the frame shows.

    **Legacy `dashboard` style.** `html` renders in the same sandboxed frame
    (fixed height, default 320 px). `html_embed` there still sets the HTML
    directly on the page, where scripts and inline handlers run: pass only
    content you wrote.

#### Theme variables

These CSS custom properties are defined on the page in both themes and copied
into every `html` frame, where they follow light/dark changes live:

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `--aiui-fg` | Body text |
| `--aiui-muted` | Secondary text, axis labels |
| `--aiui-border` | Hairlines, grid lines |
| `--aiui-bg` | Page background |
| `--aiui-surface` | Card / panel background |
| `--aiui-accent` | Brand accent (follows the theme preset) |
| `--aiui-success` / `--aiui-warning` / `--aiui-danger` / `--aiui-info` | Status colours |
| `--aiui-font` / `--aiui-font-mono` | Font stacks |

The frame's body already uses `--aiui-fg` and `--aiui-font` and has a
transparent background, so plain HTML matches the page.

### `aiui.html_embed(content, *, height, csp, trusted, title)`

The older name of [`aiui.html`](#aiuihtmlcontent-height-csp-trusted-title):
same parameters, same sandboxed frame in the app shell. The block keeps its
`html_embed` type, so the legacy `dashboard` style renders it as before
(directly on the page). New code should use `aiui.html`.

### `aiui.pagination(*, total, page, per_page, id, action)`

Pagination controls.

```python
aiui.pagination(total=250, page=3, per_page=25)
aiui.pagination(total=250, page=3, per_page=25, action="explore")
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `total` | `int` | ✅ | — | Total items |
| `page` | `int` | ❌ | `1` | Current page (1-based) |
| `per_page` | `int` | ❌ | `10` | Items per page |
| `id` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | Identifier echoed in the page-change event |
| `action` | `str` | ❌ | `None` | App shell: POST `{id, page, per_page, total}` to `/api/pages/{page}/action` |

The control is optimistic: clicking ←, →, or a page number updates the active
page and dispatches a bubbling `aiui:pagination` DOM event. Buttons that would
go out of bounds are disabled and emit nothing. `page` is clamped to the valid range.

```javascript
container.addEventListener('aiui:pagination', (e) => {
  const { id, page, per_page, total } = e.detail;
  renderRows(rows.slice((page - 1) * per_page, page * per_page)); // or fetch()
});
```
